sections.heading: What resit support costs in Abu Dhabi, and what moves the number
paragraphs: Resit tuition sits at the upper end of the market, because the work is specification-specific and time-bounded. Market rates in the UAE run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online and university-student tutors, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit including travel, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB, IGCSE or A-Level specialist. Premium named or examiner-led tuition has been advertised at AED 650. Those are market figures published by providers and rate trackers, not IB Gram prices.

Three things move the number in this emirate specifically. The first is format: in-home rates carry travel, and in Abu Dhabi travel between the mainland communities and the island is a genuine cost, which is why in-home bands sit AED 50 to 150 above online for the same tutor quality. The second is proximity to the series, because availability tightens in the eight weeks before a paper and the specialists are booked first. The third is subject scarcity: a resit in Mathematics has a wide tutor pool, a resit in Cambridge Art and Design or a less-entered language has a very narrow one.

Package structures seen in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. A resit plan is usually denser than a weekly habit, so budget against total hours rather than against a monthly figure.

For context, Abu Dhabi school fees are set and approved through the emirate's regulatory process, and in Dubai the KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Tutoring is the variable line in a family's education budget, which is exactly why a resit plan should state a total hour count up front rather than running open-ended. IB Gram does not publish a price list on these pages; the first lesson is free with no card required, and pricing is confirmed in the consultation.

sections.heading: Coursework, practicals and what carries over
paragraphs: This is the question families ask last and should ask first. Whether a coursework or practical mark carries into a resit depends on the specification, and the answer changes what the resit actually involves. Some components can be carried forward from a previous series; others must be sat again. The centre's examinations officer can confirm this against the current syllabus for the exact code, and that confirmation should happen before the entry is made rather than after.

Where a practical or coursework component must be re-taken, a private candidate has a real problem, because not every centre can host it. A Cambridge science specification with a practical-skills paper needs a centre with the apparatus and the willingness to run it for an external candidate. A language with a speaking component needs an examiner. If the centre cannot deliver the component, the entry has to move to a centre that can, and that decision changes both the timetable and the fee.

Where a mark does carry forward, the resit narrows to the written papers and the plan gets correspondingly tighter. That is the best case for a resit candidate: a known weak paper, a fixed number of weeks, and no coursework to rebuild. It is also where the biggest grade movements happen, because every available hour goes into the component that actually lost the marks.

On the coursework itself, the boundary is absolute and worth stating plainly. A tutor teaches, explains, models technique, and gives feedback on work the student has written. A tutor does not write, complete or redraft assessed coursework, and no IB Gram tutor will do so. Providers in this market sell completed assessed work; that is a malpractice trigger for the student and the reason we say what the boundary is rather than leaving it implied.

sections.heading: Resits, equivalency and what the Ministry actually counts
paragraphs: A resit sometimes matters for reasons that have nothing to do with a sixth-form offer. For the British track, the UAE Ministry of Education requires a student to pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

That last point catches families out. A student holding five IGCSEs where two are Arabic and Islamic Education is holding three for equivalency purposes, not five, and needs two more qualifying subjects. One competitor page ranking for these queries states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced requirement is five accredited subjects excluding Arabic and Islamic education. Getting the count right is the difference between one targeted resit and a year of unnecessary work.

For the American track the Ministry sets test requirements instead: English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics through at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold appears in the sourced material we hold, so we publish none; verify any IB figure against the Ministry's own channel.

IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency or attestation. We describe the requirement, point to the authority, and make sure a resit plan is aimed at a subject that actually counts. Tutoring is not required for equivalency, university admission or school progression, and anyone telling you otherwise is selling urgency rather than teaching.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, not left open. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

MoHRE's own service page for this is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, listing no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anyone, including us.

Two further points matter for a resit. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the permit-holder's own school. So a plan built around your child's own class teacher tutoring them privately is not a plan we will arrange, and you should be cautious of anyone offering it. Verify current wording against the live ADEK policy document.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal again: it needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no regulator permit or accreditation and does not claim one. We are an online tutor-matching platform with no UAE office, and we say so because several pages in this search result imply otherwise.

sections.heading: The twelve-week resit plan, and what happens if the subject is scarce
paragraphs: Twelve weeks is the shape most resit plans take, because it is long enough to rebuild two or three topics properly and short enough that a family can hold the schedule. Weeks one and two are diagnosis: component marks read, one full paper sat under timing, a ranked topic list produced with marks attached. Weeks three to eight are the rebuild, one or two sessions a week, each ending with a question set returned before the next lesson. Weeks nine to twelve are paper discipline, where content stops and timing starts.

The measure of progress is marks recovered on repeat questions, not topics ticked off. A student who could not earn the last four marks on a structured question in week two and earns three of them in week seven has moved; a student who has covered nine topics and still loses the same marks has not. That distinction is why the plan gets reviewed every fourth session and rewritten when the evidence says to, rather than run to completion because it was written down.

Availability is where most platforms stop being honest, so here is the position. For a mainstream resit subject in Abu Dhabi, a specialist match usually takes two to four working days. For a narrow specification, a less-entered language, or a creative subject with a coursework component, it can take longer, and in the eight weeks before a series it takes longer still because the specialists fill up first. If we cannot cover a subject at the standard a resit needs, we say so rather than putting a general tutor in front of a specification they have never marked.

Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the match may be a tutor based elsewhere teaching into Gulf Standard Time, which for an online lesson changes nothing about the lesson and everything about the pool available. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; home visits are a service we run only in India, and the comparison table on this page exists so you can judge that trade on its merits rather than on our description of it.

process.title: Send the statement of results

Send the statement of results, the subject and the exact syllabus code, and the target grade with the reason behind it. That is enough to tell you whether the target fits the time left.

process.title: Confirm the series and the centre
process.description: Before any teaching plan is fixed, settle which series you are entering and which centre is taking the entry, with the centre's own cut-off date and zone timetable in writing. The teaching plan is built backwards from that examination date, not forwards from today.

process.title: Agree the hour count
process.description: The plan states a total number of hours against the ranked topic list, so you are agreeing to a block of work rather than an open-ended arrangement. If the honest hour count does not fit the series, we say so and recommend the next one.

whyPoints.title: The plan starts from the real paper
whyPoints.description: A resit plan built on a tutor's own diagnostic test ignores the most informative document you have. We start from the component marks and, where the centre can request it, the original script, because that removes guessing about which paper lost the grade.

whyPoints.title: Syllabus codes, not subject names
whyPoints.description: 0580 and 4MA1 are both called Maths and they examine differently. Every plan names the code, the tier and the components, so the practice your child does matches the paper they will sit rather than a generic version of the subject.

whyPoints.title: The hour count is stated up front
whyPoints.description: Resit work is time-bounded, so the plan carries a total hour estimate against a ranked topic list. If the target grade does not fit the weeks remaining before the entry deadline, we tell you that before you pay for anything.

whyPoints.description: Because lessons are online and one-to-one, the match is made from tutors who have taught that specification to examination rather than from tutors who can reach your community by 5pm. For a scarce specification that difference decides whether a match exists at all.

whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, models and gives feedback on your child's own work. No IB Gram tutor writes or completes assessed coursework. Providers in this search result sell finished assessments; we state the boundary because the student carries the malpractice risk, not the seller.

whyPoints.description: Mainstream resit subjects match in two to four working days. Narrow specifications take longer, and inside eight weeks of a series they take longer again. When we cannot cover a subject properly we say so instead of filling the slot with a generalist.

faqs.question: Can my child resit just one IGCSE subject, or does the whole set have to be taken again?
faqs.answer: One subject is fine. IGCSE results are reported per subject, so a candidate can be entered for a single syllabus in a later series and leave everything else as it stands. That is the most common resit in Abu Dhabi: one science or Mathematics standing between a student and a sixth-form offer. The entry is made against the specific syllabus code, and the only thing that has to be re-sat is whatever that specification requires, which may include a practical or coursework component. Confirm the component list with the centre before entering so the revision plan matches the papers actually being taken.

faqs.question: Which exam series should an Abu Dhabi resit candidate enter, November or June?
faqs.answer: Work backwards from the date the grade is needed. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, with a March series in some regions, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. If a sixth form needs the grade before the academic year starts, June is usually the answer. If the student has already started Year 12 and the offer is conditional, November can work provided the school has confirmed in writing that it will accept a January results date. Check your centre's zone timetable, because Cambridge allocates centres to six administrative zones with different versions.

faqs.question: Does a resit grade replace the original grade on the certificate?
faqs.answer: A resit produces a new certificated result for that subject in that series. The earlier result still exists in the student's record, but in practice sixth forms and universities read the grade the applicant presents, and the higher one is the one that gets used. For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, what counts is holding five accredited subjects at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, so a resit that lifts a subject into range solves the requirement directly. Verify current rules on the Ministry's own channel.

faqs.question: Can my child sit an IGCSE resit as a private candidate if their school will not re-enter them?
faqs.answer: Yes, but it takes arranging. The student becomes a private candidate and needs a centre willing to accept external entries for that exact syllabus code in that series. Not every school licensed by ADEK is a centre for every board, and a Cambridge centre will not necessarily take a Pearson entry. Ask three questions in writing: do you accept external candidates for this code, what is your internal cut-off date, and can you deliver every component including practicals or speaking papers. Centre fees sit on top of the board entry fee and are set by the centre.

faqs.question: How many weeks of tutoring does a one-grade IGCSE improvement usually take?
faqs.answer: Nobody can promise a grade, and anyone who does should be treated with real scepticism. What can be said is the shape of the work. A one-grade move in a science or Mathematics typically needs eight to twelve weeks of one or two weekly sessions, with the last four to six spent entirely on timed papers. Two grades usually needs a full term or the next series. The variable is not effort but how many of the lost marks came from content versus timing and command-term misreading, and the first diagnostic session exists to establish exactly that.

faqs.question: What does specialist IGCSE resit tuition cost per hour in Abu Dhabi in 2026?
faqs.answer: Market rates, not IB Gram prices: roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online or university-student tutors, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 200 to 450 or more for an IGCSE or A-Level specialist, and AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit once travel is priced in. Premium named tuition has been advertised at AED 650. Resit work sits in the specialist band because it is specification-specific and time-bounded. Ask any provider for the total hour count rather than the hourly rate, because that is the number that matters.

faqs.question: Does a coursework or practical mark carry over into a resit?
faqs.answer: It depends on the specification, and this is the question to settle before entering rather than after. Some components can be carried forward from a previous series; others must be sat again. The centre's examinations officer can confirm the position against the current syllabus for the exact code. Where a practical or speaking component must be re-taken, a private candidate needs a centre with the apparatus or the examiner to deliver it, which rules some specifications out entirely at some centres. If a mark does carry forward, the resit narrows to the written papers and the plan gets considerably tighter.

faqs.question: Will a resit grade still count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: For the British track the Ministry requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. A certificated resit result is a certificated result, so a subject lifted into range counts. One ranking competitor states six subjects are required; the sourced figure is five. Equivalency is handled by the authority, not by IB Gram, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

faqs.question: My child needs a grade 5 in Mathematics 0580 for sixth form. Is one term realistic?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and the component report tells you whether. If the first attempt was Extended and the marks were lost mainly on Paper 4 structured questions, a term of method-writing discipline plus functions and probability work is a realistic route to a 5. If marks were lost evenly across both papers, the content base needs rebuilding and a term is tight. A Core entry is the other option: it caps the grade but makes the cap far more achievable, and if the offer asks for a 5 rather than a 7 that trade is worth putting on the table.

faqs.question: Can a student in Abu Dhabi enter the Cambridge March series rather than waiting for June?
faqs.answer: Where the centre offers it, yes, and the dates show why it has to be planned early. For the March 2027 series Cambridge published an examination period of 3 February to 4 March 2027 with final entries due 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results to centres on Cambridge International Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. The entry deadline therefore sits more than two months before the paper. Confirm with your centre that it runs the March series for your syllabus code and which zone timetable applies to it.

faqs.question: Should a resit candidate move from Extended down to Core, or stay on Extended?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what the grade is for. A Cambridge candidate entered for Core faces a lower grade ceiling but a far more achievable one, because the papers are shorter in content reach and the questions are more direct. If a sixth-form offer needs a 5 and the first Extended attempt landed at 3, a secure Core entry can be the better bet. If the subject is being continued to A Level and the department expects a 6 or 7, Core closes that door and a second Extended attempt with proper diagnosis is the right call.

faqs.question: How do we see the actual paper our child sat to know where the marks went?
faqs.answer: Through the centre. Cambridge and Pearson both operate access-to-script services requested by the examinations officer, not by the family directly, and the statement of results already gives you marks by component without any request at all. Start with the component breakdown, because it tells you which paper lost the grade and that one fact reorganises the whole plan. We do not reproduce or supply board papers, mark schemes or syllabus documents; we work from what your child wrote and cite the board's own published material by link.

faqs.question: Can my child resit with Pearson Edexcel if the first attempt was Cambridge?
faqs.answer: Switching boards is possible, since the two are separate qualifications, but it usually makes the resit harder rather than easier. Pearson International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 and Cambridge 0580 cover similar mathematics with different paper structures, question phrasing and tiering, so a student switching boards is learning a new examination on top of fixing the original problem. The switch is worth it only where a centre will take one board and not the other, or where a component the student struggles with does not exist on the other specification. Otherwise, resit the specification they know.

faqs.question: Do resit lessons happen at our villa in Khalifa City, or online?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one, over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a resit that matters in your favour, because the specialist pool stops being tutors who can reach Khalifa City through the evening traffic and becomes tutors who have taught and marked the exact specification your child is re-sitting. Screen sharing also means the marked paper and the question set sit in front of both of them in the same window.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for the subject we need to resit?
faqs.answer: We tell you. For mainstream resit subjects in Abu Dhabi a specialist match usually takes two to four working days; for a narrow specification, a less-entered language or a creative subject with coursework it can take longer, and inside eight weeks of a series it takes longer again because specialists fill first. Where no UAE-based tutor covers the specification, the match may be a tutor elsewhere teaching into Gulf Standard Time, which for an online lesson changes the pool and not the lesson. We would rather decline a subject than put a generalist in front of a specification they have never marked.

abu-dhabi/igcse-resit-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the component marks, not the calendar
abu-dhabi/igcse-resit-tutor.closingBody: A resit is a solvable problem with a deadline attached, and the two things that decide it are which component lost the grade and how many weeks remain before the entry closes. Send the statement of results, the syllabus code and the target grade, and the first lesson is free with no card required. The tutor will finish it with a written statement of what cost the grade and an honest hour count for fixing it. If the target does not fit the series, we will say so and point you at the next one rather than sell you a plan that lands on the same grade twice. Lessons are one-to-one, online, and timed to your week in Abu Dhabi.

intro.heading: Tuition you can audit, not tuition you have to trust
paragraphs: Most IGCSE tuition is sold on reassurance and reviewed on feeling. A parent books an hour a week, the student says the sessions are useful, the next report arrives, and nobody can say which of those three things caused the other. That is a poor way to spend AED 200 an hour for eighteen months. The alternative is not more faith in the tutor. It is a small, dull set of documents that exist whether the term went well or badly, and that let you see the difference between a child who is learning and a child who is being kept company for sixty minutes.

This page is built around those documents. A marked script with the mark scheme beside it. An error log that separates a knowledge gap from a method slip from a misread command term. A session note that names the paper and the component rather than the subject. A draft history on any coursework piece that shows whose thinking produced it. None of this is exotic. It is what a working subject teacher already produces for a class of twenty-five, and it is reasonable to expect it for one student at a private rate.

Abu Dhabi sharpens the case. Private schools here answer to ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which u.ae describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Enrolment sits in three rough bands: the island schools around Al Bateen, Al Khalidiyah and Al Mushrif; the Khalifa City, Al Raha and Yas Island corridor; and the newer mainland communities out towards Al Shamkha and Mussafah. A family in Al Reef and a family in Al Rawdah face the same syllabus and completely different evenings.

Delivery here is online and one-to-one. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an Abu Dhabi address; in-home visiting is a service we run only in India. That is said plainly because it changes what you are comparing. A visiting tutor is limited to whoever can reach Al Reef before seven in the evening. A live video session is limited only by who is free at that hour, which is how a household ends up with an IGCSE Chemistry 0620 specialist instead of a generalist with a car and a free Thursday.

What follows is the market in numbers, the evidence to ask for, the Cambridge and Pearson calendar read backwards from the entry deadline rather than forwards from the exam, and the point at which the honest answer is to stop paying. Figures in AED are market rates published by other providers, with the band attributed to whoever published it. They are context for your decision rather than a price list of ours; our own commercial answer is a first lesson at no charge followed by a consultation.

abu-dhabi/igcse-tuition.programmesIntro: An IGCSE plan in Abu Dhabi has to know which board your child sits, which tier the school has entered them for, and what comes after Year 11. Those three decisions change the papers, the grade ceiling and the university paperwork more than any choice of tutor does.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Subjects carry four-digit codes that decide everything about the plan: Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, First Language English 0500, English as a Second Language 0510. Two children in the same Abu Dhabi year group can sit different codes in the same subject.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your child's exams officer which zone the school sits in before you build a revision calendar around any published date.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. Codes begin 4: Mathematics A is 4MA1, Physics 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1, Biology 4BI1, English Language A 4EA1. The structure differs from Cambridge in ways that matter for revision, including tiering by Foundation and Higher rather than Core and Extended, and a different balance of question styles across the papers.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools enter students for both boards across a nine-subject timetable, so a household can be running 0580 Mathematics and 4PH1 Physics at once. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why a plan should be built against the live official timetable rather than against a date someone remembered from last year.

programmes.name: Core, Extended, Foundation and Higher tiers
programmes.description: Tiering is the single most consequential decision in an IGCSE timetable, and it is usually made by the school rather than the family. Cambridge Core and Extended papers differ in content and in grade ceiling. Pearson Foundation and Higher do the same under different names. A child entered for the wrong tier is either being capped or being asked to sit material the lessons never covered.
programmes.countryNote: Tier decisions in Abu Dhabi schools are commonly confirmed around the final entry deadline, which for the Cambridge March 2027 series fell on 27 November 2026. That means the conversation has to happen in the autumn term, with marked evidence in hand, rather than in the spring when the entry is already lodged.

programmes.name: After IGCSE: A Level, IB Diploma and equivalency
programmes.description: IGCSE grades act as the entry gate to A Level and to the IB Diploma Programme, and as part of the Ministry of Education equivalency file for students who later apply to UAE universities. Subject choices made in Year 9 therefore reach into Year 13. The jump in reading load and independent work between Year 11 and Year 12 catches out students who were carried by memory at IGCSE.
programmes.countryNote: On the British track, Gulf Today reported the UAE equivalency requirement as five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among those five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Verify the current rule on the Ministry's own channel before relying on it.

abu-dhabi/igcse-tuition.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Abu Dhabi households ask for most often, with the syllabus codes that decide which papers are sat. A plan that says Physics is not a plan. A plan that says 0625 Extended, Papers 2 and 4, with Paper 6 as the alternative to practical, is one you can check.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Marks leak in three predictable places: multi-step algebra where method marks are lost to arithmetic, the wordy later questions where the problem is never translated into mathematics, and bearings or transformation work that is rehearsed once and then forgotten. Extended candidates also need fluency in topics Core never touches.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Electricity and waves produce the heaviest losses, usually because formulae are recalled but units and rearrangement are not. The alternative to practical paper rewards a specific skill set, including reading a scale correctly, identifying a control variable and describing a method precisely enough for somebody else to repeat it.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Moles calculations split into a mass-to-moles step and a ratio step, and students who lose marks almost always lose them at the second. Organic chemistry rewards pattern recognition rather than memory, and the extended-response questions on electrolysis and rates need a structure the mark scheme can follow.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The content volume is the trap. Students revise the topics they enjoy and arrive at the paper strong on transport in plants and silent on homeostasis. Command-term discipline decides the longer answers: describe, explain and suggest ask for different things and are marked differently.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0653 / 0654)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, double or single award
subjects.description: A child on Combined Science is not studying a reduced version of three separate sciences; the content map is different. Revising from separate-science notes wastes hours on material that will never be examined, and leaves gaps in the parts the award does assess.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Reading questions are marked for selection and inference rather than for retelling, and the directed writing task is assessed on audience and register as much as on accuracy. Students who write well and read quickly tend to lose marks for answering the question they expected rather than the one on the paper.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: The entry choice between First Language and Second Language English sets a ceiling that affects later applications, so it deserves a conversation with the school rather than a shrug. Within the paper, the summary task and the note-making task carry marks that respond quickly to technique work.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (Cambridge 0455 / 0450)
subjects.description: Both reward a diagram or a definition before the explanation, and both punish a student who writes a general essay. Evaluation marks on the longer questions need a judgement with a reason attached, which is a teachable habit rather than a talent.

subjects.name: Geography and History (Cambridge 0460 / 0470)
subjects.description: Case-study recall is the differentiator in Geography; source handling is the differentiator in History. In both, the mark scheme rewards specific named detail, and a student who has learned the concept but no example will stall at the middle of the mark range.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT (Cambridge 0478 / 0417)
subjects.description: Theory papers need precise vocabulary, and the practical components need methodical evidence rather than clever shortcuts. Pseudocode and trace tables are the two skills that most reliably move a grade, because both are examined and both are rarely practised at home.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Foreign Language (Cambridge 0508 / 0544)
subjects.levels: First Language and Foreign Language routes
subjects.description: Arabic runs alongside an international curriculum for most students in the emirate under federal requirements, and the first-language and foreign-language routes assess very different things. Treating one as an easier version of the other is the most common planning error families make here.

abu-dhabi/igcse-tuition.regionsIntro: Abu Dhabi is three different school-run problems wearing one city's name. Where a household sits decides what time a session can realistically start, which schools the children attend, and how much a visiting tutor would have to charge to make the trip worth taking.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Dense island addresses within a short drive of several British-curriculum schools, which keeps local tutor supply high for Mathematics and English and thin for the rarer IGCSE options. Sessions here can start early because the school run is short.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Rawdah
regions.note: Villa communities feeding the long-established island schools. Families often run two or three children at different stages at once, which makes a fixed weekly slot per child more valuable than a flexible one shared between them.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: A large low-rise spread with internal distances that surprise newcomers. A tutor crossing from the island adds a real drive in each direction, which is why households here tend to compare an online hour against a visiting hour on cost per teaching minute.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: Corridor addresses between the island and Khalifa City, close to several large academies. Evening slots compete with sport and extracurricular commitments, so Year 11 households often move the weekly session to a Friday or Saturday morning.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: A short bridge from the island but a distinct catchment, with families whose children often transfer in mid-course from other systems. Mid-year joiners usually need a syllabus-gap audit before anybody books a weekly hour.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: High-rise living with lift and parking delays that quietly eat into a visiting tutor's hour. Study space is often a shared dining table, so a session plan here has to assume headphones and a defined sixty minutes rather than a quiet study.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: A newer residential catchment where several families are on their first IGCSE cycle. Questions here lean towards how the two boards differ and what the tier decision actually means, rather than towards last-minute exam rescue.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Mussafah
regions.note: Mainland communities with a wide spread of school fees and curricula, and the longest drives to the island schools. Online delivery removes the single largest cost a household here would otherwise pay a visiting tutor for.

regions.name: Al Shamkha and Al Reef
regions.note: Outer communities where a weekday visiting session often cannot start before seven in the evening once traffic is counted. A live video slot at half past four is a different lesson entirely, because the student is not yet tired.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi island: Al Bateen, Al Khalidiyah, Al Mushrif and Al Rawdah
schoolClusters.note: The longest-established British and international schools in the emirate sit within a few kilometres of each other here, which means households often compare IGCSE results across three schools their neighbours attend. Students we support in this cluster most often ask for Mathematics, Chemistry and First Language English.

schoolClusters.city: Saadiyat, Al Reem and the Khalifa City to Al Raha corridor
schoolClusters.note: A newer band of academies serving the island fringe and the inland communities. Transfers in and out are more common here, so IGCSE gap audits and tier conversations come up more often than straight exam rescue. ADEK publishes inspection ratings for all of them.

schoolClusters.note: A wider fee range and a wider spread of curricula, with several large schools entering big IGCSE cohorts. Distance from the island schools is what pushes households here towards online delivery rather than a visiting tutor's travel premium.

modes.description: A fixed slot on the same evening each week for one subject and one syllabus code. The hour opens with the error log from last week, works a past-paper question type under time, and closes with one named thing to practise. This is the format that produces a usable record, because each session is comparable to the one before it.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition in Abu Dhabi buys that the school day cannot
paragraphs: IGCSE tuition in Abu Dhabi buys three things a classroom cannot give one child: time on that child's specific errors, a second reading of a marked script, and a plan that names a paper rather than a subject. Market rates run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor working online, and AED 200 to 450 and above for a subject specialist, on the figures other providers publish. None of that buys more content. The content is already being delivered six hours a day by a school ADEK licenses and inspects.

The gap a private hour fills is diagnostic. A Year 11 teacher marking thirty IGCSE Chemistry 0620 Paper 4 scripts can tell you that your child lost marks on moles and on the six-mark electrolysis question. A private hour can tell you that the moles marks went because the mass-to-moles step was right and the ratio step was not, and that the electrolysis answer had the chemistry in it but no structure the mark scheme could reward. The first of those is a grade. The second is something to practise on Tuesday.

That is why the rest of this page is about evidence rather than enthusiasm. Every claim a tutor makes about progress can be checked against a document, and a provider who will not produce the document is telling you something useful about the provider. The sections below set out what should exist after four paid sessions, how to decide which subject gets the money when nine are running at once, what the Abu Dhabi market actually charges and who published those figures, and the dates that decide whether a plan has any room left in it at all.

sections.heading: The paper trail a term of IGCSE tuition should leave behind
paragraphs: Five documents, and none of them is difficult to produce. A marked script, an error log, a dated session note, a draft history on anything assessed inside school, and a written plan carrying the syllabus code. If all five exist at the end of a half-term, you can answer the only question that matters: has this child's performance on the actual papers moved, and in which direction.

The marked script is the anchor. It has to be a past paper sat under time, marked against the published scheme rather than against a tutor's sense of it, with the lost marks annotated by cause. The error log is the memory of the tuition. Without it, each session fixes something and the fix evaporates, which is how a family can pay for twenty hours and find the same mistake in the February mock that was in the October one.

The session note is the cheapest of the five and the one most often missing. Three lines is enough, provided those lines name the paper, the component and the specific skill worked on. The plan is what lets you say no to drift: when a tutor proposes a different topic every week, the plan is the document that asks why. A provider who produces none of these is not necessarily teaching badly, but you have no way of knowing either way, and at a private rate that is the thing you are actually buying.

sections.heading: Nine subjects, two funded hours: triage by evidence
paragraphs: Almost no Abu Dhabi family funds tuition in nine subjects, and the ones who try usually buy a thin hour in each and move nothing. The useful question is which single subject, in which single paper, will convert the next two hundred dirhams into the most marks. The evidence answers that better than the student's opinion does, and better than the subject the parent found hardest at school.

Start by sorting the lost marks into four causes. Content never learned. Method known but executed carelessly. Structure missing on extended-response questions. Time run out. Only the first and the third reliably respond to paid teaching hours. The second responds to a checking protocol that costs nothing, and the fourth responds to sitting papers split against a clock at the kitchen table, also free.

The second filter is the shape of the timetable. A child with a grade 4 in one subject and grade 7s elsewhere has a certificate problem in one place, and funding that subject alone is the efficient move. A child who is a grade 5 across the board has a study-habit problem that one subject's tuition will not touch. The table below is the version of this conversation we have most often with households in Khalifa City and on Al Reem Island, where two children and one budget is the normal case. One more filter is worth applying before any money is spent: how many papers are left to sit in that subject. Funding a subject whose final paper is three weeks away buys very little, while the same hour in a subject with a full year of assessment ahead compounds. Sort the nine subjects by papers remaining, then by cause of lost marks, and the funding order usually becomes obvious without anybody arguing about which subject is hardest.

sections.heading: The data drop: what an Abu Dhabi school report measures, and what it leaves out
paragraphs: Three times a year a school sends home a set of numbers, and families reasonably treat them as the scoreboard for whatever tuition they are paying for. They are not quite that. A reported grade is usually a blend of class assessments, a mock, teacher judgement and a target derived from a baseline test the parent never saw. Two of those four inputs can move without the student's examination performance changing at all.

Ask the school two questions. First, what is this grade actually based on: a full paper under time, a topic test, or a professional judgement. Second, which paper and which components does it cover, because a Chemistry grade built from Paper 2 alone tells you very little about how the Paper 4 extended responses are going. Most schools answer both questions readily, and the answers reshape the tuition plan more than any report ever does.

The inspection rating sits in the same category. ADEK licenses and inspects private schools in the emirate and publishes its ratings, and that rating is genuine information about the institution. It is not information about your child's Paper 4 technique. A strongly rated school can have a weak year in one subject because a teacher left in October, and a lower-rated school can have a maths department that gets results. Treat the rating as context for choosing a school and the marked scripts as evidence for choosing tuition. There is one more thing a report cannot show you, which is the gap between a grade and a boundary. Published grade boundaries move every series, so a student three marks below a boundary and a student fifteen marks below it can be reported with the same grade for months. Only the raw component marks reveal which of those two students you are dealing with, and that distinction decides whether a term of tuition is a rescue or a refinement.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition costs around Abu Dhabi, with the sources named
paragraphs: Most providers in this market publish no price at all, and two of the pages ranking for these searches quote in dollars, which is not the currency the household transacts in. The table below collects the AED figures that are actually published, attributed to whoever published them. Read it as the market, not as our rate card: a tier tells you what an hour in that band usually contains, which is more useful than a single number.

Monthly packages are where comparisons quietly break. Figures seen in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visiting sessions. Those two things are not the same purchase: one is eight contacts with eight error-log updates, the other is four longer contacts with a travel component inside the price. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support.

Two practical notes. A visiting rate always contains a drive that nobody invoices separately, which is why the in-home band sits above the online band for the same teacher. And the cheapest hour is frequently the most expensive, because an hour that produces no marked script and no error log has to be bought again. Ask any provider what their hour includes in writing before comparing it with another provider's hour.

sections.heading: Entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers
paragraphs: Families plan backwards from the exam. Boards plan backwards from the entry. The gap between those two habits is where most of the avoidable damage in an IGCSE year happens, because the decisions that are still reversible, such as which tier a student is entered for, close long before the revision starts to feel urgent.

Cambridge's March 2027 series is the clearest worked example available. The exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, but final entries were due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades on 27 February 2027, results on Cambridge International Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. Read that sequence in order: the tier choice had to be made nearly ten weeks before the first paper, with whatever marked evidence existed in November.

Pearson works to its own rhythm. International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so every plan should be built against the live official timetable rather than a remembered date. IB Diploma session dates are deliberately absent from this page: the IB's own site cannot be checked automatically, and an unverified date on a planning page is worse than no date at all. The habit worth building is simple. Take the entry deadline for your child's series, mark it on a wall calendar, and count the weeks between today and that date rather than between today and the first paper. Everything reversible lives inside that shorter window, and everything after it is execution.

sections.heading: Controlled components, coursework and where a paid tutor stops
paragraphs: Every board requires that assessed work submitted under a student's name is the student's own. That rule is not a formality, and the consequences of breaking it land on the student rather than on the tutor. So the boundary has to be stated before the money changes hands, in words specific enough to be enforced.

Here is where the line sits in practice. A tutor may explain the published criteria in the board's own language, teach the skills the piece demands, read a draft the student has written and say which criterion it currently fails, ask questions that make the student rethink a section, and show a worked example on a different topic entirely. A tutor may not supply sentences for the submission, rewrite a paragraph into its final form, choose the topic on the student's behalf, or hand over material the student then presents as their own thinking.

The practical safeguard is the draft history. If every version is kept, with the tutor's comments visible as comments rather than as edits, then the development of the work is documented and the student can show their own progression if anybody asks. This is also where essay-selling operations in this market expose their customers: a finished piece bought for a fee is a malpractice trigger, it is the fastest way to lose a qualification, and it is the one service this page will not sell at any price. Ask any prospective tutor to describe the boundary in their own words before the first session. The answer is diagnostic. A tutor who describes it precisely, and who volunteers how they keep drafts so authorship stays visible, has worked inside a school's academic-honesty process. A tutor who treats the question as paperwork has not, and that is worth knowing while the engagement is still hypothetical rather than in March with a deadline approaching.

sections.heading: Movement that is real, and movement that is noise
paragraphs: Grade movement is lumpy, and the first month is the most misleading month of the whole engagement. A student who scored poorly because they ran out of time can gain several marks in one session purely from pacing, and that gain is real but it does not repeat. A student who has genuinely closed a content gap will often show nothing for three weeks and then move on two papers at once.

So measure component marks before you measure grades. A Physics score that goes from eleven to seventeen on the Paper 6 practical questions is evidence, whether or not the overall grade has changed yet, because the mark scheme attributes those marks to identifiable skills. A reported grade that moves from 5 to 6 between two different assessments of different components is not evidence of anything in particular.

Three honest caveats. Boundaries move every series, so the same raw mark can be a different grade in June and in November. A mock paper marked generously flatters everybody, and a mock marked harshly to motivate a cohort does the opposite. And no tutor, however experienced with 0580 past papers, can promise a particular outcome; what a tutor can do is show you the component marks each month and let you draw the line yourself. Any provider who offers certainty about a final grade is selling something other than teaching. The practical consequence is a reporting rhythm rather than a weekly verdict. Record component marks at each timed paper, compare them across a half-term rather than across a fortnight, and ignore the single good session entirely. Noise lives in the short window and signal lives in the longer one, which is why the review date on the plan sits at the end of a half-term rather than at the end of a week.

sections.heading: When the evidence says change the plan
paragraphs: Tuition should be cancellable on the evidence, which means deciding in advance what evidence would make you stop. Our own answer is the fourth session and then the end of the half-term. If the error log has not shrunk, if no paper has been sat under time, and if the component marks have not moved in either direction, something in the plan is wrong and more of the same hour will not fix it.

Four things are usually wrong. The subject is wrong, because the real problem is in a different one. The tier is wrong, and the student is sitting material the lessons never covered. The format is wrong, because a weekly hour cannot repair eighteen months of gaps and the household needs a block of paper clinics instead. Or the match is wrong, and a competent tutor and a particular fifteen-year-old simply do not work together, which is common and nobody's failure.

A fifth possibility deserves naming. Sometimes the honest conclusion is that paid tuition is not the thing this child needs right now, and that sleep, a workable revision routine or a conversation with the school's head of department would do more. A provider who cannot reach that conclusion out loud has an incentive problem. We would rather say it at session four than take the money for another term and have you work it out in May. Write the stopping rule down before the first session, in one sentence, and give a copy to the tutor. Something like: if no paper has been sat under time and no component mark has moved by session four, the engagement pauses while we work out why. A tutor who agrees to that in advance has nothing to hide, and a household with that sentence in writing never has to have an awkward conversation about whether to carry on.

process.title: Send the syllabus codes, not just the subjects
process.description: Tell us which board and which code each subject sits under, and which tier the school has entered. Cambridge 0580 Extended and Pearson 4MA1 Higher are different purchases. If you do not know, the exams officer at the school does, and the question takes one email.

process.title: Send the last two marked scripts
process.description: Photographs are fine. Two marked papers tell a subject specialist more in ten minutes than a half-hour conversation about how the term has gone. What we are reading for is the cause of each lost mark, which decides whether the first hour should be content, structure or timing.

process.title: Use the first lesson as a diagnostic
process.description: The first lesson is at no charge and no card details are taken before it. It is not a sales demonstration. The tutor works a past-paper question type under time, finds where the method breaks, and writes the first entry in the error log before the hour ends.

process.title: Agree a written plan with a review date
process.description: One page: the syllabus code, the components in scope, what will be sat under time and when, and the date you will both look at the evidence. The plan is what makes drift visible, and it is the document to ask for if a provider offers you nothing else.

process.title: Review at four sessions and decide
process.description: Put the marked scripts, the error log and the session notes on the table and ask whether the component marks have moved. Continue, change subject, change format, or stop. All four are legitimate outcomes, and deciding in advance to have the conversation is what stops a term drifting.

whyPoints.title: Every plan carries a syllabus code
whyPoints.description: A plan that says Physics could mean 0625 Extended, 0625 Core or 4PH1 Higher, and the revision for each is different. Writing the code down at the start prevents a term of teaching material the student will never be examined on, which is the most expensive error available.

whyPoints.title: Marked scripts rather than progress adjectives
whyPoints.description: Progress is reported as component marks on papers sat under time, annotated by cause. That is harder to produce than a cheerful message after each lesson, and it is the only version you can check, disagree with, or take to your child's head of department.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published, our own position stated plainly
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are other providers' published figures with the source named, so you can see where any quote sits in the market. Our own commercial answer is a first lesson at no charge followed by a consultation, rather than a tier list invented for a web page.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Teaching, criteria explanation and comments on a student's own draft, with the draft history kept. No part of a submitted piece is written for the student. The boundary is in writing because it protects the qualification, and because operations in this market sell the other thing.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed before you pay
whyPoints.description: Some IGCSE subject and tier combinations have thin specialist availability in the UAE time zone, and we say so before taking a booking rather than after. If the match will take a fortnight, or if the session has to sit at a different hour, you hear that first.

whyPoints.title: One delivery format, described honestly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video. IB Gram runs no visiting service in the UAE and claims none, which means the comparison on this page between online and visiting tuition is about cost and logistics rather than about selling you the more expensive option.

faqs.question: What should I be holding after four paid IGCSE sessions in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Five things. At least one past paper sat under time and marked against the published scheme. An error log that sorts the lost marks by cause rather than by topic. A dated note for each session naming the paper and component worked on. A one-page plan carrying the syllabus code and a review date. And, if coursework is in scope, a draft history showing the student's own versions with the tutor's comments visible. If any of those is missing at session four, ask for it before booking the next block. A provider who cannot produce them is not necessarily teaching badly, but you have no way to tell.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subject should I fund first if I can only afford one hour a week?
faqs.answer: Sort the lost marks across all nine subjects into four causes: content never learned, method known but carelessly executed, missing structure on extended-response questions, and time running out. Paid hours move the first and third reliably. The second needs a checking protocol, which costs nothing, and the fourth needs papers sat in halves against a clock at home. Then look at the shape of the timetable. One grade 4 among grade 7s means funding that subject alone; a flat set of grade 5s is a study-method problem that a single subject's tuition will not touch.

faqs.question: Does my child's school report tell me whether the tuition is working?
faqs.answer: Only partly. A reported grade usually blends class assessments, a mock, teacher judgement and a target from a baseline test you never saw, and two of those inputs can move without examination performance changing. Ask the school what the grade is actually based on, and which components it covers. A Chemistry grade built from Paper 2 alone says very little about Paper 4 extended responses. Component marks from papers sat under time are the measure that answers your question, which is why the tuition should be producing them independently of the school's reporting cycle.

faqs.question: What does an hour of IGCSE tuition cost in Abu Dhabi right now?
faqs.answer: On published figures, roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for a budget or university-student online tutor, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for a visiting tutor with travel inside the rate, and AED 200 to 450 and above for a subject specialist. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end and TutorChase publishes AED 270. Monthly packages seen in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are other providers' numbers, cited so you can place any quote you receive, not a price list of ours.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our villa in Khalifa City for the lessons?
faqs.answer: Not from us. IB Gram does not provide in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; visiting tuition is a service we run only in India. Lessons for Abu Dhabi households are one-to-one over live video. The visiting market here is real and this page quotes its rates honestly, at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the figure. What you give up by choosing online is a person in the room; what you gain is a tutor chosen for the syllabus code rather than for the drive from the island to Khalifa City.

faqs.question: Why does the Cambridge entry deadline matter more than the exam date?
faqs.answer: Because the reversible decisions close at the entry, not at the exam. For the Cambridge March 2027 series, final entries were due 27 November 2026 while the exam period ran 3 February to 4 March 2027. The tier a student is entered for, Core or Extended, is fixed at that deadline on whatever marked evidence existed in November. Forecast grades followed on 27 February 2027 and results on 13 May. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used, so confirm the zone with the exams officer early.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 10 and already behind. Is it too early to pay for tuition?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is the cheapest place to spend the money, because a gap closed now is not sitting underneath Year 11 content later. It is also the year in which the tier decision is still genuinely open, and that decision affects the grade ceiling more than any number of hours later will. Start with one subject rather than four, run it for a half-term, and keep the evidence. If the component marks move, extend. If they do not, you have learned something useful about the cause while there is still a full year of runway left.

faqs.question: Do we need tuition in all nine of my child's IGCSE subjects?
faqs.answer: Almost never, and families who try usually buy a thin hour in each subject and move nothing. Nine subjects at a weekly hour is a timetable no fifteen-year-old can absorb on top of school, homework and sleep. One or two subjects taught properly, with papers sat under time and an error log that survives between sessions, produces more marks than nine shallow contacts. If more than two subjects are genuinely failing, the problem is usually a revision routine rather than nine separate content gaps, and that is cheaper to fix.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for my child's subject and tier?
faqs.answer: You are told before a booking is taken, not after. Some combinations have thin availability in the UAE time zone, particularly less common options and the higher tiers of minority subjects. In that case we say how long a match is likely to take, whether a session would need to sit at a different hour, and whether a nearby alternative would serve, such as supporting the examined components with a specialist in the adjacent discipline. The thing we will not do is take a booking and then find somebody approximately suitable afterwards.

faqs.question: Should we move my child from Extended to Core to protect the grade?
faqs.answer: It is a real option and it carries a real cost, because tiers differ in grade ceiling as well as in content. The decision needs marked evidence rather than a feeling, and it needs to happen before the entry deadline, which for the Cambridge March 2027 series was 27 November 2026. Ask the school which tier the current scripts support, and ask what the ceiling means for the subjects your child wants at post-16. A tutor can tell you which Extended content is missing and how many hours it would take; the entry itself is the school's decision with you.

faqs.question: How do I check that the person teaching my child is permitted to tutor in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring here runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted at no charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit, Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through its app, website and e-services, with a two-working-day completion time. Ask to see the permit. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: How far can a tutor go on an IGCSE coursework or controlled-assessment draft?
faqs.answer: A tutor may explain the published criteria in the board's own language, teach the skills the piece needs, read what the student has written and say which criterion it currently fails, ask questions that force a rethink, and demonstrate on an unrelated topic. A tutor may not supply sentences for the submission, rewrite a paragraph into its final form, pick the topic on the student's behalf or hand over material presented later as the student's own thinking. Keep every draft, with comments visible as comments. That history is what demonstrates authorship if the school ever asks.

faqs.question: Is an hour a week enough for IGCSE Mathematics in Year 11?
faqs.answer: It is enough to fix a diagnosed problem and not enough to teach the course a second time. One hour a week buys roughly thirty contacts across a year, which will close two or three substantial content gaps and build one examination habit, provided the student practises between sessions. If the gap is two years wide, an hour a week will not close it and a block of concentrated paper clinics before the series is a better use of the same money. The honest test is whether component marks move by the fourth session.

faqs.question: What does the error log actually look like after a month?
faqs.answer: A page, usually a shared document, with one row per mistake. Each row names the paper and question, the cause sorted into content, method, structure or timing, the correction, and the date it was next tested. After four sessions a useful log has perhaps fifteen rows, with several already struck out because the student got them right under time later. A log that only grows is diagnosis without teaching. A log that never gets written is why the February mock contains the same errors as the October one.

faqs.question: Do Abu Dhabi families need a different plan from Dubai families?
faqs.answer: The syllabus is identical; the regulator and the logistics are not. Private schools in Abu Dhabi answer to ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes its own inspection ratings, while Dubai schools answer to KHDA. For a household in Al Shamkha or Al Reef the practical difference is the evening: distances to the island schools are long enough that a visiting tutor cannot realistically start before seven, which is why a live video slot at half past four is a different lesson rather than the same lesson delivered differently.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Cambridge and Pearson papers in the same subject?
faqs.answer: A strong subject specialist usually can, but ask them to prove it on the detail rather than the principle. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 differ in tiering language, in question style and in how marks are allocated across the papers. The test question is simple: ask which paper carries which weighting in each specification, and what the tiering is called. A tutor who answers both precisely has taught both. A tutor who talks about IGCSE in general has probably taught one and assumed the other is similar enough.

abu-dhabi/igcse-tuition.closingHeading: Start with two marked scripts and a syllabus code
abu-dhabi/igcse-tuition.closingBody: The quickest way to find out whether IGCSE tuition in Abu Dhabi will help your child is to send the last two marked papers and the syllabus code for the subject that worries you most. A subject specialist reads them, says where the marks are going and how many hours that is likely to take, and runs a first lesson at no charge with no card details taken beforehand. After four sessions you look at the error log and the component marks together and decide whether to continue. If the evidence says the plan is wrong, we will say so rather than sell you another term.

abu-dhabi/igcse-tuition-near-me.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach IGCSE subjects to Abu Dhabi families over live video. Each works from the four-digit syllabus code on your child's statement of entry, because two subjects with the same name can sit different papers, be marked on different scales and reward completely different exam habits.

intro.heading: A distance question with an academic answer
paragraphs: Typing IGCSE tuition near me in Abu Dhabi produces a map, a handful of tuition centres clustered on the island and around Khalifa City, and a few agency pages that name no school, no syllabus code and no price. The map is answering a question about geography. Your child's grade is decided by something else entirely: which specification they are entered for, which papers that specification makes them sit, and which of those papers is currently leaking marks. None of that appears on a map pin.

This matters more in Abu Dhabi than in most cities, because the emirate is long. A tutor who is genuinely nearby for a family in Al Mushrif is forty minutes from Al Reef and closer to an hour from Al Shamkha at six in the evening. Proximity, treated as the main filter, shrinks the list of candidates to whoever happens to live on the right side of the bridges and then asks that short list to cover Extended chemistry, English First Language and Additional Mathematics. That is how families end up with a general tutor for a specific problem.

The alternative is to filter on the specification instead. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 candidates sit either Paper 5, a timed practical, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, and the two require different preparation that has almost nothing in common. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 is graded A* to G while 0980 is graded 9 to 1 on the same content. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 tiers its papers differently again. A tutor who has not asked which of those applies is guessing, however short the drive.

So this page is arranged around the paper rather than the postcode. It explains what a near-me search actually returns and what each result type conceals, then works through the components an IGCSE candidate sits, the two grade scales in circulation, and the specific places marks disappear in the subjects Abu Dhabi families ask about most. After that there is a section that prices proximity honestly: what a drive across the emirate costs in time, and what time of evening a session can realistically start in each community.

Two practical points before the detail. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition over live video to families across the emirate and does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; visiting tutors are a service available only in India. And every AED figure on this page is a published market rate attributed to whoever published it, not a price list. Abu Dhabi's private schools are inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and your child's school report plus its published inspection outcome is free reading that will tell you more about what help is needed than any search result will.
bullets: The four-digit code on the statement of entry fixes the board, the paper set and the grade scale before any tutoring decision is made

Published market rates for IGCSE specialists in the UAE cluster between AED 150 and AED 450 an hour online
