abu-dhabi/igcse-tuition-near-me.programmesIntro: IGCSE is one stage in a longer sequence, and Abu Dhabi families arrive at it from several directions. The stage your child is at changes what a session is for: diagnosis, repair or exam technique. These are the four stages where families in the emirate most often ask for help.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE, assessed by Checkpoint tests that Cambridge offers in March, May and October. Checkpoint is not a public qualification and no admissions office will ever read it, which is exactly why it is useful: it is an unpressured read on whether a child is heading for the Core or the Extended tier in maths and science. Gaps found here are cheap to close because no entry deadline is pressing on them.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi, several of the larger British-curriculum schools in the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor set maths groups from Year 8, and that setting tends to follow a child into the tier decision two years later. A parent who reads the Year 8 Checkpoint breakdown closely often finds the same topic strand named in the Year 10 report. Acting at this stage is the one point where tuition is genuinely optional rather than remedial.

programmes.name: IGCSE Year 10
programmes.description: The first of the two examined years. Content is taught for the first time, tier decisions are made or confirmed, and coursework folders open in subjects that still carry them. Most of the syllabus a candidate will be examined on is delivered this year, which makes Year 10 the cheapest year to buy tuition in and the one families most often skip. A weak Year 10 foundation becomes a Year 11 revision problem that revision cannot fix.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools vary in when they commit a child to Core or Extended, and some confirm it only after the Year 10 end-of-year papers. Families here benefit from asking the subject lead directly, in writing, which tier the child is provisionally entered for and what would change it. A session in Year 10 that closes an algebra or a stoichiometry gap removes a whole category of Year 11 panic.

programmes.name: IGCSE Year 11 and the examined series
programmes.description: The year of mocks, final entries and the series itself. Teaching gives way to paper practice, and the useful work changes character: marked scripts, command-word drills, timing under pressure and the specific components a child keeps losing marks in. Demand for tutors across the emirate concentrates in the eight to ten weeks before a series, which is also when the best subject specialists stop having free slots.
programmes.countryNote: Entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series, for example, put final entries on 27 November 2026 for an exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027. A family deciding in January what to do about a June entry is deciding late, not early, and the cost of lateness in Abu Dhabi is availability rather than money.

programmes.name: After IGCSE: A Level, IB Diploma or a retake
programmes.description: IGCSE grades become entry conditions for the next stage, and a single weak grade can close a route. Schools set their own thresholds for A Level or Diploma subjects, usually a grade 6 or 7 for a subject taken at the harder level. Retake entries are available in the following series, and a candidate may enter privately for one subject while studying the next qualification full time.
programmes.countryNote: For Abu Dhabi families, the other consideration is Ministry of Education equivalency, which the UAE requires for certificates used in the national system. The British track asks for five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. That count is worth checking before a subject is dropped.

abu-dhabi/igcse-tuition-near-me.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Abu Dhabi families ask about most, with the syllabus codes in circulation here and the component where marks tend to go. The code matters: the same subject name can mean a different paper structure, a different grade scale and a different practical route depending on which board and specification the school entered.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 and 0980, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: The most requested subject in the emirate. Extended candidates lose marks in algebraic manipulation under time pressure, in vectors, and in the 'show that' questions where method marks sit unclaimed because no working was written down. Core candidates more often leave the final questions blank than answer them wrongly, which is a pacing problem rather than a knowledge one.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 and 0972, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: The practical route is the thing to establish first: Cambridge candidates sit Paper 5, a timed practical, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, and schools decide which. Marks leak in graph axis choice, in significant figures carried through a calculation, and in describing a control variable rather than merely naming it. Electricity and moments are the recurring content gaps.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 and 0971, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles work separates grades more cleanly than any other strand, because it compounds: a shaky relative formula mass makes every titration and yield calculation unreliable. Organic chemistry rewards pattern recognition that students rarely build from notes alone. The alternative-to-practical paper asks for observation language that is specific and testable, not descriptive prose.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 and 0970, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content volume is the problem rather than difficulty. Marks go missing in extended-response answers that describe a process without using the command term's required depth, and in data questions where a trend is stated without a quoted value. Transport in plants, genetics crosses and enzyme experiments are the strands that most often need rebuilding from first principles.

subjects.name: English First Language (0500 and 0990)
subjects.description: A technique subject, which is why it responds quickly to tuition. The directed-writing task and the summary task have scoring conventions that are learnable in a handful of sessions: audience and register for the first, and ruthless compression without copied phrasing for the second. Analysis answers lose marks when a quotation is presented rather than used.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: The reading tasks reward accuracy in locating and transcribing information, and candidates lose marks in the note-making and summary exercises by writing too much. Common in Abu Dhabi's mixed-intake schools, and often the subject where a strong student is entered on the wrong specification variant because the speaking component differs between 0510 and 0511.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Sciences (0654 and 0653)
subjects.description: Double and single award routes that cover all three sciences in fewer papers. The content is narrower than the separate sciences but the papers move faster between disciplines, and candidates who revise biology, chemistry and physics as separate subjects are often unprepared for how little depth each question wants. Useful to confirm which award your child is entered for.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside or after Extended Mathematics by students heading for A Level Maths or a Diploma analysis course. Calculus, trigonometric identities and functions arrive early and without the scaffolding of the main syllabus. Tutor supply is thinner for this code than for 0580, which is the clearest case on this page for matching on subject rather than on location.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: A diagram subject disguised as an essay subject. The marks in the structured questions hang on correctly labelled axes, a shifted curve and a stated new equilibrium, and candidates who explain in prose what a diagram should show lose the easiest marks on the paper. Evaluation questions need a position taken and defended, not a list of advantages and disadvantages.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: The theory paper and the problem-solving paper reward different habits. Trace tables, pseudocode conventions and the distinction between validation and verification are where marks are routinely dropped, and the practical programming element needs regular short practice rather than long revision sessions. A code-focused session with a screen shared is a natural fit for online delivery.

abu-dhabi/igcse-tuition-near-me.regionsTitle: What proximity means in each Abu Dhabi community
abu-dhabi/igcse-tuition-near-me.regionsIntro: These notes are about time rather than geography. Abu Dhabi's school population is spread across the island, the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, and the newer mainland communities, and the gap between them is what makes a near-me search misleading. What follows is the practical reality of session timing in each.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Several large campuses sit within a few kilometres, so the school run here clears late. A 4pm start is rarely kept; 5.30pm and 7pm are the slots families actually hold onto. Demand concentrates on maths and the three separate sciences in Year 11.

regions.name: Al Reef
regions.note: Far enough from the island that a visiting tutor is pricing eighty minutes of driving into a sixty-minute lesson. Families here are the clearest case for online delivery, because the saving is not a discount: it is travel that never happens.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: A short hop from the island but a single access route, which makes evening timing unpredictable in term time. Subject demand skews towards the harder tier and towards Additional Mathematics, where local tutor supply is thin and a specialist match matters more than a short drive.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Dense, vertical and well served by schools, so parents here often assume proximity is solved. It is, for general tuition. It is not for a specific code: a 0606 or 0478 specialist is a different search from a maths tutor in the same tower.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Villa communities with a predictable school run and reliable home study space, which makes a fixed weekly slot easy to keep. Families here most often ask for Extended science support and for help with the move from IGCSE into a Diploma or A Level course.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Mushrif
regions.note: Established island neighbourhoods near some of the emirate's longest-running British-curriculum schools. Tuition centres are closest here, which makes this the one part of Abu Dhabi where a near-me search returns something genuinely near. The question becomes whether the centre teaches your child's specification.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Mussafah
regions.note: A large schooling population with a wide spread of boards, and heavy evening traffic on the approach roads. Group classes are common here and cheap; one-to-one supply for Extended science is the gap, and online matching removes the drive from both sides of the lesson.

regions.name: Al Shamkha and Shakhbout City
regions.note: Newer mainland communities where school provision has grown faster than tutor supply. A visiting tutor from the island is a genuinely long trip, so published in-home rates for this area carry the most travel inside them. Evening sessions from 6.30pm onwards are the realistic window.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi island: Al Mushrif, Al Bateen and the Corniche
schoolClusters.note: The island holds the emirate's longest-established British-curriculum schools, several running IGCSE into A Level. Their inspection outcomes are published by ADEK and are the fastest free read on where a school is strong and where a family is likely to need outside help. Students we support attend schools across this cluster.

schoolClusters.city: Saadiyat, Al Reem and Yas
schoolClusters.note: The island-adjacent developments where most of the emirate's newer international schools opened. Cohorts here tend to be mobile, which means transfers mid-IGCSE are common and a child may arrive having studied a different specification for the same subject. Checking the code on arrival avoids a term of mismatched preparation.
schools: The British International School Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and the mainland corridor
schoolClusters.note: Much of the emirate's British-curriculum IGCSE cohort sits in this corridor, which makes subject demand here predictable: maths, separate sciences and English First Language in Year 11. Demand peaks in the eight weeks before a June series, when local tutor availability is at its thinnest.

sections.heading: What a near-me search actually returns in Abu Dhabi, and what each result hides
paragraphs: A near-me search in this emirate returns four kinds of thing, and only one of them is a tutor. The map pack lists tuition centres with premises, which are licensed businesses teaching groups on a timetable. Below that come agency pages that rank on the phrase without naming a single school, specification or rate. Then classified listings, where an individual advertises availability and a subject list. Then school-run support, which is not a search result at all but is often the cheapest option a family has not asked about.

Each type conceals something different. A centre's map pin tells you where the building is, not whether it teaches your child's specification; a centre running a Cambridge 0580 group cannot also run a Pearson 4MA1 group for two students in the same room, so one of them is being taught the wrong paper structure. An agency page that quotes no figure is concealing a rate it does not want compared. A classified listing conceals whether the person holds the private tuition work permit that UAE law requires. School-run support conceals nothing, which is why it should be the first call rather than the last.

The practical move is to stop filtering on distance and start filtering on four facts: the board, the specification code, the tier, and the component currently losing marks. All four are available to you this week. The first three are printed on the statement of entry the school issues before a series, or obtainable from the subject lead in one email. The fourth is in the most recent marked mock paper. A tutor who can answer what Paper 6 asks for differently from Paper 5 is more useful than one who lives eight minutes away and cannot.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE candidate is actually assessed on, component by component
paragraphs: IGCSE grades are built from components, and a component is a specific paper with its own rules, timing and reward structure. A candidate who knows the content but has never been taught what each component wants will drop marks in predictable places. This is the part of the qualification that tuition can move fastest, because component technique is learnable in weeks where content mastery takes terms.

Across the subjects Abu Dhabi families take, six component types recur. There is a short-answer or multiple-choice paper that tests breadth, a structured or extended-response paper that tests depth and command-term discipline, a practical or alternative-to-practical paper in the sciences, a directed-writing or composition paper in the languages, a speaking or listening component in some language specifications, and in a shrinking number of subjects a coursework or portfolio element assessed internally and moderated by the board.

The combinations differ by board. A Cambridge candidate in a science will sit either the practical test or the alternative to practical, decided by the school, and preparation for one is close to useless for the other. A Pearson Edexcel candidate may sit a different number of papers for the same subject at the same level. What this means for a parent is simple: the question to ask a prospective tutor is not whether they teach chemistry but which chemistry papers your child is entered for and what each one rewards. A tutor who answers that precisely has read the specification. A tutor who answers it vaguely will teach content and hope.

sections.heading: Two grade scales are in circulation, and your child is on one of them
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi parents comparing notes at the school gate are often comparing different scales without knowing it. Cambridge issues some IGCSE syllabuses on an A* to G scale and others, with a nine in the code, on a 9 to 1 scale. Mathematics 0580 is the A* to G version and 0980 the 9 to 1 version of the same content. Physics 0625 and 0972 pair the same way, as do chemistry 0620 and 0971 and biology 0610 and 0970. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses a 9 to 1 scale across its specifications.

This is not cosmetic. A grade 7 is not a grade A, and the two scales divide the top of the ability range differently: where A* was one grade, the 9 to 1 scale separates 9, 8 and 7, which changes what a sixth-form entry requirement of a grade 7 actually demands. A family targeting a grade for an A Level or Diploma place needs to know which scale the school entered the child on before they can know whether the target is realistic or already met.

There is a second consequence for tuition planning. A child one mark below a boundary on a nine-point scale has a smaller gap to close than the same child on a seven-letter scale, because the bands are narrower. That makes a late, targeted intervention more likely to show up as a grade change on 9 to 1 than on A* to G. It also makes it more likely that a small slip costs a grade. Either way, the honest version is that no tutor can promise a boundary will be crossed; what a tutor can do is put the marks in reach and show you, from a marked paper, how far away they currently are.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually go, subject by subject
paragraphs: Mark loss at IGCSE is repetitive. Across a few hundred marked scripts the same leaks appear, and almost none of them are failures of intelligence. They are habits: working not written down, a command term read as a synonym for a different one, a graph drawn to the wrong scale, an answer to the question the candidate expected rather than the one printed. A parent who knows which of these their child does has already narrowed a vague worry into a job of work.

The useful discipline is to diagnose from a script rather than from a report. A school report says a child is working at grade 6 and needs to show more detail in extended answers. That is true and not actionable. A marked paper says the child scored full marks on the recall questions, lost four marks on a single six-mark explain question, and left the last two parts blank. Those three facts point to three different fixes, two of which are technique and one of which is pacing.

The table below sets out the leaks that recur most in the subjects Abu Dhabi families ask about, with the repair beside each. None of them requires a tutor who lives nearby. All of them require a tutor who has seen enough scripts in that specific specification to recognise the pattern in minutes rather than weeks, which is an argument for matching on subject depth rather than on postcode.

sections.heading: Proximity priced out: what a drive across this emirate really costs
paragraphs: Distance is not free, and in Abu Dhabi it is rarely cheap. A tutor who travels is selling an hour of teaching inside two hours of their evening, and that cost sits in the rate whether or not it is itemised on the invoice. Published UAE market figures show the gap plainly: in-home one-to-one rates are quoted from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, with IGCSE and A Level specialists quoted between AED 200 and AED 450 by rate aggregators. The difference is travel, not teaching quality.

The second cost is scheduling. A visiting tutor who has to reach Al Shamkha from the island at six in the evening cannot hold a 5.30pm slot reliably, and the slot that gets dropped is usually the one nearest the exam. Families in the newer mainland communities feel this most, because the supply of tutors lives disproportionately on the island and in the central corridor. An online slot starts when it was booked, which in an exam term is worth more than the rate difference.

The third cost is the one nobody prices: the shortlist. Filtering by drive time from a villa in Al Reef reduces the pool of available tutors to a handful, and then asks that handful to cover Additional Mathematics 0606, Extended chemistry and English First Language. Removing the drive widens the pool to every tutor who can teach the specification in the Gulf timezone. To be plain about it: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, and visiting tutors are a service we provide only in India. The case for online delivery here is not that it is a cheaper substitute; it is that it is the only format in which a 0606 specialist and a family in Al Shamkha can share a Tuesday evening.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that sets the grade ceiling
paragraphs: In tiered IGCSE subjects the tier decides the top grade available. A Core maths candidate cannot reach the highest grades on the scale however well the papers go, because the Core papers do not contain the questions those grades are awarded for. This makes the tier decision more consequential than any choice of tutor, and it is usually made by a subject lead in Year 10 on the evidence of internal assessments.

Parents can engage with that decision, and in Abu Dhabi they often need to, because cohorts here are mobile. A child who joined in Year 10 from a different system may have been placed on evidence that reflects an unfamiliar curriculum rather than their ceiling. A child who was set into a lower maths group in Year 8 may still be carrying that setting three years later. The question to ask, in writing, is which tier the child is provisionally entered for, what evidence that rests on, and what performance would change it. Schools answer that question properly when it is asked specifically.

Tuition changes the arithmetic in two ways. Moving from Core to Extended requires covering content the child has not been taught, which is a term of work rather than a few sessions, and it is only worth starting if the entry deadline is far enough away. Staying on Core and targeting the top of that tier is a smaller job with a certain ceiling. Neither route is the obviously right one; what is wrong is discovering in April which tier the entry was made on. A grade ceiling reached by accident is the most expensive thing on this page, and it costs nothing to check.

sections.heading: The UAE subjects that run alongside your child's IGCSE courses
paragraphs: Every private school in the UAE teaches Arabic, Islamic education and social studies alongside its licensed international curriculum. The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. So an Abu Dhabi child on a Cambridge IGCSE programme is also carrying a mandatory stream that sits outside the board's specifications and is examined on the school's own terms.

Families are often surprised by how much timetable this occupies, and by the rules around it. Dubai's regulator publishes the clearest written requirements, and they give a sense of how seriously the stream is treated: separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic education and social studies, with combined classes prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ; Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for Islamic education for Arab students; and a requirement that teachers of Islamic education and Arabic hold the regulator's approval to teach those subjects. Instructional time is calculated in 40-minute lesson units.

Two things follow for a tutoring plan. The mandatory stream is where a child's weekly study time quietly goes, so a plan that assumes an empty Thursday evening is often wrong. And the content itself is constrained: for these subjects the use of different or additional material without prior permission from the Ministry is not permitted, which means honest tutoring here is support with the school's own material and with language skills rather than an alternative syllabus. For Arabic as an additional language in particular, steady short practice outperforms exam-season intensity, because the gains are vocabulary and confidence rather than technique.

sections.heading: What one session can fix, and what it cannot
paragraphs: It is worth being specific about the unit of work, because families buy tuition in hours and think in terms. Some problems genuinely resolve in a single session. A graph-plotting convention, a trace-table method, the structure of a directed-writing answer, the first line of a moles calculation: these are procedures, and a procedure can be taught, practised and checked inside sixty minutes. If a marked paper shows marks lost to one procedure, a single session is the right purchase and a term of weekly tuition is not.

Other problems take a block. Rebuilding algebraic fluency, learning to read a six-mark explain question properly across a whole subject, or recovering a topic that was taught during a term the child missed: each of these needs repetition over weeks, because the work is habit formation rather than instruction. Four to eight sessions is the honest estimate, and the thing to watch is whether the error rate on repeated question types is falling, not whether the child feels more confident.

A third category cannot be fixed by tuition at all, and saying so is more useful than selling against it. A tier ceiling is an entry decision. A missed entry deadline is an administrative fact. A child who is not doing any independent work between sessions will not progress however good the tutor is, because the lesson is where errors are diagnosed and the week is where they are corrected. And no tutor can promise a grade: the papers are marked by the board against boundaries set after the series. What a tutor can do is show you, from marked evidence, how many marks separate where the child is from where they want to be, and what kind of work closes that specific gap.

sections.heading: Coursework, drafts and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Several IGCSE subjects still carry internally assessed components, and in those subjects the honesty rules matter more than anywhere else on this page. The principle is simple and the boards are unambiguous about it: assessed work must be the candidate's own. A teacher or tutor may teach the skills, explain the criteria, discuss a plan and give feedback on what the student has produced. Supplying text, rewriting a paragraph into shape, or correcting a draft to the point where the sentences are no longer the student's is malpractice, and the consequences fall on the candidate.

This is not a theoretical risk in this market. One of the pages competing for searches like this one openly sells completed Internal Assessments. A family who buys that is buying a malpractice investigation with a qualification attached. Our position, stated plainly because the distinction is the one worth paying for: a tutor here teaches, questions, marks against criteria and gives written feedback on the student's own draft, and nobody will produce assessed work on a student's behalf.

There is a related rule about materials. Boards hold copyright in their specifications, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables, and those documents are published on the boards' own sites for anyone to read. A tutor should point you to the official page rather than hand over a folder of copied files, and a tutor who offers unreleased material should end the conversation. The useful version of document access is knowing which document answers which question: the specification for what is examined, the mark scheme for how marks are awarded, the examiner report for what went wrong last time.

process.title: Send the code, not the subject name
process.description: Tell us the four-digit syllabus code from the statement of entry, the tier if it has been set, and the series your child is entered for. That one line removes most of the guesswork, because it fixes the board, the paper structure and the grade scale before anybody has taught a lesson or quoted a rate.

process.title: A free trial lesson, one per family
process.description: Thirty minutes with the matched tutor at no charge and with no card details taken, limited to one trial per family. The purpose is not a sales call. It is to watch whether your child will talk to this particular adult about a question they got wrong. If they will not, we match again rather than argue that they will settle in.

process.title: Diagnose from a marked script
process.description: The first full session works from a mock or past paper the school has already marked, with the mark scheme alongside. Marks lost to unknown content, to a misread command term and to running out of time are three separate problems with three separate fixes, and only the script shows which one your child actually has.

process.title: Scope the work to a component
process.description: Once the script has been read, the plan is scoped to something nameable: Paper 6 observation language, the summary task, trace tables, moles. Named scope makes progress checkable and keeps the hours honest, because a component either stops losing marks or it does not.

process.title: Review against the live timetable
process.description: Every few weeks the plan is checked against the official timetable for the entered series and against the school's own internal deadlines. If a component has stabilised, the hours move to one that has not. A good plan shrinks as the year goes on rather than growing to fill the term.

whyPoints.title: Matched on specification, not on driving distance
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means the filter is which tutor knows Cambridge 0606 or Pearson 4CH1, rather than who can reach Al Reef by six. In an emirate this spread out that is the difference between the right tutor and the available one, which is the whole argument for the format rather than a consolation for it.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis from marked evidence
whyPoints.description: Work starts from a script the school has already marked, with the published mark scheme beside it. That turns a report comment about needing more detail into a countable number of marks lost in a named component, which is the only version of the problem a tutor can actually act on.

A parent comparing quotes needs a reference band more than another promise.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built around the Abu Dhabi evening
whyPoints.description: Sessions are set in Gulf Standard Time around the school run, and the slot that was booked is the slot that starts. Families in Al Shamkha, Al Reef and Mohammed Bin Zayed City lose the most to traffic, and removing the drive from both ends of the lesson is what makes a 6.30pm start reliable in an exam term.

faqs.question: Does it matter where my child's IGCSE tutor is based if the lessons are online?
faqs.answer: It matters for timezone and for curriculum familiarity, not for distance. A tutor teaching into Abu Dhabi needs to work in Gulf Standard Time so a 6.30pm session is actually convenient, and needs to know the specification your child is entered for rather than a national curriculum that resembles it. Beyond that, the physical location stops being a useful filter. What replaces it is a harder and better question: has this tutor taught Cambridge 0606 or Pearson 4CH1 to candidates who sat the papers, and can they say what each paper rewards? That question eliminates more unsuitable tutors than any radius ever will.

faqs.question: Where on the school paperwork does the IGCSE syllabus code actually appear?
faqs.answer: The school issues a statement of entry before each series, and the four-digit code sits next to each subject on it. If the series is still months away, email the subject lead and ask for the code, the tier and whether the science practical route is the practical test or the alternative to practical. Schools answer that readily when the question is specific. It is worth doing early, because the code decides the grade scale, the number of papers and what preparation is useful. Two children in the same class can be on different codes if they joined from different systems.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE tuition centre near Khalifa City, and would a centre beat online lessons?
faqs.answer: Centres cluster on the island and around the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, so a family in Khalifa City has genuinely nearby options. Whether a centre is better depends on what you need. A centre teaches groups to a timetable, which suits a child who is broadly on track and needs structure, and group rates are lower. It suits a child with a specific component problem far less, because the group follows one specification at one pace. Ask which code the group is taught to before booking; a room containing both Cambridge and Pearson candidates is teaching one of them the wrong paper structure.

faqs.question: My child sits Cambridge Paper 6 rather than Paper 5 in science. What changes?
faqs.answer: Almost everything about the preparation. Paper 5 is a timed practical where the candidate handles apparatus, records real readings and processes them, so the practice is in recording conventions, table layout, units and significant figures. Paper 6 is the alternative to practical: no apparatus, written reasoning about experiments the candidate has not performed. It rewards precise observation language, correctly identifying variables and justifying conclusions from supplied data. Preparing for one does little for the other. Schools decide which route a cohort sits, so confirm it before a single revision session is planned around the wrong paper.

faqs.question: What is the practical difference between the 0580 and 0980 maths grading scales?
faqs.answer: The content is the same; the scale is not. Cambridge 0580 is graded A* to G and 0980 is graded 9 to 1. The 9 to 1 scale separates the top of the range into 9, 8 and 7, where A* was a single grade, so a sixth-form requirement of a grade 7 is not equivalent to a requirement of an A. For planning, the narrower bands on 9 to 1 mean a small number of marks can move a grade in either direction. Check which code appears on the statement of entry before comparing your child's grade with a classmate's.

faqs.question: Can a tutor move my child from Core to Extended partway through Year 11?
faqs.answer: A tutor cannot change the entry; the school makes that decision and the board's entry deadline closes it. What a tutor can do is cover the content the Extended papers contain and the Core papers do not, which is a term of work rather than a revision block. Whether that is worth starting depends on how far away the entry deadline is and what the child's current marks look like. Raise it with the subject lead in writing, ask what evidence would support the change, and be realistic: a tier move decided late in Year 11 is usually not available.

faqs.question: How many sessions does it take to repair one weak IGCSE component?
faqs.answer: If the problem is a procedure, often one session plus a week of practice: graph conventions, a trace-table method, the first line of a moles calculation, the planning routine for a directed-writing task. If the problem is a habit across a whole subject, such as reading command terms properly or writing method before answers, plan four to eight sessions, because habit change needs repetition. The measurable sign that it is working is a falling error rate on repeated question types, not a child reporting more confidence. Ask for the marked evidence at the four-session mark.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Abu Dhabi need a permit before teaching my child?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 on private tuition work permits. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Because the permit costs nothing, a tutor who cannot show you one has no cost excuse for not holding it.

faqs.question: Who inspects Abu Dhabi private schools, and what does an inspection outcome tell me?
faqs.answer: In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain it is ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Dubai has KHDA, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. An inspection outcome describes the school's provision, not your child's performance. Read it for where teaching is reported as weaker, because that is where outside help tends to be needed, then check the finding against your child's own marked work.

faqs.question: Does my child still have to study Arabic and Islamic education alongside IGCSE subjects?
faqs.answer: Yes. UAE private schools are required to teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside whatever international curriculum they are licensed for, and they must follow the Ministry's general regulations on this. The stream is organised tightly: Dubai's regulator, for instance, requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic first language, Islamic education and social studies, and sets the language of instruction for each. It also means your child's week has less free study time than a subject timetable suggests, which is worth factoring into any tutoring plan before you book a second weekly slot.

faqs.question: How late in Year 11 is it still worth starting IGCSE tuition?
faqs.answer: Later than most families assume, provided the work is scoped tightly. Six weeks before a series there is no time to learn a subject, but there is time to stop a specific leak: finishing papers, writing method lines, handling one recurring question type, or rehearsing the alternative-to-practical observation language. That work can be worth several marks a paper, and on a 9 to 1 scale several marks can cross a boundary. What is not realistic that late is broad coverage or a tier change. Bring the most recent marked mock and expect the honest answer to be a short block, not a term.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both maths and physics for the same child?
faqs.answer: Often yes at Core or lower Extended level, where the physics content leans on maths a specialist mathematician handles comfortably. At the top of Extended it is usually better to split, because the mark-winning detail in physics is practical and specification-specific: which practical paper is sat, how observations must be phrased, how graphs are expected to be drawn. Two subjects also means two sets of marked scripts to read. If budget pushes you towards one tutor, put the specialist on the subject with the weaker marks and use school support for the other.

faqs.question: What should we bring to the first IGCSE session for it to be useful?
faqs.answer: Three documents. The statement of entry or an email from the subject lead giving the syllabus code, the tier and the practical route. The most recent marked mock or past paper, ideally with the mark scheme the school used. And the school's internal deadline list for any coursework component. With those, the first session diagnoses rather than interviews, and you get a written note at the end naming the component that is losing marks. Without them, the first hour goes on finding out what should have been established before anybody was booked.

faqs.question: How does the UAE Ministry of Education count IGCSE subjects for equivalency?
faqs.answer: For the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That rule matters before a subject is dropped in Year 10. Equivalency is a Ministry process, not something a tutoring platform performs or can speed up, so verify the current requirement on the Ministry's own channel before acting on any summary, including this one.

faqs.question: Can my child sit IGCSE exams in Abu Dhabi as a private candidate?
faqs.answer: Private candidate entries are made through a registered examination centre rather than directly with the board, and centres set their own deadlines ahead of the board's. Fees, available subjects and whether practical components can be accommodated all vary by centre, and some will not accept entries for subjects with internally assessed work. If this is the route you need, start by asking the centre two questions: which specifications they accept private entries for, and what their internal deadline is relative to the board's. Then build any tutoring plan backwards from the centre's date, not the exam date.

faqs.question: Will online lessons work if my child needs someone sitting beside them?
faqs.answer: For most students, yes, with one condition: the lesson has to be worked rather than watched. A session where the tutor talks and the student listens fails online faster than it fails in a room. A session where the student's working is visible on camera as it is written, the tutor annotates a shared paper and the student does the next question live is at least as effective, and it produces a record both of you can look back at. Take the free trial and watch for one thing: does your child pick up a pen in the first ten minutes?

intro.heading: Four decisions that set an IGCSE grade before any teaching begins
paragraphs: Most Abu Dhabi families start looking for an IGCSE tutor at the same moment: a Year 10 or Year 11 report lands, a subject has slipped, and there are five or six months on the clock. The instinct is to buy weekly teaching in that subject. Often that is right. But before you buy anything, there are four facts about your child's entry that are worth ten weekly sessions, and most parents do not know them, because nobody at school had a reason to spell them out.

The first is the tier. In several Cambridge IGCSE subjects a candidate is entered for Core or Extended, and in Pearson's International GCSE for Foundation or Higher. The lower tier carries a grade ceiling. A child sitting Core Mathematics cannot be awarded the top grades however well they perform, which means a family paying for tuition aimed at a grade 8 in a subject entered at Core is paying for something the entry form has already excluded. Tier changes have deadlines, and the deadline is usually months before the exam.

The second is the scale. Cambridge reports some IGCSE syllabuses on a 9 to 1 numeric scale and others on A* to G, and Pearson reports International GCSE on 9 to 1. Two subjects on the same child's report can therefore be measured on different scales, and a parent comparing a 6 with a B is not comparing like with like. The third is the subject count. For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. One competitor page ranking for this query publishes a six-subject requirement; the sourced figure is five.

The fourth is the series. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with additional March arrangements, and every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones with its own version of the timetable - Cambridge states plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. Pearson International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Entries close months ahead: for Cambridge's March 2027 series, final entries were due on 27 November 2026 for examinations between 3 February and 4 March 2027.

This page works through all four, then through the things a tutor actually does week to week: which subject to buy an hour in when nine are slipping, when Year 10 tuition is worth more than Year 11 tuition, what the step into the Diploma Programme or A Level demands of each IGCSE subject, and how a private candidate sits papers in Abu Dhabi without a school place. Lessons themselves are delivered one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India, and this page says so before it sells anything.

abu-dhabi/igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: An IGCSE tutor is almost never hired for IGCSE alone. The question behind the search is usually what the grade is for, and that answer sits one stage either side of Years 10 and 11. These are the four stages Abu Dhabi families ask about.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Year 9
programmes.description: The years before the entry form exists. Checkpoint tests are available in March, May and October, and they are the last low-stakes signal a family gets before tiering decisions start to matter. Algebraic fluency, scientific vocabulary and extended writing built here are what make an Extended or Higher entry viable two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi families moving in from CBSE, American or Ministry-curriculum schools usually land in Years 8 or 9, and the gap that shows up is algebra and written explanation rather than arithmetic. Year 9 is the cheapest moment in the whole sequence to fix it, and almost nobody buys tuition then.

programmes.name: IGCSE and International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight to ten subjects, each with its own syllabus code, tier and paper structure. Cambridge and Pearson syllabuses for the same subject differ in assessment design, not only in content, so a tutor working from the wrong code teaches the right physics into the wrong paper.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools sit both boards and some sit both within one year group, which is why the first thing we ask for is the entry form or the exam-board name from the school, not the subject. A parent in Al Reem Island and a parent in Khalifa City can have children in the same subject on different syllabuses.

programmes.name: AS and A Level
programmes.description: Three or four subjects taken in depth, with entry requirements expressed directly in IGCSE grades. The jump is not volume but independence: content arrives faster, worked examples stop, and the written answers expected are longer and more structured than anything IGCSE asked for.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi British-curriculum schools set subject-specific IGCSE grade thresholds for sixth-form entry, so a Year 11 grade is simultaneously a qualification and an admissions decision. That is the real reason a Year 11 grade 6 in Mathematics causes more anxiety than it looks like it should.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subject groups at Higher or Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internal assessment carries real weight in every subject, which is a different working style from IGCSE where almost everything is decided in a final written paper.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi has both British-curriculum and IB schools, and a number of Year 11 families are choosing between them during the exam term itself. The IGCSE subjects that most affect that choice are Mathematics and the separate sciences, because they determine whether Higher Level is realistic.

abu-dhabi/igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: Below are the IGCSE subjects Abu Dhabi families most often ask for, with the syllabus codes we work from and the tier or entry decision that matters most in each. The code is the thing to send us; the subject name alone is not enough to plan a session.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The tiering decision that matters most, because the lower tier caps the grade and because sixth-form and Diploma mathematics entry is usually expressed as a Mathematics grade. Algebraic manipulation is the single most common blocker; most lost marks in later topics trace back to it.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken alongside or instead of the main syllabus by students heading for Higher Level or A Level mathematics. Calculus and trigonometric identities appear earlier than students expect. Worth tutoring in Year 10 rather than Year 11, because it front-loads the hardest material.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism account for a disproportionate share of lost marks, and the practical-skills component is rehearsed least of all. Extended-only topics appear on specific papers, so a Core candidate revising from an Extended textbook wastes weeks.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry decide the grade and are usually taught once, early, and never revisited. Organic chemistry is a memory problem with a structure, and students who learn the structure stop losing the marks. Equation-writing precision is where Extended candidates slip.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A content-heavy subject in which marks are lost to imprecise language rather than missing knowledge - describing instead of explaining, naming a process without its location. Data and graph questions are the reliably fixable part and respond fastest to tutoring.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Science
subjects.description: Two or one IGCSE grades covering all three sciences, often chosen for timetable reasons rather than ability. The common problem is coverage: students assume a topic is out of scope because it was not taught, when it sits on the paper. A syllabus audit is the first session.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0500 First Language; 0510 and 0511 as a Second Language
subjects.description: The entry route sets the ceiling here too: the Second Language syllabus is a different qualification from First Language and is read differently by sixth forms and universities. Directed writing and summary are the two most teachable components in the whole IGCSE set.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Marks are decided by how closely a student argues from the text rather than by how much they have read about it. The fixable skill is quotation selection and integration. Unseen poetry is where unprepared candidates lose most, and it is the component that rewards drilling.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Case-study command words carry the marks: identify, explain, analyse and evaluate each demand a different answer length and shape. Students who write everything they know score in the lower bands. Taught as answer structure rather than content, these two move quickly.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Two very different qualifications routinely confused at option time. Computer Science examines algorithms, data representation and pseudocode under timed conditions; ICT examines practical application work. Choosing the wrong one for a target A Level is a decision tuition cannot undo later.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Source-handling and case-study recall in defined proportions. In Geography, the loss is almost always failure to use named examples; in History, failure to answer the question asked rather than narrating the period. Both respond to structured answer frames more than to further reading.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0508 First Language Arabic; 0544 Arabic Foreign Language
subjects.description: Two separate syllabuses on different pacing, and a student placed in the wrong one spends two years either bored or drowning. Federal regulation requires private schools to teach Arabic language, so for most Abu Dhabi students this is a timetabled subject rather than an elective.

abu-dhabi/igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: Abu Dhabi IGCSE families are concentrated in a handful of residential corridors, and what changes between them is not the syllabus but the evening: when the bus drops, how late clubs run, and what time a Year 11 student can realistically do focused work. Session planning starts there.

regions.name: Al Khalidiyah and Al Bateen
regions.note: Established island neighbourhoods close to several long-standing British-curriculum schools, so journeys home are short and a 16:30 session is realistic. Year 11 families here most often ask for Mathematics and the separate sciences.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: High-density towers with schools within a short radius and a large proportion of recently arrived families. Mid-year transfers are common, which makes syllabus-code checks more valuable here than anywhere else in the emirate.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Villa housing with long bus runs to island schools, so a 17:00 start is the practical floor for a Year 10 or Year 11 student who needs to be alert. Two 50-minute sessions beat one two-hour block in this corridor.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Families feeding a mix of British and IB schools, which is why the IGCSE-to-Diploma question comes up here more often than the IGCSE-to-A-Level one. Weekend morning sessions are heavily requested in the spring term.

regions.name: Yas Island and Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Newer school capacity and a younger year-group profile, so Year 9 and Year 10 enquiries outnumber Year 11 ones. That is the better-value end of the two-year arc, and families here tend to arrive earlier than average.

regions.name: Al Reef and Al Ghadeer
regions.note: Mainland communities a long drive from the island, where a visiting tutor's travel premium is at its highest and online delivery changes the arithmetic most. Evening slots from 17:30 are standard.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Mussafah
regions.note: Large mixed districts with students travelling across the emirate to school. Timetables vary household by household, so we set the weekly slot after the first week rather than guessing at booking.

regions.name: Between the Bridges and Al Nahyan
regions.note: Central districts with access to schools on both sides of the water. A common pattern here is a Year 11 student taking one subject with a tutor while the school runs its own after-school clinic for another.

schoolClusters.city: The island: Al Mushrif, Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
schoolClusters.note: The emirate's longest-established British-curriculum provision, which means IGCSE entry practice here is settled and well documented. Boards and tiers still differ school by school, so ask your school's examinations officer which board and which code before buying tuition in any subject.

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha, Yas and Saadiyat
schoolClusters.note: Newer capacity across the mainland corridor and the islands, with a higher share of families who changed curriculum within the last two years. This is where syllabus-code mismatches and tier misplacements most often surface, usually in Mathematics.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE tutor in Abu Dhabi is actually hired to fix
paragraphs: The literal answer: an IGCSE tutor teaches one or more Cambridge or Pearson International GCSE subjects to a student in Years 10 or 11, outside school hours, usually weekly. In Abu Dhabi the service exists as visiting tutors who drive to the family's address and as one-to-one tuition over live video. Published market rates put the first at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel, and a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors advertising IGCSE tuition from AED 150. IB Gram delivers only the second. We run no home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service.

What families ask for and what they need are different about half the time. The request is usually a subject and a worry. The need is often a decision that has already been made badly: a tier that caps the grade, a syllabus the tutor is not teaching to, a second-language English entry where a first-language one was assumed, or a subject count that will not satisfy Ministry of Education equivalency later. None of those is fixed by weekly teaching, and all of them are cheaper to fix in Year 10 than in March of Year 11.

A second recurring gap is the scale itself. Cambridge reports some IGCSE syllabuses on 9 to 1 and others on A* to G; Pearson reports International GCSE on 9 to 1. A parent reading a report with a 6 in one subject and a B in another is reading two different measurement systems, and school reports rarely explain which is which. Before you buy an hour of anything, get the board, the syllabus code and the tier for every subject in writing from the school's examinations officer. That email is free and it changes what you should spend money on.

sections.heading: Tiering: the decision that sets a ceiling before teaching starts
paragraphs: In tiered IGCSE subjects a candidate sits one of two sets of papers. Cambridge calls them Core and Extended; Pearson calls them Foundation and Higher. The lower tier examines less of the syllabus and awards a restricted range of grades. That restriction is the whole point of this section: a family planning around a top grade in a subject entered at the lower tier is planning around an outcome the entry has already removed, and no quantity of weekly tuition changes it.

The decision is usually made by the school on the basis of Year 9 and Year 10 performance, which is reasonable. What is less reasonable is how rarely it is explained to the family in those terms. Parents are told their child is doing Core Mathematics and hear a reassurance about workload rather than a statement about a ceiling. Then in Year 11 they buy tuition aimed at a grade 8, and the tutor spends the first session explaining that the papers cannot award it.

Tier changes are possible and they have deadlines. Those deadlines are set by the board and administered through your school's examinations officer, and they sit months before the examination itself - Cambridge's final entry deadline for the March 2027 series was 27 November 2026, with forecast grades due 27 February 2027. The practical sequence is: ask which tier, ask what the ceiling is, ask what evidence would support a move up, and ask by when. If the answer to the last question has already passed, the honest tutoring plan is to maximise the grade available at the current tier, which is a different plan with different content.

sections.heading: How many IGCSEs your child actually needs, and which ones do not count
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi students typically sit eight to ten IGCSE subjects. The number that matters for UAE recognition is smaller and specific. For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

That last clause is where families get caught. A student with a strong Arabic grade and a strong Islamic Education grade has two excellent results that do not count towards the five, which can leave a thinner margin than the report card suggests. It is worth doing the arithmetic in Year 10 rather than after results day, because the remedy - entering one further subject in a later series - needs an entry deadline that has not yet passed. One competitor page currently ranking for UAE IGCSE queries states that candidates must take six subjects; the sourced requirement is five.

Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs, not something a tutor performs or guarantees, and tutoring is not a requirement for it. The American track has different conditions, including English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics through at least 450 in the SAT Math test. For the IB there is no points threshold we are willing to publish, because we have not read one on the Ministry's own site. sections.heading: Year 10 against Year 11: when an hour is worth most
paragraphs: Almost all IGCSE tutoring in this market is bought in Year 11, and almost all of it would have been worth more in Year 10. The reason is not motivational. It is that an hour in Year 10 can teach, and an hour in February of Year 11 can mostly only triage. Teaching builds something the student keeps; triage redistributes a fixed amount of attention across topics that are all now urgent. The same money buys different goods.

There is a specific mechanism behind this in the quantitative subjects. Algebraic manipulation underpins the later topics in Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry. A student with insecure algebra in Year 10 can have it rebuilt in six to eight weekly sessions, after which the rest of the syllabus becomes teachable. The same student in Year 11 with four months to go cannot be taken off the syllabus for eight weeks, so the tutor patches topic by topic and the underlying weakness keeps reappearing. The grade usually still moves. It moves less, for more money.

The honest version of the Year 11 conversation runs like this. With four to six months, pick two subjects, not five. Start from a marked mock rather than a syllabus list, because the mock shows where marks are actually being dropped and the syllabus shows only what exists. Work in order of marks available rather than textbook order. Accept that paper technique - reading the command word, allocating time by marks, showing the step the marker needs - is often worth more than additional content at this point. And if the tier has capped the grade, say so in week one rather than week ten.

sections.heading: The exam series counted backwards from results day
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market publishes a session calendar, which is strange, because the calendar is the thing that constrains every tutoring plan. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and a March series for some qualifications. Pearson's International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026.

Two mechanical details catch families out. The first is zones: every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Download the timetable your school's examinations officer confirms, not the first one a search returns. The second is that provisional timetables are published ahead of each series and can be revised, so a plan should be built against the live official timetable rather than against dates copied from a page like this one.

Counted backwards, a series has a fixed shape. Entries close months before the papers. Forecast grades are collected weeks before them. Mocks sit a term earlier and are the only realistic data a tutoring plan should be built on. Results reach centres before candidates - Pearson's June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Enquiries about results and retake entries both have their own deadlines after that, which is why a family deciding in September to resit in November is often already late.

sections.heading: Nine subjects slipping, one budget: which hour to buy first
paragraphs: A Year 11 report with five amber subjects produces a predictable instinct: tutor all five. Spread across five subjects, a typical household budget buys roughly fortnightly contact in each, which is below the frequency at which anything consolidates. The result is five subjects that each feel attended to and none that moves. Triage is unpleasant and it is the correct response.

The ranking logic is mechanical rather than emotional. Subjects that gate the next stage come first: Mathematics and the separate sciences determine whether Higher Level Diploma or A Level science is viable, so a grade there is worth more than the same grade elsewhere. Next come subjects where the gap is technique rather than content, because technique moves fastest - Business Studies and Economics case-study structure, English directed writing and summary, Geography named examples, History answering the question rather than narrating. Last come content-heavy subjects where the student is simply behind, since those need more weeks than the calendar has.

Two subjects should usually be dropped from the tutoring plan rather than added to it. The subject the student is already passing comfortably, because the marginal grade there buys nothing. And the subject where the student has given up entirely, unless the problem is diagnosably narrow - in which case it belongs in the first group, not the last. A tutor willing to tell you which two subjects not to pay for is giving you better advice than one who agrees to all five.

sections.heading: From IGCSE into the Diploma Programme or A Level: the gap by subject
paragraphs: Year 11 families in Al Raha and Khalifa City are frequently choosing between a British sixth form and an IB Diploma place while the examinations are still running. The choice is usually discussed in terms of breadth against depth, which is accurate and not very actionable. What is actionable is the specific gap between each IGCSE subject and the first term of the course that follows it, because that gap is what makes the first report of Year 12 look worse than anybody expected.

The pattern is consistent. Mathematics at Extended or Higher covers most of what Analysis and Approaches or an A Level course assumes, except that the pace of algebraic work doubles and worked examples largely stop. The sciences assume a practical write-up style that IGCSE only gestures at, and Diploma internal assessment requires a level of independent design that no IGCSE component asks for. English Literature moves from close reading of set texts to sustained argument. Economics and Business introduce diagrammatic analysis that must be drawn correctly under time pressure.

Which is why the highest-value block in the whole sequence is often four to eight sessions in the summer between Year 11 and Year 12, aimed at content rather than study skills. Not a general bridging course: the actual algebra, the actual write-up conventions, the actual essay structure the specific course assumes on day one. Students who do that arrive in September able to listen to the first lesson instead of decoding it, and the first Year 12 report reflects it.

sections.heading: Sitting IGCSE as a private candidate in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: Some students need an IGCSE grade without a school place for it: a subject the school does not offer, a resit after a disappointing series, a child being educated at home, or a family that arrived mid-cycle. That route exists and runs through examination centres rather than through tutors. Entries for private candidates are made by a centre registered with the relevant board, and the centre decides what it will accept, what it charges and what deadlines it imposes on top of the board's own.

The practical constraints are worth knowing before planning around this. Subjects with assessed practical or coursework components are the hardest to arrange privately, because somebody has to administer them; written-only syllabuses are more straightforward. Entry deadlines are the board's, and they are early - Cambridge's final entries for the March 2027 series closed on 27 November 2026 - but centres frequently set their own earlier cut-offs, and a centre's fee is separate from the board's entry fee. Zone timetables apply to private candidates exactly as they do to school candidates.

Tutoring a private candidate is a different job from tutoring a school student. There is no school scheme of work setting the pace, no teacher issuing deadlines and no mock unless somebody arranges one. So the plan has to supply all three: a syllabus-ordered sequence with dates, written tasks with hand-in dates, and at least two full papers sat under timed conditions and marked against the real criteria. We do not enter candidates, administer examinations or arrange centres, and we are not permitted to supply board syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes - those come from the board's own site and from the centre.
