process.title: Send the subject, the board and the code
process.description: Subject name alone is not enough to plan a session. Send the board, the syllabus code and the tier for each subject, plus the year group and the target series. If you do not have them, your school's examinations officer can send all four in one email and it costs nothing.

process.title: Free 45-minute trial lesson
process.description: A tutor works with your child on one topic from the actual syllabus, ideally starting from a marked piece of school work. No charge and no card details taken. You end the session with a written note naming the gap, the tier position and what a block of sessions would target.

process.title: Tier and entry check before anything is bought
process.description: We read the entry details against the board's own published key dates and state plainly what grade the current tier can award and whether any change deadline is still open. If the tuition you were about to buy is aimed above the tier ceiling, you find out in week zero.

process.title: Weekly sessions against a marked baseline
process.description: Fifty to sixty minutes, one-to-one over live video, working from your child's marked mock or past paper rather than a syllabus checklist. Topic order is set by marks available. Each session ends with one short written task carrying a hand-in date.

process.title: Half-term review against the syllabus
process.description: Every half term the plan is checked against the board's published syllabus rather than the textbook, so topics the school has not reached yet are visible as a risk instead of a surprise. You get the revised topic order in writing, with what changed and why.

process.title: Pre-series technique block
process.description: In the final weeks the work shifts to timed sections, command-word reading and time allocation by marks, with papers marked against the real criteria. This stage has an end date set by the series, which is the point: a plan that cannot end has no shape.

whyPoints.title: We work from the syllabus code, not the subject name
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different assessments of similar mathematics, and 0500 and 0510 are different English qualifications entirely. Teaching the right content into the wrong paper structure is the most common way tuition fails to move a grade.

whyPoints.title: The tier ceiling is stated in week zero
whyPoints.description: If a subject is entered at Core or Foundation, we say what grade the papers can award before you pay for anything aimed above it, and whether a change deadline remains open. That conversation costs us sales and saves families months of misdirected work.

whyPoints.title: Plans are built on a marked paper, not a syllabus list
whyPoints.description: A syllabus shows what exists; a marked mock shows where marks are actually dropped. Topic order follows marks available rather than textbook order, which usually means starting somewhere other than where the student expected.

whyPoints.title: Session dates are set against the board's published calendar
whyPoints.description: Entry deadlines, forecast-grade dates and the zone timetable all constrain a plan, and they are read from the board's own key dates rather than from memory. A pre-series block that ends after the paper has been sat is not a plan.

whyPoints.title: A tutor pool that is not limited by a drive
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means a family in Al Reef or Al Ghadeer selects from everyone who teaches their specific syllabus, rather than from the adults willing to drive out there at 17:30. For minority subjects and second-language English routes that is the entire difference.

whyPoints.title: Clear limits on coursework and board materials
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on work the student has produced. We do not produce assessed work for a student, and we do not supply board syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes - those come from the board's own site. Both limits are stated before anybody pays.

faqs.question: My child is entered for Core Mathematics in Abu Dhabi - can a tutor still get them a grade 8?
faqs.answer: No, and that is the most important thing on this page. Tiered Cambridge and Pearson subjects award a restricted range of grades at the lower tier, so Core and Foundation entries cannot reach the top grades however well a candidate performs. Tuition aimed at a grade the papers cannot award is wasted money. What is worth doing is asking the school's examinations officer two questions in writing: what is the maximum awardable grade at the current tier, and is the deadline for a tier change still open. If it is open, the tutoring plan is evidence for a move up. If it has passed, the plan is to maximise the grade available at the current tier, which is different work.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to our home in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tuition is a service we offer only in India. Abu Dhabi lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, with your child's marked papers shared on screen and annotated live. Published market rates for a visiting tutor here run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel folded in, against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, so the drive is most of the premium. The practical gain is the pool: a family in Al Reef chooses from everyone who teaches their syllabus rather than from those willing to make the journey.

faqs.question: We are in Abu Dhabi - how many IGCSE passes will the Ministry of Education actually count towards equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track, five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two accredited AS Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. That exclusion catches families out, because two strong results may not count towards the requirement. One ranking competitor page states six subjects; the sourced figure is five. Equivalency is a Ministry process - verify the current rules on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority, since IB Gram neither performs nor guarantees any part of it.

faqs.question: Why does my child's report show a 6 in one subject and a B in another?
faqs.answer: Because they are different scales. Cambridge reports some IGCSE syllabuses on a 9 to 1 numeric scale and others on A* to G, and Pearson reports International GCSE on 9 to 1. A report can therefore legitimately mix the two, and the numbers and letters are not aligned in the way parents instinctively assume. This matters when setting targets and when comparing two subjects to decide where to spend money. Ask the examinations officer which scale applies to each syllabus your child is entered for, alongside the board, the code and the tier. One email answers all four and changes what you should buy.

faqs.question: Is it better to start IGCSE tutoring in Year 10 or wait until Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10, by a wide margin, and this is a mechanical point rather than a motivational one. In Year 10 an hour can teach something the student keeps - insecure algebra rebuilt over six to eight sessions makes the later topics in Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry teachable. In February of Year 11 the same hour mostly triages: the tutor cannot take a student off the syllabus for eight weeks, so weaknesses get patched topic by topic and keep resurfacing. Grades still move in Year 11. They move less, for more money, across fewer subjects. If you are reading this in Year 10, the cheap window is now.

faqs.question: Five of my child's subjects are slipping - should we tutor all five?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not. A typical household budget spread across five subjects buys roughly fortnightly contact in each, which is below the frequency at which anything consolidates, so five subjects feel attended to and none moves. Rank them instead. Subjects that gate the next stage come first, which usually means Mathematics and the separate sciences, because they decide whether Higher Level or A Level science is viable. Technique gaps come second, because they move fastest: case-study command words, directed writing, named examples in Geography. Drop the subject your child already passes comfortably, since the marginal grade there buys nothing.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE exams actually take place, and when do entries close?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with a March series for some qualifications. Pearson International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November. Entries close months ahead: Cambridge's final entries for the March 2027 series were due 27 November 2026 for examinations between 3 February and 4 March 2027, with forecast grades due 27 February 2027. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and it is essential to use the correct timetable for your zone, because Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong version.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE tutor cost per hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published market figures as at October 2026, none of them ours: Unitors advertises IGCSE tuition from AED 150 per hour and IB from AED 200; EdFlik lists from AED 45 to AED 65; Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52; TutorChase quotes AED 270; BartyED AED 650 at the premium end. Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350, with home tutors advertising up to AED 500, and specialist exam-year tuition at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Monthly packages seen in the market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions. Ask any provider for the rate, the session length and whether marking is included.

faqs.question: Do Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel teach the same IGCSE content?
faqs.answer: Similar content, genuinely different assessment. The syllabuses diverge on paper structure, component weighting, tiering arrangements and how practical skills are examined, which is why a tutor needs the code rather than the subject name. Pearson also operates differently in how series are structured across the year. A student who moves school mid-course can end up with notes written for one board and an entry for the other, and that mismatch costs real marks on paper technique even when the underlying knowledge is sound. Send us the code from the entry form; where a child sits subjects across both boards, that is workable but the plans have to be kept separate.

faqs.question: My child moved to Abu Dhabi from a CBSE school in Year 9 - what is the actual gap?
faqs.answer: Rarely arithmetic, usually algebraic fluency and written explanation. Students arriving from Indian-curriculum schools are often ahead on procedural calculation and behind on the extended written answer that IGCSE science and humanities papers require, where marks depend on explaining rather than stating. The second gap is coursework-style working: showing the step a marker needs rather than the answer alone. Year 9 is the cheapest point to address both, because nothing has been entered yet and a tier decision is still ahead. A single diagnostic session on one past paper from the intended board usually identifies which of the two is dominant.

faqs.question: Is my child's tutor legally allowed to tutor privately in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's own channels, with the service page listing a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you. ADEK's ethics rules also bar school staff from paid tutoring of pupils enrolled at their own school.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with IGCSE coursework or controlled assessment?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits, yes. A tutor may teach the skills the component assesses, explain what the criteria reward, discuss a plan the student has made, ask questions that expose a weak argument, and give feedback on a draft the student has written themselves. A tutor may not supply content for submission, rewrite a draft into their own prose, or hand over finished sections. The work has to be the student's own, and boards treat breaches as malpractice with consequences that fall on the student. We also do not supply board syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes; those are the board's material and come from the board's own site.

faqs.question: Can my child resit one IGCSE subject in November without changing school?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and the mechanics run through a centre rather than through a tutor. Cambridge offers a November series and Pearson offers November for International GCSE, so a single-subject resit is a normal arrangement. The constraints are deadlines and components: entries close well ahead of the papers, centres often impose their own earlier cut-offs and charge their own fee on top of the board's, and subjects with assessed practical components are harder to arrange than written-only ones. Decide in the weeks around results rather than in September, because by then the useful preparation window has already narrowed and some deadlines have passed.

faqs.question: What is actually worth buying in the summer between Year 11 and Year 12?
faqs.answer: Content, not study skills - and the specific content the next course assumes on day one. For Mathematics that is algebraic fluency at roughly double the IGCSE pace, with function notation and early calculus vocabulary, because worked examples largely stop. For the sciences it is formal practical write-ups, uncertainty and data analysis, which IGCSE only gestures at and Diploma internal assessment demands. For English Literature it is sustained comparative argument rather than close reading of set texts. Four to eight sessions aimed at the real Year 12 course beat a generic bridging programme, and students who do it can listen to the first lesson rather than decode it.

faqs.question: How quickly can you match an IGCSE tutor, and what if the subject is unusual?
faqs.answer: For mainstream subjects on either board - Mathematics, the three sciences, English, Business, Economics - a match is normally within a few days, and the free trial lesson comes before any payment. For minority subjects, second-language English routes and some language syllabuses it can take longer, and if nobody suitable is available we say so rather than offering an approximate match. Where no UAE-based specialist covers a niche syllabus, the tutor may be based elsewhere and teaching into Gulf Standard Time; we state that up front, because a tutor who does not know your board is worse than a wait.

abu-dhabi/igcse-tutor-near-me.tutorsIntro: Each tutor below teaches one or two IGCSE subjects to a named specification, works one-to-one over live video with Abu Dhabi students, and produces marked scripts and session notes from the first week rather than from the first review. Distance to your address is not a variable.

intro.heading: Two questions hiding inside one search
paragraphs: Typing igcse tutor near me is shorthand for something more specific, and it is worth separating the parts. The first part is competence: can this person teach Cambridge 0620 Extended, or Pearson 4MA1 Higher, well enough to move marks. The second is logistics: can a session happen on a Tuesday at half past four without the family rearranging the evening. Distance is relevant to the second question only, and even then it is a proxy for time rather than for kilometres.

The reason this matters in Abu Dhabi is that the two questions pull in opposite directions. The pool of people who can reach Al Reef before seven in the evening is small. The pool of people who can teach Chemistry 0620 Extended to a student aiming at the top of the scale is also small. Intersect those two sets and you are often left with nobody, which is how families end up paying specialist rates for a generalist who happens to live nearby.

Private schools in the emirate are licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, and the school map is spread across three broad bands: the island schools around Al Bateen, Al Khalidiyah and Al Mushrif; the Khalifa City, Al Raha and Yas Island corridor; and the newer mainland communities out towards Al Shamkha, Al Falah and Mussafah. A household in each of those bands has a materially different evening, and the clock table further down this page sets out what that means in practice.

Our own position is simple and stated up front. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram sends nobody to a UAE address; visiting tuition exists in our India operation only. So the honest version of near me here is not a shorter drive, it is a tutor who is available at your hour and matched to your specification, with the evidence of their work arriving in writing every week.

Everything below is built around things you can check. What time a session can realistically begin from each part of the emirate. How common your child's subject and tier actually are, and what happens when nobody suitable is free. What the first four marked scripts should contain and in what order to read them. What a session note has to say to be worth keeping. The arithmetic of a drive, in dirhams per teaching minute. And how to verify, yourself, that the person teaching your child is permitted to do so. None of that requires you to judge teaching you cannot see. Each item is a document, a timetable fact or a number you can put beside a competing quote, which is the only basis on which a stranger's hour is worth buying at a specialist rate.

abu-dhabi/igcse-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: Matching on specification means knowing three things before anybody is proposed: the board, the tier and the series. The blocks below set out what each of those changes about who is a suitable tutor, which is the part a postcode search cannot answer.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, by code
programmes.description: A tutor for Cambridge needs the specification rather than the subject: 0580 Mathematics, 0607 International Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0653 Combined Science, 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences, 0500 First Language English, 0510 English as a Second Language. Tiering is Core and Extended, and the tier changes which past papers are the right practice set.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June and a November series, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, stating that using the correct zone timetable is essential and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. Confirm the zone with your Abu Dhabi school's exams officer before building a schedule.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, by code
programmes.description: Pearson codes begin with 4: Mathematics A is 4MA1, Physics 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1, Biology 4BI1, English Language A 4EA1. Tiering is Foundation and Higher. A tutor who has taught only Cambridge will recognise the content and misjudge the question style, the mark distribution across papers and the balance of short to extended responses.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August. Provisional timetables are published ahead of each series, so plan against the live official document.

programmes.name: Tier, and why it narrows the tutor pool
programmes.description: The higher tier of a minority subject is where availability becomes genuinely thin, because the number of people who teach it well in any one city is small. A tutor comfortable with Core content may be out of their depth on Extended material, and the gap is invisible for several weeks because the early topics overlap.
programmes.countryNote: Tier entries are fixed at the entry deadline rather than the exam, and for the Cambridge March 2027 series final entries were due on 27 November 2026. That means the tier question, and therefore the question of who is a suitable tutor, needs settling in the autumn term with marked evidence in hand.

programmes.name: Resits and private candidates
programmes.description: Students resitting one or two subjects, or sitting as private candidates, need a tutor who knows the entry mechanics as well as the content. The content has usually been taught before, so the work is paper practice with forensic marking rather than a second pass through the specification.
programmes.countryNote: A private candidate has to be entered through a centre that accepts external candidates, and the entry deadlines are the board's rather than the school's. Confirm both the accepting centre and its deadline early, because the availability of centre places in the emirate is the binding constraint more often than tutor availability is.

abu-dhabi/igcse-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Abu Dhabi households ask for most, with a note on what a tutor needs to demonstrate before taking the booking. Specification knowledge is checkable in one conversation; it does not need a trial term to establish.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Ask which tier they usually teach and how the papers differ between the two boards. A tutor who answers precisely has taught both; one who talks about IGCSE maths generally has taught one and assumed the other is close enough, which produces the wrong practice set.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The useful test is the practical paper. Ask what an alternative-to-practical question actually assesses. A specialist will name scale reading, control variables and method description precisely, because those marks are predictable and rarely rehearsed at home.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: One of the thinner pools at the higher tier in this market. Ask how they teach the two steps of a moles calculation separately, and how they structure an extended response on electrolysis, since those two things account for a large share of recoverable marks.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The breadth of recall makes a topic-confidence audit the right first session. Ask how they decide what to cover first, because a tutor who answers with the textbook order has not planned around which specification points carry the most marks.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Ask how they mark a reading answer, specifically how selection and inference are credited against retelling. English is the subject where reassuring feedback most often substitutes for marking against the published scheme, so a sample annotated answer is worth requesting.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: The summary and note-making tasks are formula-driven and respond quickly, so a competent tutor should be able to describe the formula in a sentence. Also ask whether the route choice between first and second language English has been settled with the school.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (Cambridge 0455 / 0450)
subjects.description: Ask what earns an evaluation mark. The answer should mention a judgement with a stated condition attached, not a balanced discussion. Tutors who describe these subjects as essay writing tend not to be marking against the band descriptors.

subjects.name: Geography and History (Cambridge 0460 / 0470)
subjects.description: Both reward specific named detail, so ask how case studies and sources are built into weekly work. A tutor who produces one case-study card per topic leaves the student with a usable revision set, which is worth more than an hour of discussion.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT (Cambridge 0478 / 0417)
subjects.description: Ask them to complete a trace table in the format the mark scheme expects. It takes two minutes and it separates tutors who have taught the examined course from programmers who know the material but not the paper.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Foreign Language (Cambridge 0508 / 0544)
subjects.levels: First Language and Foreign Language routes
subjects.description: Confirm which route the school has entered, because the two assess very different things. A tutor comfortable with the foreign-language route is not automatically suitable for first language, and the mismatch is usually discovered late.

abu-dhabi/igcse-tutor-near-me.regionsIntro: The map below is about time rather than distance. What matters for a weekday session is when the student is home, fed and able to concentrate, and that varies by an hour and a half across the emirate even though the syllabus does not vary at all.

regions.name: Al Bateen, Al Khalidiyah and Al Zahiyah
regions.note: Short school runs and the densest concentration of British-curriculum schools, so local tutor supply is at its best here for common subjects. A session can often start by half past four, which is the single biggest advantage any household can have.

regions.name: Al Mushrif, Al Karamah and Al Nahyan
regions.note: Villa addresses within the island's school belt. Households here frequently run two or three children at different stages, so staggered fixed slots matter more than a single flexible one that becomes whoever is available.

regions.name: Al Rawdah and Al Maryah Island
regions.note: Central addresses close to several schools but with parking and lift delays that eat into a visiting hour. A live session loses none of that time, which is worth more than it sounds across a thirty-session year.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: The corridor between the island and the inland communities, with internal distances that surprise newcomers. A visiting tutor crossing from the island adds a real drive each way, so comparisons here are usually made on cost per teaching minute.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island and Yas Island
regions.note: Distinct catchments with high rates of mid-course transfer. New arrivals usually need a specification audit before anybody is matched, because the subject names carry across systems and the papers do not.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: High-rise living where study space is often shared and evenings are noisy. Headphones, a defined sixty minutes and a timer on screen do more here than any change of tutor, and a visiting hour loses minutes at the lift.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Mussafah
regions.note: Long drives to the island cluster, which pushes the earliest realistic visiting start past seven on a school night. Weekend morning sessions are common and usually more productive than a tired weekday hour.

regions.name: Al Shamkha, Al Falah and Al Reef
regions.note: Outer communities with large school cohorts. The practical consequence of distance here is that the local tutor pool for a higher-tier minority subject is often empty, so matching on specification means matching beyond the neighbourhood.

sections.heading: The proximity question, answered with a map and a clock
paragraphs: Distance only matters because of what it does to the clock. A tutor twelve kilometres away is not worse than one two kilometres away; a session that cannot begin until a quarter past seven is worse than one that begins at half past four, because the student is a different person at those two times. So the useful way to think about near me is to ask what hour is reachable, and then ask who is good, rather than the other way round.

Run the arithmetic on your own evening before comparing any tutors. What time does the student actually walk through the door? How long before they are fed and able to sit down? What else is already in that evening, including Arabic or Islamic Education homework, sport and the other eight subjects? For most island households the answer is a workable slot from about half past four. For most mainland households on a school night it is closer to half past six, and for a visiting tutor it is later again once the drive is added at both ends.

The second half of the calculation is what proximity costs in choice. Abu Dhabi has a real tutoring market, but the subset of it that can be physically present in Al Reef on a Tuesday at six is narrow, and the subset of that subset which teaches Chemistry 0620 Extended confidently is narrower still. Families who insist on both usually end up compromising on the part they cannot see, which is teaching quality.

Removing the drive from the equation does not make a tutor good. It just stops geography making the decision for you. That is why the rest of this page is about the evidence a tutor produces in the first month, since once proximity is no longer the filter, something else has to be, and the only honest candidate is the marked work.

sections.heading: Corridor arithmetic: what time a session can actually start
paragraphs: The table below is the version of this conversation we have with families several times a week. It is not a traffic report; it is a planning tool. The numbers are the realistic earliest start for a weekday session, and the difference between the two right-hand columns is the drive that a visiting arrangement has to absorb somewhere, either in the rate or in the student's concentration.

Two things to notice. First, the live-video column is roughly the same everywhere, because what sets it is when the student gets home rather than when a tutor can arrive. Second, the gap between the columns widens the further out you live, which means the cost of insisting on physical presence is unevenly distributed across the emirate. A family in Al Mushrif pays very little for it. A family in Al Shamkha pays an hour of their child's best concentration.

The practical response for outer communities is to invert the week. Put the demanding work, particularly a full paper under timing, on a weekend morning when there is a genuine two-hour window, and keep weekday contacts short and mechanical. Two thirty-minute sessions on a school night often achieve more than one tired hour, and they survive a term better.

Ramadan shifts all of this, and planning for it in advance is easier than improvising. Session times commonly move later in the evening, after Iftar, and concentration patterns change for most students. A plan that spans Ramadan should put the timed papers either side of it and keep the intervening weeks light and consistent rather than ambitious.

sections.heading: Why the nearest tutor is rarely the right specification
paragraphs: Availability is not uniform across subjects, and no provider in this market publishes where it thins out. We do, because the alternative is taking a booking and then finding somebody approximately suitable, which is how a household discovers in February that their Chemistry tutor is a biologist who did chemistry at school.

The pattern is consistent. Mathematics and the common sciences at the lower tier are well covered almost everywhere. Higher-tier minority subjects, second-language English at the Extended route, Computer Science and the first-language Arabic route are where the pool is genuinely thin in any one city, and insisting on a local match in those cases means choosing from a list of one or two.

What should happen when nobody suitable is free is a stated position rather than silence. Ours is to say how long a match is likely to take, whether the session would need to sit at a different hour, and whether a nearby alternative serves, such as supporting the examined components with a specialist in the adjacent discipline while the right person becomes available. Sometimes the honest answer is that we cannot help with that combination at present.

There is a question worth asking any provider here, and the answer is diagnostic. Ask what happens if the tutor they propose turns out to be wrong for your child in week three. A provider with real depth will describe a replacement process with the records handed over. A provider without it will reassure you that the match will be right, which is not a process.

sections.heading: The first four marked scripts, read in order
paragraphs: Once proximity has stopped being the filter, the marked work is what you judge a tutor on, and four scripts across the first month is enough to form a view. Read them in a deliberate order, because the questions they answer build on each other.

The first script answers whether the tutor marks against the published scheme or against their own sense of the subject. Look for marks allocated per point, annotations naming the command word or the missing step, and a total that could be defended to an examiner. A script covered in encouraging comments and no mark allocation tells you the marking is impressionistic.

The second answers whether the diagnosis is specific. Lost marks should be attributed to a cause rather than a topic: method known but executed carelessly, structure missing on the extended response, content never learned, time run out. Four causes, counted. A diagnosis that says revise electrolysis is a topic label; one that says the chemistry is sound and the answer has no structure the scheme can credit is a plan.

The third and fourth answer the only question that matters, which is whether anything moved. The same question type, sat a fortnight apart, with the earlier losses marked. If the second attempt gains marks on precisely the thing the first attempt lost them on, the teaching is working. If the second attempt is a different question type entirely, nobody can tell, and that is worth raising before another month passes.

sections.heading: A session note worth keeping, and three that are not
paragraphs: A session note takes two minutes to write and makes a term auditable. Most providers either do not produce one or produce something that cannot be used, and since the note is the only record of what happened in a room you were not in, it is reasonable to be particular about it.

A useful note names four things. The paper and component worked on, with the syllabus code. What specifically was addressed, at the level of the question type rather than the topic. What the student did unaided by the end of the hour. And the one named task set before the next session. Four lines. A parent can read thirty of these in ten minutes and see the shape of a term.

Three notes that are not worth keeping. The first says good progress on algebra today, which names neither the paper nor the component and could describe any hour of any week. The second lists topics covered, which records delivery rather than learning and will look identical in October and in March. The third is a long narrative about the student's attitude, which is occasionally useful and never a substitute for a record of what was taught.

There is a reason to insist beyond tidiness. When a tutor changes, or when you need to take evidence to a head of department, the notes are what travels. A household with thirty readable notes can hand over a term of work in an email. A household without them is starting again, and paying for the restart.

sections.heading: What ten minutes of drive costs, per teaching minute
paragraphs: Visiting rates in this market sit above online rates for the same teacher, and the gap is the drive. Published figures put in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the rate, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, on what other providers publish. Bestimate's 2026 table shows 180 to 350 for in-home work and independent home tutors are quoted at 200 to 500.

Those figures are per hour, which conceals the thing that actually varies. Convert to dirhams per teaching minute and the arithmetic changes shape, because a visiting hour routinely contains fewer teaching minutes than it looks: arrival, settling, a parent conversation at the door, and an early finish because the tutor has another household to reach. None of that is dishonest. It is simply what a drive does to an hour.

The table runs the comparison on a single assumed rate so the structure is visible rather than the price. Use your own quoted figures in the same frame and the question answers itself: which arrangement delivers the most teaching minutes for the money, and who is absorbing the travel. In every visiting arrangement somebody pays for the drive, and it is either the household in dirhams or the tutor in unpaid time, which eventually becomes the household's problem anyway.

One further note on monthly packages, because they are where comparisons break. Figures seen in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visiting sessions. Those are not the same purchase: eight contacts with eight sets of notes against four longer contacts with a travel component inside the price. Compare contacts and teaching minutes, not monthly totals.

sections.heading: Checking the permit yourself, in four steps
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit, and a parent can check the position in a single conversation. The permit exists because individual tutoring is regulated activity: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and MoHRE's own service is Issuance of a New Work Permit, Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through its app, website and e-services system with a two-working-day completion time.

Four steps. Ask whether the person holds the private tuition work permit. Ask which eligibility category they hold it under, since the permit is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Ask to see it, because a document that exists can be shown. And check the fee claim: the permit is granted at no charge for two years, so anybody describing a fee they paid for it is describing something else.

Two things not to accept. Do not accept a claim of regulator approval. No tutoring individual or platform holds KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, IB or Cambridge accreditation by virtue of tutoring, and a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific thing issued to training institutes with premises. IB Gram holds none of those and claims none. And do not accept a quoted fine figure for tutoring without a permit: individuals operating without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, but no fine schedule is published, so any specific amount you are quoted is invented.

There is a related arrangement to avoid entirely. Press reporting indicates that ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and that the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat the detail as press-reported and confirm the current ADEK document before quoting it, but do not build a plan around your child's own teacher.

sections.heading: Where proximity genuinely wins
paragraphs: A page that argued physical presence never helps would be selling rather than explaining. There are situations where a tutor in the room is better, and they are worth naming so the comparison is honest rather than convenient.

Younger children are the clearest case. A nine-year-old who needs an adult to keep them at the table for forty minutes is not well served by a screen, whatever the subject. Practical laboratory technique is another: a student who needs to handle apparatus benefits from somebody beside them, although at IGCSE the assessed practical skills are often examined through a written paper rather than a performance. And a household with genuinely poor connectivity has a real problem that no amount of argument fixes.

There are also legitimate preferences. A student who has had a bad experience with screen learning, or a parent who wants to see the session happening in their own home, is not making an error. These are reasonable positions and the right response is to say what the visiting market charges, which is roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the rate, and let the household choose.

What proximity does not deliver is specification match, and that is the trade this page is actually about. IB Gram does not run visiting tuition in the UAE; it is an India-only service, so we have no stake in talking you out of a local tutor. If a nearby specialist teaching exactly your child's code is available at an hour that works, that is a good outcome. The point is to check all three of those things rather than just the first.

process.title: Tell us the hour before the subject
process.description: The most useful first fact is what time a session can realistically begin on a school night at your address, and whether a weekend morning is available. That single constraint removes more unsuitable options than anything else, and it is the one thing a family knows for certain.

process.title: Send the code sheet and two marked papers
process.description: The syllabus code, tier and series for the subject in question, plus photographs of the last two marked papers. A specialist reads those in ten minutes and can say where the marks are going. Without them, the first session is spent discovering what the scripts would have shown.

process.title: Hear the coverage position honestly
process.description: If the subject and tier are well covered, you will have options within days. If they are thin, you will be told the likely wait and whether a different hour would help, before any booking is taken. If we cannot sensibly cover the combination, we will say that rather than approximate it.

process.title: Use the first session as a diagnostic
process.description: The first session costs nothing and no card details are taken before it. It produces a marked piece of work, the first entry in the error record, and a short plan. If the honest conclusion is that the school's support is adequate and nothing needs buying, that is what you will hear.

process.title: Read four scripts and four notes, then decide
process.description: After a month, put the marked scripts and the session notes side by side and ask whether the same question type has improved. Continue, change the hour, change the tutor or stop. The records exist so the decision is yours rather than a matter of trusting anybody's impression.

whyPoints.title: Matched on specification, then on your hour
whyPoints.description: The code and tier come first, because a tutor who teaches the wrong specification cannot be rescued by being available. Once that is fixed, the hour is the second filter, and distance plays no part in either, since every session is delivered over live video.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits published, not discovered later
whyPoints.description: Higher-tier Chemistry, Extended second-language English, Computer Science and first-language Arabic are genuinely thin in this market. We say so, state the likely wait, and sometimes decline, rather than taking a booking and finding somebody approximately suitable afterwards.

whyPoints.title: Marked scripts in the first week
whyPoints.description: Marking against the published scheme, with lost marks attributed to a cause rather than a topic, from the first session rather than from the first review. Four scripts in a month is enough for a parent to judge whether the teaching is working, which is the whole point of producing them.

whyPoints.title: Four-line session notes you can actually use
whyPoints.description: Paper and component with the code, what was addressed at question-type level, what the student did unaided, and the one task set. Thirty of those read in ten minutes, and they travel with you if the tutor changes or you need evidence for the school.

whyPoints.title: Permit status you can verify
whyPoints.description: Ask for the private tuition work permit and the eligibility category. It is granted at no charge for two years, so it can be shown. We claim no regulator accreditation of any kind, because no tutoring provider holds one by virtue of tutoring, and we quote no fine figures because none are published.

whyPoints.title: No stake in talking you out of a local tutor
whyPoints.description: IB Gram runs no visiting service in the UAE, so this page quotes the visiting market's published rates straight and names the cases where a tutor in the room is genuinely better. If a nearby specialist teaching your child's exact code is free at a workable hour, take it.

faqs.question: Does it matter how far away my child's IGCSE tutor lives?
faqs.answer: Only through the clock, and only if someone is travelling. Our sessions are one-to-one over live video, so the tutor's address is irrelevant and the binding constraint is what time your child is home, fed and able to concentrate. For most island households that is a workable start around half past four; on the mainland it is closer to half past five. If you are hiring a visiting tutor, distance matters a great deal, because the drive comes out of either the rate or the lesson.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor in the first ten minutes to test their subject knowledge?
faqs.answer: Ask three specification questions. Which tier do you usually teach in this subject, and how do the papers differ between Cambridge and Pearson? What does an alternative-to-practical question actually assess? And how do you mark a six-mark extended response against the published scheme? Precise answers that name papers, components and mark allocations mean they have taught the course. General answers about covering the syllabus and building confidence mean they may be competent but have not been examined on this before.

faqs.question: How long does it take to be matched with an IGCSE specialist here?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on subject and tier, and the honest answer varies. Mathematics and the common sciences at the lower tier are usually available within a few days. Higher-tier Chemistry or Extended second-language English can take up to around two weeks. Computer Science 0478 and first-language Arabic are thin enough that the wait is genuinely variable and sometimes we decline. You should be told the expected wait before a booking is taken, not after, and a provider who promises immediate availability in every subject is not describing a real pool.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are hardest to find a specialist for in this emirate?
faqs.answer: Higher-tier Chemistry, English as a Second Language at the Extended route, Computer Science and Arabic as a First Language. The pattern holds across the market rather than being peculiar to one provider: the number of people who teach a minority subject at the top tier well in any one city is small. Insisting on a local match in those subjects usually means choosing from a list of one or two, which is how families end up paying specialist rates for somebody who studied the subject rather than taught the paper.

faqs.question: What should the first four marked scripts show me?
faqs.answer: Read them in order. The first shows whether marking is against the published scheme, with marks allocated per point and annotations naming the missing step. The second shows whether the diagnosis is specific, attributing lost marks to a cause rather than a topic. The third and fourth show whether anything moved, by repeating the same question type a fortnight later with the earlier losses marked. If the second attempt is a different question type entirely, nobody can judge progress, and that is worth raising immediately.

faqs.question: What makes a session note useful rather than decorative?
faqs.answer: Four lines. The paper and component with the syllabus code. What was addressed, at question-type level rather than topic level. What the student managed unaided by the end of the hour. And the single task set before the next session. Notes saying good progress today, or listing topics covered, record delivery rather than learning and will read identically in October and March. The reason to insist is practical: when a tutor changes or you need evidence for the school, the notes are what travels.

faqs.question: Is a visiting tutor's hour really shorter than an online hour?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes, and not through any dishonesty. A visiting hour contains arrival, settling, a conversation at the door and sometimes an early finish because another household is waiting. Fifty to fifty-five teaching minutes out of sixty paid is normal for a nearby address and less for a long cross-city drive. A live video session starts at the agreed minute and runs to the end. Convert any quote into dirhams per teaching minute rather than per hour and the arrangements become genuinely comparable.

faqs.question: How do I verify that someone is allowed to tutor privately in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Four steps. Ask whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. Ask which eligibility category: registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18 all qualify. Ask to see it, since a real document can be shown. And check the fee story: the permit is granted at no charge for two years, so anybody describing a fee paid for it is describing something else entirely.

faqs.question: A tutor says they are approved by KHDA. Should that reassure me?
faqs.answer: No, and it should prompt a question. A KHDA educational services permit is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes operating from premises, and it is a Dubai instrument. An individual tutor holds a MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is a different document. No individual or platform acquires KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, IB or Cambridge accreditation by virtue of tutoring. IB Gram holds none of those and claims none. Ask instead to see the tuition permit, which is the document that actually applies.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor turns out to be wrong for my child in week three?
faqs.answer: You should be able to change without starting from nothing, which is the practical reason the records matter. Marked scripts, session notes and the error record transfer to the next tutor, so the new person begins from a diagnosis rather than from a conversation. Ask any provider to describe their replacement process before you book. A described process with handover of records is a real answer; reassurance that the match will be right is not a process and tells you what to expect when it is not.

faqs.question: Can sessions start before the school run finishes on the mainland?
faqs.answer: Not usefully. From Al Shamkha, Al Reef or Mussafah the honest earliest weekday start is around a quarter past five for a live session, and later for anything involving a drive. The workable pattern is to invert the week: put the full timed paper on a weekend morning when a genuine two-hour window exists, and keep weekday contacts to thirty or forty minutes of mechanical work. Two short sessions sustain across a term better than one tired hour that gets cancelled in November.

faqs.question: Do we need a tutor in the same time zone as us?
faqs.answer: You need a tutor available at your hour, which is a slightly different thing, though in practice it amounts to the same. All slots are agreed and held in Gulf Standard Time, and the time zone the tutor happens to be sitting in is their scheduling problem rather than yours. What does matter is consistency: a slot that moves every week because of somebody else's clock produces a record you cannot compare session to session, which defeats the point of keeping one.

faqs.question: What do we need at home for a live session to work properly?
faqs.answer: Less than families expect. A laptop or tablet with a working camera, headphones, a desk or a cleared table, and the ability to photograph handwritten work. A printer helps considerably for timed papers but is not essential, since papers can be worked on paper and photographed. Reliable connectivity is the genuine requirement, and if that is a real problem at your address then a visiting tutor is the better answer, which this page says plainly because we do not provide one in the UAE.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take two children in the same household?
faqs.answer: If both are entered for the same code and tier and are at a similar point, a shared slot is efficient and each child gets roughly half the attention. If they are on different boards, different tiers or different years, it is a false economy, because the tutor alternates and each child receives a fragmented version of a different course. Households here frequently have siblings on different boards in the same subject, so check the codes before assuming a shared slot will work.

faqs.question: Should we book my child's own school teacher privately instead?
faqs.answer: It is the arrangement to avoid. Press reporting indicates that ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and that the private tuition permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat the detail as press-reported and confirm the current ADEK document before quoting it. A different teacher who knows the same specification carries none of that difficulty and can mark without a conflict of interest.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying more for a tutor who lives in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Only for things proximity actually provides. Local knowledge of a specific school's scheme of work is real but modest; the specification is national to the board, not local to the emirate. What a local tutor genuinely offers is the option of being in the room, which matters for younger children, for a student who struggles with screen learning, and where connectivity is poor. The visiting market charges roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the figure. Pay the premium for presence if you need presence, not for familiarity with the syllabus.

abu-dhabi/igcse-tutor-near-me.closingHeading: Tell us the hour, the code and the tier
abu-dhabi/igcse-tutor-near-me.closingBody: The quickest route to a useful match is three facts: what time a session can realistically start at your address, the syllabus code and tier your child is entered for, and the last two marked papers. A subject specialist reads the scripts, says where the marks are going, and we tell you honestly whether that subject and tier is well covered or thin and how long a match is likely to take. The first session costs nothing and no card details are taken beforehand. If the nearest good option is a local tutor rather than us, we will say so.

intro.heading: What the school covers, what it cannot, and what closing the difference costs
paragraphs: Khalifa City is a large mainland community of villa plots and low-rise housing between the airport road and the city, with Khalifa City A and B and the newer edges running towards Al Raha and Mohammed Bin Zayed City. It has one of the densest school clusters in the emirate, across British, American and IB continuum routes, and households here tend to be settled rather than transient. Many have been in the same school for years.

That produces an unusually well-informed parent and an unusually specific question. The enquiries from this community are rarely about what the IB Diploma is or how IGCSE works. They are about value: how many hours, at what rate, for what outcome, and whether the thing being sold is the thing that is needed. Nobody in this market publishes the answers, which is the gap this page tries to close.

Start with the structure of the problem. A school week has a fixed number of taught periods per subject and those periods carry new content. Consolidation is set as homework and checked rather than taught. Everything after that — rehearsal, timed practice, drafting an assessed piece, reviewing a marked script for patterns — belongs to the student alone. That third category is substantial, and in an examined programme it is where the grade is largely decided.

There are three different gaps that live inside that third category, and conflating them is the most expensive mistake available to a parent. A technique gap means the student knows the content and loses marks in the writing of answers. A content gap means specific topics were never learned. A habit gap means the independent hours do not happen at all. They look identical on a report card and cost very different amounts to close.

The cheapest is the technique gap, which often moves within six to eight sessions because the fix is behavioural. The most expensive is the content gap across a two-year syllabus, which needs a term or more of teaching. The habit gap is the odd one out: it is cheap to diagnose, cheap to fix structurally, and almost impossible to fix with money alone, because the thing required is a protected window and a reviewed output rather than another paid hour.

What follows prices each of those honestly, compares six provider models on more than rate, lists the extras that quietly change a quoted figure, sets out how many hours different goals actually take, and says what no budget buys. Market rates are presented as the market's with each publisher named; they are not an IB Gram price list. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, and IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in the UAE — visiting tutors are a service we run only in India.

abu-dhabi/khalifa-city.programmesIntro: Khalifa City households sit across the IB continuum, British and American routes, and the cost question looks different in each. Each note below is about where money is well spent in that programme.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across Higher and Standard Level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an internally assessed component against published criteria, submitted and moderated before external papers sat in one window. More of the result depends on self-managed work than in any other route, and the second year concentrates deadlines into an eight-week autumn.
programmes.countryNote: This is the programme where households overspend most reliably, because six subjects and three core components create six or nine places to buy help. The spending that works is narrow: one or two components where the marks are most recoverable, usually a Higher Level paper and one internally assessed piece. The spending that does not work is a tutor per subject, which costs several times as much and dilutes the student's attention across the week.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year externally examined courses, with Cambridge codes such as 0580 Mathematics and 0620 Chemistry and Pearson International GCSE codes such as 4MA1 and 4CH1. Cambridge mathematics and the separate sciences are tiered into Core and Extended, which fixes the available grade range before papers are sat. Eight to ten subjects are usually taken together.
programmes.countryNote: With eight or more subjects running at once, the question in Khalifa City is almost always which one gets the hour. The answer is the subject where a grade change alters a sixth-form entry decision, not the subject with the lowest mark. A low mark in a subject the student will drop at sixteen is a poor place to spend, however uncomfortable it looks on a report.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, labelled A to D and scored 0 to 8 against task-specific rubrics, combining to a total out of 32 that converts to a grade from 1 to 7. The final year carries the Personal Project, an extended independent piece with its own criteria and interim deadlines set by the school.
programmes.countryNote: Middle Years tutoring is the cheapest useful tutoring available in this community, because the purchase can be precise. Identify the criterion letter that is low across several subjects, buy six to eight sessions on that one skill, and several grades move together. A standing weekly subject lesson at this stage usually costs more and achieves less than a targeted block.

programmes.name: American curriculum and Advanced Placement
programmes.description: Continuous assessment across a grade point average, with Advanced Placement courses taken individually and examined separately on a 1 to 5 scale. Risk is distributed across a year, which rewards steady submission and does not build examination stamina. Standardised tests sit alongside the transcript and carry their own preparation.
programmes.countryNote: On this route the spending question is unusual: the transcript responds to consistency rather than to intensive intervention, so money spent on a crisis block near the end of a year buys very little. Where it does buy something is standardised test preparation and examination stamina, both of which are specific, measurable and separable from the school course.

abu-dhabi/khalifa-city.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Khalifa City households ask about most. Each description names what is actually being bought when a family pays for that subject, because the answer differs more than the subject names suggest.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 and 4MA1)
subjects.levels: IGCSE Core and Extended · Pearson Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The most requested subject in the community and the one where the gap type matters most. A student losing method marks needs script marking, which is cheap and fast. A student missing two years of algebraic fluency needs teaching, which is not. A marked script separates the two in twenty minutes.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Calculus, algebra and proof, with an optional-topic paper at Higher Level. The expensive version of this purchase is a weekly lesson for two years. The efficient version is a specialist for a defined block on the specific paper where marks are lost, plus a protected independent window the rest of the time.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and calculator technique. What is usually being bought here is the interpretation sentence rather than the mathematics, and that is a short, teachable skill. Families who buy general tuition in this subject frequently pay for content the student already has.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE Core and Extended
subjects.description: Mechanics, electricity, waves and, at Higher Level, fields and quantum topics. Experimental-design questions are the reliable loss and the cheapest to fix, because they are a small, well-defined set of question types. Formula provision differs between Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE Core and Extended
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms. Mole arithmetic is rehearsal, not teaching, and paying a specialist rate for rehearsal is poor value. Paying a specialist for mechanism work and internally assessed investigation design is good value.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE Core and Extended
subjects.description: Physiology, genetics, ecology and data analysis, with the heaviest command-term load of the sciences. Most of what families buy here is command-term technique, which transfers across the whole subject and often across other subjects as well, making it one of the better-value purchases available.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.levels: IB Language A HL and SL · IGCSE First Language
subjects.description: Analysis, comparative writing, the individual oral and the higher level essay. The purchase that works is marked written work with feedback on structure and argument. The purchase that does not is content coverage, because the student has usually read the texts and cannot yet write about them under time.

subjects.name: Economics and Business
subjects.levels: IGCSE 0455 and 0450 · IB HL and SL
subjects.description: Markets, macroeconomics, marketing, operations and finance, assessed largely through essays and case studies. Diagram accuracy, application to an unfamiliar business and the evaluation paragraph are the three things worth paying for, and all three are short blocks rather than year-long arrangements.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Mandatory in UAE private schools whatever the licensed curriculum. The spending pattern here is backwards in most households: it gets the smallest budget and the worst slot, and it appears on the report every term. Short frequent sessions cost less per week than one long one and work better.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Points that are cheap to earn relative to lifting a Higher Level grade, and almost always under-bought. A small number of well-timed sessions on reading a prescribed title and structuring an argument around knowledge claims competes well with any other use of the same money.

subjects.name: Standardised tests
subjects.description: Separable from the school course and measurable, which makes them the easiest purchase to judge. The Ministry of Education's American-track equivalency requirements include specified minimum scores, so for some families this is a requirement rather than an enhancement.

sections.heading: Three different gaps, three different prices
paragraphs: Before any rate is discussed, work out which gap you have. They present identically — a mark lower than expected — and they cost very different amounts to close, so buying the wrong remedy is the main way money is wasted in this market. A marked script with the teacher's annotations still on it tells you which in about twenty minutes.

A technique gap shows as marks lost in the writing rather than the knowing. Working not shown, so method marks go. An 'explain' answered as a 'describe'. Units omitted, axes mislabelled, an answer abandoned because the timing collapsed. The student knows the material and cannot convert it. This is the cheapest gap to close, because the fix is behavioural and transfers across every topic at once.

A content gap shows as blank or badly wrong answers in specific topics, consistently. Something was taught while the student was absent, or taught in a different school, or taught and never understood. This is the expensive gap: content has to be taught and then practised, and across a two-year syllabus that is a term or more of sessions. There is no shortcut and anyone selling one is selling something else.

A habit gap shows as a student who understands everything in a lesson and cannot reproduce it a fortnight later. Nothing is wrong with the teaching or the technique. The independent hours are not happening, so nothing consolidates. This gap is cheap to diagnose, cheap to fix structurally and almost impossible to fix by buying more teaching, which is why a household that responds to it with three weekly lessons gets poorer value than one that responds with a protected window and a fortnightly review.

sections.heading: Six provider models compared on more than rate
paragraphs: Comparing tutors by hourly rate is like comparing cars by fuel capacity. The rate is one variable among several that determine what a household actually receives, and the others are rarely published. The table below compares models rather than brands, with every quoted rate attributed to the provider that published it and dated.

The variables that matter beyond rate are these. Whether marking of work set between sessions is included. Whether a replacement is offered if the match is wrong, and how quickly. Whether a trial exists and what condition attaches to it. Whether the person teaching holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit. And whether delivery is actually what was implied — several providers in this market route UAE enquiries to numbers outside the country without saying so.

On the permit specifically: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories from registered school teachers to university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing with a two-working-day completion time. Because it is free and quick, a provider who cannot answer the question has told you something.

We have not put an IB Gram rate in the table, and that is deliberate rather than evasive. Publishing a single hourly figure would be less useful than telling you what sits inside the hour, which varies by level and format. Ask for the trial and the consultation and you will get both numbers and inclusions in writing before anything is booked.

sections.heading: The extras that quietly change the real hourly figure
paragraphs: A quoted rate is a headline, and the number a household actually pays per hour of teaching is often different. None of the items below is dishonest in itself; they become a problem only when they are not disclosed, and in this market they frequently are not. Ask about each one in writing before a first session and the comparison between providers becomes real.

The commonest adjustment is marking. If work is set between sessions and marked in the next session, that is teaching time consumed by administration, which effectively raises the price of the teaching. If marking is billed separately, the headline rate understates the cost. If no work is set between sessions at all, the rate is lower and so is the value, because consolidation is the point.

The second is session length versus the hour. A rate quoted per session where sessions run fifty minutes is a higher hourly rate than it appears. The third is cancellation policy, which determines what a missed session costs and in a household with travel can be a meaningful annual figure. The fourth is exam-term repricing, where demand peaks and some providers raise rates or restrict availability exactly when a family needs it.

Then there are the smaller items that add up: materials fees, platform fees, charges for written reports, minimum terms that prevent stopping after a poor match, and package structures that expire unused sessions. The table sets out what to ask about each. A provider who answers all of them in writing is usually a safe choice; one who treats the questions as unreasonable has answered them differently.

sections.heading: How many hours does a result actually take?
paragraphs: Nobody can honestly promise a grade, and anybody who does is telling you something about themselves rather than about your child. What can be said, with ranges rather than certainties, is roughly how many hours different goals have taken for students in similar positions, and what else has to be true for the hours to work. That is the information families in this community actually want and nobody publishes.

The ranges below assume a student who attends, does the work set between sessions, and has a protected independent window. Remove any of those three and the hours stop predicting anything, which is the honest reason tutoring sometimes fails. The variable that most changes the number is not the tutor's quality but whether the independent work happens.

Read the right-hand column as carefully as the hours column. It names the condition that has to hold, and in several rows that condition is the whole intervention. A student whose problem is timing does not need more content hours; they need timed practice and somebody marking it. A student who will not open a book between lessons needs a structure, and buying them a third weekly session is the most expensive way to discover that.

The last row is the one most worth reading. Some targets are not reachable in the time remaining, and the honest response is to revise the target or the plan rather than to sell more hours into it. We will say that when the evidence says it, because the alternative is a household spending a term on the lowest-return hour in its week.

sections.heading: Tutoring set against the cost of the school year
paragraphs: The comparison most households make is between one tutor's rate and another's. The more useful comparison is between a year of tutoring and a year of school fees, because that is the proportion that tells you whether a purchase is sensible. School fees are the dominant educational cost in every household in this community, and tutoring at one session a week in one subject typically sits at a small fraction of them.

That framing changes two decisions. First, it makes a steady year-long arrangement look more reasonable than it does in isolation, and a crisis block in the spring look worse: the same money spread across the year buys more hours and far more improvement. Second, it stops a household treating tutoring as an emergency expense, which is the mindset that produces the three-lessons-a-week panic in March.

It also raises a question worth asking directly. If a school's fees are substantial and a child still needs tutoring in a core subject across two years, that is information about the fit between the child and the provision, and it belongs in a conversation with the school rather than being quietly solved with money. Schools in this corridor generally respond well to specific, evidenced questions from parents.

Abu Dhabi's regulator, the Department of Education and Knowledge, supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes inspection outcomes, and fee arrangements for private schools sit within the regulator's remit rather than being set freely. For current fee rules and for any school's published inspection outcome, go to ADEK's own channels rather than to a tutoring website, including this one.

sections.heading: If the budget is one hour a week, which subject gets it?
paragraphs: This is the most common real question in Khalifa City and it has a clear answer, which is not the one most families reach. The hour should go to the subject where a grade change alters a decision, not to the subject with the lowest mark. Those are frequently different subjects, and the difference is worth a great deal.

Work through it in order. First, which grades are load-bearing: a sixth-form entry requirement, a university offer condition, a subject that must be passed for a progression rule. Second, within those, where is the gap closest to closeable — a technique gap in a load-bearing subject beats a content gap in one, because the same hours buy more. Third, only then consider how uncomfortable the mark looks.

A worked example. A Year 11 student has a 4 in a subject they will drop at sixteen and a 6 in a subject where the sixth form requires a 7. The 4 is the uncomfortable number and the 6 is the one that decides the next two years. The hour belongs to the second subject, and explaining that to a teenager is part of the job.

There is one exception worth naming. Where a subject is at risk of failing in a way that affects progression or an equivalency requirement, it takes priority regardless of comfort, because a failure has consequences that a middling grade does not. On the British track, Ministry of Education equivalency requires five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five, so the count is worth checking before any subject is written off.

sections.heading: The cheap end: what it can do and what it cannot
paragraphs: Published budget rates in this market run from AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik listing AED 45-65 and Tutopiya AED 33-52. Those are real prices for real teaching and they are the right purchase for some jobs. Pretending otherwise would be dishonest, and most providers at the specialist end do pretend otherwise.

What the cheap end does well: routine homework support in lower secondary, keeping a younger student moving through set work, conversational language practice, and basic rehearsal where the task is repetition rather than instruction. For a Year 7 student who needs somebody to sit with them while they finish the week's mathematics, a budget rate is appropriate and a specialist rate is waste.

What it generally does not do: mark written work against a board mark scheme with the authority of someone who knows how marks are awarded, diagnose a gap from a script, supervise an internally assessed component within the honesty rules, or prepare a Higher Level candidate for a paper the tutor has never taught. At this end the hour is usually teaching time alone, with no marking between sessions, and marking is the mechanism that makes consolidation visible.

One thing applies at every price point. Anyone providing private tutoring in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free and valid for two years, and individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here. Ask the question at every band; a low rate is not a reason for the answer to be vague.
