sections.heading: Where the marks sit in a Diploma science, component by component
paragraphs: Parents are often surprised by how much of a science grade is not an examination. In the current Biology, Chemistry and Physics guides the two written papers carry 36% and 44%, and the scientific investigation carries 20%. That last fifth is marked by the teacher against published criteria and then moderated by the IB. It is the only part of the grade that is banked long before the examination, and it is the only part a student can improve with certainty, because the deadline is months away and the criteria are published.

That changes where tutoring money should go. A student twelve months out from the papers who is averaging a 4 has two levers: raise the examined performance, which is slow and uncertain, or secure the investigation properly, which is fast and controllable. Most families reach for the first and ignore the second. The investigation is the better buy, and it is the component a one-to-one hour is best suited to, because it is a single piece of work with four named criteria and a draft on the screen.

The table below sets out the components for the subjects we are asked for most from Masdar City. Weightings change when a subject guide is rewritten, so each row carries the status we are confident about, and the Environmental Systems and Societies row is deliberately marked for confirmation: that course was rewritten for first assessment in 2026 and Higher Level is new, so publishing a percentage for it without reading the current guide would be guessing. Your school's subject guide, or the IB coordinator, is the place to settle every figure here before you plan around it.

One further point about Paper 3 in mathematics. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level carries a third paper worth 20%, built from two extended problems that develop an unfamiliar idea over several parts. It is unlike anything in the rest of the course, and because it sits at the end of the examination schedule it is routinely the least practised component in the whole Diploma. If your child is on AA HL, that paper is worth a block of sessions on its own.

sections.heading: Environmental Systems and Societies, the course this address asks for by name
paragraphs: Environmental Systems and Societies is the only Diploma course that can satisfy either the individual-and-societies requirement or the sciences requirement, which makes it structurally useful to a student who wants a sixth subject without a third science. It is also the course Masdar City families raise more often than any other, for obvious reasons: the development exists as a low-carbon experiment, the International Renewable Energy Agency has its headquarters here, and children who grow up surrounded by that work tend to want to study it.

It has a reputation among students for being gentle, and that reputation is wrong. The examined papers reward precise systems vocabulary — flows, stores, feedback, resilience, carrying capacity — used correctly about a named case study, and they punish fluent generalities about the environment harder than almost any other course. The evaluation questions ask for a judgement supported by evidence, and most of the marks lost are lost by students who assert a position and then describe rather than weigh. It is a language-dense subject disguised as a science.

The course was rewritten for first assessment in 2026 and Higher Level became available, so anything written about it before that date should be treated as out of date, including component weightings. We say so explicitly rather than publishing a number we have not read in the current guide. What has not changed is the shape of the internal assessment: an individual investigation on a question the student frames themselves, which is where the same problems appear as in the other sciences — a research question with no measurable variable, insufficient data, and an evaluation that lists limitations without explaining their effect.

The supply point is sharper here than anywhere. A student sitting Environmental Systems and Societies at Higher Level in Abu Dhabi may be one of a handful in the emirate. There is no realistic prospect of finding somebody nearby who has taught that specific component, and a generalist science tutor will coach it as though it were Biology, which is how students end up writing beautifully about ecosystems and scoring in the middle band. Subject matching across a wide pool is not a convenience for this course; it is the only way it gets covered at all.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The scientific investigation in the current Biology, Chemistry and Physics guides is marked out of twenty-four against four criteria, each worth six marks: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Those four letters are the whole of the mark scheme, and reading them with your child is the single highest-return hour available to a Diploma science family. Most students have never read them. They have been told to do an investigation and have inferred the requirements from a classmate's.

Each criterion fails in a predictable way. Research design loses marks when the research question names no measurable dependent variable, or when the method would not actually produce data capable of answering it. Data analysis loses marks when raw data is processed without uncertainties, when graphs lack error bars that the data supports, or when the processing is correct but undocumented. Conclusion loses marks when the student states a result without comparing it to accepted scientific context. Evaluation loses marks almost universally, because students list limitations as a shopping list instead of explaining how each one would have shifted the result and in which direction.

A tutor is useful here in a very specific way: reading the student's own draft against those four descriptors and saying which band it currently sits in and why. That is feedback on work the student has produced. It is not authorship, and the distinction matters more on this component than anywhere else in the Diploma, because the investigation is submitted with a declaration that it is the student's own work. We return comments, questions and criterion references. We do not supply text, data, graphs or paragraphs for submission.

The table below is the version we hand to families at the start of a coursework block. Mark allocations are stated as we understand the current guide; confirm them against your school's copy, because the science guides were rewritten recently and a school may still be running a cohort under an older specification.

sections.heading: IGCSE science routes, and why the code on the entry form decides everything
paragraphs: Before Year 10 ends, somebody at your child's school has made three decisions that will shape the IGCSE science result: which board, which award, and which tier. None of them is usually explained to parents in those terms. Cambridge Physics is 0625 and Pearson International GCSE Physics is 4PH1; they are different courses with different papers and different practical arrangements. Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 is a double award covering all three sciences in one; Combined Science 0653 is a single award covering less. And in several Cambridge subjects the entry is tiered, so a Core entry caps the available grade while Extended runs the full range.

Those distinctions decide which past papers are worth doing, which is the whole of a revision plan. A student working through Pearson 4CH1 papers for a Cambridge 0620 examination is practising a different question style, a different mark-scheme convention and in places different content. We see this every year, usually because a family bought a revision guide by subject name rather than by code. The fix costs nothing: read the code off the statement of entry, write it on the front of the folder, and buy nothing that does not match it.

The practical question matters too. Cambridge offers both a practical test and an alternative-to-practical written paper, and most international centres use the alternative. That paper tests whether a student can read a method, identify a control, spot a source of error and draw a table — written skills about practical work rather than practical skills themselves. It is highly teachable in a one-to-one hour over video, which is worth knowing for any parent who assumes a laboratory subject cannot be supported remotely.

The table sets out the routes we meet most often from this part of Abu Dhabi, with the codes next to them. Confirm each one against the board's current syllabus page, because codes and paper structures are revised on their own cycles.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs around Masdar City, in AED, with the source of each figure
paragraphs: Most pages competing for this search publish no price at all, and the few that do quote United States dollars, which is not the currency an Abu Dhabi family transacts in. So here are the market bands in dirhams, with the provider or source that published each one. These are market rates read in October 2026. They are not an IB Gram price list: our own arrangement starts with a free consultation and a trial session, and the figure that applies to your child depends on the subject, the level and how scarce the specialist is.

Read the table with two things in mind. The first is that the in-home band is higher than the online band for the same tutor quality, and the gap is travel. A tutor driving to Masdar City from the island or from Khalifa City is spending forty to eighty minutes on the road for a sixty-minute lesson, and somebody pays for that time. The second is that the top of the range is a scarcity premium, not a quality premium. A Higher Level Environmental Systems and Societies specialist costs more than a Mathematics Standard Level tutor because there are very few of them, not because the hour is better taught.

A third figure worth holding next to these: Dubai's regulator confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package. School fees are the dominant number in a family's education budget, and tutoring is usually a tenth of it or less. Setting the two side by side is a more honest way to decide what to spend than looking at an hourly rate in isolation.

On value: the cheapest effective purchase for a Diploma science student is almost never a standing weekly subscription from September. It is a short, dense block on the investigation, timed to the school's internal deadline, followed by nothing until the mock results arrive. Buy the component that is banked and controllable before you buy general revision.

sections.heading: A tutor driving to Masdar City against one-to-one online
paragraphs: This is the comparison the search term implies, so it deserves a straight answer rather than a sales line. A home tutor in the UAE is a real market with real prices, and for some families in some districts it is the right arrangement. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE — those are a service we run only in India — so what follows is a comparison of two models rather than a pitch, and you should weigh it against your own address and your child's subject.

The arithmetic from Masdar City is unusually one-sided, for a geographic reason rather than an ideological one. The development sits near the airport road with Khalifa City, the island and the Mohammed Bin Zayed corridor all a meaningful drive away. A tutor travelling in for a sixty-minute lesson commits two to three hours to that lesson, which has three consequences: the rate carries the travel, the number of evenings a week they can offer collapses, and the pool of people willing to make the trip shrinks to those who happen to live close. For a Standard Level maths student that pool may be adequate. For Higher Level Physics, Design Technology or Environmental Systems and Societies it is not.

Online delivery changes two variables and leaves the rest alone. The lesson is still sixty minutes of one-to-one teaching on the student's own work. What changes is that the specialist can be anywhere, and that nobody spends an hour in a car. What is genuinely lost is the physical presence of an adult in the room, which matters for younger children and for students who need somebody to notice them drifting. We say that plainly rather than pretending the formats are identical.

There is also a practical point about laboratory subjects, because it is the objection we hear most. Almost none of the assessed practical skill in IGCSE or Diploma science is manual. It is method design, variable control, uncertainty handling, data processing, graph work and evaluation — all of it done on paper, all of it reviewable on a shared screen with the student's own data in front of both people. The hands-on work belongs to the school laboratory, and it stays there.

sections.heading: The coursework year, counted backwards from the school's internal deadline
paragraphs: The dates that decide a Diploma grade are mostly not the examination dates. They are the school's internal deadlines for the investigation, the exploration, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge components, and they sit months earlier. Schools publish them, usually in a document handed out once in DP1 and then never referred to again. Finding it and putting the dates on a wall calendar in September is worth more than any amount of revision advice.

We have to be careful about examination dates themselves. The IB blocks automated access to its own site, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly, and we will not publish one. What we can say is that UAE schools overwhelmingly sit the May session, and that the date your child needs is the one their IB coordinator gives them. Cambridge and Pearson dates are a different matter: both boards publish them, and they are worth reading because they show how far ahead the real deadlines sit.

Cambridge's March 2027 series is the clearest worked example available. The examination period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027. Final entries are due 27 November 2026 — more than two months before the first paper. Forecast grades are due 27 February 2027, results reach centres on Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. Pearson's International GCSE runs May/June and November series; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and the board states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. That is not a detail: it is a single administrative error that costs a whole subject. Ask the examinations officer at your child's school which zone the centre sits in, and work from that timetable only.

sections.heading: Academic honesty on a scientific investigation, stated plainly
paragraphs: The Diploma asks a student to sign that internally assessed work is their own. A tutor who crosses that line puts the student at risk of a malpractice finding, which can cost the diploma, and the tutor is not the person who pays. So the boundary has to be stated before any coursework block starts, not discovered halfway through it.

What a tutor may do is teach and give feedback. That means explaining a concept the student has not understood, teaching uncertainty handling or graph conventions as skills, reading the published criteria with the student, reading what the student has produced and saying which band it sits in and why, asking the questions a good supervisor would ask, and teaching the student how to find and cite a source. All of that is ordinary teaching, and it is what moves marks.

What a tutor must not do is become the author. No text for submission. No data. No graphs produced for the student to paste in. No restructuring of a report so thoroughly that the voice is no longer the student's. No supplying a research question and method ready-made. If a tutor offers any of that, the correct response is to end the arrangement, because the offer tells you what else they are prepared to do. The essay mills competing for these searches sell completed internal assessments outright; that is a malpractice trigger dressed up as a service.

There is one more boundary worth naming, because it is specific to this region. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the national private-tuition permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Treat that as press-reported and verify it against the current ADEK policy before relying on the exact wording. The practical consequence for a Masdar City parent is simple: do not try to hire your child's own subject teacher privately, however convenient it looks.

sections.heading: Starting from Masdar City, including what we say when nobody is free
paragraphs: The first conversation is a consultation, not a sales call, and it is free. We ask for the subject, the level, the board and syllabus code where there is one, the school's internal deadlines, and the most recent piece of marked work. That last item is the important one. A returned script with a teacher's annotations on it tells us more in five minutes than a parent's account of the problem can in half an hour, because it shows where marks actually left the page rather than where the student felt uncertain.

Then we match on subject and level. For common combinations — IGCSE Mathematics Extended, Diploma Biology Standard Level, English — that usually happens within a few days. For the scarce ones it can take longer, and sometimes it does not happen at all this term. Environmental Systems and Societies at Higher Level, Design Technology, Film, Music and the less common language options are the names that come up. When we cannot cover something, we say so on the call rather than offering a generalist and hoping. A Biology tutor coaching an ESS investigation produces a competent piece of work that misses the criteria the course actually marks.

Where a UAE-based specialist is not available, the fallback we offer is a specialist from the wider pool, delivering the same one-to-one online lesson from a different time zone. That is disclosed before anything is booked, including what it means for scheduling, because a 19:00 slot in Abu Dhabi is a different hour elsewhere and the arrangement only works if both sides can hold it reliably. Families who would rather wait for a UAE-based match are told how long that is likely to be.

Two practical notes for this address. Keep the slot after half past five if your child travels to Khalifa City or the island, because a four o'clock session with a student who has been awake since half past five produces very little. And if the request concerns an investigation or an exploration, start the block eight weeks before the school's deadline rather than two; the difference between those two timings is the difference between improving a draft and rescuing one.

process.title: Send the last marked script
process.description: Before anything is booked, send the most recent returned paper or coursework draft with the teacher's comments on it, plus the syllabus code if you have it. This is the diagnostic. It shows which component is losing marks and whether the problem is content, technique or timing, which decides what the first sessions should contain.

process.title: A free consultation with the subject in front of us
process.description: A short call to confirm the board, the level, the school's internal deadlines and what the family actually wants from the term. We say at this point whether we can cover the subject at that level, and if we cannot, we say so rather than offering a near miss.

process.title: A trial session on real work
process.description: The first session runs on the student's own script or draft rather than on a placement test. At the end you get a written note naming what was covered, what the student should practise and what the tutor thinks the realistic target is for the term. If the match is wrong, say so and we change it.

process.title: A term-length pattern with a stop date
process.description: Agree a slot, a frequency and an end point, then review at the halfway mark against something measurable: a timed paper, a criterion band, a mock. The review can end the arrangement, and sometimes should. A pattern that drifts on without a review is how families overspend on tutoring.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the component, not the subject name
whyPoints.description: An enquiry about Physics is really an enquiry about Paper 2 extended response, or about uncertainty handling in the investigation, or about Paper 3 technique. We match on the part of the course that is losing marks, which is why the first thing we ask for is a marked script rather than a report card.

whyPoints.title: Geography stops limiting the match
whyPoints.description: Masdar City is a small residential population inside a large emirate, and the number of people nearby who have taught Higher Level Environmental Systems and Societies is effectively zero. Delivering online means the filter is the subject and the level rather than the drive, which is the only way scarce courses get covered.

whyPoints.title: Every figure carries its source
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page name the provider or source that published them and the month they were read. We do not publish a satisfaction percentage, a student count or a star rating, because we cannot show you the data behind one. If a tutoring page quotes a statistic with no n and no date, treat it as marketing.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line is written down before you book
whyPoints.description: Feedback on the student's own work, criterion references, questions a supervisor would ask. No text, data or graphs supplied for submission, and no syllabus documents or mark schemes sent to you. The boundary is in the arrangement from the start, because it protects the diploma your child is working towards.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed, not concealed
whyPoints.description: When no specialist is free for a scarce subject this term, we say so on the first call and explain the alternative, including what a different time zone means for a weekly slot. Several pages competing for this search route UAE families to an overseas number without mentioning it. We would rather lose the enquiry than hide the arrangement.

faqs.question: Are there any private schools inside Masdar City itself?
faqs.answer: Masdar City is built as a research, business and free-zone district with residential buildings attached, and it does not contain a large private school campus of the kind families here need for IB or IGCSE. In practice children travel out: most commonly to Khalifa City, with others going to Al Raha, Mohammed Bin Zayed City, Al Reef or across to the island. That is why the tutoring question at this address is usually about the evening rather than about the school. Check current provision against ADEK's own published school directory, since the emirate adds campuses regularly.

faqs.question: Which IB and IGCSE schools do Masdar City children usually attend?
faqs.answer: The nearest concentration is in Khalifa City and along the airport corridor, where both the IB continuum and the English National Curriculum route to IGCSE are available. Families from this development are also enrolled in Al Raha, on Saadiyat and on Al Reem Island. We name schools on this page as context for the student's ecosystem only; no relationship with any school or group is implied. The practical question for a tutoring plan is not which school but what time the bus returns, because that decides whether a five o'clock or a six o'clock slot is realistic.

faqs.question: Can a Masdar City student get a tutor for Environmental Systems and Societies?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and we will tell you honestly before you book. Environmental Systems and Societies is a small-entry course, it was rewritten for first assessment in 2026, and Higher Level is new, so the number of people who have taught the current specification is genuinely small. Matching across a wide pool rather than a local one is what makes coverage possible at all. If no specialist is free in a given term we say so on the first call rather than offering a Biology tutor to coach it, because a generalist will coach it as a science and miss the criteria that actually carry marks.

faqs.question: How much should a Masdar City family expect to pay for Diploma science tutoring?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150-300 an hour and an IB or IGCSE specialist at AED 200-450 or more, with in-home one-to-one running AED 180-500 because travel sits inside the rate. Those are figures other providers published, not ours. A Higher Level specialist costs more largely because the pool is small. Our own arrangement starts with a free consultation and a trial session, and what applies to your child depends on the subject, the level and how scarce that specialism is.

faqs.question: Do tutors come to apartments in Masdar City?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not run in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For a Masdar City family every lesson is delivered online, one to one, over live video, with the student's own script or draft on a shared screen. The in-home market does exist here and publishes rates of roughly AED 180-500 an hour, and for some families in some districts that is the right choice. From this address the drive is long enough that a visiting tutor commits two to three hours to a sixty-minute lesson, which is why the comparison usually settles the way it does.

faqs.question: What is the collaborative sciences project, and can a tutor help with it?
faqs.answer: It replaced the Group 4 project in the 2023 science guides. Every Diploma science student takes part, it asks around ten hours, and it is not separately marked, which is exactly why it gets dropped by a tired student in a busy term. A tutor can help the student plan their contribution, understand what the school expects and manage the time, but the work itself is collaborative and belongs to the group. Because it carries no marks of its own, a missing project becomes a programme compliance problem rather than a grade problem, and those are harder to fix late.

faqs.question: My child has no usable data for the scientific investigation. Is it too late?
faqs.answer: It depends on how far the school's internal deadline is away, and that is the first thing to establish. With eight weeks there is time to reframe the research question so that the data already collected can answer it, or to design a smaller second run that is actually completable. With two weeks the honest work is salvaging the analysis, conclusion and evaluation criteria from what exists, which is still twelve of the twenty-four marks. What a tutor cannot do is supply data or produce the write-up. Bring the current draft and the criteria to the first session.

faqs.question: How many hours does a Diploma science subject usually need?
faqs.answer: There is no single answer, but a useful planning frame is this: a weekly sixty-minute session through DP2 is roughly thirty hours, and a coursework block on the investigation is four to eight sessions timed to the school deadline. Students who are losing marks to technique rather than knowledge often need less than their parents expect, and a short block followed by a review beats a standing commitment from September. Agree a stop date and a halfway review against something measurable, such as a timed paper or a criterion band, so the arrangement does not drift.

faqs.question: Khalifa University is in Masdar City. Does that change our subject choices?
faqs.answer: Only in the sense that the destination's own published requirements should drive the decision, and having a university nearby makes those easy to read. Whether a student needs Mathematics Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, and at which level, is settled on the admissions page of the actual course they want, not on a general rule. We will not tell you what any university requires, because requirements change and because tutoring is not a route into admission. Read the university's own page, then choose, then plan the support around that choice.

faqs.question: How do I find out which exam board my child's IGCSE science is on?
faqs.answer: Read the statement of entry, which the school issues for each series, and write the code down. Cambridge codes look like 0625, 0620 and 0654; Pearson International GCSE codes look like 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1. If the statement has not been issued yet, ask the examinations officer rather than the subject teacher, since entries are an examinations-office function. The code decides which past papers are worth doing and which revision material is relevant, so buying anything before you have it is a gamble on a coin toss.

faqs.question: Can lessons start after the Khalifa City school bus gets back to Masdar City?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most families at this address that is the only pattern that works. A child who boards a bus before seven in the morning is not usefully teachable at four in the afternoon. The slots that hold through a whole term from Masdar City tend to start between half past five and seven, with a later start in DP2 where activity blocks run after the final bell. Pick the slot you can defend every week for a term rather than the earliest one that is technically free, because consistency does more than frequency.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring actually work for laboratory subjects?
faqs.answer: For the assessed skills, yes. Almost nothing that earns marks in IGCSE or Diploma science is manual dexterity. The marks go to method design, variable control, uncertainty handling, data processing, graph conventions, conclusions supported by accepted values and evaluation that explains effect. All of that is paper work, and all of it is reviewable on a shared screen with the student's own data visible to both people. Cambridge's alternative-to-practical paper, used by most international centres, tests exactly those written skills. The hands-on laboratory work belongs to the school, and it stays there.

faqs.question: What does ADEK actually do about my child's school in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes inspection outcomes, according to the UAE government's own information portal. In practice that means it decides whether a school may operate, inspects it, and publishes a judgement you can read before you choose a tutor. An inspection band describes a whole school, not your child's set in one subject, so a strong overall judgement tells you very little about whether Higher Level Chemistry is well covered in that building. Read the subject-level commentary inside the report instead.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor covers the subject my Masdar City child needs?
faqs.answer: We tell you on the first call. For scarce courses — Environmental Systems and Societies at Higher Level, Design Technology, Film, some language options — a UAE-based specialist may not be free in a given term. The alternative we offer is a specialist from the wider pool delivering the same one-to-one online lesson from another time zone, disclosed before anything is booked, including what it means for holding a weekly slot. If you would rather wait for a UAE-based match, we tell you roughly how long that is likely to take. We do not substitute a generalist quietly.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Physics HL and Mathematics AA HL for a Masdar City student?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and it is worth asking, because the content overlap at Higher Level is real and a single tutor can save a scheduling slot. More often it is better to split them. Physics Higher Level and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level both have their own component technique — the extended-response style in one, Paper 3 in the other — and somebody who has taught both to the current specification is rarer than somebody who has taught either. We would rather put two specialists on the two subjects than one competent generalist on both.

abu-dhabi/masdar-city.closingHeading: Start with the marked script, not the subject name
abu-dhabi/masdar-city.closingBody: If you are in Masdar City and weighing up support for a Diploma or IGCSE student, the useful first step costs nothing: find the most recent returned paper or coursework draft, find the syllabus code, and find the school's internal deadline for the investigation or exploration. Send those three things and we will tell you what the problem actually is, whether we can cover it at the level your child is working at, and what a term of work should realistically achieve. Lessons are delivered online, one to one, over live video. If we cannot cover the subject, we will say so on the call.

abu-dhabi/mohammed-bin-zayed-city.tutorsIntro: Tutors matched to MBZ City households are chosen for paper technique as much as for subject knowledge: the ability to mark a student's answer against a published scheme, explain why a correct method scored four out of six, and build the habit that stops it happening again.

intro.heading: The teaching is fine. The paper is where the marks go
paragraphs: Mohammed Bin Zayed City is a planned mainland district south of the island, laid out in numbered zones of villas and apartment blocks between Mussafah and the Abu Dhabi to Dubai road. It is one of the largest residential areas in the emirate by population, it has schools inside it rather than around it, and those schools serve very large cohorts across British, Indian and other curricula. Abu Dhabi's private schools are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes its own inspection outcomes.

The pattern we see from this district is consistent and quite specific. Families are not describing a school that has failed to teach the content. They are describing a student who understands the material, works reasonably hard, and comes out of every assessment three or four marks below where the family expected. Sometimes that happens across several subjects at once, which is the clue: when a student loses marks in physics, chemistry and biology simultaneously, the problem is almost never the physics.

What is actually happening is that examinations test two different things. One is whether you know the subject, which the school teaches well. The other is whether you can convert what you know into marks inside a mark scheme and a time limit, which is a separate set of skills, and those skills are extremely difficult to teach to thirty students at once. A teacher can explain a command term to a class; they cannot sit with each student while they rewrite four answers until the register matches the question. There is no criticism of the school in that. It is arithmetic.

The skills in question are unglamorous and short in number: reading the command term before the content, working to the clock rather than to completeness, reading a mark scheme to see where marks are allocated, setting out a calculation so method marks survive a wrong answer, drawing a graph that earns the scale and plotting marks, checking units, and planning a long answer before writing it. Each one is learnable in a small number of hours. Together they are worth a grade or more across a set of papers, and almost nobody in this market sells them as the thing being bought.

What follows is built on that. Which skills are taught in class and which have to be rehearsed alone. What entry structure and resit options your child's board actually offers, because that changes the recovery plan entirely. How the Cambridge science practical component works and what the written alternative really asks for. How to use past papers properly rather than as a comfort activity. What an inspection report does and does not tell a parent. What tutoring costs on the mainland. And what the Ministry of Education's equivalency rules require, including the detail one ranking competitor gets wrong.
bullets: Losing marks in three sciences at once is a paper-technique problem
The practical component is 20% of a Cambridge IGCSE science grade

abu-dhabi/mohammed-bin-zayed-city.programmesIntro: MBZ City schools cover several systems, and the entry structure of each one decides what a recovery plan can look like. These four matter most for families here.

programmes.name: IGCSE at Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel
programmes.description: Cambridge splits most subjects into Core and Extended and assesses the sciences through a multiple choice paper worth 30%, theory papers worth 50% and a practical component worth 20%. Pearson Edexcel tiers mathematics as Foundation and Higher and assesses practical skills inside its written papers rather than in a separate component. Both are end-of-course qualifications, so a resit means re-sitting the subject rather than a unit.
programmes.countryNote: In a large MBZ City cohort, a student can go through two years without ever having a single answer marked individually against the published scheme. That is the gap one-to-one work fills here: not content delivery, which the school does at scale, but the marking conversation that a class of thirty makes impossible.

programmes.name: A Level and International A Level
programmes.description: Pearson's International A Level is unitised: units are sat across different series and an individual unit can be re-sat, with the better result counting. Cambridge International AS and A Level allows a staged entry where AS is sat separately and carried forward. That structural difference is the single most useful thing a sixth-form parent can understand, because it determines whether one bad paper is a setback or a disaster.
programmes.countryNote: Ask the sixth form which specification it enters, because the two routes behave differently under pressure. A student on a unitised route who had a bad January has a repair option. A student on a fully terminal route has one attempt per series, which changes how early a tutoring plan needs to start.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, usually three Higher and three Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internal assessment carries 20% in the sciences and both mathematics courses. A Standard Level subject is built around 150 guided hours and a Higher Level subject around 240. The Diploma is terminal at the end of two years, with internal assessments completed along the way.
programmes.countryNote: For an MBZ City family weighing the Diploma against A Level, the practical difference is breadth against repairability. The Diploma covers more and commits earlier; the unitised International A Level route forgives a bad paper more readily. Neither is better in the abstract; it depends on the student and on what the next step requires.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four published criteria, each marked out of eight and converted to a grade from 1 to 7. There is no paper technique to learn in the examined sense, which makes this the one stage where the gap described on this page does not apply. The equivalent gap is criterion literacy: a student who never reads the descriptors sits in the middle bands regardless of knowledge.
programmes.countryNote: A Middle Years student heading for an examined course at sixteen has a predictable adjustment ahead, because nothing in criterion-based assessment rehearses working to a clock against a mark scheme. The summer before that transition is the cheapest time to build the habit, and it is almost always skipped.

abu-dhabi/mohammed-bin-zayed-city.subjectsIntro: These notes name the specific marking behaviour that costs marks in each subject, rather than describing the course. That is the level at which a single weekly hour can change an outcome.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: Most lost marks here are method marks, not answers. A student who writes only the final figure loses everything when the arithmetic slips, while a student who sets out each stage keeps most of the question. Extended candidates also sit a non-calculator paper, which punishes anyone who routes every calculation through a device.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Pearson Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.description: Two papers with a calculator permitted in both, tiered Foundation and Higher. The recurring loss is in multi-step structured questions where the student answers the first part correctly and abandons the rest. Reading the whole question before starting is worth more in this specification than any additional content.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: The multiple choice paper carries 30%, theory 50% and the practical component 20%. Electricity and circuits decide more grades than any other topic. The most common avoidable loss is a formula rearranged in the head rather than on paper, which removes the method marks a wrong number would otherwise have kept.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Mole calculations, concentration and yield separate Extended from Core, and the marks are procedural: units, significant figures and the final rounding. The practical component, whether sat as a test or as the written alternative, is 20% of the grade and is routinely the least prepared part of the course.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: Decided by command terms more than by content. A student who answers every question as describe caps well below their understanding, because explain and evaluate questions carry marks for reasoning that a description cannot earn. Correcting this habit is a matter of hours and shows up across the whole paper.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Sciences
subjects.description: Two grades or one covering all three sciences, common where a timetable must stay broad. The content is wide and shallow, so the main risk is a student revising it as three separate subjects and running short. One plan across the whole paper, with the practical component included, is usually enough.

subjects.name: English as a first language
subjects.description: Directed writing and the analysis of unseen passages. The marks that go missing are structural: an answer that discusses the whole passage rather than answering the question asked, or a directed writing task that ignores the specified audience and form. Both are fixable with marked timed attempts.

subjects.name: English as a second language
subjects.description: A separate specification from first language English, with its own papers and purpose. Reading comprehension technique, particularly the questions requiring a specific number of details, is where most marks are lost. Frequent short practice outperforms long sessions in this subject consistently.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Highly procedural and therefore highly recoverable. Diagrams must be labelled on both axes, and a question asking for a justified recommendation earns nothing for a list of advantages and disadvantages. A student who learns the answer shapes gains quickly here, often more quickly than in any other subject on their timetable.

subjects.name: Mathematics and sciences at Diploma level
subjects.description: The internal assessment carries 20% in each, which makes it the highest-value single component to support. The usual loss is in evaluation: limitations listed rather than weighed for direction and size of effect. Higher Level mathematics adds a third paper worth 20% that rewards sustained reasoning across a long unfamiliar problem.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.description: Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies form the federal baseline that private schools must deliver whatever curriculum they are licensed for. The mandatory stream and any examined IGCSE qualification in Arabic are different things, and support must work from the school's own material rather than a parallel course.

abu-dhabi/mohammed-bin-zayed-city.regionsIntro: MBZ City sits in the middle of Abu Dhabi's mainland residential belt. These notes are about what each neighbouring district means for a school run and an evening study slot.

regions.name: Mussafah
regions.note: Immediately west, largely industrial with residential pockets, and the district most MBZ City routes pass through. Traffic here at the start and end of the working day is the main variable in a school bus arrival time, which is why measured arrival times beat estimated ones.

regions.name: Shabiya
regions.note: The adjacent residential zones built on a similar grid, with their own schools and a very similar household profile. Families here and in MBZ City face the same question about large cohorts and individual attention, and reach the same answers about what to buy.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: North-east towards the airport, with a concentration of larger international campuses. A number of MBZ City families travel in this direction, which produces longer bus runs and pushes a realistic weekday session past five o'clock.

regions.name: Shakhbout City
regions.note: Directly adjacent, sharing several school routes and bus services. Children from both districts frequently attend the same campuses, which makes shared sibling and paired arrangements workable where the board and tier match exactly.

regions.name: Al Shamkha
regions.note: South-east along the mainland, a growing residential district with newer school provision. The run between here and MBZ City is straightforward outside peak hours and long enough during them to matter for session planning.

regions.name: Baniyas
regions.note: East on the mainland, long-established, with its own schools serving several curricula. Bus routes from this direction into the MBZ City schools are among the longer ones, with correspondingly earlier pickups.

regions.name: Al Reef and Al Falah
regions.note: Towards the airport road, villa communities with their own campuses nearby. Families here share the mainland pattern: schools with large year groups, strong content delivery and limited scope for individual marking conversations.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi island
regions.note: Across the bridges, where the older established schools and the premium island campuses sit. An MBZ City child attending an island school has the longest commute in this set, which generally rules out any weekday session before half past five.

schoolClusters.city: Schools inside Mohammed Bin Zayed City
schoolClusters.note: Campuses within the district itself, serving large cohorts across British, Indian and other curricula. Short bus runs and early arrivals home, which gives families here a wider choice of session times than most Abu Dhabi districts.

sections.heading: Which skills a class of thirty cannot rehearse one at a time
paragraphs: Start with the diagnosis, because buying the wrong thing is the usual mistake. A student who is losing marks because content was never understood needs teaching. A student who is losing marks while understanding the content needs something quite different, and the two are easy to confuse from a school report that says only that a grade is below target. The quickest test is a pattern check: a student weak in one subject probably has a content problem in that subject, and a student losing three or four marks per paper across several subjects almost certainly has a technique problem that is costing them everywhere.

The table below separates the skills that decide marks into those a school teaches well at scale and those that need a one-to-one marking conversation. The distinction is not about teacher quality. Explaining to a class what the command term evaluate requires is straightforward and every good teacher does it. Sitting with one student while they rewrite four answers until the register actually matches the question, three times, across a term, is not something a timetable with thirty students per class and a specification to finish can accommodate.

This is also why these skills are so often missing in students who look conscientious. A student who revises diligently is practising content, which is the part that was already fine. Nothing in their routine forces them to confront the fact that their correct physics is earning four marks out of six because the working is in their head. They are not being lazy; they are practising the wrong thing, and nobody has shown them the mark scheme that would make it obvious.

sections.heading: Entry structure and resit options: what your child's board allows
paragraphs: Before any tutoring plan is made, it is worth knowing what recovery is structurally available, because that determines how urgent the work is. Parents often assume a bad paper can be retaken in isolation, and sometimes it can. At International A Level, Pearson's specifications are unitised: units are sat across different series and an individual unit can be re-sat, with the better outcome counting. Cambridge International AS and A Level allows a staged entry in which AS is sat separately and carried forward. Those two structures make a bad paper survivable.

At IGCSE level, both main boards are essentially end-of-course. A resit means re-sitting the subject in a later series rather than repairing one unit, and the availability of more than one series a year is what creates the options instead. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, with a March series as well, and Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSEs are available in May or June and in November each year, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series.

The practical instruction for an MBZ City parent is to ask the school three questions in writing: which specification is my child entered for, in which series, and what resit routes exist for it. The answers change the plan completely. A Year 11 student on a terminal IGCSE route with one series available is in a different position from a sixth former on a unitised route with a January option. The table below sets out the structures. It also carries a warning worth repeating: every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone version was used.

sections.heading: The science practical component, and what the written alternative asks
paragraphs: A fifth of a Cambridge IGCSE science grade sits in a component most families never discuss. In physics, chemistry and biology the multiple choice paper carries 30%, the theory papers 50%, and the practical component 20%. Schools choose between entering students for a practical test or for the written alternative to practical, and the choice is usually made for the whole cohort on the basis of laboratory capacity rather than per student. Confirm which one applies with the school, and confirm it against the current syllabus, because specifications are revised.

The written alternative is widely misunderstood as an easier option. It is not a theory paper. It asks a student to work on experiments they have not performed: to complete a results table, plot a graph from supplied data, identify a source of error in a described method, suggest an improvement, read a measuring instrument from a diagram, or draw a conclusion that the data actually supports. Those are practical skills assessed in writing, and a student who has done laboratory work without ever being asked to write about it in that register will lose marks on a paper that looks deceptively familiar.

The preparation is specific and it is almost never done at home, because it does not look like revision. Plotting graphs to scale by hand, with axes chosen so the points fill the grid, is a markable skill with marks attached to the scale and to the plotting accuracy. Reading a scale off a drawn instrument is a markable skill. Writing an error source that names the measurement and its direction, rather than saying human error, is a markable skill. Each takes a handful of practised attempts and each is worth marks on every paper in the component, which makes this the highest-return twenty per cent available in the sciences.

sections.heading: Past papers: the unsupervised skill, used properly
paragraphs: Every family in this district knows past papers matter, and most use them in a way that produces very little. The common pattern is to work through a paper with the answers available, check each question as it goes, feel reassured by the ones that were right, and move on. That is a comfort activity. It rehearses content the student already has and tells them nothing about where the marks are actually going.

The version that works has four parts and is slightly unpleasant, which is why it is rare. First, the paper is attempted in one sitting under the real time limit with no interruptions and no textbook. Second, it is marked against the official mark scheme rather than against a model answer, because the mark scheme shows where each mark sits and a model answer does not. Third, every lost mark is categorised rather than corrected: was it not known, misread, mistimed, or known but badly expressed. Fourth, the categories are counted, and the biggest category becomes the next fortnight's work.

The categorisation is the part that cannot be skipped and is the part a student will not do alone. It takes a conversation, because a student will almost always classify a lost mark as not known when it was actually known and badly expressed, which sends them back to revising content that was never the problem. Doing this properly for two papers per subject usually produces a list of six to ten recurring errors, and most of them take an hour each to fix. One more constraint worth respecting: do not publish or circulate board papers and mark schemes outside their official source. They belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, and the right behaviour is to use the official site and link to it.

sections.heading: What an inspection report tells an MBZ City parent, and what it does not
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi's private schools are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes inspection outcomes. Parents here read those outcomes carefully and often draw more from them than the document actually supports, which is worth unpicking, because the inference people make is usually about their own child rather than about the school.

An inspection report is a judgement about a school as an institution: the quality of teaching across a sample of lessons, the progress of groups of students, leadership, safeguarding, provision for students with additional needs, and the school's own capacity to improve. It is a genuinely useful document and it is the best independent information a parent has. What it is not is a prediction about one student in one subject. A strong overall outcome is compatible with a weak department, an unstaffed subject in one particular year, or a cohort in which your child's set is the fourth of four.

So the useful move is to read the report and then ask the questions it cannot answer. Which board and tier is my child entered for in each subject, and on what evidence. Who teaches that subject in that set, and has that been stable this year. What were the cohort's outcomes in that specific subject last series, rather than overall. What intervention or clinic provision exists, and when. Those four questions take one meeting and tell a parent more about their own child's prospects than any published rating can. sections.heading: What tutoring costs on the Abu Dhabi mainland
paragraphs: Published rate information in this market is poor. Of the competitor pages reviewed for this project in October 2026, several published no price at all, and two quoted in US dollars rather than in the currency a UAE family transacts in. The table below gives the market bands in AED, what each band buys in practice, and the source of each figure, taken from published platform and agency rate pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. These are market rates rather than an IB Gram price list, and nothing on this page is a quote.

A note specific to the mainland. In-home rates include the tutor's travel, and the travel component is larger here than on the island, because an in-home tutor crossing the bridges or coming out through Mussafah at the end of the working day spends a substantial part of the booked hour in a car. That is priced in or the booking is declined, which narrows the field of people available to those with gaps in their diary rather than specialists with full ones. For technique work, where the tutor needs to know the exact specification and mark scheme, that trade-off matters.

What to ask before paying anything, including us. Is the quoted figure per hour or per session, and how long is a session. Does it include VAT, and will it appear on the invoice. What happens to a prepaid balance if you stop after one lesson. And specifically for technique work: will my child's own written answers be marked against the official mark scheme in front of them, or will the session be spent on explanation. The last question separates the format described on this page from general homework support that happens to cost the same.

sections.heading: Equivalency: five subjects, and the detail a ranking page gets wrong
paragraphs: Ministry of Education equivalency is the process by which a foreign secondary qualification is recognised for use in the UAE, and for a family in this district it matters if a child may apply to a UAE university or continue their education here. It is a Ministry process. No tutoring provider performs it, speeds it up or guarantees it, and nobody should suggest that tutoring is required in order to obtain it, which would be a false claim about a regulatory process.

The British-track requirements, as reported in July 2026, are precise. A student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects. One competitor currently ranking for these searches states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the reported requirement, and inheriting that error would be an expensive thing for a family to do.

On the American track, English proficiency is shown by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB Diploma, this page publishes no points threshold, because no figure could be verified against the Ministry's own pages during research for this project, and an unsourced number on a page like this one is a liability rather than a service. Check moe.gov.ae or the relevant attestation authority directly, and keep original certificates rather than photographs.

sections.heading: Why these searches say home tutor, and what is delivered
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default expectation in much of this district, and the reason is sound. A student who is losing marks through habit rather than ignorance needs somebody who will sit there and make them redo the answer, and physical presence is the most obvious way to achieve that. In a household where a parent works long hours, a tutor in the room is also supervision, which is a separate service from teaching and a genuinely valuable one.

The market position is straightforward. Published in-home rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with the tutor's travel inside the fee, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online and AED 200 to 450 for a specialist. On the mainland the travel component is substantial, and the people who accept those bookings tend to be those with diary gaps rather than specialists in a named board and tier. For technique work specifically, the specification knowledge is the thing being bought, because marking an answer against the wrong board's scheme is worse than not marking it at all.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and nobody will be sent to a Mohammed Bin Zayed City address. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, with screen sharing so the student's own scanned or photographed answer and the official mark scheme can be read side by side, which is in fact easier on a shared screen than on a kitchen table. For the supervision problem, the format carries its own answer: the student attempts the paper before the session, so the session cannot happen unless the work was done.

sections.heading: Starting from Mohammed Bin Zayed City, with the limits stated
paragraphs: Begin with a diagnosis rather than a booking. Send the school, the board and syllabus code, the tier or level, and if possible a photograph of one marked piece of work with the marks visible. That last item is worth more than a paragraph of description, because it usually shows within a minute whether the marks were lost on content or on expression, and those two problems need different tutors and different formats. We then name who would teach it, where they are based and what they have taught at that exact level, before any payment.

Ask the school two things before paying anybody. What clinic, surgery or intervention provision already exists in that subject, because it is frequently free and staffed by the teacher who marks the work, and it is routinely under-used because it is not advertised. And which board, series and tier your child is entered for, in writing, because every plan on this page depends on that answer and a surprising number of families do not have it.

The limits. Coverage is uneven in narrow Higher Level subjects, in less common languages and in uncommon Pearson Edexcel options, and the honest answer is a different hour with the right specialist, an adjacent level or board where the overlap is genuine, or a plain statement that we cannot cover it. On assessed work, an internal assessment or Extended Essay must be the student's own work, authenticated by a school supervisor; a tutor reads the criteria with the student, reads their draft and comments on it in writing, and authors nothing. We do not distribute board syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes, because those belong to the boards. Data collected through this site is handled under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 and can be deleted on request.

process.title: Send one piece of marked work
process.description: A photograph of a marked paper or assessment, with the marks visible, usually settles the diagnosis in under a minute: whether marks were lost because content was missing or because known content was badly expressed. Those two problems need different formats, and buying the wrong one is the most common waste in this market.

process.title: Get the board, series and tier in writing
process.description: Ask the school which specification your child is entered for, in which series, and at which tier. Every plan on this page depends on that answer, and a surprising number of families do not have it. It also tells you what resit routes exist, which decides how urgent the work actually is.

process.title: Ask what the school already runs free
process.description: Clinics, subject surgeries and intervention sessions exist in many MBZ City schools, cost nothing and are staffed by the teacher who will mark the coursework. They are under-used because nobody markets them. Establish what is available at no cost before paying for anything, this service included.

process.title: The attempt happens before the session
process.description: For technique work the student sits the questions in advance, timed and closed-book, and brings the attempt. Without that there is nothing to mark and the hour collapses into explanation. This is stated up front because it is a real requirement on the student, not a preference, and it is what makes the format work.

process.title: Count the error categories and decide
process.description: After two marked papers per subject the lost marks sort into categories: not known, misread, mistimed, or known and badly expressed. The biggest category sets the next fortnight's work, and at the end of a term there is a decision rather than a drift: continue, switch focus, change tutor, or stop because the technique is now in place.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before format
whyPoints.description: A student losing marks in three sciences at once does not have three content problems. We ask for one piece of marked work first and say which of the two problems you actually have, because selling weekly content teaching to a student who already knows the content is the easiest money in this market and the least useful thing to buy.

whyPoints.title: Marking against the official scheme, not a model answer
whyPoints.description: A mark scheme shows where each mark sits; a model answer shows what a good answer looks like. Only the first explains why correct physics earned four out of six. Sessions here are built on the student's own written answer and the official scheme read side by side, which is the whole method rather than a feature of it.

whyPoints.title: The practical twenty per cent taken seriously
whyPoints.description: A fifth of a Cambridge IGCSE science grade sits in the practical component, and the written alternative is a skills paper rather than a theory paper. Graph scales, instrument readings and named error sources are markable skills that take a handful of practised attempts, and almost nobody prepares them.

whyPoints.title: Structure explained before urgency is assumed
whyPoints.description: Whether a bad paper can be repaired depends on the specification. A unitised International A Level route allows a unit resit; a terminal IGCSE entry does not. We explain what recovery exists before recommending how much to buy, because urgency created by a provider is not the same as urgency that exists.

whyPoints.title: Sourced figures and stated limits
whyPoints.description: AED bands on this page are market rates with their publishers named, not our prices. The equivalency requirements are quoted from the reported source with the error a ranking competitor makes identified. And where we cannot cover a subject at the hour you need, you get a plain no rather than a generalist described as a specialist.

faqs.question: My child understands the subject but keeps losing marks. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly paper technique rather than content, and the pattern gives it away: a student weak in one subject usually has a content gap there, while a student losing three or four marks per paper across several subjects has a habit that costs them everywhere. The usual culprits are answering without reading the command term, keeping working in their head so method marks are lost with a slipped number, and running out of time by answering completely rather than to the mark allocation. Each is fixable in hours rather than terms.

faqs.question: Does a big school cohort actually disadvantage my child?
faqs.answer: Not for content delivery, which large well-organised cohorts handle efficiently, and MBZ City schools generally do this well. It disadvantages one specific thing: the individual marking conversation. Explaining a command term to a class is straightforward; sitting with one student while they rewrite four answers until the register matches the question, repeatedly across a term, is not something a full timetable can accommodate. That is the gap one-to-one work fills here, and it is a scheduling limit rather than a criticism of anyone.

faqs.question: How should past papers be used to actually gain marks?
faqs.answer: Four steps, and the third is the one everybody skips. Sit the paper in one go under the real time limit with no textbook. Mark it against the official mark scheme rather than a model answer, because only the scheme shows where each mark sits. Categorise every lost mark as not known, misread, mistimed, or known and badly expressed. Then count the categories and let the biggest one set the next fortnight's work. Working through a paper with the answers open is a comfort activity that rehearses content the student already had.

faqs.question: What is the alternative to practical paper, and is it easier?
faqs.answer: It is a practical skills paper written on experiments the student has not performed, and it is not easier, only different. It asks for completed results tables, graphs plotted to scale with the axes chosen sensibly, instrument readings taken from diagrams, named error sources with a direction of effect rather than human error, and conclusions the supplied data actually supports. In Cambridge IGCSE physics, chemistry and biology the practical component is 20% of the grade. Confirm with the school which route your child is entered for and check it against the current syllabus.

faqs.question: How much of a Cambridge IGCSE science grade comes from each paper?
faqs.answer: In the main Cambridge IGCSE sciences the multiple choice paper carries 30%, the theory papers 50%, and the practical component, whether sat as a laboratory test or as the written alternative, carries 20%. That distribution is worth knowing because families often concentrate entirely on theory content, which is half the grade, while the two components that make up the other half, multiple choice technique and practical skills, get almost no dedicated preparation. Both are highly trainable. Confirm the current structure with the school, since specifications are revised.

faqs.question: Can my child resit just one bad paper?
faqs.answer: It depends on the qualification. At International A Level, Pearson's specifications are unitised, so an individual unit can be re-sat across a later series with the better outcome counting, and Cambridge International AS and A Level allows AS to be sat separately and carried forward. At IGCSE level both main boards are end-of-course, so a resit means re-sitting the whole subject in a later series. Cambridge offers June, November and a March series; Pearson Edexcel offers May or June and November. Ask the school which specification and series apply.

faqs.question: What does an ADEK inspection outcome tell me about my own child?
faqs.answer: Less than most parents assume, though it is still the best independent information available. Abu Dhabi's private schools are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, and a published outcome judges the institution: teaching across a sample of lessons, progress of groups, leadership, safeguarding and provision. It cannot tell you who teaches your child's set, which set they are in, or how that specific subject performed last series. Read the report, then ask the school those four questions in a single meeting.

faqs.question: What does tutoring cost on the Abu Dhabi mainland?
faqs.answer: Published market bands, surveyed in October 2026, run from AED 45 to 150 an hour for a generalist, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit with travel inside the fee, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB or IGCSE specialist. Named or examiner-branded tutors are quoted from AED 500 to 650 and above. Those come from published platform and agency rate pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, and they are market rates rather than our price list.

faqs.question: Can a tutor visit our villa in Mohammed Bin Zayed City?
faqs.answer: Not through us. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India, and nobody will be sent to an MBZ City address. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. For the work described on this page that is genuinely the better format, because the student's own answer and the official mark scheme can be read side by side on a shared screen, which is more practical than passing one printed copy across a table.

faqs.question: A tutoring site says six IGCSEs are needed for equivalency. Is that right?
faqs.answer: Five, according to the requirement reported in July 2026: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among them, plus either one accredited Advanced Level subject at grade E or better or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One competitor ranking for these searches states six subjects are required, which does not match the reported rule. Equivalency is a Ministry process that no tutoring provider performs, so verify the current requirement on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for help with a Diploma internal assessment?
faqs.answer: It is usually the highest-value single component to support, because the internal assessment carries 20% of the subject grade in the sciences and in both mathematics courses and runs over months with very little supervision between the school's own internal deadlines. The legitimate work is substantial: reading the published criteria line by line, planning dated checkpoints backwards from the deadline, commenting in writing on a draft the student produced, and checking statistical treatment and notation. The student is the author of every word, and that boundary does not move.

faqs.question: Does the person tutoring my child need a permit in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring across the UAE operates under a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with MoHRE's own service page quoting a two working day completion time and listing no fee. Eligibility covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Separately, ADEK has set professional-ethics rules reported to prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school; verify that with the school directly.

faqs.question: Should we start technique work in Year 10 or wait for Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10, if the pattern is already visible. Technique is a habit rather than a topic, and habits take a term to establish and then cost nothing to maintain, whereas the same work attempted in the spring of Year 11 competes with revision for the same hours. The practical argument is also structural: IGCSE entries are end-of-course and a resit means re-sitting the whole subject, so there is no unit-level repair available. Earlier is cheaper here in a way it is not in a unitised sixth-form specification.

faqs.question: What if you cannot cover the subject we need?
faqs.answer: You get told in the first reply. Coverage in narrow Higher Level subjects, in less common languages and in uncommon Pearson Edexcel options is genuinely uneven across this market, and the usual response is to put a generalist in front of a student and call it coverage. We will give whichever of three answers is true: a different hour of the week where the right specialist is free, an adjacent level or board where the overlap is real and the gap can be named, or a plain statement that we cannot do it with a suggestion of where to look next.

abu-dhabi/mohammed-bin-zayed-city.closingBody: The fastest way to a useful answer from here is a photograph of one marked piece of work with the marks visible, plus the school, the board, the syllabus code and the tier. That usually shows within a minute whether your child has a content problem or a technique problem, which decides what is worth buying and what is not. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video, with the student's own answer and the official mark scheme read side by side. If the answer is that the school's own free clinic would fix it, that is what you will hear.

abu-dhabi/mussafah.tutorsIntro: Mussafah requests cluster in the late-afternoon and evening slots, and in two subject groups: IGCSE maths and the sciences where a tier or a grade is at stake, and Diploma subjects where coursework is overdue.
