intro.heading: The slot is harder than the tutor
paragraphs: Mussafah is a working district. The industrial sectors, the residential Shabiya blocks and the Gardens all sit south of the island, and the roads out of here carry freight as well as families. That shapes an afternoon in a way no tutoring website usually mentions: a school bus leaving a campus at half past two with a long stop sequence does not deliver a child home at three. It delivers them somewhere between five and half past, hungry, hot and finished with thinking for the day.

Most tutoring arrangements in this district fail for that reason and not for any academic one. A parent books a four o'clock slot in September because that is when school ends on paper. The first two lessons are missed or cut short. By week five the arrangement is being rescheduled weekly, the tutor has lost the rhythm, and everybody concludes the tutoring is not working. The teaching was never the problem. The timetable was.

The fix is unglamorous: establish the real arrival time before booking anything, and then set the slot after it with a margin. For a household in the Shabiya sectors travelling to the island, that usually means six o'clock rather than four, and half past six in heavy term weeks. For a family using a Mohammed Bin Zayed City campus it can be five. For anyone on a bus with a multi-stop route, add half an hour to whatever the school's own timetable implies. The number is worth asking for directly rather than estimating, because a parent who collects by car and a parent whose child is the last stop on a bus route are describing two different afternoons even when they live on the same street and use the same campus every single day.

A second factor sits on top of the first. The evening in a Mussafah household is not empty before the lesson; it contains food, prayer, homework set by the school and often the mandatory Arabic or Islamic studies work, and in many homes two or three children competing for the same quiet corner. A lesson placed badly displaces something else, and the thing displaced is usually sleep, which costs more marks in May than any tutor can recover.

All of this is easier because the lessons are online. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE - that is an India-only service - so no tutor is sitting in the same traffic your child is. A slot can be moved, shortened or split in two without re-planning a driving route, which for a district with this road profile is the practical difference between an arrangement that survives a term and one that quietly stops in October.

abu-dhabi/mussafah.programmesIntro: Three stages account for nearly all the enquiries from Mussafah. What matters for each one in this district is how much concentrated time it needs and when that time can realistically exist.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Eight to ten subjects, with maths and the sciences tiered on Cambridge specifications. The work that moves grades is timed paper practice, which needs a clear ninety minutes rather than a tired twenty. For a student arriving home at five thirty, that argues for a weekend block alongside the midweek hour rather than against the midweek hour.
programmes.countryNote: Entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers, which matters for planning around a long commute because the decisions cannot be deferred. Cambridge sets final entries for its March 2027 series at 27 November 2026, with examinations running 3 February to 4 March 2027. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative timetable zones and warns that candidates who use the wrong zone timetable and miss an examination carry that risk themselves.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. The internal assessments carry roughly a fifth to a quarter of most subject grades and are written at home, in exactly the evening hours this district has least of. Coursework supervision here is usually booked as ninety-minute sessions at a weekend.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools enter the May session, so the autumn of Year 13 carries internal assessment drafts, the Extended Essay and predicted grades at once. A student with a long daily commute should be finishing coursework before February rather than inside the mock and exam window. Confirm each IB date with the school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org rather than with any date printed on a tutoring site.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria per subject, each out of eight. Younger students in this district arrive home least able to concentrate, which is why two short sessions a week beat one long one at this stage. Spaced practice also retains better, so the format that fits the commute happens to be the format that works.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Mussafah family moves between an MYP school and a GCSE school the content overlaps and the reporting does not. One marked task, read against the descriptors in plain language and rewritten to the next band, changes how a student reads every future brief. That is a two-session job and it fits into forty-five minutes twice rather than needing a long block.

abu-dhabi/mussafah.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Mussafah households ask about most, with the component that costs marks named. Where a subject needs sustained concentration it is flagged, because in this district that affects when it can be taught.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Extended sits on Papers 2 and 4, Core on Papers 1 and 3, and practice does not cross between them. The long structured questions on Paper 4 need a clear stretch of time to practise properly, so they belong in a weekend session rather than a tired weekday one.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1
subjects.description: Structured differently from Cambridge, with its own paper pattern and formula provision. Students moved between schools mid-course sometimes find themselves practising the wrong board's papers for a term, which is why the syllabus code matters more than the subject name.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Electricity, moments and momentum take most of the marks lost. The alternative-to-practical paper rewards a student who has learned to criticise someone else's method, which is a teachable habit rather than a content gap.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Mole calculations and the qualitative analysis tables separate the middle from the top. The ion tests learned as a memorised list collapse under pressure; learned as chemistry they survive, and that distinction is most of the tutoring.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: A long syllabus with precise examinable detail. Good for short sessions, because topics are discrete: a focused forty-five minutes on transport in plants is a complete piece of work in a way that a maths paper is not.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Justification carries the marks. Proof, the harder calculus and Paper 3 at Higher Level all need written reasoning rather than answers. Paper 3 in particular is an extended investigation and needs a ninety-minute slot to practise honestly.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Uncertainty handling separates the top grades, in Paper 2 and again in the internal assessment. Fields and circuits are where the quantitative work hardens, and where a student who memorised definitions instead of relationships stops being able to progress.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics carry the heaviest Higher Level load. The internal assessment is a full scientific report with its own criteria and is the component most often left too late in a household with little spare evening.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language and First Language English
subjects.description: Two courses that look similar and grade differently, with consequences for later university language conditions. Reading inference under time pressure is the part that needs practice, and it practises well in short bursts.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first language and as an additional language
subjects.description: Two separate courses with different starting points, assessed in Standard Arabic. Written register and grammar are the recurring gaps, and both respond well to short frequent sessions rather than long occasional ones.

sections.heading: The commute arithmetic, sector by sector
paragraphs: A parent in Mussafah asking when lessons can start deserves a number rather than a reassurance. The numbers below come from how families in each part of the district actually describe their afternoons, and they are deliberately conservative, because a slot that works on a good day and fails on a normal one is not a slot.

Three factors drive the variation. The first is direction: north across the bridges to the island is the hardest run, while a local journey within Mohammed Bin Zayed City is the easiest. The second is whether the child travels by car or by school bus, because a bus with a multi-stop route adds twenty to forty minutes that no map will show. The third is the freight traffic that shares these roads, which does not keep school hours and makes the afternoon less predictable than the morning.

Having the real number changes the booking. A family that establishes an arrival time of 17:30 books an 18:30 slot and keeps it for a year. A family that assumes 15:30 books 16:00 and spends October renegotiating. The second family concludes that tutoring does not suit their child; in fact their child never attended a full lesson.

The last column of the table is the one to act on. It is not the earliest slot that is theoretically possible but the earliest that survives a full term, including the weeks with a traffic incident on the bridge and the weeks with an extra activity after school.

sections.heading: Why a four o'clock lesson fails here and a six o'clock one works
paragraphs: The four o'clock failure is not only about arrival. Even when a child is home by half past three, the first forty minutes after a long hot journey are worthless for anything demanding. They need food and a pause. A lesson that starts inside that window spends its first fifteen minutes getting a student present and its last fifteen with a student who has been concentrating since seven in the morning.

Six o'clock, or thereabouts, catches a different state. The student has eaten, the body has cooled, the day's homework is either done or visible, and the specific question they wanted to ask has surfaced. Tutors consistently report that the same student covers more in an evening hour than in a late-afternoon one, and in this district the gap is wide enough to be worth organising the household around.

There is an upper limit. Past about half past eight the trade starts going the other way, particularly for students below Year 10, because sleep lost in term time shows up in the examination hall. A reasonable rule for a Mussafah family is to place the lesson in the window between an hour after arrival and two hours before the student's normal bedtime, and to shorten rather than postpone when the day has already been long.

Where that window is genuinely too narrow - three children, one connection, two activities - the answer is usually to move the demanding work to the weekend and keep the weekday session short and specific. Forty-five minutes on one topic, with practice set for the following day, is a real piece of teaching. A ninety-minute slot nobody can attend is not.

sections.heading: What 45, 60, 90 or 120 minutes actually buys
paragraphs: Session length is treated as an afterthought in most tutoring arrangements and it should not be. Different work needs different amounts of unbroken time, and matching the two is most of the reason one arrangement produces marks and another produces attendance.

A single past-paper section with marking and discussion does not fit in forty-five minutes. One discrete biology topic does, comfortably, and fits better there than it would stretched across an hour. A coursework draft reviewed properly needs ninety minutes because the first twenty go on reading it. A complete paper sat and marked in the same sitting needs two hours and is worth doing two or three times before a series, not weekly.

The hourly band does not change much with length. Published market rates for a qualified subject tutor working online sit roughly between AED 150 and 300 an hour, and for an IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist between AED 200 and 450 and above. What changes is how much of the hour is productive. A tutor travelling to a home often imposes a two-hour minimum precisely because the travel has to be amortised, which is one of the reasons the in-home bands published by Bestimate sit at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500.

For a Mussafah household the practical consequence is freedom. Because nothing depends on a drive, a term can run as two short sessions in winter when evenings are tight and one long weekend block in the spring when papers need sitting, without renegotiating anything. sections.heading: The school year, Ramadan, and when revision really happens
paragraphs: Revision does not happen evenly across a year, and a tutoring plan that pretends otherwise wastes hours in September and runs out of them in April. The UAE academic year has its own shape, and the month of Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, so its position relative to mock season and the examination series changes annually.

During Ramadan school hours are reduced across the Emirates and household routines move later. For tutoring the practical answer is to agree the replacement timing before the month begins rather than improvising inside it. Many families here prefer sessions after Iftar, often shorter and more frequent than their usual arrangement, and some pause entirely for the first week and resume. Both are reasonable; what does not work is leaving the question open and losing four weeks to rescheduling.

The examination calendar is fixed and published, which makes it the spine of any plan. Cambridge runs June and November series with a March series for some specifications, and for the March 2027 series final entries close on 27 November 2026, examinations run from 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades are due on 27 February 2027 and results reach centres on Direct on 13 May 2027 with certificates in late June. Pearson Edexcel's International GCSE November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and its June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day.

IB dates are not stated here. Abu Dhabi schools sit the May session, which is safe to say; the specific windows and results dates were not confirmed from the IB's own site for this page, so confirm them with your school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org. A provider quoting an IB date without naming a source is guessing, and a guess that moves a revision plan by a fortnight does more harm than no date at all.

sections.heading: Sequencing two or three children through one evening
paragraphs: Plenty of households in this district have more than one child needing help, and the constraint is rarely tutor availability. It is rooms, devices and bandwidth. Two live video lessons running at once in a two-bedroom apartment is difficult; three is not realistic. So the planning question is sequence rather than simultaneity.

The arrangement that works most often is back-to-back rather than parallel. Two consecutive hours on one evening, with two different specialists, keeps the rest of the week clear and means the household only has to be quiet once. A younger child takes the earlier slot while concentration is still available, and the exam-year student takes the later one, when the house has settled and they are at their most alert anyway.

Where three children need support, the honest answer is usually to stagger across two evenings and to accept that one of them gets a shorter session. Alternatively, and often better value, the youngest gets twice-weekly forty-five-minute sessions in earlier slots that nobody else wants, which costs the same per hour and suits that age group better than a long block.

One sibling can share a tutor where the subject, the board and the stage genuinely match, which does happen with brothers a year apart in Cambridge IGCSE maths. It should not be arranged for coursework. An internal assessment is individual work with an individual research question, and two siblings supervised together in the same session is a route to submissions that resemble each other, which is an academic-honesty problem rather than a saving.

sections.heading: What an online lesson needs from a Mussafah apartment
paragraphs: Since every lesson here runs over live video, it is worth being specific about the setup, because the difference between a good and a bad hour is often technical rather than pedagogical. The requirements are modest and all of them are worth sorting out before the trial lesson rather than during it.

A laptop or a tablet rather than a phone, because the student needs to see a worked solution appear and a phone screen cannot show a page of working. A wired connection where one exists, or a position close to the router where it does not. Headphones, which matter more in a shared apartment than anywhere else, both for concentration and so the rest of the household is not listening to quadratics. And pen and paper in view of the camera, or a second device propped to show the page, because in maths and the sciences the student has to write.

A door that closes is the single biggest predictor of whether the hour is productive. Where no room is available, the next best arrangement is a fixed corner with the household's agreement that it is quiet for that hour, which in practice means telling the other children in advance rather than hoping. A television in the same room will beat any tutor.

Everything written during the session is annotated on screen and saved afterwards, so the student keeps the marked version rather than a memory of it. That matters more in a crowded home than in a quiet one, because the chances of a paper surviving the week on a kitchen table are low and the digital copy does not get lost.
bullets: A laptop or tablet, not a phone, so working can be seen as it is written

sections.heading: Where marks go when a student is tired
paragraphs: Fatigue has a signature in an examination script and it is not the same as not knowing the material. The first sign is unanswered questions at the end of the paper: twelve marks left blank because the pacing collapsed, which costs more than any single misunderstood topic. The second is arithmetic slips in questions where the method is plainly correct. The third is answers that address a related question rather than the one asked, because the command word was skimmed.

All three are common in students who travel a long way to school and study late, and all three are fixable without teaching any new content. Pacing is trained by sitting papers to time with a visible clock, which is uncomfortable and effective. Slips are reduced by a habit of checking the units and the magnitude rather than by working more carefully in general. Command-word errors disappear when a student is drilled to underline the instruction before reading the question body.

This is why a diagnostic matters more than a syllabus plan for a Mussafah student. A marked mock paper will show which of the three is happening, and the remedy for each is different. A family that assumes the problem is content buys twenty hours of teaching for a problem that four hours of technique work would have solved.

It is also why session placement is an academic decision rather than an administrative one. Practising pacing at seven in the evening after a two-hour journey trains a student to perform tired, which is realistic but demoralising. Doing it at ten on a weekend morning trains the skill properly, and the weekday hour then goes on teaching, which tolerates tiredness far better.
bullets: Unanswered final questions are a pacing failure, not a knowledge failure
Slips in correct methods are fixed by checking units and magnitude, not by trying harder
Command-word errors go away when the instruction is underlined first
Train pacing when the student is fresh; use the tired hour for teaching

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with coursework
paragraphs: Families under time pressure ask this question more often than families with spare evenings, which makes it worth stating plainly on a page about a district with a long commute. At least one site competing for these searches sells finished Internal Assessments outright. Submitting one is malpractice under IB rules, the consequence falls on the student rather than on the seller, and it can end a diploma.

The legitimate scope is wide. A tutor can teach the content the assessment rests on, explain each criterion and what its descriptors are actually asking for, challenge a research question that cannot be answered in the word count, read a draft the student has written and identify where the argument fails, and teach referencing properly. For a student with four usable evening hours a week, that targeted help is worth a great deal.

The line is text. Nothing composed by the tutor may appear in the submitted document - not a paragraph, not a rewritten conclusion, not a worked data analysis dropped into a results section. Heavy line-editing crosses the same line, because a sentence the tutor wrote is a sentence the student did not. Supervisors sign an authenticity declaration and similarity checking applies.

The sequence that fits a short evening is: agree the research question in one session, learn the report format in a second before writing anything, draft alone over two weekends, bring the draft for one ninety-minute review, then revise alone. That is roughly four hours of paid supervision across a term and it produces a better piece than ten hours of someone improving a draft, because the student has actually learned how the thing is built.
bullets: Allowed: teaching, criterion explanation, scoping, feedback on the student's own draft
Not allowed: any tutor-composed text reaching the submitted document
Heavy line-editing is the same breach in a politer form
Four hours of supervision across a term, properly sequenced, is usually enough

process.title: Tell us the real arrival time
process.description: Not when school finishes - when the child walks through the door, including the bus stop sequence. That one number decides the slot, and getting it right at the start is why some arrangements run for a year and others are being rescheduled weekly by October.

process.title: Choose a session length that matches the evening
process.description: Forty-five minutes twice a week, one hour, ninety minutes at a weekend, or a two-hour block in the final weeks. The hourly band is similar across all of them, so the choice is about what work needs doing and how much unbroken attention the student actually has.

process.title: Confirm the board, the code and the tier
process.description: Cambridge 0580 Extended and Pearson 4MA1 need different practice material, and a Core entry caps the grade. The school's entry confirmation settles it. Cambridge candidates should also ask the examinations officer which of the six timetable zones the centre sits in.

process.title: Settle the Ramadan arrangement in advance
process.description: Before the month starts, agree whether the slot moves to after Iftar, shortens, splits into two shorter sessions or pauses. Families who decide this in advance keep the arrangement; families who leave it open generally lose three or four weeks to rescheduling.

process.title: Trial lesson, then review after four sessions
process.description: One hour with the matched specialist, ending with a written view on whether the issue is content, technique or pacing. Four sessions later we check whether the slot is holding and whether the diagnosis was right, and change either if not.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling treated as part of the teaching
whyPoints.description: The slot is set against the household's real arrival time, with a margin, and reviewed when the term gets busy. In a district where buses run long routes and the bridges decide the afternoon, that is the difference between a term of lessons and a term of reschedules.

whyPoints.title: Length chosen by the work, not by convention
whyPoints.description: Forty-five minutes for a discrete topic, ninety for a paper section or a coursework draft, two hours to sit a full paper and mark it. Because no tutor is travelling, there is no minimum session length imposed to cover a drive.

whyPoints.title: Nobody is in the traffic
whyPoints.description: Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, so a missed Tuesday becomes a Thursday without re-planning a route, and a slot can move later during Ramadan by agreement rather than by negotiation with a driver's schedule.

whyPoints.title: Technique before content
whyPoints.description: A marked paper is read first, because unanswered final questions, arithmetic slips and command-word errors are different problems with different and much shorter fixes than a general course of teaching.

whyPoints.title: Dates from the boards themselves
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson deadlines and results dates on this page are attributed to their own published timetables. Where a date could not be verified from an official source, as with the IB sessions, it is omitted and you are pointed to the coordinator.

whyPoints.title: Clear limits on coursework
whyPoints.description: Teaching, criterion explanation and feedback on the student's own draft. No supplied text at any stage, and no heavy line-editing dressed up as proofreading, because the student signs the authenticity declaration and carries the consequence.

faqs.question: What time can lessons actually start for a family in Mussafah?
faqs.answer: It depends which part of the district you live in and which direction the school run goes. Households in the Shabiya sectors travelling north across the bridges are generally home between 17:00 and 17:45, so 18:00 is the earliest slot that survives a term and 18:30 is safer in busy weeks. Families in Mussafah Gardens using Mohammed Bin Zayed City campuses are often home by 16:30 and can hold a 17:00 start. Add half an hour to any estimate if the child travels on a bus with multiple stops.

faqs.question: Why did our last tutoring arrangement fall apart after a month?
faqs.answer: In this district the usual cause is the slot rather than the teaching. A four o'clock booking made in September assumes the child is home when school finishes, which the bus route makes untrue. Two sessions get cut short, the rest get rescheduled, the rhythm goes, and the family concludes tutoring does not suit their child. Establishing the real arrival time first and then adding a margin fixes it. The teaching rarely needed changing; the timetable always did.

faqs.question: Is a 45-minute session long enough to be worth paying for?
faqs.answer: For the right work, yes. One discrete topic - transport in plants, moments, solving a particular equation type - fits comfortably into forty-five minutes and sits better there than stretched across an hour. What does not fit is a past-paper section with marking and discussion, or a coursework draft review. Two short sessions a week also retain better than one long one through spaced practice, which makes the format the commute forces also the better format for Years 7 to 9.

faqs.question: Do you teach after Iftar during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families in this district prefer it. School hours are reduced across the Emirates during the month and household routines move later, so the usual arrangement shifts to after Iftar, often as shorter and more frequent sessions. The important part is agreeing the change before the month begins. Families who settle the new timing in advance keep their arrangement intact; those who leave it open tend to lose three or four weeks to rescheduling, which in an exam year is expensive.

faqs.question: Can two of my children have lessons at the same time in one apartment?
faqs.answer: It is possible but rarely advisable. Two live video lessons running simultaneously in a two-bedroom apartment compete for quiet space, devices and bandwidth, and three is not realistic. Back-to-back hours on the same evening work better: the household is quiet once, the younger child takes the earlier slot while concentration is still available, and the exam-year student takes the later one when they are most alert. Siblings may share a tutor only where the subject, board and stage genuinely match.

faqs.question: Does the freight traffic on the Mussafah roads really affect schooling?
faqs.answer: It affects the predictability of the afternoon, which is what matters for a weekly commitment. The roads out of the industrial sectors carry commercial traffic that does not keep school hours, so the same journey can vary by twenty minutes between days. That variance is why the recommendation here is always a slot with a margin rather than the earliest theoretically possible time. A lesson booked at the optimistic end gets missed often enough to break the arrangement.

faqs.question: Should my child do timed papers on a weekday evening or at the weekend?
faqs.answer: At the weekend, if the week includes a long commute. Practising pacing while exhausted trains a student to perform tired, which is realistic but demoralising and produces marks that understate them. A Saturday or Sunday morning paper, sat to time with a clock visible, trains the skill properly. The weekday hour then goes on teaching and review, which tolerates tiredness far better. Most exam-year students in this district end up on exactly that split.

faqs.question: Which board will my child be entered for, and does it matter?
faqs.answer: It matters more than the subject name. Cambridge IGCSE maths runs as 0580 or 0607 and tiers into Core and Extended on different papers; Pearson Edexcel runs 4MA1 with its own paper structure and formula provision. Practice material does not transfer between them, and a student who changed schools mid-course can spend a term drilling the wrong papers. The entry confirmation from school or the header of a past paper the student has sat will tell you which specification applies.

faqs.question: How many hours before an exam series does a student need?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families expect, if they are the right hours. A diagnostic paper marked against the official scheme usually shows that two or three specific causes account for most of the lost marks, and each has a short fix. Ten to fifteen well-targeted hours across a term, with the hard work moved to weekends, routinely does more than forty hours of general teaching. Anyone quoting a standard number of hours before seeing marked work is guessing at your child's problem.

faqs.question: What equipment do we need at home for lessons in Mussafah?
faqs.answer: A laptop or tablet rather than a phone, so the student can see working appear line by line. A position close to the router, or a wired connection if one exists. Headphones, which matter more in a shared apartment than anywhere else. Pen and paper in view of the camera, or a second device propped up to show the page, because maths and science require writing. And a door that closes, or at minimum an agreed quiet corner with the television off.

faqs.question: Do you cover Arabic for students at schools near Mussafah?
faqs.answer: Yes, both routes. Arabic as a first language is for Arab students and is assessed on grammar, classical and modern texts and formal written register in Standard Arabic. Arabic as an additional language starts from spoken competence. Private schools in the Emirates teach Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside whatever international curriculum they are licensed for, so these subjects appear on the report regardless of board. Short frequent sessions suit this work better than one long weekly block.

faqs.question: When do the exam entries for next year close?
faqs.answer: Much earlier than the papers, which catches families out annually. For the Cambridge March 2027 series, final entries close on 27 November 2026, examinations run from 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades are due on 27 February 2027 and results reach centres on Direct on 13 May 2027. Pearson's International GCSE November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Both boards publish their own timetables, and Cambridge warns that using the wrong zone version is the candidate's own risk.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my Year 13 finish an overdue internal assessment?
faqs.answer: A tutor can help the student finish it, which is a different thing. They can teach the content, explain the criteria, challenge a research question that is too broad, review a draft the student has written and point out where the argument fails. They cannot supply text that reaches the submitted document, and heavy line-editing is the same breach in a politer form. Where the deadline is close, the useful intervention is a ninety-minute review of what exists plus a realistic plan for the remaining weekends.

faqs.question: What do you actually send after each lesson?
faqs.answer: The annotated work from the session and a short note saying what was covered, what was marked and what to practise before next time. In a busy household the digital copy matters, because a paper sheet rarely survives a week on a kitchen table. What you will not get is a weekly percentage or a progress score, since a number invented by the person being paid is not evidence. The measures worth tracking are external: timed paper marks, criterion scores and mock results.

faqs.question: Will you come to our home if we pay the travel cost?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are not part of the UAE service at any price; they are offered only in India. The practical reasons are the ones this page is about. Travel narrows the pool of tutors to those willing to drive into this district on a weekday evening, which is the wrong constraint when the need is a specific subject specialist. It also sets a minimum session length to make the journey worthwhile, and it makes rescheduling a missed slot far harder than it needs to be.

abu-dhabi/mussafah.closingHeading: Start with the arrival time, then pick the tutor
abu-dhabi/mussafah.closingBody: For a Mussafah household the first question is not which subject but what time the door actually opens. Tell us that, tell us the board and syllabus code, and say which evenings are already taken. From there the arrangement builds itself: a session length that matches the attention the student has left, a slot with a margin for the bridges, demanding work moved to a weekend, and a Ramadan timing agreed before the month rather than during it. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, every board date on this page comes from the board, and nobody is sitting in the traffic to reach you.

intro.heading: The crossing, the clock and who is allowed to teach your child
paragraphs: Saadiyat Island sits off the north-east of Abu Dhabi island, connected by bridge and built out in distinct pieces: the beach villas and HIDD Al Saadiyat on one side, Mamsha Al Saadiyat and the apartment buildings on the waterfront, the Cultural District with the Louvre Abu Dhabi, and New York University Abu Dhabi's campus. It is a planned, relatively low-density community, and the household profile is senior professional and academic, with a high proportion of families who have arrived in the last few years.

For tutoring that produces two specific conditions. The first is the crossing. A family either uses a school on the island or crosses to Abu Dhabi island, Yas Island or out towards Khalifa City and Al Raha every school day. School buses here run long routes and the return is late by the standards of a compact city, so the first workable lesson slot sits later in the afternoon than new arrivals expect.

The second condition is that parents here ask harder questions about credentials than most. The common ones are whether a tutor is legally permitted to teach privately in the UAE, whether a child's own school teacher can be hired, and what ADEK actually regulates. Those are good questions with real answers, and almost nobody in this market publishes them. This page does, with the sources named, because an answer you can check is worth more than a reassurance you cannot.

The short version: private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories from registered school teachers to university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing with a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its app, website and e-services. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount is quoted here.

On hiring your child's own teacher, the answer in this emirate is no. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, with teachers tutoring outside school hours required to hold the MoHRE permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Treat that as press-reported and confirm the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it.

Everything below is built for a Saadiyat household: when a lesson can start after the crossing, who may legally teach, what the Abu Dhabi market charges with each figure attributed, and what happens when the specialist you need is not free in the slot you want. Lessons are online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India.

abu-dhabi/saadiyat-island.programmesIntro: Saadiyat households sit mainly on British routes into A Levels and IB continuum routes into the Diploma, with a smaller American-curriculum group. The notes describe what each programme means for a family that crosses a bridge twice a day.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher and Standard Level with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every subject carries an internally assessed component with published criteria, submitted and moderated before the written papers. The qualification rewards consistency across components and across two years, which makes it unusually sensitive to a disrupted term. Offers are typically expressed as a points total with named Higher Level minimums.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students crossing from Saadiyat have the tightest weekday evening in the community, because the independent workload is heaviest in this programme and the return from a mainland school is the latest. The arrangement that works here is one 90-minute weekend slot for timed paper work and marking, with a shorter weekday session added when an assessed deadline is close rather than kept all year.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year externally examined courses, with Cambridge codes such as 0580 Mathematics, 0620 Chemistry and 0625 Physics, and Pearson International GCSE codes such as 4MA1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. Cambridge mathematics and the separate sciences are tiered into Core and Extended, setting the available grade range before papers are sat. Results at sixteen act as the entry gate for sixth form, which in this part of Abu Dhabi often carries subject-specific minimums.
programmes.countryNote: Saadiyat families arriving mid-course frequently change board as well as school, because the previous country used a different one. That transfer costs weeks unless it is treated as a project: audit both syllabuses, close gaps in order of paper weighting, and teach the new board's mark-scheme conventions explicitly. Ask the receiving school which board and code it enters before the first tutoring session is booked.

programmes.name: A Levels after IGCSE
programmes.description: Three or four subjects studied in depth, assessed almost entirely by external papers with coursework in a minority of subjects. The narrower load means a weak subject cannot be offset by breadth, and offers name grades in named subjects. Students who prefer depth and dislike the Diploma core often perform better here; students who need breadth to stay engaged generally do not.
programmes.countryNote: A noticeable share of Saadiyat households are weighing a UK pathway, sometimes including boarding from sixteen. That decision has an academic component and a logistical one, and the academic part should be settled on marked scripts rather than on reputation. Where a child is likely to board, the useful tutoring in Year 11 is independent-study discipline as much as subject content.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, labelled A to D, with levels out of eight and task-specific rubrics rather than percentages. The Personal Project in the final year is an extended independent piece with its own criteria. The programme rewards process, planning and reflection, and reports describe those rather than giving marks, which takes a term or two for a new parent to read fluently.
programmes.countryNote: Families moving onto Saadiyat from a marks-based system often read a criterion-level report as a percentage and reach the wrong conclusion. Before buying tutoring, it is worth having the report translated: a 5 out of 8 on criterion C is a specific statement about a specific skill. We will do that in a first conversation at no charge, because half the enquiries that start this way do not need tutoring at all.

abu-dhabi/saadiyat-island.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Saadiyat households request most often. Each description names where marks actually leave the page rather than restating the syllabus.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Calculus, algebra and proof, with a third paper at Higher Level on an optional topic. The losses are in method lines skipped by students who can reach the answer mentally, and in explorations built on a topic too broad to control. Higher Level here is one of the most commonly over-chosen subjects in the Diploma.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and calculator-led work. The written interpretation of a model carries real marks and is the part students under-practise. Higher Level is substantial and accepted for many quantitative degrees, so switching down should follow evidence rather than anxiety.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE Core and Extended
subjects.description: Mechanics, waves, electricity and, at Higher Level, fields and quantum topics. Experimental-design questions are the reliable loss: students give a method where a control variable was asked for. Formula provision differs between Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1, which changes what must be recalled.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE Core and Extended
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms. Mole arithmetic under time pressure caps more grades than any single topic. Mechanism questions want arrows and intermediates rather than descriptions, and that distinction alone moves Paper 2 marks within a few sessions.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE Core and Extended
subjects.description: Physiology, genetics, ecology and data analysis, with the heaviest command-term load of the sciences. Students who revise by rereading plateau; those who write answers against mark schemes do not. Data questions reward reading axes and units before the question stem.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Markets, macroeconomic objectives and the global economy, assessed through essays, data response and, at Diploma level, commentaries built on news articles. Diagram accuracy and the final evaluation sentence decide more marks than content recall does. Higher Level quantitative work rewards short regular practice.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.levels: IB Language A HL and SL · IGCSE First Language
subjects.description: Analysis, comparative writing, the individual oral and the higher level essay. The commonest ceiling is a student who describes what a text says rather than analysing how it works. Directed writing at IGCSE is marked on audience and register as much as on content, which responds quickly to teaching.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.levels: IB ab initio and Language B · IGCSE 0544
subjects.description: A high-demand subject on Saadiyat, where many children started Arabic recently. Progress depends on daily low-volume contact rather than long weekly sessions, and the assessed speaking components reward rehearsed fluency in a narrow range of topics over broad shallow vocabulary.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Marketing, operations, finance and organisational structure, assessed largely through case studies. Marks come from applying a tool to the business in the stem rather than defining the tool. The Diploma research project needs an organisation that will actually supply information, which is worth testing before the question is fixed.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the prescribed-title essay, contributing points alongside the Extended Essay. Rarely revised, routinely underestimated, and cheap to improve relative to lifting a Higher Level subject. Reading a prescribed title precisely is a teachable skill and most students have never been taught it.

abu-dhabi/saadiyat-island.regionsIntro: Saadiyat Island shares schools, bridges and bus contractors with the communities below. The notes describe what each one changes for a household planning an afternoon around a crossing.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Dense apartment towers on the other side of Abu Dhabi island, reached by a different crossing. Reem and Saadiyat households often use the same mainland schools, so they share arrival times and compete for the same late-afternoon tutoring slots.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: A short connection east, with its own school and a large leisure traffic load at weekends. Saadiyat families whose children attend a Yas school face a run that is quick in the morning and slower on the return.

regions.name: Al Bateen
regions.note: Established Abu Dhabi island housing with several long-standing schools. One of the main crossing destinations from Saadiyat and the reason a 16:30 weekday slot is rarely realistic for a family on that route.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Waterfront apartments and townhouses out towards the airport road, with schools in the adjacent communities. Shares with Saadiyat the profile of recently arrived families and the same demand for Arabic as an additional language.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Large villa communities on the mainland with a dense school cluster. The longest regular crossing from Saadiyat, which pushes a weekday lesson start past five o'clock for families on that route.

regions.name: the Corniche
regions.note: The city-island waterfront, with apartment living and short school runs. Relevant to Saadiyat households as both a school destination and the comparison point for how much faster a city-island afternoon runs.

regions.name: Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Central Abu Dhabi island, mixed residential and commercial. A common workplace rather than school destination for Saadiyat parents, which is why online lessons that do not need an adult at home are easier to keep.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: Villa compounds near the airport road with a school adjacent to the community. The contrast with Saadiyat is instructive: a school inside the community frees roughly an hour a day at both ends.

regions.name: Al Reef
regions.note: Villa and apartment housing further out towards the airport. Longer runs again, and a community where tutoring slots tend to be booked later in the evening than anywhere closer in.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: A large mainland community with its own schools and a broad curriculum mix. Saadiyat and MBZ households rarely share a school, but they compete for the same specialist tutors in the same evening windows.

schoolClusters.city: Saadiyat Island and the crossing to Abu Dhabi island
schoolClusters.note: The schools reached without leaving the island or with a single crossing. The mix is British, IB continuum and American, and several run both IGCSE and a sixth-form route, which is why Year 11 planning here is usually driven by a specific published entry requirement.

schoolClusters.city: Yas Island and the Khalifa City corridor
schoolClusters.note: The longer runs east and inland, taking in the American-curriculum and IB continuum schools of the mainland corridor. Saadiyat families on these routes have the latest returns in the community and plan tutoring accordingly.

abu-dhabi/saadiyat-island.modesIntro: Three formats that fit a household organised around a crossing, all delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. None involves a tutor arriving at an address in the UAE.

modes.title: Late-afternoon weekly one-to-one
modes.description: A fixed weekly slot placed deliberately after the crossing and the decompression gap, usually between half past five and seven. Sixty minutes for IGCSE and Standard Level work, ninety for Higher Level. The slot is held for the term, which matters more here than elsewhere because the alternative is renegotiating it every week against a variable school bus.

modes.title: Weekend long session for timed work
modes.description: A 90-minute weekend slot built around one timed paper section and the line-by-line marking of it. This is the highest-value exercise a tutor does with an exam-year student and it does not fit a weekday evening after a long crossing. Scheduling it at the weekend is a design choice rather than a compromise.

modes.title: Arrival bridging block
modes.description: A defined block for a child who has just moved to Abu Dhabi, often into a different board and sometimes mid-year. The block maps what the new syllabus assumes against what the previous school taught, closes gaps in order of paper weighting, and ends with a past paper from the new board sat under timed conditions.

sections.heading: The Saadiyat crossing, and what it leaves of the afternoon
paragraphs: Work out the real clock once and the tutoring arrangement stops being a weekly negotiation. For a Saadiyat household the sequence is fixed: a morning departure early enough to clear the bridge, a school day that finishes between about two and three depending on phase, a bus route that collects several communities, and a return that lands anywhere between quarter past two and half past four. Add food and decompression and the earliest workable academic start runs from about half past three for an island school to past half past five for the Khalifa City corridor.

Three variables move it. The phase matters most: primary finishes well before secondary in the same building. The route matters next, because a bus serving Saadiyat, Al Bateen and the Corniche in one loop drops island children at different points depending on direction. And any after-school commitment adds ninety minutes and pushes the arrival into the slowest part of the evening.

The structural advantage of an online arrangement here is specific and worth stating plainly. Nothing depends on a second crossing. If the bus is twenty minutes late the family moves the start by twenty minutes and the full session still happens. A visiting tutor who arrives twenty minutes late delivers forty minutes, because the end is fixed by their next appointment. Across a fourteen-week term that difference is several hours of teaching that either took place or quietly did not.

sections.heading: Is the person teaching your child legally permitted to do it?
paragraphs: This is the question Saadiyat parents ask most often and almost nobody in this market answers. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants named in the official guidance include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

The application route is published too. MoHRE's own service is listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with no fee stated and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. That is the channel to point anyone at, and it is also the reason a tutor who says a permit is unnecessary, expensive or difficult should be treated with scepticism: it is free, it takes two working days, and the eligibility list is broad.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of fine amounts is published, so no figure appears on this page; a number circulating online could not be verified and publishing it would be an invention. What a parent needs is simpler than a fine schedule: ask the question, and prefer a tutor who answers it without hesitation.

There is a separate category for anything with premises and staff. An operation running a tuition centre is a different legal entity from an individual tutor and needs the relevant educational-services permit from the emirate's authority, with initial approval first and annual renewal. IB Gram holds no permit, accreditation or approval from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or any examination board, and no page here will suggest otherwise. We explain what each body does and link to its own pages.

sections.heading: Why you should not hire your child's own school teacher
paragraphs: It is the most intuitive idea a parent has and in this emirate it is the wrong one. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school. The same reporting notes that teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and that the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. This is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document, so confirm the current wording with ADEK directly before relying on it.

The reasoning is not hard to follow once stated. A teacher who sets and marks a student's school assessments, and who is also paid privately by that family, sits in an obvious conflict. The student's internal marks feed predicted grades and, in the Diploma, feed the final result through moderated internal assessment. A private commercial relationship running alongside that is a problem whether or not anyone behaves badly.

The practical consequence for a Saadiyat family is that the pool of acceptable tutors excludes the person who knows your child's class best, and that is as it should be. What you want instead is someone who knows the same specification to the same depth, has no stake in your child's school marks, and can tell you uncomfortable things about the work without a professional relationship to protect.

This is also why marketing that promises a child's own teacher, privately, should be read as a warning rather than an offer. Any provider doing that in Abu Dhabi either does not know the ethics rules or has decided they do not apply. Neither is a good sign about the rest of their practice.

sections.heading: What ADEK does, and what an inspection outcome is not
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi's regulator is the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. That is a wider remit than inspection alone: licensing a school, approving its operation and publishing inspection outcomes all sit with the same body. For a parent the practical point is that a school's standing is a matter of public record rather than reputation, and the record is held by ADEK rather than by a review site.

ADEK is also the regulator nobody writes about. Across the competitor pages researched for this market, Abu Dhabi's own authority is named by essentially none of them, while Dubai's KHDA appears occasionally. A Saadiyat family reading tutoring websites is therefore reading material written for a different emirate, with a different regulator, different school inspection arrangements and in some cases different rules on who may tutor.

What an inspection outcome does not tell you is how your child's subject is taught in your child's year group. A whole-school judgement is an average across phases, subjects and cohorts. A school with a strong overall standing can have a department that has lost two specialists in a year, and a school with a weaker standing can have an outstanding mathematics team. Read the report for the detail rather than the headline, and if the detail does not reach your child's subject, the report cannot answer your question.

The other limit worth stating is that no regulator accredits tutoring providers in the way parents sometimes assume. ADEK licenses schools. MoHRE issues tutoring permits to individuals. Neither one endorses a tutoring platform. Any provider describing itself as approved by an education authority is making a claim that should be checked against that authority's own register.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor across the bridge, against one-to-one online
paragraphs: This is the comparison behind most searches for a home tutor on Saadiyat, so it deserves a straight answer. A tutor physically present has real advantages: no dependence on a connection, a pen on a page, and for a child under about nine, an adult who can hold attention in a way a screen cannot. Those advantages can be decisive and we will say so when they are.

The costs are on the other side. The pool narrows to whoever will cross the bridge in the late afternoon. The rate carries the travel. The arrangement is fragile in a way that compounds: a delay on the crossing takes time off the end of the lesson, not off the start. And the specialist a Diploma student actually needs may be nowhere near Abu Dhabi, which on a bridge-connected island is a sharper constraint than in a dense inner-city district.

IB Gram delivers tutoring to Saadiyat as one-to-one online lessons over live video. We do not send tutors to addresses in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. Saying that before a parent asks is the point: this market has a habit of implying a visit and clarifying after a deposit, and a Saadiyat family that has just arrived in the country does not need to discover the arrangement by surprise.

The honest summary is that presence is the only category where the room wins outright. Reach, cost, whether the full session happens, and whether the marked script still exists next week all go the other way.

sections.heading: Arriving mid-year, which happens here more than anywhere
paragraphs: Saadiyat has a high proportion of recently arrived households, and a meaningful number of them arrive between terms rather than in August. A mid-year arrival into an examined course is a specific problem and treating it as general tutoring wastes the first month, which is the month that matters most.

The first task is an audit rather than teaching. What does the new specification assume that the previous school never covered? Which topics were taught in a different order, so the student has them but not where the course expects? Which assessed components have already been completed by the class, and what does the school intend to do about that for a new arrival? Those questions have specific answers and they determine everything that follows.

The second task is sequencing by exam weight rather than by textbook order. A new arrival has limited hours and the temptation is to start at chapter one. The better order is the topics carrying the heaviest paper weighting that the student has not met, then the mechanics of the new board's mark schemes, then everything else. A past paper from the new board, sat under timed conditions in week three, tells you more than any amount of catch-up reading.

The third task is administrative and parents often miss it. Find out whether the entry deadline for the next series has passed, whether the school can enter the student at all for the coming session, and whether an alternative route exists. Cambridge's March series key dates, for example, place final entries on 27 November 2026 for an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027. A family arriving in January has missed that window and needs to know it immediately rather than in February.

sections.heading: Where a tutor stops on assessed work
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries an internally assessed component, several IGCSE subjects carry coursework, and all of it is assessed as the student's own work. The IB's academic-honesty rules treat a breach as malpractice and the consequences land on the student. Any provider willing to supply finished work is selling a risk rather than a service, and at least one operation in this market does exactly that at a published price.

The line in plain terms. A tutor may teach the assessment criteria letter by letter with their mark allocations. A tutor may test a proposed research question and say honestly whether it is narrow enough to generate usable data in school conditions. A tutor may read a draft the student has produced and give feedback on structure, reasoning, evidence and clarity. A tutor may teach the underlying skills — referencing, uncertainty treatment, graph conventions, evaluation language — on a different example.

A tutor may not author any sentence that appears in a submission, supply text for the student to adapt, build the student's data set, or hand over a model answer to the student's own question. Where a school's rules are tighter than the board's, the school's rules apply; some schools in this emirate limit external feedback on an assessed draft to one round, and that limit is worth asking about at the start of a task rather than at the end.

The same ownership logic extends to university applications. A reference belongs to the school and nobody outside it should touch any part of it. A personal statement belongs to the student, who confirms its authorship to the university. A tutor can teach structure and comment on the student's own draft; a tutor cannot supply sentences or a template to be lightly adapted.

sections.heading: Starting from Saadiyat, including when the answer is no
paragraphs: Send four things and the first conversation is useful: the school and the board with syllabus codes, the most recent report or marked script, the two evenings that genuinely exist after the crossing, and a sentence about what you want to be true in twelve weeks. For a recent arrival, add what the previous school had covered, because that is where the audit starts.

The trial is taught rather than sold. A short diagnostic, worked through live, followed by a written note naming the specific gaps found and what the first six weeks would target. Where the diagnosis is that tutoring is not the right purchase, we say so: a child who has moved country, changed board and lost a term of sleep does not primarily need an extra hour on a screen, and saying otherwise would be easy and wrong.

On availability we are plain. The weekday window after five is the one this community needs and it is the first to fill, particularly in January. For a small number of niche Higher Level subjects the tutor who knows the paper may be based outside the UAE and teaching into a UAE evening; we tell you where a tutor is based whenever you ask, because it is a reasonable thing to want to know. If the right person is not free we say so rather than offering the nearest substitute.

What we will not do is claim an approval we do not hold, promise a grade, publish a statistic we cannot evidence, or supply assessed work. ADEK licenses and inspects Abu Dhabi's private schools; MoHRE issues the private tuition work permit. We explain what both do, link to their own pages, and hold nothing from either.

process.title: Time the crossing honestly
process.description: Track the real bus arrival for a fortnight, add the decompression gap, and name the two slots that survive. A slot chosen from the timetable you wish you had is the slot that collapses in week three, and on a bridge-connected island the variance is larger than most new arrivals expect.

process.title: Ask the permit question
process.description: Any tutor should be able to say whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit without hesitating. It is free, valid for two years and takes two working days to issue, so a complicated answer is itself the answer. Ask before the first paid session.

process.title: Rule out your child's own teacher
process.description: Reported ADEK ethics rules bar paid private tutoring of a teacher's own enrolled students, and the MoHRE permit code of conduct is reported to carry the same restriction. Confirm with ADEK, and treat any provider offering it as a warning about their wider practice.

process.title: Send a marked script
process.description: A script with the teacher's annotations shows where marks actually went rather than where anyone thinks they went. Twenty minutes with one separates technique losses from timing losses from genuine content gaps, and those need different plans and different tutors.

process.description: For recent arrivals this is the step that saves a month. Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 are different examinations, and the receiving school will confirm which it enters in one email. The audit of old against new specification follows from that answer.

process.description: The same diagnostic is repeated and compared. If the marks have not moved we change the tutor, the method or the subject taking the hours, and we say when the honest answer is that the plan or the target needs revising rather than extending.

whyPoints.description: Saadiyat has a high share of households new to the country and sometimes mid-year. The arrival work is an audit of two specifications, sequencing by paper weighting, and an immediate check on entry deadlines, which is a different job from general weekly tutoring.

faqs.question: What time can a lesson start for a child who crosses the bridge from Saadiyat every day?
faqs.answer: It depends on the direction rather than the tutor. Families here report returns from about 14:15 for a school on the island to past 16:45 for the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, with an after-school club adding roughly ninety minutes. Allow thirty to forty-five minutes for food and decompression and the earliest workable start runs from about 15:30 to 18:30. Because lessons are online there is no second crossing to accommodate, so a late slot works and a delayed bus moves the start rather than shortening the session.

faqs.question: Does my child's tutor need a permit to teach privately in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. The published eligibility list includes teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing with a two-working-day completion time through its app, website and e-services. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Can we pay my son's own maths teacher at school to tutor him privately?
faqs.answer: In Abu Dhabi you should not. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers giving paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and notes that the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Confirm the current wording with ADEK before relying on any summary. The underlying conflict is real: that teacher sets and marks the assessments feeding predicted grades and moderated internal marks.

faqs.question: What exactly does ADEK regulate?
faqs.answer: The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, which covers licensing a school to operate, approving its arrangements and publishing inspection outcomes. It regulates schools rather than tutoring companies. No education authority in the UAE accredits a tutoring platform, so any provider describing itself as approved by one is making a claim you should check against that authority's own register. IB Gram holds no permit or accreditation from ADEK.

faqs.question: Do tutors come out to Saadiyat Island for lessons?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. We deliver tutoring in the UAE as one-to-one lessons online, over live video, and we do not send anyone to a residential address in the Emirates; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. Local agencies and independent tutors do offer visits, with published market rates of AED 180-500 an hour including travel. On a bridge-connected island that premium is larger in practice than the figures suggest, because fewer tutors will make the trip at five in the afternoon.

faqs.question: We have just moved to Saadiyat mid-year. What should we do in the first month?
faqs.answer: Three things, in order. Audit the two specifications: what does the new course assume that the previous school never taught, and what was taught in a different order. Sequence the catch-up by paper weighting rather than by chapter, and sit a past paper from the new board under timed conditions in week three. Then check the administration immediately: whether the entry deadline for the coming series has passed and what the school intends to do about assessed components the class has already finished.

faqs.question: Which schools do Saadiyat Island families use?
faqs.answer: Some stay on the island, and the rest cross to Abu Dhabi island for the established British, American and IB continuum schools around Al Bateen, Al Rawdah and the Corniche, or travel east and inland to Yas Island, Raha and the Khalifa City corridor. The practical consequence is a wide spread of boards inside one community, which is why matching a tutor to the exact syllabus code matters more here than matching on area. Confirm the board with the school before booking anything.

faqs.question: How much do specialist IB tutors charge in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published market figures put IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and above per hour, with TutorChase listing AED 270 and Bestimate 200-450+, while premium or examiner-experienced tutors run from AED 500-650+, where BartyED publishes AED 650. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150-300, with Unitors listing AED 200 for IB. Those are the market's own numbers with their sources, not ours. Ask any provider whether marking of work set between sessions is inside the rate.

faqs.question: Is a 45-minute session enough for a Higher Level Diploma subject?
faqs.answer: For one specific job, yes: teaching and rehearsing a single technique, which is often all a weekday evening after a long crossing can hold. It is not enough for the exercise that matters most in an exam year, which is sitting a timed paper section and then marking it line by line against the real mark scheme. That needs ninety minutes. The usual design for a Saadiyat Diploma student is a short weekday technique session plus a 90-minute weekend slot for timed work.

faqs.question: Do you publish IB exam and results dates?
faqs.answer: No, and the reason is worth knowing. The IB's own site blocks automated access, so no IB session or results date in this project was confirmed from the IB directly, and an unverified date repeated across a large set of pages multiplies one error many times over. Treat the May session as the one UAE schools sit and take exact dates from your school's Diploma coordinator. Cambridge and Pearson dates used on this page come from those boards' own published pages and are attributed where they appear.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give feedback on my daughter's internally assessed investigation?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can teach the assessment criteria letter by letter with their mark allocations, say honestly whether her proposed research question is narrow enough to generate usable data, read a draft she has produced and comment on structure, reasoning and use of evidence, and teach skills like uncertainty treatment on a different example. A tutor must not author text that appears in the submission or build her data set. Where her school limits external feedback to one round, that limit applies.

faqs.question: My child has recently started Arabic. How should tutoring for it be organised?
faqs.answer: Frequently and briefly, rather than in one long weekly session. Language acquisition responds to daily low-volume contact, so three short sessions a week beat a single ninety-minute block, and that pattern also fits an island afternoon better. For assessed speaking components the gains come from rehearsed fluency across a narrow range of topics rather than broad shallow vocabulary. Arabic is also mandatory in UAE private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, so it affects the school report whether or not it is being examined externally.

faqs.question: What should we ask a tutor before the first paid session?
faqs.answer: Six questions cover most of it. Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit? Which board and syllabus code have you taught, and for how long? Is the rate per hour or per session? Is marking of work set between sessions included? Where are you based? And what would you expect to have changed in six weeks, measured how? A tutor who answers all six without hesitation is usually a safe bet; one who deflects the permit question or the measurement question is not.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for the subject and slot we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you and give you the real options rather than the convenient one: a different weekday or weekend time, a different tutor with the same board and component experience, or waiting until a slot opens. The post-five weekday window this community needs is the first to fill, especially in January. For a few niche Higher Level subjects the specialist may be based outside the UAE teaching into a UAE evening, and we say where a tutor is based whenever you ask.

faqs.question: Can lessons be held during the UAE school holidays or over the summer?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a Saadiyat family the holidays are often the most productive weeks of the year, because the crossing disappears and the day has room in it. Holiday work is best bought as a defined block with a written target: closing specific topic gaps identified from marked scripts, bridging from IGCSE into the Diploma, or preparing for a resit series. A diagnostic at the start and a repeat at the end gives you something to judge the block by rather than an impression.
