faqs.question: Why is a weekend block better than a weekday evening for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Because of length rather than mood. A Diploma student in Abu Dhabi who finishes school, commutes home and eats has ninety minutes to two hours of usable attention left, and homework for six subjects inside it. Nothing in the Diploma's long-form work fits there: a full paper plus marking takes two and a half to three hours, an investigation design session ninety minutes, a Theory of Knowledge argument the same. The weekend is where blocks of that length actually exist, at a time when a sixteen-year-old is rested rather than depleted.

faqs.question: How long should a weekend IB session actually run?
faqs.answer: Two hours for most work, two and a half to three when a full paper is being sat and marked in the same block, and sixty to ninety minutes for a Sunday reset session. Below two hours the long-form activities stop working, because sitting a paper in halves teaches nothing about pacing. Above three hours the student stops absorbing anything, whatever the schedule says. The shape that holds up across a term is one long morning block plus one short session, rather than two long ones on consecutive days.

faqs.question: Can my child sit a complete IB paper during a tutoring session?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the single most valuable use of a weekend block. The student sits the paper to time with the tutor present and silent on the call, so the conditions are real and pausing is not an option. The tutor then marks it against the published mark scheme, groups the lost marks by question type, and reads the script back with the student. Time per question is recorded alongside marks, because running out of clock and not knowing the content are different problems with different fixes.

faqs.question: Is Saturday or Sunday the stronger choice for a session in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Saturday morning is best for paper sittings, because a student is rested and the block is long. Sunday afternoon or evening suits core components and the week's reset, and it has the advantage of landing just before school rather than after a rest day, so the work stays live. Sport fixtures decide it for many families in the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor. The right answer is whichever block you can hold for a whole term, because a slot that moves every fortnight stops working by November.

faqs.question: Does a weekend session take away the family's only rest day?
faqs.answer: It should not, and if it does the plan is wrong. Our working rule is one half-day equivalent of weekend study in a normal term, including homework, and no more than two half-days even before mocks. That leaves a protected rest day. The long block sits in the morning so the rest of the day is free, and Friday is not scheduled into by default because it carries community and family commitments for many Abu Dhabi households. A student with no rest stops learning well before February.

faqs.question: What Diploma work genuinely cannot be done in a weekday hour?
faqs.answer: Four things. A full paper sat to time and marked, which needs two and a half to three hours. An investigation or exploration design session, where a weak research question agreed in fifty rushed minutes cannot be rescued by good data processing later. A Theory of Knowledge argument, which has to be tested aloud before it is written. And a structural review of a 4,000-word Extended Essay, which cannot be done by reading three pages. Everything else, including topic teaching and command-term drilling, is genuinely hour-shaped.

faqs.question: How do weekend blocks fit around school internal deadlines?
faqs.answer: The deadlines set the order. Send us the school's internal dates for each investigation, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge components in September, and the block plan is built backwards from them. The pattern that works is core and investigation design in the early autumn, final forms before the winter break, then paper practice from January. Families who leave the core until the spring meet it in the same term as mocks. Your coordinator's dates take precedence over anything we would propose, always.

faqs.question: Can a weekend tutor help with Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the strongest uses of the format. The essay runs to a maximum of 1,600 words on one of six prescribed titles, and the exhibition asks for three objects with a commentary of up to 950 words. Neither is a content task; both are arguments, and arguments improve by being tested out loud by somebody asking the awkward question. A student who has had their first two examples dismantled and found a third that survives is in a different position from one who has written around an uninterrogated title.

faqs.question: My child has CAS and sport commitments at the weekend. Is a block still realistic?
faqs.answer: Often yes, but it changes the shape. Where Saturday carries a fixture, the block moves to Saturday afternoon or Sunday, and the paper sittings concentrate in the weekends without fixtures. Where the commitments fill both days through a season, the honest answer is a shorter Sunday reset session in term and paper blocks during the school holidays. What does not work is squeezing a two-hour block into a day that already has two commitments in it, and we would rather say so than book it.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change a Saturday or Sunday block for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: They move later and get shorter, and the content changes. Sessions commonly shift to a post-Iftar time, which works well for review, worked examples and core discussion. What is not sensible is a two-hour timed paper sitting in the afternoon while a student is fasting, so timed sittings come out of the plan for that month and return afterwards. Planning the Ramadan pattern in advance rather than improvising is the difference between a slot that survives the month and one that quietly lapses and never restarts.

faqs.question: Are two weekend hours worth more than two weekday hours?
faqs.answer: For long-form Diploma work, considerably. For narrow work, no. Two weekday hours split across two evenings are good for teaching two topics or drilling two error classes, and they are cheaper on a student's attention. Two unbroken weekend hours are the only way to sit a paper, design an investigation or build a Theory of Knowledge argument. The best arrangement through the heavy terms is usually one of each: a weekday hour for the teachable items and a weekend block for everything that only exists whole.

faqs.question: What should my child have ready before a weekend block?
faqs.answer: For a paper block: the paper the school has set or an officially published one, blank paper, the calculator they will use in the examination, and nothing else within reach. For a core block: the current dated draft of whatever is being reviewed, the criteria for that component, and the supervisor's last written comments. For a reset session: everything returned by school that week, read or unread. Five minutes of preparation changes what a two-hour block can achieve more than any amount of enthusiasm does.

faqs.question: Do weekend slots cost more than weekday slots?
faqs.answer: The hourly band is the same in our case, but the booking is longer, so the session costs more than a weekday hour does. Across the market generally, published UAE rates for specialist IB work run roughly AED 200 to AED 450 an hour and above, with qualified online subject tutors between AED 150 and AED 300, and those bands are not split by day. What does move the number anywhere is scarcity: Saturday morning blocks are the most requested slot in the emirate, and they are gone by February.

faqs.question: How many usable weekends are there between September and a May session?
faqs.answer: Fewer than families expect. Subtract the winter and spring breaks, the mock fortnight where sitting extra papers is counterproductive, Ramadan where the pattern changes, and the final two weekends where consolidation and sleep matter more than new work. What remains has to cover core completion, investigation finishing and paper practice across six subjects. We publish no IB dates, because they come from the IB and your coordinator, but counting the weekends you actually have in September is the exercise that changes autumn behaviour.

faqs.question: When should we stop the weekend sessions?
faqs.answer: When the marked work shows the loss categories have cleared and the student is meeting internal deadlines unaided, or immediately after the session itself, which should be a stop rather than a taper. Continuing past either point is maintenance spending. A slot held all year out of habit also crowds out the rest that makes the rest of the week work. The better pattern is to stop, bank the time, and re-book for a specific component when one is genuinely in difficulty, which we would tell you rather than wait to be asked.

intro.heading: The weekend block is a pricing decision before it is a teaching decision
paragraphs: Most Abu Dhabi families arrive at weekend IGCSE tutoring with a weekly budget in mind rather than a component in mind. That is a reasonable way to start, and this page is built around it. The question underneath a search for a weekend IGCSE tutor in Abu Dhabi is almost always some version of: how much does a Saturday block cost, is it better value than two shorter weekday sessions, and how do I know the number I am being quoted is a sensible one for this market?

The headline answer is that a qualified online IGCSE subject tutor in the UAE market charges roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with specialists in the harder subjects running from about AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150; Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts specialists at 200 to 450 plus; the volume platforms advertise from as little as AED 33 to AED 65. Those are other providers' published figures. The reason to put them on this page is that three of the six competitor pages ranking for tutoring searches in the UAE publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars.

The second answer is structural, and it is where the money is actually won or lost. A two-hour weekend block almost always carries a lower effective hourly rate than two separate one-hour weekday sessions, because the tutor prepares once, the student warms up once, and nobody spends the first ten minutes re-establishing where they were. Against that, two contacts a week consolidate technique faster in Mathematics and the sciences than one longer contact does. Which of those effects wins depends on the subject and on how far from the exam series you are, and the tables below set out both.

The third answer is about what inflates a quote in this emirate specifically. Distance does, if anyone is driving: an in-home session into Khalifa City, Yas Island or Al Shamkha at five on a Saturday carries an hour of someone's day inside the fee, which is why published in-home rates sit between roughly AED 180 and AED 500 against online's AED 150 to AED 300. Proximity to a Cambridge or Pearson series does too, because the same specialists are asked for the same weekend slots by every family at once from February onwards. Tier does: Extended costs more than Core, and the harder sciences cost more than the easier humanities.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition as one-to-one lessons over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For a weekend slot that works in your favour on price, because the travel component disappears from the fee entirely and because the choice of tutor stops depending on who is willing to cross the mainland on a Saturday morning.

abu-dhabi/weekend-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Weekend IGCSE hours get bought at three different points in a child's school career, and they are worth very different amounts at each. The cheapest effective hour is almost never the one bought last.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9, before the IGCSE course begins
programmes.description: No board, no syllabus code, no exam. What exists instead is the arithmetic and writing fluency the IGCSE will later assume. Weekend hours here are the cheapest in the whole sequence per unit of eventual benefit, because a fraction or an algebra habit fixed at thirteen costs nothing to fix and a fortune to work around at sixteen.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi families rarely buy at this stage, and the enquiries that do arrive are usually prompted by a school report rather than by an exam. A single weekly hour through one term, aimed at number fluency or written structure, is the usual shape and the best value available.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight to ten subjects, assessed by terminal papers. Cambridge splits many subjects into Core and Extended with different grade ceilings; Pearson Edexcel runs a single tier in most subjects. The tier and the board set both the ceiling and the marking conventions, and they are the two facts that should be established before a single hour is paid for.
programmes.countryNote: Most British-curriculum schools in Abu Dhabi enter with Cambridge, but Pearson Edexcel entries are common in Mathematics and the sciences, and some schools split boards by subject within a year group. Get the syllabus code from the statement of entry; a tutor teaching the wrong board's conventions is an expensive mistake.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The sixth-form route most IGCSE students in Abu Dhabi continue into, assessed in June and November series with AS units that can be taken separately. It matters on a cost page because the Ministry of Education's British-track equivalency requirement is written around it, and because families budgeting for Year 11 often forget what Year 12 will ask for.
programmes.countryNote: Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track asks for one accredited Advanced Level subject at grade E or above, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3.

programmes.name: Retakes and private candidacy
programmes.description: A student who needs one grade for a sixth-form place can re-enter in a later series, sometimes as a private candidate through an approved centre. The cost structure is different: entry fees to the centre, plus a short and sharply targeted block of tutoring rather than a year of weekly support.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE and O Level in a June and a November series, with a March series in some regions; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Which series a retake can use depends on the subject and the centre, so confirm with the centre before planning the tutoring around it.

abu-dhabi/weekend-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: Rates track subject supply, and subject supply in Abu Dhabi is uneven. For each subject below, what the papers assess and where it sits in the local pricing picture.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Two papers in most entries; Extended reaches functions, transformations and harder trigonometry with a higher grade ceiling. Deep local supply, so this is the subject where rates sit lowest and where a weekend block is easiest to fill at short notice. Most lost marks come from arithmetic slips and ignored rounding instructions.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and waves are where most candidates lose marks, and the practical route differs between entries. Thinner supply than Mathematics, so rates sit mid to upper band. A weekend block is the only realistic place to work through a full paper with the formula sheet discipline that Physics rewards.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations presented without working are the single largest avoidable loss, followed by organic naming. Supply is thinner again than Physics in Abu Dhabi, which puts rates at the upper end of the qualified band and makes weekend specialist slots the ones that disappear first in spring.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume plus command-term precision, with diagram labelling worth more than candidates expect. Reasonable supply locally. Weekend time is best spent writing full long-answer responses against the mark scheme rather than reading notes, which is slow work and needs the length.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and reading response, marked for structure and control rather than vocabulary display. Good supply, moderate rates. A weekend block earns its place here because a full piece written, marked and partly rewritten is the only process that moves a writing grade.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Data response and structured essays where application to the stimulus carries the marks. Moderate supply. Candidates lose marks offering general theory where the question named a firm or a country, which is a coachable habit rather than a knowledge problem.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by stronger candidates alongside the main entry, and supported by a much smaller pool of tutors. Rates sit at the top of the local band for this reason. Weekend blocks suit it because the questions are long and multi-stage.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions, logic and a practical component depending on the entry. Supply is patchy in Abu Dhabi and uneven in quality, since coding ability and specification knowledge are different things. Check that a tutor knows the board's pseudocode style before paying.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Case-study specificity and source evaluation. A named place with figures earns marks; a described region does not. Supply is reasonable and rates sit in the middle band, but quality varies most here because the subjects look easier to teach than they are.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first and additional language
subjects.description: A Ministry-mandated subject in UAE private schools, running beside the licensed curriculum and examined on its own terms. The tutor pool barely overlaps with the subject-tutor pool, and weekend slots are the usual route because the week has no room left.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Sciences
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed into a smaller entry, which changes what can be dropped and what cannot. Families often buy single-science tutoring for a combined-science candidate and pay for content that is not on the entry. Confirm the syllabus code first.

subjects.name: French and Spanish
subjects.description: Four skills with a speaking component that students practise last. Supply in Abu Dhabi is thin for Spanish in particular, which pushes rates up. Weekend blocks suit the speaking preparation, which needs a full rehearsal rather than a quick run-through.

abu-dhabi/weekend-igcse-tutor.modesIntro: Three formats, three price structures. The cheapest per hour is not always the cheapest per grade, and the difference is worth understanding before a package is bought.

modes.title: The weekend block, paid hourly
modes.description: One two-hour slot each weekend, paid as you go, no commitment. The most flexible arrangement and the right way to start, because it lets you stop without argument if the fit is wrong. The effective hourly rate is higher than a block booking, which is the price of flexibility and usually worth paying for the first month.

modes.title: A booked block of weekend sessions
modes.description: A defined number of sessions bought together, typically six to twelve, which prices lower per hour and produces better teaching because the tutor can plan a sequence rather than react weekly. Worth moving to once a trial and a few paid sessions have shown the arrangement works. Not worth buying before you have met the tutor.

modes.description: Two to four students sharing a slot and a rate, which lowers the per-student cost substantially. It works when every student in the group sits the same board, the same tier and roughly the same target grade. It works badly otherwise, because the session drifts towards the weakest or the strongest and your child pays for somebody else's gaps.

sections.heading: The arithmetic: one weekend block against two weekday hours
paragraphs: This is the comparison almost every Abu Dhabi family makes, usually in their head and usually without the numbers written down. Written down, it resolves fairly clearly, and the answer depends on the subject rather than on the budget.

On price, the block wins. A two-hour weekend session typically prices below two separate hourly sessions in the same market band, because the tutor's preparation and the student's warm-up amortise across more teaching minutes. In the qualified online band of AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, families generally see the effective rate for a booked two-hour block land nearer the lower half of that range, while single ad hoc hours sit nearer the upper half. The saving is real but modest, usually ten to twenty per cent.

On teaching, it splits by subject. Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry reward two contacts a week in Year 10 and early Year 11, because the technique only sticks through practice and a four-day gap between contacts beats an eight-day one. English, the humanities and the longer-answer subjects reward the block, because a full piece of writing produced, marked and partly rewritten is the process that moves those grades, and it does not fit in an hour. In the final two months before a series, every subject reverts to the block, because what matters then is complete papers sat to time.

On reliability, the weekend block wins decisively in this emirate, and reliability is worth more than either of the first two factors. A weekday session at five in the afternoon competes with traffic, activities and a tired child; a Saturday or Sunday slot competes with family plans but not with the school day. A slot that runs forty times in a year teaches more than a better-designed slot that runs twenty-five times, and the published rate on the unreliable one is a fiction.

sections.heading: Counting the weekends backwards from the exam series
paragraphs: The most useful thing a parent can do with a calendar is count weekends rather than weeks, because a weekend slot is the unit you are actually buying. A family starting in late September for a June series has around thirty weekends before the papers, minus winter and spring breaks and minus the weekends nobody will realistically use. Starting in February leaves fewer than fifteen. The difference in price per weekend is small; the difference in what those weekends can achieve is enormous.

The board calendars give the fixed points, and they are published. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. For the March 2027 series, Cambridge's own key-dates document puts the exam period from 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. That gap between the entry deadline and the exam is the point worth internalising: the decision that fixes your child's tier is taken months before the paper.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year, and the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why any plan should link the live official timetable rather than rely on a restated date that can be revised.

One Cambridge administrative detail catches UAE families out and is worth checking before you plan weekends around a date. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask your school's examinations officer which zone the centre sits in, then build the weekend plan on that timetable.

sections.heading: What moves the number up, and what moves it down
paragraphs: A weekend IGCSE quote in Abu Dhabi can vary by two hundred dirhams an hour for the same named subject, and the variation is not random. Six things explain nearly all of it, and every one of them is something you can ask about before committing.

Tier and subject scarcity move it up. Extended costs more than Core because the ceiling is higher and the teaching is harder. Within the sciences, Chemistry and Physics specialists are thinner on the ground in this emirate than Mathematics or Biology, and Additional Mathematics, Spanish and the board-specific Computer Science entries are thinner again. Scarcity is a supply fact rather than a quality claim, which is why a high rate is not by itself evidence of a better tutor.

Timing moves it up sharply, and this is the lever most families pull in the wrong direction. From February onwards, every household in Abu Dhabi with a Year 11 candidate is looking for the same weekend slots in the same handful of subjects. Booking a September weekend costs less per hour than booking a March one and achieves considerably more, because in September the tier decision is still open and habits are still formable. Format moves it down: online removes the travel component that puts in-home rates between AED 180 and AED 500.

Commitment and session length move it down. A booked run of sessions prices below ad hoc hours, and a two-hour block prices below two singles. Group sharing moves it down furthest of all, at the cost of the diagnosis being shared too. What should never move the number is a promise about outcomes: no tutor at any rate controls the examiner, the cohort or the boundaries, and a quote justified by a predicted grade is a quote justified by something the seller cannot deliver.
bullets: Up: Extended over Core, scarce subjects, late booking, in-home delivery, single ad hoc hours
Down: online delivery, longer blocks, booked runs, group sharing, early booking
Neutral: the tutor's own description of their results, which nobody audits
Never a reason to pay more: a promise about the grade, which nobody can deliver

sections.heading: The tier decision that sets the ceiling, and what it costs to change
paragraphs: In Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended, the tier your child is entered for sets the maximum grade available, and the decision is made at entry rather than at the exam. For the March 2027 series, final entries were due on 27 November 2026, which means the decision sits roughly ten weeks before the first paper. Families who treat tutoring as an exam-season purchase often discover the ceiling after it has been fixed.

The cost of moving a child from Core to Extended is not mainly the tutoring; it is the time. Extended covers additional content and expects a different level of algebraic and analytical confidence, so a student moving up needs the extra material taught and then practised, which is a term's work rather than a block's. Done from September, it is a reasonable project. Attempted in January, it usually produces a student sitting a harder paper less well prepared, which is worse than a strong Core entry.

The decision should be made from evidence rather than ambition, and the evidence is a marked mock sat under proper conditions. A candidate comfortably above the Core ceiling on the Core paper has a case for moving. A candidate scraping the top of Core has a case for staying and converting that into a secure grade. What should not drive the decision is a sixth-form entry requirement expressed as a wish: ask the receiving school what it actually requires, in writing, before changing the entry.

The same evidence logic applies to the practical route in the sciences. Depending on the entry, candidates sit either a practical examination or an alternative-to-practical paper, and they reward different preparation. Weekend sessions aimed at the wrong one are hours spent on the wrong paper, which happens more often than it should because the syllabus code is never checked. Get the code and the component list from the statement of entry, then plan the hours.
bullets: Tier is fixed at entry, months before the paper is sat
Core to Extended is a term's work, not a block's
Decide from a marked mock, not from a target
Confirm the receiving school's actual requirement in writing
Check whether the entry uses the practical or the alternative-to-practical paper

sections.heading: Weekend tutoring set against what an Abu Dhabi family already pays
paragraphs: Tutoring is rarely assessed against the rest of the education budget, which makes it feel either trivially small or alarmingly large depending on the month. Setting it in context helps, and the context in Abu Dhabi is a private school sector where fee changes are regulated: schools apply to ADEK for tuition increases rather than setting them freely, which is a useful reminder that tutoring sits entirely outside that framework and is priced by the market alone.

On a per-hour basis, weekend tutoring looks expensive next to a school fee divided by teaching hours. On a per-outcome basis the comparison is meaningless, because the two things do different jobs: the school teaches the course, and a tutor works on the specific places an individual student loses marks. The useful comparison is internal, between the tutoring options available to you, and the honest framing is that a modest number of well-targeted weekend hours generally beats a larger number of unfocused ones.

Bestimate's published monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions give a reasonable planning band: roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Advertised UAE packages show the same shape from another angle, with around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four in-home double sessions. Per hour of teaching, the in-home package is roughly double the online one, and the difference is travel.

The table below is a planning frame rather than a price list. IB Gram does not publish a rate card on these pages; your rate is confirmed before any paid session and the first lesson is free with no card held. What the table is for is deciding how many weekend hours a year actually requires, which is a question most families answer by accident in February rather than on purpose in September.

sections.heading: Questions to ask before you pay for a weekend slot
paragraphs: Because nothing in this market is audited, price only becomes meaningful next to a set of questions whose answers are hard to improvise. These are the ones that separate a tutor who knows the specification from one who knows the subject, and they take about ten minutes.

Start with the entry. Which board and syllabus code does my child sit, which tier, and which papers? A tutor who cannot answer from the statement of entry you sent them has not read it. Then the mechanics: what is the cancellation window, does the rate change as the series approaches, what does a two-hour block cost per hour against a single hour, and is anything charged beyond teaching time? Those four questions remove almost every unpleasant surprise that arrives in month two.

Then the teaching. What would you do with a marked mock in the first session? The answer you want involves reading the mark scheme against the script and attributing each lost mark to a cause, not re-teaching the topic. How do you handle command terms? A tutor who talks about understanding rather than about instruction vocabulary will spend your weekends re-explaining content your child already has.

Finally, the things that should end a conversation. Any promise about a grade, because no tutor controls the examiner or the boundaries. Any claim of approval, accreditation or partnership with Cambridge, Pearson, ADEK, KHDA or the Ministry of Education, which for individual tutors is almost never checkable on the body's own register. Any offer to supply mark schemes, unreleased papers or completed coursework, which is a copyright or malpractice problem that lands on your child rather than on the seller.
bullets: Which board, syllabus code, tier and papers does my child actually sit?
What is the cancellation window, and does the rate move before the series?
What does a two-hour block cost per hour against a single hour?
What would you do with a marked mock in the first session?
Any grade promise, approval claim or offer of assessed work: walk away

sections.heading: Who is permitted to tutor privately in the UAE
paragraphs: A weekend tutor is subject to exactly the same rules as a weekday one, and the rules here are clearer than most of this market. Private tuition in the UAE runs on a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page for it lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website or e-services system.

Who may hold it is broader than parents assume: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, which is why no amount appears on this page and why any page quoting one is quoting something unverified.

Abu Dhabi adds a restriction that matters most at weekends, because weekends are when a school teacher's spare hours sit. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar bar. This is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document here, so verify the current wording with ADEK before relying on it. The working rule for a parent is to look outside your child's own school.

A centre with premises and staff needs an educational services permit from the emirate regulator, which is a different thing again from an individual tutor's permit and is not a quality rating. IB Gram holds no such permit and claims none. It is an independent matching platform, delivery is online and one-to-one, and no tutor on this site is described as approved, accredited or licensed by ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson.

sections.heading: When to stop buying weekend hours
paragraphs: A weekend slot costs a family more than its fee, because it takes a block out of the two days a Year 10 or Year 11 student has for rest and everything else. That is worth paying while the hours are fixing identifiable things, and it stops being worth paying the moment they are not. A tutor who will tell you that is worth more than one who will not, and it is a fair question to ask at the outset.

The signals are readable without knowing the subject. If three consecutive session notes describe the same error, either the diagnosis is wrong or the practice between sessions is not happening, and buying more hours changes neither. If the notes describe topics covered rather than mistakes corrected, the session has become a lecture. If your child arrives each weekend with nothing marked, the slot has replaced independent work instead of supporting it, which is the most expensive failure mode available.

There is a positive stopping point too, and families resist it. When a student starts arriving with their own marked script and their own account of where the marks went, the tutoring has done its job. The right move then is a monthly review rather than a weekly block, and the weekend goes back to the student. For a Year 11 candidate in the spring, that is not a minor benefit.

If no UAE-based specialist is free in the subject, tier and weekend slot you need, we say so rather than putting a generalist into the block at a specialist rate. A generalist in a two-hour weekend session is worse value than a shorter session with the right person and considerably worse than waiting a fortnight. That disclosure is the thing this market does not publish, and it is why the first lesson is free and takes no card.
bullets: Same error in three sets of notes: change the diagnosis, not the hours
Notes listing coverage rather than corrections: the slot has drifted
Nothing marked arriving each weekend: the slot is replacing study, not supporting it

process.title: Send the statement of entry
process.description: Board, syllabus code, tier and papers, straight from the school's statement of entry rather than from memory. This single document removes the commonest expensive error in IGCSE tutoring, which is paying for content that is not on your child's entry or for the wrong practical route.

process.title: Say what the weekend budget and the weekend slot are
process.description: Tell us the hours you can commit and the time you can actually hold. We would rather design one reliable two-hour block around a real constraint than quote for an arrangement that will be cancelled twice a month and cost the same.

process.title: Add whatever is already marked
process.description: A marked mock, a returned paper with a teacher comment, or a report with grades by paper. One marked script tells a specialist more than a conversation, and it means the free trial lesson is spent diagnosing rather than establishing the starting point.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: A full lesson, no payment and no card held. Your child should leave with one thing fixed; you should leave knowing whether this tutor can read a mark scheme against a script. The rate is confirmed before anything is paid, and no package is required to continue.

process.title: Move to a block only once it is working
process.description: Pay hourly for the first few weeks, then convert to a booked run if the session notes show progress. Blocks price lower per hour and teach better, but buying one before you have evidence is paying for commitment you cannot yet justify.

whyPoints.title: The price conversation happens first
whyPoints.description: Market bands are published on this page with their sources, and your own rate is confirmed before the first paid session. Nothing is quoted after a trial lesson has been used to build pressure, and no package is required before you have met the tutor.

whyPoints.title: Board and tier checked before hours are sold
whyPoints.description: We ask for the syllabus code and the component list before matching, because a tutor teaching the wrong board's conventions or the wrong practical route is the most common way weekend money gets wasted in this market.

whyPoints.description: Sessions are set in Gulf Standard Time around the Saturday and Sunday weekend, activities and travel, and shift to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan. The same tutor keeps the same slot through the term.

whyPoints.description: Hourly or block, your choice, and you can stop. We would rather tell you the hours have done their job than keep selling them, which is why session notes are written to show what is left to fix.

faqs.question: What does a two-hour weekend IGCSE block cost against two weekday hours?
faqs.answer: A booked two-hour block usually prices ten to twenty per cent below two separate hourly sessions in the same market band, because the tutor prepares once and the student warms up once. In the qualified online band of AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, families generally see block rates land in the lower half of that range and ad hoc single hours in the upper half. Those are market figures from published sources rather than our price list. The saving is real but modest; the bigger difference is what fits inside two uninterrupted hours.

faqs.question: How many weekends are there between September and the June IGCSE series?
faqs.answer: Roughly thirty, before you subtract winter and spring breaks, travel, and the weekends nobody will realistically use, which usually leaves the low twenties. Starting in February leaves fewer than fifteen. Counting weekends rather than weeks is worth doing because the weekend block is the unit you are buying, and it makes the cost of delay concrete: the per-weekend price barely changes between September and February, but what a September weekend can achieve is far greater, because the tier decision is still open.

faqs.question: Can two siblings sitting IGCSEs share a weekend tutoring budget?
faqs.answer: They can share a weekend, and often should, but sharing a session only works when both sit the same board, the same tier and roughly the same target. Otherwise the hour drifts to whichever child is further behind and the other pays for it. The arrangement that usually works in Abu Dhabi households is back-to-back blocks on the same morning with the same or different tutors, which keeps one disruption to the weekend instead of two and sometimes attracts a lower effective rate for the combined booking.

faqs.question: Does a weekend IGCSE package usually work out cheaper per hour?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it usually teaches better too, because a tutor with a committed run of sessions can plan a sequence instead of reacting weekly. The caution is what you buy before you have evidence. Pay hourly for the first four to six sessions, read the notes, then convert to a block. Before paying for any package, ask three things: what the cancellation window is, whether sessions can be paused around exams and travel, and what happens to unused sessions. A package that cannot be paused is a worse deal than its hourly rate suggests.

faqs.question: What should I pay for IGCSE Extended support at a weekend in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published market rates for a qualified online IGCSE tutor run about AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with harder-subject specialists from roughly AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Unitors advertises IGCSE from AED 150 and TutorChase lists AED 270; Bestimate's 2026 table puts specialists at 200 to 450 plus. Extended sits above Core within whatever band a tutor occupies, and Chemistry, Physics and Additional Mathematics sit above Mathematics and Biology because local supply is thinner. Those are other providers' figures; ours is confirmed before any paid session.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects can one weekend realistically support?
faqs.answer: Two, properly, and three only if the sessions are short and narrowly targeted. A two-hour block covers one subject well: a paper sat to time and marked, or a full piece of writing produced and reworked. Splitting the same block across three subjects produces twenty-five useful minutes each, and the second and third inherit whatever the first overran. Families with four weak subjects are usually better served by picking the two closest to a grade boundary and leaving the others to school provision for a term.

faqs.question: Is a weekend group class cheaper than one-to-one for IGCSE revision?
faqs.answer: Substantially cheaper per student, and genuinely useful in the right conditions. Those conditions are strict: everyone in the group sits the same board, the same tier and roughly the same target grade, and the session is paper practice rather than diagnosis. Where the group is mixed, the hour drifts towards the weakest or the strongest and your child pays for somebody else's gaps. Ask who else is in the group and what entry they sit before agreeing. For diagnosis, individual time is the only format that works.

faqs.question: When do weekend IGCSE slots start getting expensive in the year?
faqs.answer: From February onwards, and the mechanism is simple scarcity rather than opportunism. Every Abu Dhabi household with a Year 11 candidate starts looking for the same weekend slots in the same handful of subjects at the same time, and the specialist pool in this emirate is small. Rates firm up and availability narrows together. A September booking costs less per hour and achieves more, because the tier decision is still open and command-term habits are still forming. If you are reading this in March, book narrow and specific rather than broad.

faqs.question: What does the Cambridge March series mean for a weekend plan?
faqs.answer: It compresses everything. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series put the exam period from 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027 and results on Direct on 13 May. That means the tier decision is taken roughly ten weeks before the first paper, and the winter break sits immediately before the series rather than comfortably ahead of it. Check which series your centre uses, and which of Cambridge's six administrative zones it sits in, before planning weekends around any date.

faqs.question: Does my child need the practical paper or the alternative to practical?
faqs.answer: It depends on the entry, and it is on the statement of entry rather than being a matter of preference. The two components reward different preparation: one assesses laboratory technique and recording under supervision, the other assesses understanding of experimental method through written questions. Weekend sessions aimed at the wrong one are hours spent on the wrong paper, which happens more often than it should because nobody checks the syllabus code. Ask the examinations officer for the code and the full component list, then plan the hours around what is actually being sat.

faqs.question: Should we move from Core to Extended, and what does that cost in tutoring?
faqs.answer: Decide from a marked mock sat under proper conditions, not from a target. A candidate comfortably above the Core ceiling has a case for moving; one scraping the top of Core usually does better converting that into a secure grade. The real cost is time rather than money: Extended covers extra content and expects more analytical confidence, so a move is a term's work. Done from September it is reasonable. Attempted in January it tends to produce a student sitting a harder paper less well prepared, which is the worse outcome.

faqs.question: What is a fair cancellation policy for a weekend tutoring slot?
faqs.answer: Twenty-four hours' notice either way is the common standard and a reasonable one, since a weekend slot cancelled on the morning cannot be refilled. What to watch for is asymmetry: a policy that charges you for a late cancellation but offers nothing when the tutor cancels is not a policy, it is a term of trade. Ask what happens if your child is ill, whether a missed session can be made up within the month, and whether sessions can be paused during the exam series itself. Get the answers before the first paid session rather than after.

faqs.question: How does weekend IGCSE tutoring compare with what we pay in school fees?
faqs.answer: Different jobs, so a per-hour comparison misleads. Abu Dhabi private school fees sit inside a regulated framework where schools apply to ADEK for increases; tutoring sits entirely outside that and is priced by the market. The useful comparison is internal: Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly hour run about AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 plus for specialist exam-year support. Judge a tutoring spend against other tutoring options and against what the school already provides free.

faqs.question: Can weekend IGCSE sessions run during the exam series itself?
faqs.answer: They can, and sometimes a short session between papers helps with timing and nerves rather than content. More often the honest advice is to stop. By the time the series opens, new material cannot be absorbed usefully, and a weekend spent on a two-hour session is a weekend not spent resting before Monday's paper. Where sessions continue, keep them short, keep them to papers already sat, and plan the finish date in advance so the slot ends deliberately rather than drifting into the final fortnight.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for a weekend tutor in Year 10, or should we wait for Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is better value and almost nobody buys it. In Year 10 the tier decision is still fully open, content gaps can be closed without exam pressure, and the habits that cost marks across every paper, such as showing method and reading command terms, are still forming. In Year 11 the same money buys technique polishing on a narrower base. If the budget allows only one year of weekend support, take Year 10 and keep a short targeted block for the spring of Year 11.

abu-dhabi/weekend-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Send the entry, the budget and the slot you can hold
abu-dhabi/weekend-igcse-tutor.closingBody: The fastest way to a sensible quote is to stop asking what tutoring costs in general and start asking what your child's entry needs. Send the board, the syllabus code, the tier, whatever has already been marked, and the weekend time your family can realistically keep. We will tell you which specialists cover it, whether a two-hour block or two shorter sessions suits the subject, and the rate before anything is paid. The first lesson is free and takes no card. Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time; there are no home visits anywhere in the UAE.

intro.heading: The half of the week nobody supervises
paragraphs: Yas Island is a planned leisure and residential island east of Abu Dhabi: Yas Acres, Mayan, Water's Edge, Ansam and the newer villa phases, with the marina circuit, the mall and the theme parks occupying a large share of the land. Households are a mix of long-lease families and newer arrivals, and the school picture is dominated by a strong American-curriculum presence on the island with British and IB continuum options a short drive away across the crossings.

The enquiries that come from here have a recognisable shape. The child is attending, the teachers are not complaining, the homework is going in, and a report or a mock result has still disappointed. Parents reasonably conclude that something is being missed in class. Usually it is not. What is being missed is the work that no timetable contains and no teacher can mark: consolidation, past-paper practice, the first draft of an assessed piece, the reading that makes the next lesson comprehensible.

A school week has a fixed number of taught periods per subject, and those periods have to carry new content. Consolidation gets set as homework, which is checked rather than taught. Everything beyond that is genuinely unsupervised, and it is a substantial share of what produces the final grade. In an examined programme this is not a defect of the school; it is the design. The student is expected to do it, and nobody is responsible for noticing when they do not.

On Yas specifically, two local factors make that unsupervised half harder. The first is a continuous-assessment habit: students on American routes are used to work being graded regularly, which builds coursework discipline and does not build examination stamina. The second is the island itself. Yas is organised around leisure, and the weekends and event weeks that make it attractive also absorb the time a revision plan quietly assumes is free.

What follows names the gap component by component, then writes out an independent-study week with an output for each slot, compares the three sixth-form routes on evidence rather than reputation, sets out the published Ministry of Education requirements for the American track, and explains how to use past papers properly. It also says what we will not do: supply board papers, mark schemes or syllabus documents, which are the board's copyright and are freely available at source.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. ADEK licenses and inspects Abu Dhabi's private schools and does not accredit tutoring providers, and we hold no approval from it or from any examination board. Every figure quoted on this page carries the source that published it, and where a figure could not be verified we have left it out rather than guessed at it.

abu-dhabi/yas-island.programmesIntro: Yas households sit across American, British and IB routes, sometimes within one family. Each note below is about the independent workload the programme assumes rather than its general shape.

programmes.name: American curriculum and Advanced Placement
programmes.description: Continuous assessment across a grade point average, with credit-bearing Advanced Placement courses taken individually and examined on a 1 to 5 scale in a window set by the College Board. The structure distributes risk across a year, rewards steady submission and class participation, and produces a transcript rather than a single terminal result. Students accumulate evidence gradually rather than facing one high-stakes window.
programmes.countryNote: The independent gap on this route is examination stamina rather than content. A student who has never sat three hours of unseen questions in one sitting meets that for the first time in an AP paper or on moving to an examined system, and the losses are in pacing and endurance rather than knowledge. The useful preparation is timed full papers, spaced out, from February onwards, with the exact AP dates taken from the school.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across Higher and Standard Level with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every subject carries an internally assessed component against published criteria, submitted and moderated before the written papers. The share of the final result that depends on self-managed work is larger here than in any other route available in Abu Dhabi.
programmes.countryNote: For a Yas Diploma student the unsupervised load is the programme's defining feature. The Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and six internal assessments are all produced outside taught periods, on school-set deadlines, and the school cannot supervise the drafting. A weekly slot used for project supervision rather than content teaching is usually the better purchase in the second year.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year externally examined courses, with Cambridge codes such as 0580 Mathematics and 0625 Physics and Pearson International GCSE codes such as 4MA1 and 4PH1. Cambridge mathematics and the separate sciences are tiered into Core and Extended, which sets the available grade range. Assessment is concentrated at the end, so the independent work in Year 11 term two carries more weight than anything else in the course.
programmes.countryNote: Year 11 term two is the term nobody schedules. Content teaching is finishing, mock results have arrived, and the gap between what has been taught and what can be reproduced under time pressure becomes visible for the first time. For a Yas household that term is also crowded with island events and travel, so the revision plan has to be written rather than assumed.

programmes.name: A Levels after IGCSE
programmes.description: Three or four subjects in depth, assessed almost entirely by external papers with coursework in a minority. The narrower load concentrates risk in three named grades and rewards examination technique heavily. Independent work is mostly practice rather than project: past papers, mark schemes, worked problems, and the reading that supports extended written answers.
programmes.countryNote: A Level students in this part of Abu Dhabi often have fewer taught periods per subject than they expect, on the assumption that sixth-formers manage their own consolidation. For a student arriving from continuous assessment that assumption is a trap, because nobody checks whether the consolidation happened until a mock. A fortnightly supervised practice slot is often enough to make it visible.

abu-dhabi/yas-island.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Yas households ask about most, with each description naming the independent work that actually produces the grade rather than restating the course content.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Calculus, algebra and proof, with an optional-topic paper at Higher Level. No amount of class teaching substitutes for worked problems done alone and checked. The reliable independent task is a set of unseen questions, timed, with every method line written out, because the marks sit in the lines students skip when they can see the answer.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and calculator technique. The independent work that pays is writing the interpretation sentence: what the model implies, in context, in plain language. Students practise the calculation and skip the sentence, and the sentence is where the marks are.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE Core and Extended
subjects.description: Mechanics, electricity, waves and, at Higher Level, fields and quantum topics. The independent task that moves marks most is experimental-design questions, which cannot be learned by reading. Formula provision differs between Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1, which changes what has to be recalled under pressure.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE Core and Extended
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms. Mole arithmetic has to be automatic, and automaticity only comes from repetition done alone. Mechanism questions need arrows and intermediates drawn repeatedly rather than read once, which is exactly the work a timetable has no room for.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE Core and Extended
subjects.description: Physiology, genetics, ecology and data analysis. The subject has the heaviest command-term load of the sciences, and the independent work that pays is writing full answers to past questions and comparing them against the official mark scheme, line by line, which almost no student does unprompted.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Markets, macroeconomics and the global economy. Independent work splits cleanly: diagrams practised until accurate, and evaluation paragraphs written to a timer. At Diploma level the commentaries also need article selection done early, because a weak article caps the marks before any economics is written.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.levels: IB Language A HL and SL · IGCSE First Language
subjects.description: Analysis, comparative writing, the individual oral and the higher level essay. The independent work is reading and then writing about what was read, under time, without notes. Students who annotate thoroughly and never write to a timer arrive at the paper with excellent understanding and no delivery.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies, research methods and ethics, with answers that must name and use specific research precisely. The independent task is building a small, memorised bank of studies with dates, methods and findings, which is pure rehearsal and entirely unsupervised. The internal assessment is a replication with strict conventions.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Marketing, operations, finance and structure, assessed through case studies. The independent work is applying each tool to an unfamiliar business repeatedly until the application is automatic, because the examination never asks about the business that was studied in class.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Algorithms, data structures, networks and system fundamentals. Programming experience transfers; written theory precision does not. The independent work is writing pseudocode by hand in the board's own conventions and tracing it on paper, which self-taught programmers rarely do and which the papers test directly.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the prescribed-title essay, contributing points alongside the Extended Essay. Entirely self-managed, rarely revised and cheap to improve relative to lifting a Higher Level grade. Reading a prescribed title precisely is the single teachable skill that changes the mark most.

It belongs at the weekend.

sections.heading: What the timetable delivers, and what your child is left holding
paragraphs: Before buying anything, it is worth separating what a school can do from what it cannot. Taught periods are finite and they have to carry new content. Consolidation is set as homework, which is collected and checked rather than taught again. Beyond those two categories sits a third that belongs to the student alone, and in an examined programme it is large.

The third category includes consolidation that was never set, past-paper practice, the first draft of an assessed piece, the memorisation that makes a paper possible, and the reading that makes the next lesson comprehensible. None of it appears on a timetable. None of it is marked. Nobody is responsible for noticing when it does not happen, and that is exactly why a report can say the child is attending and engaged while the marks drift.

Parents on Yas frequently reach a different conclusion, which is that the school is at fault. Occasionally it is. More often the school is doing what schools do and the gap is structural. Testing which it is takes one exercise: ask the student to produce, under time and without notes, something they were taught six weeks ago. If they can, the teaching landed and the problem is elsewhere. If they cannot, the content was covered but never consolidated, which is a different purchase.

Use the table as a diagnostic rather than a description. Work down the component column for your child's subject and ask honestly which of the last three columns each row belongs in. The rows that fall into the unsupervised column, with nobody noticing, are where the tutoring hours should go.

sections.heading: An independent-study week, written down
paragraphs: The fix for an unsupervised half-week is not more hours; it is defined outputs. 'Revise biology' produces the appearance of study. 'This past-paper section, timed, marked against the scheme, with the three biggest losses listed' produces a document, and a document can be reviewed. The difference in results between those two instructions is larger than the difference between a good tutor and an average one.

The week below is a template rather than a prescription, built for a Year 11 or Diploma student on a Yas school run. It assumes five short weekday windows and one longer weekend slot, because that is what the commutes here leave. Adjust the subjects; keep the structure, and keep the rule that every slot ends with something written that someone will look at.

Two rules make it hold. Fix the place and the time, so the student stops deciding when and where each day, and let someone see the output in the next tutoring session. The second rule is the one that does the work: an hour whose product is reviewed by another person stops being optional. That is the real function of a weekly slot, and it is almost never how tutoring is sold.

The weekend slot is where timed work belongs. A student used to continuous assessment needs to build examination stamina deliberately, and that means sitting full sections without notes, at full length, repeatedly. Nothing in a continuous-assessment school week asks for that, which is why it has to be scheduled rather than assumed.

sections.heading: Advanced Placement, the Diploma and A Levels compared
paragraphs: Yas families reach this decision more often than most Abu Dhabi households, because the island's school mix puts an American route alongside British and IB options within a short drive. The three are genuinely different products and the choice should follow the student rather than the brand.

Advanced Placement is modular in the most useful sense: courses are taken individually, a strong student can take several and a cautious one can take one, and each is examined separately on a 1 to 5 scale in a window set by the College Board. It fits a student who performs steadily across a year and wants to demonstrate depth in selected subjects without committing to a fixed programme shape. It does not build the examination stamina that a terminal system demands.

The Diploma is a fixed shape: six subjects, three core components, and a points total. It spreads risk, so one weak subject does not sink a result, and it demands sustained independent project work. A Levels concentrate risk in three named grades and reward examination technique above everything else, with the most predictable workload of the three and the least room to absorb a poor result.

Decide on marked timed work rather than on reputation. Sit a timed written piece and a timed problem paper in the student's two strongest subjects and have them marked honestly. Where the evidence is balanced, choose the school and the department rather than the qualification; a well-staffed cohort in any of the three beats a thin one in the other two.

sections.heading: The American track and what the Ministry actually publishes
paragraphs: Families on an American route who intend to study in the UAE will meet the Ministry of Education's equivalency process, and the published requirements for this track are specific and testable rather than vague. They also differ in kind from the British-track requirements, which are expressed in subject counts and grades.

For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. Mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test, and the published source states this applies before applying rather than afterwards. The same source does not mention EmSAT, so no EmSAT requirement is stated here.

The practical implication for a Yas household on an American route is that two of those requirements are standardised tests with their own preparation and their own sittings, and they need to be planned into Grade 11 and Grade 12 rather than discovered in the spring of the final year. A student whose transcript is strong and whose SAT Math sits below the stated threshold has a problem that is entirely solvable with notice and awkward without it.

Two cautions apply. Equivalency is run by the authority; it is not something a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or accelerates, and we point families to the Ministry's own channels for current rules. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency or for a university place — any page suggesting otherwise is manufacturing urgency about an administrative process, which is a reason to treat the rest of its claims with caution.

sections.heading: Where marks leave the page in a timed examination
paragraphs: A student moving from continuous assessment into terminal examinations loses marks in a pattern that has very little to do with knowledge, and recognising the pattern is most of the repair. The first and largest loss is pacing. A student who has always worked to a deadline measured in days writes the first two questions beautifully and abandons the last one, which in most papers is where the heaviest marks sit.

The second loss is the absence of notes. Continuous assessment usually permits reference material, and a student whose understanding is sound but whose recall was never rehearsed finds the examination asks for memory rather than comprehension. Definitions, equations, named studies and command-term conventions have to be in the head, and that is rehearsal rather than learning.

The third loss is command-term mismatch, which costs marks in every written subject. 'Explain' requires a causal chain, 'describe' does not, and 'evaluate' needs a judgement with support. A student who writes the same quality of answer to all three earns the marks for only one of them. It is a vocabulary problem and it takes a handful of sessions to fix.

The fourth is mechanical: units dropped, significant figures ignored, axes mislabelled, working not shown, an answer written outside the space. These are the cheapest marks in the building and they are lost by strong students more often than weak ones, because strong students work quickly. A marked script shows all four patterns in twenty minutes, which is why we ask for one before suggesting a plan.

sections.heading: Past papers done properly, and what we will not supply
paragraphs: Most students use past papers badly: they read a question, decide they could answer it, and move on. That produces familiarity rather than capability. Used properly, a past paper is a measuring instrument. Sat under time, without notes, then marked against the official scheme by someone who knows how the marks are awarded, it gives a number and a list. Both are necessary.

The method that works is short and rarely followed. Choose one section rather than a whole paper. Time it exactly. Put the notes away. Mark it immediately against the official mark scheme, line by line, awarding marks the way a marker would rather than the way a sympathetic parent would. Then write down the three largest losses and treat that list as the next fortnight's work. Repeat with a different section, and compare.

There is one thing we will not do, and it is worth saying plainly because competitors in this market do otherwise. We do not reproduce, host or supply board papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or syllabus documents. They are the copyright of Cambridge International, Pearson, the IB and the College Board, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure on top of the copyright problem. We reference them, cite the official source and link out to it.

The practical route for a parent is simpler than it looks. Schools hold the materials their students are entitled to use and will usually release past papers for revision on request. The boards publish specimen and past material through their own channels. Ask the school first; it costs nothing and it keeps everyone on the right side of a rule that at least some providers in this market ignore.

sections.heading: What support costs on Yas, and which band fits which job
paragraphs: Published rates in this market span a wide range and most of the best-ranking pages give no figure at all. The table sets out the market's own numbers in AED with the provider that published each. They describe the market rather than an IB Gram rate card; ask us for the trial and the consultation if you want our figures and what sits inside the hour.

The useful question is not which band is best but which band fits the job. A supervised practice slot whose purpose is to look at work the student produced does not need the top of the market; it needs someone who marks accurately and tells the truth. A Higher Level subject that a university offer turns on may genuinely justify a specialist. Buying the specialist for the practice slot is the commonest overspend here.

At the bottom of the market the hour is usually teaching time alone, with no marking of work set between sessions. For the independent-study problem this page is about, that is the least useful possible purchase: the entire mechanism depends on someone reading what the student produced. Paying less for an hour that excludes the marking is not a saving.

Three questions settle most comparisons. Is the rate per hour or per session? Is marking of work set between sessions included or billed separately? Does the rate change in the exam term? Those answers vary far more between providers than the headline numbers do.

sections.heading: Event weeks, weekends and a Yas Island timetable
paragraphs: Yas is built around leisure, and that shapes the academic year in ways no revision timetable accounts for. Event weekends bring heavy traffic onto and off the island, the mall and the parks are a short walk or drive from most of the residential phases, and houseguests arrive in the cooler months. A plan that assumes a quiet Friday and Saturday will survive about three weeks.

The sensible response is to plan around it rather than pretend otherwise. Identify the weekends that will not be available and move the long timed session rather than skipping it: a Thursday evening or a Sunday morning is better than a lost week. Treat the cooler months as the period when the household is busiest socially, which is the opposite of the assumption most revision plans make.

Ramadan has a separate effect and is worth planning a fortnight ahead. Schools run shortened days, so the afternoon returns earlier and the usual late slot often stops working because the household's rhythm has shifted. Many families move to a later evening session after Iftar or to a mid-morning weekend slot. Because lessons are online, the change is one line in a calendar rather than a renegotiation of anyone's driving route.

The long summer break is the other structural feature of the UAE year. For a Yas household it is the cheapest period to buy improvement in, because the commute disappears and the day has room in it. Holiday work is best bought as a defined block with a written target and a diagnostic at each end, rather than as general sessions to keep a student ticking over.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with assessed work
paragraphs: Every programme on this island carries work that is assessed as the student's own: internal assessments and the core in the Diploma, coursework in several IGCSE subjects, research tasks and projects on the American route. Academic-honesty rules treat a breach as malpractice and the consequences land on the student, not on whoever helped.

The line stated plainly. A tutor may teach the assessment criteria letter by letter with the marks attached to each. A tutor may test a proposed research question and say honestly whether it is narrow enough to generate usable data. A tutor may read a draft the student has produced and give feedback on structure, reasoning, evidence and clarity. A tutor may teach the underlying skills — referencing, uncertainty treatment, graph conventions, evaluation language — on a different example.

A tutor may not author any sentence that appears in a submission, provide text for the student to adapt, build the student's data set, or supply a model answer to the student's own question. Where a school's rules are tighter than the board's, the school's rules apply, and some schools limit external feedback on an assessed draft to one round. Ask about that at the start of a task rather than at the end.

For standardised tests the rule is simpler and absolute: a tutor teaches technique and supervises timed practice, and has no involvement of any kind during a live assessment. Any provider whose offer blurs that boundary is selling a risk that falls entirely on the student, and at least one operation in this market already sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price.

sections.heading: Starting from Yas Island
paragraphs: Send three things and the first conversation is useful: the school with board and syllabus codes, the most recent marked script with the teacher's annotations still on it, and an honest account of what the student actually does in the unsupervised hours. The third item is the one families hesitate over and the one that decides the plan, because the whole question on this page is what happens outside taught periods.

The trial is taught rather than sold. The tutor sets a short diagnostic, works it through live, and writes afterwards naming the specific losses found and what the first six weeks would target. For most Yas enquiries that plan is a supervised practice arrangement rather than content teaching, which is usually cheaper than the family expected and less dramatic than they feared.

Where the honest answer is that tutoring is not the right purchase, we say so. A student who is attending, engaged and simply not consolidating needs a structure and someone to look at the output, which can sometimes be built without a weekly paid lesson at all. We would rather tell you that and keep the fortnightly review than sell a term of teaching into a problem that is not a teaching problem.

On availability: the post-five weekday window is the most requested in Abu Dhabi and the first to fill, with January the tightest month. For a few niche Higher Level subjects the specialist may be based outside the UAE and teaching into a UAE evening; we say where a tutor is based whenever you ask. We claim no approval or accreditation from ADEK, the Ministry of Education or any examination board, because we hold none.
