ajman/al-jurf.programmesIntro: Three programmes cover almost every Al Jurf enquiry. The International GCSE years are where the tiering decision bites, the primary years are where a transfer is cheapest to fix, and the Diploma is where a commute out of Ajman usually starts. Each note below says what the programme does to a weekly plan in this district specifically.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Cambridge and Pearson
programmes.description: The qualification nearly every Al Jurf secondary student holds. Cambridge splits most subjects into a Core tier capped at grade 5 or C and an Extended tier reaching grade 9; Pearson runs Foundation and Higher. Papers are sat in a June series and a November series. The tier, the code and the series all appear on one document - the school's entry letter - and that document decides what a tutor should be teaching from the first session.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman's private schools fall under the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority, so there is no local inspection portal to search for an Al Jurf school's tiering practice. Ask the school which tier it enters by default and on what evidence. Schools serving the industrial-belt catchment often default to Core for borderline students, which is defensible and still worth questioning with a timed paper.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with units of work organised around transdisciplinary themes rather than subject chapters. Reporting is descriptive rather than numerical, which unsettles parents used to a percentage. The strength is the habit of explaining reasoning aloud; the gap that shows up later is arithmetic fluency, because practice volume is lower than in an Indian-curriculum or traditional British primary.
programmes.countryNote: PYP places near Al Jurf are limited, so families in the programme have usually chosen a campus towards the Emirates Road belt or over the Sharjah border. For a primary child the useful tuition is short and frequent: two half-hour sessions a week on number facts and written method beats one long session, and it is far easier to hold online than to arrange around a driver.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the service requirement. Each subject carries an internal assessment marked by the teacher against named criteria and then moderated externally. The load is not evenly spread: DP1 looks manageable and DP2 arrives with coursework deadlines, mock examinations and the May papers inside a few months of each other.
programmes.countryNote: A Diploma decision made in Al Jurf almost always means leaving Ajman for the school day, which turns a 4pm finish into a 5.30pm arrival. That single fact rules out most afternoon tuition and makes a fixed evening slot the only workable shape. Families who try to add a visiting tutor on top of that commute usually cancel by the third week of DP1.

ajman/al-jurf.subjectsIntro: The requests from this district cluster around the sciences and the commercial subjects rather than around literature, and the syllabus code matters as much as the subject name. Where a code is given below it is the one Ajman schools most often enter; check it against your own entry letter before a tutor plans anything.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics (0625)
subjects.description: Electricity and waves generate most of the questions we are asked here. Extended candidates meet quantitative treatment that Core candidates do not, and the alternative-to-practical option paper rewards students who have actually handled apparatus. A student who can rearrange a formula but cannot read a ticker-tape trace loses marks that revision notes never touch.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and the reactivity series are the recurring blockages. The paper rewards a written method: a correct answer with no working scores less than a nearly correct answer that shows the steps. Organic chemistry at Extended is a small topic with a large mark return, which makes it the first thing to fix in a short run-up.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology (0610)
subjects.description: The content volume tempts students into pure memorisation, and the paper then asks them to apply it to an unfamiliar organism or a data table. Genetics and transport in plants are where that strategy breaks. Work here is built around unseen data questions rather than around reading the textbook a second time.

subjects.name: Pearson International GCSE Mathematics (4MA1)
subjects.description: Two papers, both calculator-permitted, with a Higher tier reaching grade 9 and a Foundation tier capped well below it. Pearson's question styling differs from Cambridge's in ordering and in mark tariffs, so practice papers must come from the right board. Algebraic fractions, vectors and the harder probability questions carry the marks that separate a 6 from an 8.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Popular in this catchment because so many households run or work in a business. The subject looks easy and marks badly: candidates describe when the command term says analyse, and they answer about business in general rather than about the case study in front of them. Case-study discipline is most of the tutoring job.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510)
subjects.description: Reading, writing and listening with a speaking component, taken by students who use English at school and another language at home. The writing paper is scored on task fulfilment as much as on accuracy, so a grammatically clean answer in the wrong register still loses marks. Short, frequent writing practice with feedback beats grammar drilling.

subjects.name: IB Business Management
subjects.description: Tools, techniques and theories applied to a real organisation, with Higher Level adding depth and an extra paper. The internal assessment is a research project on an actual business issue, which means the research question has to be answerable with evidence a student can legitimately obtain. Getting that question narrow is the work of the first three sessions.

subjects.name: IB Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-permitted work throughout, which suits students heading for business or social science. Regression, hypothesis testing and the use of a graphic display calculator carry marks that are lost to presentation rather than to mathematics: an untitled graph or an unstated assumption costs the same as a wrong answer.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Compulsory in UAE private schools under federal rules regardless of the international curriculum a school is licensed to teach. For non-Arab students it is usually the subject with the weakest home support, and it does not count towards the five subjects in the British-track equivalency file - which is exactly why families under-resource it and then need it passed anyway.

sections.heading: Who lives in Al Jurf, and when they can actually study
paragraphs: Three populations share this district and none of them keeps school hours. The industrial belt runs rotas. The university quarter runs semesters. The residential streets run the school bus. Any tuition plan that assumes a 4pm to 6pm window because that is when children are free has ignored the question of who is supervising, and in Al Jurf the answer to that question changes week to week.

The practical consequence shows up in cancellations. A visiting tutor with a fixed Tuesday 5pm slot loses the week when a parent's shift changes, and after three of those the arrangement quietly ends. An online slot booked on a two-week rolling basis survives it, because moving a video call costs nothing and moving a driver costs an evening. That difference is worth more in this district than any teaching method, because the sessions that help are the ones that happen.

There is a second pattern here worth naming honestly. A household with an Ajman University student in it has cheap help available, and for a Year 8 who needs someone to sit next to them while they practise long multiplication, that is a sensible use of a relative. It becomes a problem at IGCSE Extended and at Higher Level, where the help needed is not explanation of content but knowledge of how a specific board awards marks. An undergraduate who got an A in school mathematics five years ago does not have that, and nobody involved can tell the difference until a mock comes back.

What these families should actually be buying is diagnostic accuracy. Not more hours, not more worksheets, but a clear statement of which question types their child loses marks on and what the fix is. That takes one timed paper and one honest conversation, and everything after it is cheaper because it is aimed.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the Year 10 decision that sets a ceiling
paragraphs: Every Cambridge IGCSE candidate is entered at a tier, and most Al Jurf parents learn which one after the fact. The Core tier covers a reduced subset of the syllabus and cannot be awarded above grade 5 or C. The Extended tier covers the full content and reaches grade 9. Pearson does the same thing with Foundation and Higher. Schools default borderline students to the lower tier for understandable reasons - a secured grade looks better than a risked one - and that default is worth testing rather than accepting.

The test is cheap. Give the student a past paper at the higher tier under timed conditions and mark it against the published scheme. The result is not a prediction, it is a map: which question types return marks already, which return partial marks, and which return nothing. A student scoring poorly across the whole paper is correctly placed at the lower tier. A student losing marks in two identifiable areas is not, and four weeks of work on those two areas changes the answer.

Timing is the part families miss. The entry is submitted months before the papers are sat. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series put final entries on 27 November 2026 for an exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027, with forecast grades due 27 February 2027 and results on Direct on 13 May. The shape is the same for the June and November series: the decision closes long before anyone feels any urgency about it.

The table sets the two tiers against each other on the things that actually differ. Note the last row especially - a tier can be changed up to the entry deadline, and after it cannot be changed at all.

sections.heading: The five-subject equivalency rule, read the way the ministry wrote it
paragraphs: Equivalency is the step that turns a foreign school certificate into something a UAE university will accept, and it is a Ministry of Education process rather than a school one. For British-curriculum leavers the requirements were set out in the ministry's clarification reported in July 2026: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The exclusion is the detail that costs families a year. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. They remain compulsory school subjects under federal rules, so a child studies them and must pass them, but they do not count towards the five. A student with six certificates, two of which are Arabic and Islamic education, has four that count. At least one tutoring site ranking for UAE queries tells parents the requirement is six IGCSE subjects, which is simply the wrong count, and a page that gets this right is more useful than a page that ranks.

The American track in the same clarification runs on test scores rather than subject counts: English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and at least 450 in SAT Mathematics, taken before applying. For the IB the clarification states no points threshold, and none appears on this page for that reason. If a provider quotes you an IB points figure for equivalency, ask which ministry page it came from.

IB Gram does not submit, process or guarantee equivalency for anybody. What tuition can do is make the subject arithmetic work: check in Year 9 which five subjects will carry the file, and make sure the grades in those five clear the line with a margin rather than exactly.

sections.heading: What the Al Jurf market charges, by provider model
paragraphs: Comparing tutoring prices in Ajman is hard because most providers do not publish one, and the ones that do compare themselves against an unnamed competitor rather than against a model. The useful comparison is by model: a freelance tutor, an agency, an international marketplace, a budget platform, a centre with premises, and a matching service. Each has a different cost structure, and the structure explains the price better than any claim about quality does.

The figures in the table are the providers' own, read in October 2026. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist support. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 for budget online work, Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 and specialist exam-year work at AED 200 to 450 and above. BartyED's premium tier reaches AED 650. None of those is IB Gram's price, and none of them is wrong for the thing it describes.

Two things to look for when you compare. First, whether travel is inside the rate: an in-home figure that looks competitive against an online one is usually carrying forty minutes of driving each way. Second, whether the provider will say anything about permits. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a MoHRE permit, and a provider who has never mentioned it is either not thinking about it or hoping you are not.

IB Gram's own position is deliberately not a price list: a free trial lesson with the tutor who would teach the course, then a consultation that prices the actual plan. The right number depends on the level, on how scarce the subject specialist is, and on how many weeks are left before the series.

sections.heading: Five ways to buy tuition in Al Jurf, side by side
paragraphs: The honest version of the home-tutor question starts with admitting that a visiting tutor is a real product with real advantages. Someone sitting beside a nine-year-old can take the pencil, watch the hand, and notice in two seconds what a webcam takes a minute to show. If that is what your child needs, buy it from somebody who offers it, and expect to pay AED 180 to 500 an hour for it with travel inside the figure.

IB Gram delivers to Al Jurf as one-to-one online tuition over live video. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service runs in India only. In a district where the local specialist pool is small and shared with every neighbouring district, matching by driving distance means matching to availability rather than to expertise, and for an Extended IGCSE or a Higher Level Diploma subject that trade is a bad one.

The table adds the three other options families in this district actually use, because the real choice is rarely binary. A tuition centre group class on the Sheikh Ammar Bin Humaid axis is cheaper per hour and useful for common content, and useless for an individual gap. An undergraduate relative is cheaper still and appropriate for a specific range of work. A school's own support class is usually included in the fees and worth taking before anything is paid for.

One boundary to state while on this subject. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that bars the same thing. Whatever emirate you are in, nobody should be marketing your child's own teacher to you as a private tutor, and we never do.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside a Cambridge timetable
paragraphs: Every UAE private school teaches these subjects whatever international curriculum it is licensed for. The federal position on u.ae is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must follow the ministry's general regulations. In Ajman that oversight is the Ministry of Education's directly; in Dubai the same requirement is administered by KHDA, whose published mandatory-subjects guidance is the most detailed public description of how it works and a reasonable guide to what any UAE school is doing.

That guidance is worth reading even from Ajman, because it explains things parents find puzzling. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for the two groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and the advice is that no mandatory-subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes. Teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education in Dubai need approval from KHDA to teach those subjects specifically.

One more line in that guidance constrains tutoring directly: for the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the ministry is prohibited. A tutor supporting Arabic as an additional language therefore works from the school's own materials and the ministry-approved content, not from an imported workbook that happens to be easier. Saying so is a limitation and also the only honest way to describe the work.

Where this bites for Al Jurf families is the equivalency arithmetic already covered. These subjects are compulsory and they do not count towards the five. Under-resourcing them is rational until the year a pass is needed, which is why a short weekly session from Year 9 costs less than an intensive in Year 11.

sections.heading: Is the tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work, not unregulated work, and the rule is specific. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE. The u.ae portal states that it is granted free of charge for two years and that eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

The same portal states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE will be subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published anywhere we could verify, and Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, so no figure appears on this page. A provider quoting you a specific fine is quoting something they have not read.

The application route is MoHRE's own service, listed as issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with no fees listed and a two-working-day completion time. That is short enough that a tutor who has not done it has chosen not to. For an Al Jurf family the practical move is to ask, once, and to notice the answer.

The table separates the categories because the eligibility rules differ and because one of them is not a tutor at all. A centre operating from premises needs a different instrument entirely - in Dubai, an educational services permit for a training institute from KHDA, with initial approval first and renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. An individual permit does not authorise running a centre, and IB Gram holds no regulator permit of any kind: it is an independent matching platform, not a licensed institute.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when there is a university student in the house
paragraphs: The academic-honesty line is usually explained as a rule about tutors. In Al Jurf it is more often tested by a relative. An older cousin at Ajman University, home in the evenings, helping with a Business Management internal assessment because they did something similar last year. Nobody in that room intends malpractice, and the work can still end up being partly somebody else's, which is exactly what the IB's rules are about.

The boundary does not depend on who is helping. A student's submitted work must be their own. Teaching the content, explaining a criterion, arguing about whether a research question is answerable, reading a finished draft and saying which criterion is under-served: all of that is legitimate support from a tutor, a teacher or a relative. Supplying sentences, reorganising somebody else's draft for them, handing over a dataset, or returning a document with new material in it is not, regardless of good intentions.

There is a practical test families can apply. Could the student explain, unprompted, why each choice in the work was made? A supervisor is required to see drafts and to authenticate the submission, and a conversation with a student who cannot account for their own method is how malpractice surfaces. The consequence falls on the student, which is the part worth repeating in a house where the help is free and well-meant.

The same rule covers materials. Past papers, mark schemes and syllabus documents belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. They are referenced and linked, not reproduced or handed out in bundles, and a provider offering a library of unreleased material is offering an exposure rather than an advantage.

sections.heading: Booking around a rota, and what we say when nobody is free
paragraphs: Scheduling is the part of this service that fails most often in Al Jurf, so it is worth describing the mechanics. Slots are held on Gulf Standard Time and booked on a two-week rolling basis for households that need it, with the same tutor each time. Late-evening sessions are available because a 9pm start is the only workable time for some rotas. Friday and Saturday sessions are available for the same reason. None of that requires a conversation about travel.

Ramadan changes the shape of the week rather than the amount of work. School days shorten, energy moves to after Iftar, and the sensible plan is shorter sessions more often, with the heavier cognitive work moved earlier in the day where a family's routine allows. Revision timetables built in February for a May or June series need rewriting around that window rather than ignoring it, and the rewrite is part of the plan rather than an interruption to it.

On availability the position is stated before money changes hands. Specialists in the smaller Diploma subjects and at Higher Level are scarce, and scarcer in the northern emirates than in Dubai. If nobody teaching that syllabus at that level has a slot in the window you need, you are told, and the alternative offered may be a specialist working from outside the UAE on Gulf Standard Time. That is disclosed at matching rather than discovered later.

What to ask any provider in this district, in order: which syllabus code and tier will you teach to, what will you do in the first two sessions, how will I know in six weeks whether this is working, and what happens if the tutor is wrong for my child. Four questions, and the answers are usually enough to decide.

process.title: Tell us the tier, not just the subject
process.description: Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher, and the syllabus code. All three sit on the school's exam-entry letter. A tutor who knows the tier can plan from the first session; a tutor who does not spends two sessions working it out from the student's exercise book.

process.title: Free trial lesson at the time you would actually use
process.description: If 9pm on a Thursday is the slot that fits your rota, the trial happens at 9pm on a Thursday. Testing the arrangement at a convenient hour and then discovering the real slot does not work is how three weeks get wasted in this district.

process.title: Timed paper, marked, with the breakdown written down
process.description: The first or second session is a past paper under exam conditions from the correct board and tier, marked against the published scheme. What comes back is a list of question types with marks attached, which is a document you can take to the school rather than an impression.

process.title: Rolling schedule with a six-week decision point
process.description: Slots are confirmed a fortnight ahead so a shift change does not cost a lesson. At six weeks the plan is checked against the written breakdown: what moved, what did not, and whether the subject or the tutor needs changing. The decision is yours and the evidence is on paper.

whyPoints.title: A schedule that survives a shift change
whyPoints.description: Rolling two-week booking, late-evening slots and weekend availability, because the most common reason tuition stops working in Al Jurf is a rota, not a tutor. Moving a video call costs nothing; moving a driver costs an evening and eventually the arrangement.

whyPoints.title: The tier question answered with evidence
whyPoints.description: A timed paper at the higher tier, marked against the published scheme, before the entry deadline closes the option. That is a four-session piece of work and it is the single highest-return thing a Year 10 family in this district can buy.

whyPoints.title: The permit rule quoted with its resolution number
whyPoints.description: Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, a MoHRE permit granted free of charge for two years, and no invented fine figures because none are published. You can check every part of that for yourself, which is the point of writing it down.

whyPoints.title: Rates attributed to whoever published them
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here names its source and the month it was read. Of the pages ranking for Ajman tutoring queries, several publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars. Attribution is the difference between a figure and a claim.

whyPoints.title: The honest list of alternatives, including free ones
whyPoints.description: The school's own support class and a competent relative are on the comparison table because for some students they are the right answer. A page that only compares itself to a straw man is selling, and a family can tell.

faqs.question: Do you send a home tutor to an Al Jurf address in Ajman?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers tuition to Al Jurf families as one-to-one lessons over live video, and home visiting is a service we run in India only. Local providers do offer visits and charge roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the rate, so if someone in the room is what your child needs, that market exists. The reason we work the other way is the size of the specialist pool: Al Jurf shares a small local pool with every neighbouring district, and matching by driving distance means matching on availability rather than on subject expertise.

faqs.question: My daughter's school entered her for IGCSE Core. Can that still be changed?
faqs.answer: Up to the board's final entry deadline, yes, and after it, no. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series put final entries on 27 November 2026, months before the exam period, and the June and November series follow the same pattern. The way to argue the case is evidence rather than opinion: a timed Extended paper marked against the published scheme, showing which question types already return marks. Take that to the school. A student losing marks in two identifiable areas is usually misplaced at Core; a student losing them everywhere is not.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the UAE equivalency certificate actually count?
faqs.answer: Five. The Ministry of Education's clarification, reported in July 2026, requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One competing tutoring site tells UAE parents the figure is six, which is wrong. Check the current wording on moe.gov.ae before relying on it, because this is the ministry's process and the rules can be updated without any tutoring provider noticing.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic education included in the equivalency subject count?
faqs.answer: They are not. The ministry's clarification states explicitly that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. They are still compulsory school subjects under federal rules, so your child studies them and needs to pass them, but they sit outside the count. The planning consequence matters in Year 9: a student taking six subjects, two of which are Arabic and Islamic education, has only four that count towards the file. Count the qualifying subjects before the options form is signed rather than when the university application is being prepared.

faqs.question: What does a private tutor in Al Jurf charge per hour in 2026?
faqs.answer: Rates read in October 2026 put budget online work at roughly AED 33 to 150 an hour, a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300, an in-home visit at AED 180 to 500 with travel included, and specialist IB, IGCSE or A-Level support at AED 200 to 450 and above. Those figures come from providers' own pages, including Unitors from AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB, TutorChase at AED 270, EdFlik from AED 45, Tutopiya from AED 33, and Bestimate's Dubai rate table. IB Gram prices after a free trial lesson and a consultation rather than from a list.

faqs.question: Does the MoHRE private tutor permit cost anything, and how long does it last?
faqs.answer: The u.ae government portal states that the private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is applied for through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system; the service page lists a two-working-day completion time and no fees. Anyone tutoring privately without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat a specific amount quoted at you as unverified. A tutor who has not applied has chosen not to, given how short the process is.

faqs.question: Can my nephew, who studies at Ajman University, tutor my son legally?
faqs.answer: University students are listed among those eligible for the MoHRE private tuition work permit, so with the permit in place the arrangement is legitimate. Two cautions, though. A permit says somebody may tutor; it says nothing about whether they know how a particular board awards marks, and that is most of what an exam-year student is paying for. And if the work involves a Diploma internal assessment, a well-meaning relative is the most common route to accidental malpractice, because the help slides from explaining to improving without anybody deciding to cross a line.

faqs.question: Can my child's own schoolteacher tutor him privately in the evenings?
faqs.answer: That is the one arrangement to avoid. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Those rules exist because of the obvious conflict: the person teaching the class, setting the internal assessment and authenticating the work should not also be paid privately by the family. We never market a child's own teacher as a private tutor, in any emirate.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre group class near Sheikh Ammar Bin Humaid Street worth it?
faqs.answer: For revising content the whole group needs, often yes, and the per-student rate is lower than any one-to-one option. For an individual gap it is the wrong instrument: a class of eight moves at one pace and your child's two weak question types are not that pace. A reasonable pattern is a centre class for broad revision plus a short one-to-one block aimed at the specific losses a marked paper identified. Note also that a centre operating from premises needs a different permit from an individual tutor, which is worth asking about.

faqs.question: We work rotating shifts in Al Jurf. Can lessons move week to week?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for households here that is the default rather than an exception. Slots are confirmed about a fortnight ahead with the same tutor each time, so a shift change moves the appointment instead of cancelling it. Late-evening starts are available, as are Friday and Saturday sessions, all on Gulf Standard Time. The written note after each session matters more in this arrangement than in a conventional one, because the parent who booked the lesson is often not the parent who was home for it.

faqs.question: How do sessions work during Ramadan for an Al Jurf family?
faqs.answer: School days shorten and the family's energy moves to after Iftar, so the plan changes shape rather than volume. Shorter sessions more often works better than the usual weekly hour: three half-hours beat one ninety-minute block when a student is fasting. Where a household's routine allows, the heavier analytical work goes earlier in the day and lighter consolidation goes to the evening. A revision timetable written in February for a May or June series should be redrafted around the Ramadan weeks rather than assuming they will behave like ordinary ones.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a Cambridge Core paper and an Extended paper?
faqs.answer: Core papers assess a defined reduced subset of the syllabus and cannot be awarded above grade 5 or C. Extended papers assess the full syllabus, including the harder topics, and reach grade 9. The difference is not simply that Extended questions are harder: some Extended content is absent from Core teaching altogether, which is why moving a student up a tier mid-year means teaching the missing subset before anything else. Pearson's Foundation and Higher tiers work on the same principle with different names and a different paper structure.

faqs.question: Can a tutor look at my son's Business Management internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Yes, within the limits the IB sets. A tutor can teach the tools and theories the project draws on, explain each assessment criterion and the marks attached to it, press on whether the research question is answerable with evidence he can legitimately obtain, and read a draft he has already written to say which criterion is under-served. A tutor cannot supply sentences, restructure his work on his behalf, or add content to the document. Everything in a session should be something his school supervisor could see without concern, because the supervisor must see drafts and authenticate the submission.

faqs.question: Is online tuition in Al Jurf as useful as someone sitting next to my child?
faqs.answer: It depends on the child's age and the subject's scarcity. For a seven-year-old learning written subtraction, somebody in the room is better. For an Extended IGCSE science or a Higher Level Diploma subject, the specialist matters more than the proximity, and the specialist probably does not live in Ajman. Screen-shared work also leaves a record: the annotated document stays with the family, which a parent coming off a late shift can read at midnight. And the slot survives a traffic evening on the Emirates Road, which a visiting arrangement does not.

ajman/al-jurf.closingHeading: Two documents and one timed paper
ajman/al-jurf.closingBody: Everything on this page reduces to three practical steps for an Al Jurf family. Get the school's exam-entry letter, so you know the board, the code and the tier. Count the subjects that will carry the equivalency file, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, while there is still time to change them. And have your child sit one timed paper at the higher tier, marked properly, before the board's final entry deadline closes the question. Lessons for Al Jurf run one-to-one over live video, on a slot that moves with your week rather than against it.

intro.heading: In Al Mowaihat the calendar decides more than the tutor does
paragraphs: Al Mowaihat 1, 2 and 3 sit between central Ajman and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, villa streets with reasonable space and an unusually wide spread of school destinations. Some children go south into the old city, some east to the Emirates Road belt campuses, some across the Sharjah line. The one thing every household shares is that the day is bracketed by a bus, and the brackets are tighter than most tutoring advice assumes.

Work the hours out and the planning problem becomes obvious. A bus leaving Al Mowaihat at about 6.45am means a child is awake by 6am. A return around 4.15pm, later if the route goes to Sharjah, means food and twenty minutes of nothing before anything useful happens. The usable block starts at roughly 5.30pm and runs to about 9pm, and inside it sits homework, independent reading, coursework and anything a family has paid for. Three and a half hours, five days a week.

That is the daily frame. The annual frame matters more and almost nobody writes it down. The decisions that change a result are not made in the week a parent starts worrying; they are made in September, when the entry letter is issued and the tier is set, in late November when a board's final entry deadline closes, in the three weeks after a mock script comes back, and in the summer before a course starts. Miss those windows and the best tutor in the emirate is doing remedial work at the worst possible rate.

So this page is a calendar before it is a service description. The academic year is laid out window by window, with what happens in school, what a family should do, and what each window is already too late for. Then mock season is treated properly, because a mock script is the most informative document a family will see all year and most are filed unread. Then session length and frequency by age, and what an exam-term intensive actually costs in AED.

Ramadan gets its own section rather than a sentence. School days shorten, routines shift to after Iftar, and a revision timetable written in February that ignores those weeks is abandoned in the first one. So does the Friday and Saturday weekend, which in a commuting district is the only reliable window for work that needs an adult present and a decision to be made.

On delivery, once and plainly: tuition for Al Mowaihat families runs one-to-one online over live video on booked slots. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses - home visiting is a service we offer in India only - and in a district whose evening block is three and a half hours long, an arrangement that adds nobody's drive to it is the point rather than the compromise.

ajman/al-mowaihat.programmesIntro: Three programmes appear in these streets, and the calendar runs differently for each. The International GCSE year is deadline-driven, the Diploma is coursework-driven, and the Diploma core runs for two years with almost no timetable attached to it at all.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Cambridge and Pearson
programmes.description: Two years of teaching ending in a published series, with the tier fixed at entry and entries closing months before the papers. Cambridge runs June and November series and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable; its exams officers' guide states plainly that using the wrong zone version is the candidate's own risk. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series that can still be revised.
programmes.countryNote: Because Ajman's private schools answer to the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate authority, there is no local portal where an Al Mowaihat parent can check how a school handles entries or how much timed practice it builds in. The substitute is the exams officer, in September: ask for the zone-specific timetable, the final entry deadline and the tier, and put all three in a calendar the household can actually see.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, each with an internal assessment the student designs and writes. The annual rhythm is uneven: DP1 feels manageable and DP2 arrives with coursework deadlines, mock examinations and the written papers inside a few months. The students who cope are the ones whose coursework decisions were taken in DP1, not the ones who work hardest in the final term.
programmes.countryNote: A Diploma student in Al Mowaihat is commuting, usually east to the Emirates Road belt or across to Sharjah, which pushes the evening block later still. The practical consequence is that DP2 support has to be fortnightly and substantial rather than weekly and thin: a ninety-minute slot that holds a marked component and its correction does more than two sixty-minute slots that hold neither.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: A 4,000-word independent essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition, and a CAS portfolio with reflective requirements, all running alongside six subjects. The core carries bonus points and conditions that affect the diploma award. What makes it hard is not difficulty but scheduling: it has almost no timetable, so it loses every collision with a subject deadline.
programmes.countryNote: The core is the part of the Diploma that a commuting Al Mowaihat household should calendar first, precisely because nothing else will. Put the Extended Essay research question in the DP1 spring, the reflections in a weekly five-minute slot rather than a DP2 weekend, and the Theory of Knowledge essay planning before the subject mocks rather than after them.

ajman/al-mowaihat.subjectsIntro: The subject mix here is broad because the school destinations are, so this grid spans both boards and both Diploma levels. The descriptions say where the marks move in an exam term, since that is what a calendar-led plan has to target.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Case studies are only worth marks if they are precise: named places, figures, dates. Candidates write generic answers about development or migration and score in the lower bands. Map and graph skills are high-return and quick to drill, which makes geography one of the best subjects to target in a short run-up to the papers.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE History (0470)
subjects.description: Source questions follow a predictable structure and reward technique over knowledge: utility, reliability, cross-referencing. Students who have practised the structure gain marks reliably; those who summarise the source lose them just as reliably. Essay questions need a judgement sustained through the answer rather than announced at the end.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science (0653)
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed into a single award, which means breadth of coverage with limited depth and a paper that samples widely. Students who revise by topic discover their coverage is thinner than they thought. Past-paper question sets are a better revision instrument here than any textbook, because they show the sampling pattern.

subjects.name: Pearson International GCSE Biology (4BI1)
subjects.description: Practical understanding is assessed inside the written papers rather than separately, so candidates must reason about apparatus and method on paper. The extended-answer questions carry marks that are lost to structure rather than to knowledge: a list of facts where a linked explanation was wanted scores well below its content.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Marks are concentrated in a handful of recurring question types, which is why a mock script is more useful than a syllabus checklist. The non-calculator paper separates students who have practised written method from those who have not, and that difference is built in weeks rather than taught in an hour.

subjects.name: IB History
subjects.description: Source paper, essay papers and, at Higher Level, a regional depth study with an additional paper. The historical investigation has a strict allocation across its sections, and candidates routinely over-write the narrative section and leave the evaluation of sources thin, which is precisely where the marks sit.

subjects.name: IB Biology
subjects.description: The largest recall load in the group, examined through application to unfamiliar material and unseen data. Revision by re-reading feels productive and moves little. A calendar-led plan uses retrieval sets through the autumn and switches to full timed components from February, which is also what the individual investigation analysis rewards.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition on three objects and a prescribed-title essay, both marked against published criteria and both easy to leave late because nothing else in the timetable protects them. The essay needs real examples analysed rather than asserted, and the examples are better collected across DP1 than hunted for in a DP2 weekend.

subjects.name: IB Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-permitted work. Marks are lost in presentation rather than in mathematics: an unstated assumption, an unlabelled model, a regression quoted without interpretation. Those are fixable in a fortnight once a marked component has shown which of them the student actually does.

ajman/al-mowaihat.modesIntro: Three booking shapes, each tied to a part of the year rather than to a preference. Buying the wrong shape for the window is the commonest way families in this district spend money without moving a grade.

modes.title: Autumn content block
modes.description: September to November, weekly, aimed at content rather than technique. This is the window in which a gap can still be taught rather than patched, because the course is early and nothing is urgent. It is also the window in which the entry tier is still open, so a diagnostic here feeds a decision that closes in late November.

The script is read for question types rather than for a grade, the two heaviest losses are worked twice a week, and a second timed component checks whether they moved.

modes.description: From February to the series, ninety minutes every fortnight per subject rather than sixty minutes every week. The longer slot holds a full component and its correction, which is the pairing that moves marks; a shorter weekly slot usually holds one or the other and the correction gets postponed indefinitely.

sections.heading: The Al Mowaihat school run, hour by hour
paragraphs: This district has an unusually wide spread of school destinations for its size, which is what makes the hours worth setting out rather than assuming. A child going east to the Emirates Road belt is on a bus at about 6.45am and back around 4.15pm. One going south into central Ajman leaves slightly later and returns slightly earlier, though the morning run behaves worse than the distance suggests. One crossing into Sharjah for Muwaileh or University City leaves before 6.30am and is not home until after 4.45pm.

Add the two adjustments that every workable plan needs. Food and a decompression gap after a nine-hour day, which is twenty to thirty minutes for most teenagers and non-negotiable for all of them. And the supervising adult's arrival, where supervision is needed at all. Those two numbers, not the child's return time, decide the earliest slot that will still be running in week five.

What comes out of it for Al Mowaihat is a usable evening block from about 5.30pm to 9pm for the eastern routes, and from 6pm for the Sharjah routes. Three to three and a half hours, holding homework, reading, coursework and tuition. The arithmetic is why the plans on this page are finite and why DP2 support here is fortnightly and long rather than weekly and short: a ninety-minute slot every two weeks takes less from the block than two sixty-minute slots and delivers the component-plus-correction pairing that actually moves marks.

One further local point. Al Mowaihat sits close enough to Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road that families consider driving to a tuition centre in the city or east along the belt. Twenty to thirty minutes each way, twice, out of a three-and-a-half-hour block is an hour of the week's most valuable time spent in a car, and from February a twice-weekly pattern makes that two hours. That calculation is in a table further down, because it is the decision families in this district most often get wrong.

sections.heading: The academic year as a planning calendar
paragraphs: Almost every expensive tutoring decision in this district is a timing decision made late. A family that would have spent six sessions in October on a content gap spends a term in March on remediation at a higher rate. A family that could have changed an entry tier in November discovers in February that the grade is capped. Neither is a teaching failure; both are calendar failures, and a calendar is cheap to produce.

The table below is that calendar, written for an Ajman family. The fourth column is the one worth reading first, because it names what each window is already too late for. Those are the deadlines nobody announces: tier changes close with the board's final entry date, a research question cannot be narrowed after it has been written up, and new content taught in the last six weeks before a paper is not retained well enough to be worth the hours.

Board dates in it come from the boards themselves. Cambridge published 27 November 2026 as the final entry date for its March 2027 series, with the exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. Pearson's International GCSE November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026; its June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026 and its November 2025 results on 22 January 2026.

No IB dates appear in the table. The IB's own site could not be read directly for this project, so no IB session, upload or results date is published anywhere on these pages. Secondary sources circulate and they are not sources. Ask the school's diploma coordinator for the session calendar and build the family calendar around that, treating any tutoring site that states IB dates without citing ibo.org as a site that guessed.

sections.heading: Mock season: the three weeks nobody plans
paragraphs: A mock script is the most informative document a family will see in an academic year, and most are filed unread. The grade gets discussed, the comment gets read, and the script goes into a bag. Inside that script is the only honest, question-level data available before the real papers: which question types returned full marks, which returned partial marks, and which returned nothing at all.

The first thing to do is get it back. Schools will usually return a marked script with the mark scheme if asked, and almost nobody asks. Then read it for question types rather than for topics. A student who lost nine marks across three extended-response questions and two marks across the whole of the rest of the paper has one problem, not five, and it is a structural problem rather than a knowledge one.

The second thing is to act inside about three weeks. After that the term has moved on, the student has forgotten the specifics of what they wrote, and the emotional charge has gone out of it in a way that makes the correction feel academic. Three weeks of twice-weekly work on the two heaviest losses, followed by a second timed component to check, converts a mock from a verdict into a plan. That is the whole intervention and it is finite.

The table separates the mocks because they tell you different things. An autumn mock reliably shows what has not been learnt and says nothing useful about exam performance. A spring mock shows pacing and question-type weakness and still says nothing reliable about the final grade, because boundaries are set after marking against that cohort. A DP2 mock shows paper-by-paper weakness against the weightings, which is exactly what a revision order should be built from.

sections.heading: Ramadan and Eid: what changes, and how to plan for it
paragraphs: Ramadan falls inside the UAE academic year and it changes the working week materially. School days shorten, so children are home earlier than the hours set out above. Working hours shift, so a parent may be home earlier too. Energy and appetite move to after Iftar, and the late evening becomes social in a way it is not for the rest of the year. A revision plan that treats those weeks as ordinary is not a plan.

The adjustments are small and specific. Shorter sessions, more often: thirty to forty minutes three times a week rather than ninety minutes once, because concentration while fasting is a genuine constraint and pretending otherwise wastes the slot. Heavier analytical work moved to whatever part of the day a particular household actually has energy in, which varies far more between families than any general rule can capture. And an explicit decision about the Eid break, which is a holiday rather than a revision week and works better when it is planned as one.

There is an opportunity in it too, and it is the one most families miss. The shortened school day is the only period in the year when an afternoon slot genuinely works in a commuting district. A child home by early afternoon can take a session when they are still fresh rather than at the end of a long evening. Families who rewrite the timetable for those weeks often get more out of them than out of an ordinary month.

The practical mechanics: slots are held on Gulf Standard Time, the timetable is rewritten for the Ramadan weeks rather than suspended, and the plan for the period after Eid is agreed before it starts, because the gap between Eid and a May or June series is short and is where the final revision actually happens. None of this requires anybody to travel, which is the other reason the shape is easy to change at short notice.

sections.heading: The Friday and Saturday weekend, and what belongs in it
paragraphs: In a district where the weekday evening block is three and a half hours and partly unsupervised, the weekend is the household's most underused academic asset. Friday afternoons and Saturdays are the only times a working parent is reliably present and unhurried, and that changes what kind of work is possible rather than simply adding hours.

Some work needs a decision rather than practice. Choosing an Extended Essay research question. Deciding whether to argue an entry tier with the school. Reading a mock script together and agreeing what the next three weeks will target. Agreeing a Theory of Knowledge essay title. All of those go badly at 8.30pm on a Wednesday with a tired student and a parent who has just got in, and go well on a Saturday morning.

Other work needs an uninterrupted stretch. A full timed component takes the length of the paper plus the marking conversation, which is more than a weekday evening can give without displacing homework. Putting the sat component on a Saturday and the correction session on the following Tuesday evening splits it in the right place: the sitting needs time, the correction needs focus.

What should stay on weekday evenings is ordinary practice and checking - the retrieval sets, the question-type drilling, the short coursework feedback. Dividing the week that way uses the household's real availability instead of fighting it, and it is the single scheduling change that most improves whether a plan survives a term in this district.

sections.heading: Session length and frequency by age and phase
paragraphs: Session length is usually set by a provider's billing convenience and should be set by the student. A six-year-old and a DP2 candidate have opposite requirements, and the familiar one-hour-weekly default is wrong for both of them. Getting the shape right costs nothing and changes how much of each paid hour is actually working.

At the young end the binding constraint is attention. Half an hour of focused practice three times a week builds number-fact automaticity that a single hour does not, because the gaps between sessions are where forgetting happens and frequency is what fights it. The second half of a long session with an eight-year-old is spent managing fatigue, which is a poor use of any rate.

At the exam end the constraint is the component. A full timed paper plus the conversation that makes it useful does not fit into sixty minutes, so a weekly hour in DP2 tends to hold the sitting or the correction and postpone the other. Ninety minutes fortnightly per subject holds both, and two subjects then fill alternate weeks without consuming more of the evening block than a weekly pattern would.

The middle years are the exception that argues for blocks rather than a standing arrangement. Habits at that age form in weeks: four sessions on criterion reading or on study method change how a student works for a year, and a weekly session continued past that point is paying to maintain something that no longer needs maintaining. The table sets all of this out, and the fourth column explains why each shape is what it is.

sections.heading: What an exam-term intensive costs in AED
paragraphs: Intensives are where families in this district spend most, and the figures are worth seeing as weekly patterns rather than as hourly rates. The market's published numbers, read in October 2026: Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200; TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist support; Bestimate's Dubai rate table gives AED 200 to 450 and above for specialist exam-year work and AED 180 to 350 for in-home visits; EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 at the budget end.

Converted into monthly commitments, Bestimate's own estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Packages circulating in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions, with travel inside the second figure.

The table puts the patterns side by side so the arithmetic is visible before February rather than after it. Two observations that save money. First, the budget band is appropriate for supervising practice and inappropriate for marking a Higher Level component, and buying it for the second job is a false economy that shows up in a mock. Second, an in-home intensive carries two journeys per session inside the rate, which from February at twice weekly is a substantial amount of somebody's time being paid for.

IB Gram publishes no rate card here. There is a free trial lesson with the tutor who would teach the course and a consultation that prices the actual plan, because the answer depends on the level, on how scarce the specialist is, and on how many weeks are left on the calendar this page is built around.

sections.heading: From Al Mowaihat: online against driving to a tuition centre
paragraphs: This page targets a home-tutor search and the honest answer has two halves. Visiting tutors work in Ajman and charge roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the rate, and for a young child or a household without a quiet room they are often the better product. IB Gram does not offer that service anywhere in the UAE; home visiting runs in India only. The more interesting comparison for Al Mowaihat, though, is not online against in-home. It is online against the thing families here actually do, which is drive to a tuition centre.

The centre option is genuinely attractive on price. A group class costs less per student hour than any one-to-one arrangement, the timetable is fixed, and the teaching is often good. What it cannot do is move the specific marks a mock script identified, because a class of eight proceeds at the group's pace on the syllabus rather than on your child's two weak question types. For broad content revision that is fine. For a targeted exam term it is the wrong instrument.

Then there is the arithmetic the price hides. Twenty to thirty minutes each way from Al Mowaihat, twice per session, out of an evening block that is three and a half hours long. At one session a week in the autumn that is tolerable. From February at twice weekly it is two hours a week in a car, taken from the hours in which independent practice has to happen, and independent practice is what actually converts teaching into marks.

The table applies what we have called the February test to each row: does this arrangement still work when the pattern doubles? That is the question worth asking in October, because by February the pattern has doubled and changing it is another disruption in the worst possible month.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when a deadline and a holiday collide
paragraphs: Calendar pressure is what pushes coursework across the academic-honesty line, and the collisions are predictable. An internal deadline a few days after a holiday. A Theory of Knowledge essay due in the same fortnight as two subject mocks. An Extended Essay draft expected in a week when the family is travelling. Nobody plans to break a rule; a week disappears and somebody helpful fills the gap.

The rule itself does not move with the calendar. Submitted work must be the student's own, a school supervisor must see drafts, and the submission is authenticated. What a tutor, a parent or an older sibling may legitimately do is teach the content, read the criteria aloud and explain what each one rewards with the marks named, press on whether a question is answerable with available evidence, and give feedback on work the student has already written. What none of them may do is supply sentences, reorganise a draft on the student's behalf, provide a dataset, or return a document with new material in it.

The protection is scheduling rather than willpower. Put the coursework decisions in DP1 and the drafting before the holiday rather than after it, and keep the reflections in a weekly five-minute habit rather than a DP2 weekend. A student who has a draft three weeks early does not need rescuing, and a family that has planned the collisions does not meet them.

Two market notes for a family buying support in an exam term. There are providers selling completed Internal Assessments to UAE families at fixed prices, and buying one is malpractice under IB rules with the consequence falling on the student. And board materials - syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes - belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, so they are cited and linked rather than distributed in bundles.

process.title: Send the entry letter and the mock script
process.description: Two documents answer most questions. The exam-entry letter gives the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the series. The most recent marked script gives the question types that lose marks. Together they produce a plan in one session rather than in three weeks of getting to know the student.

process.title: Free trial at the slot the calendar allows
process.description: For an eastern-route household that is about 5.30pm, for a Sharjah-route household about 6pm, and for a DP2 student often a Saturday. The trial runs with the tutor who would take the course, at that hour, because a slot that works only in theory fails in week five.

process.title: Build the year's calendar in week one
process.description: Entry deadline, zone-specific timetable, coursework internal dates, mock windows and the series itself, taken from the exams officer and the boards' own pages. The weekly plan is then derived from that calendar rather than from whatever feels urgent in a given week.

process.title: Review three weeks after each mock
process.description: The review point is set by the calendar rather than by a billing cycle. Three weeks after a script comes back, a second timed component shows whether the two targeted losses moved. If they did not, the subject, the tutor or the approach changes, and that decision is yours with the evidence in front of you.

whyPoints.title: The year written down before the hours are sold
whyPoints.description: Entry deadlines, mock windows, Ramadan, the series and the summer block, with what each window is already too late for. Most of the money wasted on tutoring in this district is wasted on timing rather than on teaching, and a calendar is cheap.

whyPoints.title: Mock scripts read for question types
whyPoints.description: A grade is a verdict and a script is a plan. We ask for the script with the mark scheme, list the losses by question type with marks attached, and work only on the two heaviest for three weeks. Then a second component checks it.

whyPoints.title: Session shapes set by the student
whyPoints.description: Half-hours for primary, four-session blocks in the middle years, ninety minutes fortnightly in DP2 so a component and its correction both happen. The familiar weekly hour is a billing convention, not a pedagogical one, and it is wrong at both ends.

whyPoints.title: The driving cost made explicit
whyPoints.description: A tuition centre is cheaper per hour and costs twenty to thirty minutes each way from Al Mowaihat, which from February at twice weekly is two hours a week taken out of the block where independent practice has to happen.

whyPoints.title: Board dates from the boards, and no IB dates at all
whyPoints.description: Cambridge's and Pearson's published key dates are quoted with the board named. No IB session or results date appears here, because the IB's own site could not be read for this project and a guessed date is worse than an absent one.

faqs.question: Do tutors travel to homes in Al Mowaihat, Ajman?
faqs.answer: Some local providers do, at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the rate. IB Gram does not: lessons for Al Mowaihat families run one-to-one over live video, and home visiting is a service we offer in India only. The district-specific reason is the evening block. A bus back at 4.15pm and a usable window to about 9pm leaves three and a half hours for homework, coursework and tuition, and an arrangement that adds somebody's drive at both ends takes more of it than the lesson does.

faqs.question: When is the right month to start tutoring for a June series?
faqs.answer: October, if the issue is content, and February if the issue is technique. Those are different problems with different windows. Content taught in October can still be practised and consolidated before the papers; content taught in April is not retained well enough to be worth the hours. Technique work - pacing, question types, extended answers - responds quickly and is best done against marked components from February. The one month to avoid starting from scratch in is the last six weeks, when the only sensible activity is timed practice and correction.

faqs.question: What should we actually do with my daughter's mock script?
faqs.answer: Get it back from the school with the mark scheme, which they will usually provide if asked, and read it for question types rather than topics. List every loss with the marks attached. You will typically find two recurring question types account for most of it, which is a structural problem rather than five knowledge gaps. Then work those two twice a week for three weeks and sit a second timed component to check. After about three weeks the script stops being useful, because the term has moved and the specifics have faded.

faqs.question: Can we still change my son's entry tier in February?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not for that series. Tiers are fixed at entry, and entries close months before the papers: Cambridge published 27 November 2026 as the final entry date for its March 2027 series, which ran 3 February to 4 March 2027. The practical conclusion is that the tier conversation belongs in October of Year 10 or Year 11, supported by a timed paper at the higher tier marked against the published scheme. Ask the school in writing which tier your son is entered for, and ask in the autumn.

faqs.question: How do we plan revision around Ramadan in an Ajman school year?
faqs.answer: Rewrite the timetable for those weeks rather than suspending it. Shorter sessions more often - thirty to forty minutes three times a week instead of ninety minutes once - because concentration while fasting is a real constraint. Move the heavier analytical work to whatever part of the day your household actually has energy in. Treat Eid as a holiday and agree the post-Eid plan before it starts, since the gap to a May or June series is short. The shortened school day is also the one period when an afternoon slot genuinely works here.

faqs.question: Are Friday and Saturday sessions better for an Al Mowaihat family?
faqs.answer: For some kinds of work, clearly yes. The weekend is when a working parent is reliably present and unhurried, which makes it right for anything that needs a decision rather than practice: choosing an Extended Essay question, reviewing a mock script together, agreeing whether to argue a tier. It is also the only window long enough for a full timed component. Keep the weekday evenings for drilling, retrieval sets and short feedback, and split a component and its correction across a Saturday and the following Tuesday.

faqs.question: Why would a ninety-minute fortnightly slot beat a weekly hour in DP2?
faqs.answer: Because a full component and the conversation that makes it useful do not fit in an hour. A weekly sixty-minute slot in DP2 usually holds the sitting or the correction and postpones the other, and the postponed half is the one where marks move. Ninety minutes every fortnight per subject holds both, and two subjects then fill alternate weeks without taking more from the evening block than a weekly pattern would. For a commuting student that arithmetic matters more than the total number of hours bought.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre on the Emirates Road belt cheaper than online tutoring?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes, because the rate is shared across the group. Per mark moved, often not. A class of eight follows the syllabus at the group's pace, which cannot chase the two question types a mock script identified for your child. Add twenty to thirty minutes each way from Al Mowaihat, twice per session, out of a three-and-a-half-hour evening block, and from February at twice weekly that is two hours a week in a car taken from the time independent practice needs. Try the school's own support sessions first; they are already paid for.

faqs.question: How much does an exam-term intensive cost per month in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Using the market's own published figures read in October 2026: Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Packages in this market include about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions with travel inside the figure. Hourly, specialist support runs AED 200 to 450 and above. IB Gram prices after a free trial and a consultation.

faqs.question: Which direction does the school bus go, and does it change the slot?
faqs.answer: It changes it by about half an hour, which is enough to matter. Al Mowaihat households send children east to the Emirates Road belt, south into central Ajman, and across to Muwaileh or University City in Sharjah. Eastern routes return around 4.15pm, so 5.30pm works once food and a decompression gap are allowed for. Sharjah routes return after 4.45pm, which puts the earliest workable slot at about 6pm. Book against the actual return time rather than a nominal school finish, and add the twenty minutes.

faqs.question: Does my child need tutoring in the summer holidays?
faqs.answer: If there is a content gap heading into the next year, the summer is the cheapest and most effective time to close it, and that is the strongest case for holiday work. Six to ten weeks of targeted teaching before a course needs the content costs less and achieves more than the same material taught in November against a moving syllabus. What is not worth buying is general revision over the summer with no specific gap identified, which consumes a holiday and produces very little that survives to September.

faqs.question: What are the November and June series results dates, and does it matter which we sit?
faqs.answer: It matters if a grade is needed for an application. Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge gave results on Direct for its March 2027 series as 13 May 2027, with certificates in late June. A November entry therefore produces a grade in late January, after several application deadlines. The series is chosen at entry, months before revision begins, which is why it belongs on the autumn calendar.

faqs.question: Where should an Al Mowaihat family get the IB session dates from?
faqs.answer: Because we could not read them from the IB itself for this project, and a date taken from a secondary source and published on a tutoring page is exactly how incorrect dates spread. Cambridge and Pearson both publish their own key dates, so those appear here with the board named. For IB sessions, ask the school's diploma coordinator or read ibo.org directly, then build the family calendar around that. Treat any provider quoting IB dates without naming its source as a provider that guessed.

faqs.question: A coursework deadline falls the week after our holiday. What do we do now?
faqs.answer: Move the work, not the rule. Submitted work must be the student's own, a supervisor must see drafts, and the submission is authenticated, and none of that relaxes because a week disappeared. The fix is scheduling: get a draft written before the holiday rather than after it, and book the feedback session for the week you return. Legitimate help is explaining criteria, questioning the research question, and giving feedback on what the student has already written. It is not supplying sentences or reorganising the draft on their behalf.

ajman/al-mowaihat.closingBody: The cheapest thing an Al Mowaihat family can do this term is build one calendar: the entry deadline, the zone timetable, the coursework internal dates, the mock windows, the Ramadan weeks and the series. Then ask for the last marked script with its mark scheme. Those two pieces of paper decide what to buy, in what shape and in which month, and they usually show that less is needed than feared but sooner. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, in slots built around the bus rather than against it.

ajman/al-nuaimiya.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover the programmes Al Nuaimiya children actually sit: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, the IB Middle Years Programme at the Al Tallah and Sharjah campuses, and the IB Diploma for students who travel further for sixth form. Each one teaches a named syllabus, not a subject in general.

intro.heading: Al Nuaimiya is an apartment district, and that changes what tutoring has to solve
paragraphs: Al Nuaimiya is one of the oldest and densest residential districts in Ajman: mid-rise towers and walk-up blocks along Sheikh Khalifa Bin Zayed Street, with Ajman City Centre and the hospital at the centre of daily life. Almost nobody here lives in a villa. The typical household is a flat with two or three bedrooms holding four to six people, often with one parent driving to Sharjah or Dubai before seven in the morning and returning after seven at night. That single fact shapes every tutoring decision a family here makes, and it is the thing nobody writing about tutoring in Ajman ever mentions.

The children in those flats are spread across more curricula than the district's size suggests. Indian-curriculum schools inside Ajman take the largest share, and a steady number of those students move onto Cambridge International GCSE in Year 9 or Year 10 because the parents want a qualification a UK or Canadian university reads without translation. A smaller group travels to Ajman Academy on the Emirates Road belt for the IB Middle Years Programme, and the Diploma students almost all commute to Sharjah or Dubai. Three different assessment systems, three different vocabularies, and one shared kitchen table.

The academic pressure points cluster tightly. In the primary and lower secondary years it is English: a child who reads comfortably in one language and is assessed in another loses marks in Science and Humanities long before anyone calls it a language problem. In Years 9 and 10 it is the subject-option decision, and specifically whether a school has entered a child for Core or Extended papers, because Core caps the grade at C and most families discover this after the entry is made. In Years 12 and 13 it is Higher Level content taught to a class of six by a teacher who also teaches three other year groups.

The second pressure point is physical. A one-to-one lesson needs a door that closes, a table, and a connection that holds a video call for an hour. In an Al Nuaimiya flat with three children and two working parents, none of those three things is automatic, and a tutor who ignores the room will spend half the hour competing with a television. Working that out in advance is part of the setup, not an afterthought, and it is one of the few variables a family can fix in a single afternoon.

IB Gram does not send a tutor to an Al Nuaimiya address. Home visits are a service offered only in India; everything delivered to UAE families is one-to-one over live video. That is a deliberate position rather than a limitation. A district of this size cannot support a resident Chemistry Higher Level specialist, an Arabic first-language teacher and a Pearson Edexcel Further Maths examiner all within a fifteen-minute drive. Over video, the pool stops being geographic and the match is made on syllabus rather than postcode.
