ajman/al-zorah.programmesIntro: Three programmes account for Al Zorah's students, and the thing worth comparing between them is not difficulty but how much of the work sits outside the classroom. That proportion rises sharply from the middle years to the Diploma, and it is the single best predictor of whether a family needs support.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years of class teaching ending in a June or November series. The content is delivered in lessons and the technique is not: students who have never answered a full paper under timing lose marks to pacing and to question-type unfamiliarity rather than to ignorance. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with different timetables, and its exams officers' guide warns that using the wrong zone version is the candidate's own risk.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, so there is no emirate inspection portal for an Al Zorah family to consult about how much past-paper practice a school builds in. Ask the question directly at a parents' evening: how many full timed papers will my child sit before the series, and who marks them. The answer tells you exactly how big your own gap is.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, each with an internal assessment the student designs and writes themselves. The programme is explicit that substantial independent work is expected, which is a strength and the reason it catches out organised students who are used to being told what to do next. Independent reading, data collection and drafting are not homework; they are the course.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma provision near Al Zorah means a journey - to the Emirates Road belt, into Sharjah, or towards Dubai. A student leaving before 7am and returning after 4.30pm has a single evening block in which the independent half of the Diploma has to happen, and that block is also where any tuition must sit. Protecting it rather than filling it is the planning principle here.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject marked out of eight and converted to a 1 to 7. The programme front-loads skills the Diploma later assumes: inquiry, criterion-based writing, and the personal project in MYP 5, which is the first substantial piece of work a student organises alone. How a child handles that project is the most reliable early signal of how they will handle the Diploma core.
programmes.countryNote: An Al Zorah family with a child in MYP has a window that central-Ajman families spend on logistics. Use it: the cheapest moment to teach planning, note-taking and self-testing is MYP 4 and 5, when the stakes are low and the habits still form in weeks rather than terms. Support at this stage is short and infrequent and returns more than an equivalent spend in DP2.

ajman/al-zorah.subjectsIntro: Al Zorah students choose a slightly different subject mix from Ajman's city districts - the environmental and geographic subjects appear more often, which the nature reserve on the doorstep partly explains. The notes below say what independent work each subject demands, because that is the part a timetable does not cover.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The subject where independent practice volume decides the grade more plainly than anywhere else. Lessons can teach a method in twenty minutes; fluency under time pressure takes repetition nobody can do for the student. The non-calculator paper is the clearest test of whether that repetition happened, and it is where the gap between understanding and fluency becomes a mark difference.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The individual investigation is designed, run, analysed and written by the student, with a teacher checking that the method is safe and workable. That means the evaluation - a genuine critique of the method's limits against what the data shows - is produced without supervision, and it is the criterion most often written as a conclusion instead.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Content is taught; uncertainty treatment generally is not, or not enough. A candidate who reports a result without a defensible uncertainty, or propagates one incorrectly, loses marks in both the internal assessment and the written papers. Independent work here means practising explanation structure and error analysis, neither of which appears on a homework sheet.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The largest recall load in the group, built by self-testing rather than by re-reading. Students who revise biology by reviewing notes feel productive and improve slowly. The examination asks them to apply content to unfamiliar organisms and unseen data, which is a different activity, practised on past questions rather than on a textbook.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: An interdisciplinary course spanning ecology, resources and environmental value systems, assessed partly through an individual investigation on a question the student frames. Al Zorah's mangrove channels and the nature reserve make genuine fieldwork possible, which is rarer than it sounds - most candidates work from secondary data because no accessible system is nearby.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Case studies are only useful if the student can deploy them precisely, with named places, figures and dates, and that precision is memorised independently. The fieldwork internal assessment needs a question narrow enough to answer with data a student can actually collect, which is where most of the marks are won or lost before any writing.

subjects.name: English A: Literature
subjects.description: The reading is the course and it happens at home. A student who has not finished the set texts cannot be rescued by technique work, and a student who has read them twice can be transformed by it. The unseen commentary paper rewards analysis of how a text produces its effect rather than summary of what it says.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Taken by students heading for Higher Level mathematics, and a far better predictor of Diploma readiness than a 0580 grade alone. It introduces calculus and more demanding algebra early, which means a student who copes with 0606 will cope with Analysis and Approaches, and one who does not has useful information two years early.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Coordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: Biology, chemistry and physics in a double award, which compresses three content loads into the timetable of two. The compression lands on independent revision: the syllabus is broad, the papers sample widely, and students who revise by topic rather than by past-paper question find their coverage is thinner than they thought.

ajman/al-zorah.regionsTitle: Al Zorah and the drive out of it
ajman/al-zorah.regionsIntro: Al Zorah sits at the top of the emirate with water on one side and the nature reserve on another, so every school run is a drive. These notes describe what that distance does to a weekday rather than listing amenities.

regions.name: Al Zorah
regions.note: Villas, apartments and the marina around the golf course and the mangrove reserve. Space and quiet are not the constraint here; distance is. No school inside the development means an early departure and a return in the late afternoon.

regions.name: Al Rumailah and the Ajman Corniche
regions.note: The nearest dense district heading south, and the route most Al Zorah school runs take. Journey times double in the morning peak, which is why afternoon tuition slots rarely survive contact with reality here.

regions.name: Al Hamidiya
regions.note: Inland from the Corniche and home to several of the emirate's older schools and government buildings. Relevant to Al Zorah families mainly as a route and, for private candidates, as the kind of district where examination centres sit.

regions.name: Al Jurf
regions.note: Ajman University and the industrial belt. A different household profile entirely, and the practical reason Al Zorah families compete for evening tutor slots with a much denser population twenty minutes south.

regions.name: Al Zahya and Al Tallah
regions.note: The Emirates Road corridor, where several British and IB campuses sit. For an Al Zorah family this is the likely school destination and the longest leg of the week, roughly half an hour each way outside peak and considerably more inside it.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain, to the north
regions.note: Closer to Al Zorah than much of Ajman city, and under the same federal Ministry of Education oversight. Some families look at schools in both emirates, which changes the morning route without changing the regulator.

regions.name: Al Khan and Al Majaz, Sharjah
regions.note: Where the Sharjah school options start, under the emirate's Private Education Authority rather than the Ministry of Education. A longer drive, a different regulator, and a different route for fee and curriculum approval.

schoolClusters.city: Campuses an Al Zorah family drives to
schoolClusters.note: No school sits inside the development, so the choice is made on the drive as much as on the curriculum. Before committing, ask how many full timed papers the school runs before a series and who marks them, because that single answer tells you how much independent support you will need to arrange yourself.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah and northern options families also consider
schoolClusters.note: Going south into Sharjah or north towards Umm Al Quwain both appear on Al Zorah shortlists. The regulator changes with the emirate: Sharjah's Private Education Authority approves curricula and fees there, while Umm Al Quwain sits with the federal Ministry of Education as Ajman does.

ajman/al-zorah.modesIntro: Because the problem in this district is independent work rather than teaching, the three booking shapes below are built around supervision, marking and process coaching rather than around re-explaining lessons. Each one is deliberately finite.

modes.title: Fortnightly marked component
modes.description: The student sits one full timed component at home every two weeks and it comes back marked against the published scheme, with a written breakdown by question type. The session that follows works only on the two heaviest losses. This is the cheapest high-return arrangement available and it does not require weekly hours.

modes.title: Coursework process block, front-loaded
modes.description: Three to five sessions before the student writes anything, aimed at the decisions that determine the mark: a research question narrow enough for the words allowed, evidence that can legitimately be obtained, and a word allocation by section. Later feedback is on the student's own draft, mapped to criterion letters.

Best taken in MYP 5 or Year 10, when the habits still change quickly.

sections.heading: What the Al Zorah school day covers, and what it leaves for the evening
paragraphs: Start with the shape of the day, because in this district it is the governing fact. A child living in Al Zorah leaves the development before 7am and is back somewhere between 4pm and 5pm depending on the campus and the traffic south. That gives a usable evening block of roughly three hours, inside which homework, independent reading, coursework, revision and any tuition all have to fit. The block is not short because the family is disorganised. It is short because the development has no school in it.

Inside the school day, teaching happens and a specific set of things does not. Content gets delivered. Questions get answered. Homework gets set and marked at the volume a teacher with several classes can sustain. What does not happen, in most schools and through no fault of anyone, is enough full-length timed practice with proper marking, because marking a class set of papers against a published scheme takes hours that are not in anyone's timetable.

The second thing that does not happen is retrieval practice. Recall is built by being tested, not by being taught, and the testing has to be frequent and uncomfortable. A student who reads notes for an hour feels like they have revised; a student who answers twenty questions from memory and gets eight wrong has actually learnt something. Schools know this and still cannot run it individually for every child, which is precisely the space a tutor should occupy.

The third is coursework supervision beyond the minimum the programme requires. An Extended Essay supervisor has a defined number of meetings. A science teacher checks that an investigation is safe and feasible. A Theory of Knowledge teacher has a small weekly allocation across a whole cohort. Everything else - the reading, the data, the structure, the argument - is the student's own work by design, and the design is the point. The question is only whether anybody has told the family that.

Timed practice with proper marking is what timetables cannot afford

sections.heading: Timetabled hours against what a course actually asks for
paragraphs: The useful way to see the gap is as an hours problem rather than a quality problem. Every course has a quantity of teaching attached to it and a quantity of independent work assumed alongside. The first number is on the school timetable. The second is in the subject guide and in nobody's calendar, which is why it gets done badly or late rather than not at all.

The UAE adds a structural detail here that is worth knowing even outside Dubai. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that no mandatory-subject lesson should run shorter than 25 minutes. That is the arithmetic of a school week made explicit, and it applies to Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies, which sit alongside whatever international curriculum a school is licensed to teach. Those subjects consume timetable minutes that families often forget to account for.

The table sets the two columns side by side for the courses Al Zorah students take. The point of it is not the exact figures, which vary by school and by subject guide, but the pattern: the proportion of a course that happens outside lessons rises steeply from the middle years to the Diploma core, where it approaches all of it. A family that budgets support by subject difficulty is budgeting against the wrong variable.

What follows from the table is a planning rule. Put support where the independent proportion is highest, not where the grade is lowest. A student struggling in a well-taught subject with little independent load needs classroom help the school can give. A student coasting in a subject whose internal assessment is entirely self-directed is the one heading for a surprise.

sections.heading: The work a student does alone, and where its marks sit
paragraphs: This is the section families in Al Zorah tend to photograph. It lists the pieces of assessed work a student produces largely without supervision, says who nominally oversees each, and names the commonest way marks are lost. None of these failure modes is about ability. They are about nobody having read the criteria before the work started.

Take the Extended Essay as the clearest case. It is 4,000 words, independently researched, with a named supervisor and a limited number of formal meetings. The decision that determines the mark is made in week one: a research question narrow enough that 4,000 words can actually answer it. A student who picks a broad question writes a survey, and a survey cannot score well against criteria that reward focused argument. No amount of later editing fixes a question that was wrong at the start.

The same structure repeats across the other components. In a science investigation the evaluation criterion rewards critique of the method's limits against what the data shows, and students write a conclusion instead. In a mathematics exploration the personal engagement criterion rewards genuine ownership of the question, and technically perfect work scores poorly without it. In a language individual oral, candidates describe the extract rather than analysing how it constructs meaning. Each is a published criterion that nobody read.

The practical consequence for tuition is that the sessions worth paying for happen before the writing. Three sessions spent narrowing a question and reading criteria properly are worth more than ten spent on feedback afterwards, because the later sessions can only improve execution within a structure that is already fixed. That is the opposite of how most families buy coursework support, and it is the single clearest piece of advice on this page.

sections.heading: Revision is a skill, and the timetable does not teach it
paragraphs: Ask a competent fifteen-year-old how they revise and the answer is usually some version of reading through the notes. It is the default because it is comfortable, it produces a feeling of familiarity, and nobody has shown them anything else. The gap between that and what works is larger than the gap between a good teacher and an average one, and it costs families more than any tutoring decision they will make.

What works is unglamorous and well established. Retrieval: close the book and answer from memory, then check. Spacing: come back to the same material after a gap rather than massing it in one evening. Interleaving: mix question types so the student has to identify which method applies, because an examination does not announce the topic. Marking against a published scheme, so the student learns what an examiner rewards rather than what feels like a good answer. None of this requires a tutor, and almost none of it happens without one.

There is a UAE-specific scheduling point that belongs here. Ramadan falls inside the academic year, school days shorten, and energy shifts to after Iftar. A revision plan written in February for a May or June series that ignores those weeks will be abandoned in the first one. Shorter, more frequent sessions work better while fasting, and the heavier analytical work moves to whatever part of the day a particular household has energy in. Planning around it is ordinary practice, not a concession.

For Al Zorah families specifically there is a four-session version of this that is better value than almost anything else on offer: set up retrieval practice on the actual syllabus content, build a spaced schedule against the school's own assessment calendar, derive a revision order from the component weightings, and read one mark scheme line by line with the student. Do it in Year 10 or MYP 5 and the habits hold for the Diploma.

sections.heading: What closing the gap costs, by what you are actually buying
paragraphs: Most tutoring price comparisons are useless because they compare hours rather than products. An hour of supervised practice, an hour of teaching a specific content gap, an hour spent marking a timed component properly and an hour of coursework process coaching are four different services with four different cost structures, and a single hourly figure hides all of it.

The table splits them out and attaches the market's published figures. Those figures come from providers' own pages, read in October 2026: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 at the budget end; Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist work; Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 and specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 and above. None of them is IB Gram's price.

Read the third column carefully, because it is the one that changes the arithmetic. Supervision is a weekly, open-ended commitment. Teaching a content gap is six to twelve sessions and then it is finished. Marking a timed component is one session a fortnight. Coursework coaching is three to five sessions, front-loaded. A family that buys the finite products rather than an indefinite weekly hour spends materially less for more movement, and the plan should say when it ends.

IB Gram publishes no rate card on this page. The free trial lesson is with the tutor who would teach the course, and the consultation afterwards prices the actual plan, because the right answer depends on the level, on how scarce the specialist is, and on how many weeks are left.

sections.heading: Four ways to fill the evening gap from Al Zorah
paragraphs: A page targeting the home-tutor search should answer it properly. An Al Zorah villa is a comfortable place for a visiting tutor and the household can usually hold a regular appointment. The problem is not the house, it is the map. Al Zorah sits at the top of the emirate, and a subject specialist coming from Sharjah or Dubai is budgeting close to an hour each way outside peak, which is paid for in the rate whether or not it appears as a line on the invoice.

IB Gram delivers to Al Zorah as one-to-one online tuition over live video. We do not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists in India only. For the products this page is about - marked components, coursework coaching, study-skills work - physical presence adds nothing and distance subtracts a great deal, because the pool of people who can mark a Higher Level component properly is not a local pool.

The table includes two arrangements that cost nothing and are genuinely worth trying first. School subject-support sessions are already inside the fees, and in a well-staffed subject they are the cheapest fix available. A study group among Al Zorah families solves accountability, which is a real problem for a student working alone in a quiet house, and solves it better than paid supervision does. Neither closes a genuine content gap, which is where paid help earns its place.

One row deserves emphasis. Driving to a tuition centre in Ajman city costs twenty to thirty minutes each way from Al Zorah, twice, out of a three-hour evening block. For broad revision at a lower per-student rate that can still be worth it. For two specific question types it is an hour of travel to solve a twenty-minute problem.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when most of the work is unsupervised
paragraphs: A course where the majority of assessed work is produced alone puts the academic-honesty line under more pressure, not less. The IB's position is unambiguous: submitted work must be the student's own, a supervisor must see drafts, and the submission is authenticated. A student working in a quiet house on a 4,000-word essay with a deadline approaching is exactly the student for whom a helpful adult becomes a problem.

What support can legitimately be is wide and worth spelling out. Teaching the content the task draws on. Reading each criterion with the student and explaining what it rewards, with the marks named. Arguing about whether a research question can be answered in the words allowed with evidence the student can obtain. Reading something the student has already written and identifying which criterion is under-served. Modelling an unrelated worked example so the standard is visible.

What it cannot be is equally clear. No supplied sentences. No reorganising somebody else's work for them. No handing over a dataset. No document returned with new material in it. The household test is whether the student could explain every decision in the piece without prompting; if they could not, ownership has slipped, and the consequence of that falls on the student rather than on whoever was trying to help.

Materials follow the same rule. Syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson, and are cited and linked rather than reproduced. A provider offering a downloadable library, or anything from an unreleased session, is offering an exposure. In a market where one competitor openly sells completed Internal Assessments, saying this out loud is worth more than it should be.

sections.heading: A term plan built from the gap rather than from the syllabus
paragraphs: Put the pieces together and the plan for an Al Zorah student almost writes itself. Week one: establish what the school actually runs - how many timed papers, marked by whom - and what the independent load is in each subject. Weeks two to four: a marked timed component in the weakest subject, and three coursework process sessions in whichever component has the nearest deadline. That is the diagnostic phase, and it is finite.

From there the plan becomes a rhythm rather than a weekly hour. One marked component a fortnight in the subjects that need it. A short study-skills block if the student is still revising by re-reading. Content teaching only where a specific gap has been identified, and stopping when it closes. Nothing scheduled simply because the slot exists, because the evening block in this district is three hours long and tuition competes with the independent work it is supposed to support.

Reviews are set against marked evidence rather than against impressions. At six weeks, compare the second marked component with the first on the same breakdown. If the losses moved, continue. If they did not, change the subject, the tutor or the approach, and say so. A plan that cannot conclude that tuition should stop is a subscription rather than a plan.

On availability, the position before anything is booked. Specialists in the smaller Diploma subjects - Environmental Systems and Societies is a good example - are genuinely scarce, and scarcer in the northern emirates than in Dubai. If nobody teaching that subject at that level has a slot in the window you need, you are told. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the alternative may be a specialist working from elsewhere on Gulf Standard Time, disclosed at matching rather than discovered later.

A tutor who does not ask them is guessing at what to provide and will probably duplicate something the school already does well.

process.description: For an Al Zorah family the realistic slot is after the drive home and after food, so the trial happens then. The tutor who takes the trial is the one who would take the course, and the last five minutes are worth sitting in on to hear what they noticed.

process.description: The student sits a real component under timing and it comes back marked against the published scheme, broken down by question type with marks attached. That document is the baseline, it is yours to keep, and it is what every later review is measured against.

process.description: The plan says what happens, for how many sessions, and what finishing looks like. Content gaps close. Coursework coaching ends when the writing starts. Marked components continue to the series. Anything open-ended has to justify itself at the six-week review against the marked evidence.

faqs.question: Is there an IB or IGCSE home tutor available in Al Zorah, Ajman?
faqs.answer: Visiting tutors do work in Ajman, at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the rate, so the option exists. IB Gram is not one of them: lessons for Al Zorah families run one-to-one over live video, and home visiting is a service we offer in India only. Geography is the reason rather than cost. Al Zorah sits at the top of the emirate, and a specialist who can mark a Higher Level component properly is usually coming from Sharjah or Dubai, close to an hour each way outside peak, which the family pays for one way or another.

faqs.question: How much independent work does a Diploma subject actually need?
faqs.answer: More than most families assume, and the proportion rises with the level. A Higher Level subject adds extension content, often an extra paper, and an internal assessment the student designs and writes themselves. The Diploma core sits almost entirely outside timetabled time: a 4,000-word Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition, and a CAS portfolio with reflections spread across two years. Your child's actual figures are in the current subject guide, which the school's diploma coordinator holds. Ask for the independent-study expectation per subject and plan the evening block around it.

faqs.question: Nobody at school is really supervising my son's Extended Essay. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: It is how the component is designed. A named supervisor holds a limited number of formal meetings and authenticates the work; the reading, the argument and the drafting are the student's own, deliberately. What that means in practice is that the decision determining the mark is taken in week one, when the research question is chosen. A question too broad for 4,000 words produces a survey, and a survey cannot score well against criteria that reward focused argument. Three sessions spent narrowing the question are worth more than ten spent editing afterwards.

faqs.question: How strictly is the 4,000-word limit on the Extended Essay applied?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a hard ceiling and plan the essay to land under it rather than trimming down to it. The practical consequence is upstream: a research question has to be answerable within that allowance, with a word allocation agreed by section before drafting starts. Students who write first and count later lose argument rather than padding, because the sections they cut are usually the analytical ones. Your child's current guide, held by the school, is the authority on the exact requirements, and the supervisor is the person to confirm them with.

faqs.question: My daughter revises by reading her notes. Why is she not improving?
faqs.answer: Because re-reading produces familiarity rather than recall, and examinations test recall. The fix is retrieval practice: close the book, answer from memory, then check and correct. It feels worse and works better. Add spacing, so material returns after a gap rather than being massed into one evening, and interleaving, so she has to identify which method applies rather than being told the topic. Four sessions setting this up on her actual syllabus content, ideally in Year 10 or MYP 5, changes more than a term of weekly teaching does.

faqs.question: Al Zorah has mangroves and a nature reserve. Can my son use them for fieldwork?
faqs.answer: For Environmental Systems and Societies or Geography, that local access is a genuine advantage, because most candidates work from secondary data for the simple reason that no accessible system is nearby. The constraints are the ones that always apply to fieldwork: a question narrow enough to answer with data he can actually collect, a method that is safe and repeatable, and any permissions the reserve requires. That last point is worth checking before planning anything. The research question has to be agreed with his teacher, who supervises and authenticates the work.

faqs.question: When can a session realistically start for a child living in Al Zorah?
faqs.answer: Around 6pm, sometimes 6.30pm in the first weeks of term. No school sits inside the development, so a child leaves before 7am and is back between 4pm and 5pm depending on the campus and the traffic south through Al Rumailah. Food and twenty minutes of nothing come before anything cognitive. The usable block runs to roughly 9pm and has to hold homework, independent reading and coursework as well, which is the argument for a finite tuition product rather than an open-ended weekly hour.

faqs.question: What does it cost to have timed papers marked properly each fortnight?
faqs.answer: Marking against a published scheme sits in the specialist band, which market sources put at AED 200 to 450 an hour and above: TutorChase quotes AED 270 and Bestimate's rate table gives AED 200 to 450 plus, both read in October 2026. One component a fortnight across the final two terms is therefore a predictable, finite commitment rather than an open weekly cost, and it is the highest-return arrangement on this page because it produces a written breakdown by question type. IB Gram prices after a free trial lesson and a consultation rather than from a list.

faqs.question: Can a tutor supervise a science individual investigation?
faqs.answer: A tutor can support it; the school supervises and authenticates it. The legitimate work is teaching the content, explaining each criterion with the marks attached, pressing on whether the method is feasible and the data obtainable, and reading what the student has already written to say which criterion is under-served. The usual finding is that the evaluation criterion has been written as a conclusion rather than as a critique of the method's limits against the data. A tutor cannot supply text, restructure the work on the student's behalf, or provide a dataset.

faqs.question: How much extra Arabic practice does a non-Arabic-speaking household need?
faqs.answer: Enough to keep pace, scheduled rather than improvised. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are compulsory in UAE private schools under federal rules regardless of the international curriculum. KHDA's guidance for Dubai calculates mandatory-subject time on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises no lesson shorter than 25 minutes, which is a reasonable picture of what any UAE school allocates. For a household with no Arabic at home, two short weekly sessions on script and vocabulary from Year 7 cost far less than an intensive in Year 11, when a pass is suddenly needed.

faqs.question: What should happen to the plan after a mock result comes back?
faqs.answer: Something, which is the problem. Mocks are sat and marked and then the term moves on, because acting on the result is in nobody's timetable. The useful response is a breakdown by question type rather than a percentage: which question types returned full marks, which returned partial, which returned nothing. Then three weeks of work on the two heaviest losses and a second timed component to check. A mock that produces only a grade and a conversation has wasted the most informative data available before the series.

faqs.question: Is a study group with neighbours a substitute for a tutor?
faqs.answer: For accountability, often yes, and it is free. A student working alone in a quiet villa loses more to isolation than to ignorance, and three students sitting the same timed paper at the same hour solves that better than paid supervision does. What a study group cannot do is close a genuine content gap or mark a component against a published scheme, because nobody in the group knows what the examiner rewards. Use the group for practice volume and buy the marking, rather than the other way round.

faqs.question: Which authority oversees schools near Al Zorah, and does it matter to us?
faqs.answer: The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, as it does in Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Dubai sits with KHDA, Abu Dhabi with ADEK, Sharjah with its Private Education Authority, and Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge. It matters in two practical ways. There is no emirate inspection portal to search for an Ajman school, so you ask the school directly. And if you look at campuses in Sharjah, the regulator changes with the emirate, including who approves curricula and fees.

faqs.question: Which Al Zorah students genuinely need paid support, and which do not?
faqs.answer: The ones who need it are usually not the ones with the lowest grades. A student struggling in a well-taught subject with little independent load needs classroom help the school can give, and a tutor duplicates it. The student heading for a surprise is the one coasting in a subject whose internal assessment is entirely self-directed, or revising by re-reading with a series eight months away. Diagnose by independent load and by method, not by last term's grade, and buy a finite product rather than an indefinite weekly hour.

ajman/al-zorah.closingHeading: Count the gap before you buy hours
ajman/al-zorah.closingBody: Two questions answer most of what an Al Zorah family needs to decide. How many full timed papers will the school run before the series, and who marks them? And how much of each course is work the student produces alone? Put those answers next to the three-hour evening block this district actually has, and the plan becomes obvious: finite products, marked evidence, and support that ends when the gap closes. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot, with the marked breakdown left with you after each component.

ajman/best-ib-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB subjects to Ajman students over live video. Every claim on their profiles is meant to be checkable in a trial session: what they have taught, at which level, and how they mark. If a claim cannot be tested in an hour, it should not be the reason you hire anybody.

intro.heading: There is no league table, so build your own test
paragraphs: A superlative search is an honest expression of an impossible request. Parents want a ranking because the alternative is evaluating strangers on subjects they may not know, in a market where nobody checks anyone's claims. The uncomfortable fact is that no authority ranks IB tutors in the UAE, no register of tutor quality exists, and the pages competing for this search are advertising rather than reporting. Any page that answers the superlative question directly, including by claiming the title for itself, is telling you something that nobody in this market is in a position to know.

What can be built instead is a test. Eight or nine specific questions, each with an answer a parent can judge without subject knowledge, separate a specialist from a generalist and an honest provider from a careless one. They are questions about what the tutor has actually taught, how they mark, what they will not do, and what happens when they cannot help. None of them requires you to assess pedagogy, and all of them can be asked in a first conversation and tested in a single session.

The warning signs are equally learnable, and this market supplies plenty of examples. A published rating with no countable reviews behind it. A promise about a final score. A claim of regulator approval that the regulator does not grant to tutoring providers. A statistic with no sample size, date or method attached. A foreign telephone number on a page aimed at UAE families. Each of those is visible before you speak to anyone, and each tells you something about how the provider handles facts in general.

There is a specifically Ajman dimension to this. The emirate is small, its private schools sit under the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority with a public register, and many of its students attend school across the border in Sharjah or Dubai. The local pool of people who have genuinely taught a Higher Level Diploma subject is therefore thin, which means a family insisting on proximity is often choosing between availability and expertise without realising the choice was made.

Everything here is written on the basis that our own teaching is delivered one-to-one over live video, in evening slots that survive an Ajman commute. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. We hold no accreditation, licence or partnership from the IB, from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education, and we publish no star rating, because we have no countable, attributable review set to put behind one. Those are three claims we will not make, and you should treat any provider making them as something to verify rather than something to trust.

ajman/best-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: What you should be checking changes with the programme, because the assessment model changes. A tutor who is excellent at one of these is not automatically useful for another, and the question that exposes the difference is different in each case.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and creativity, activity, service. Part of each subject grade sits in internally assessed work marked at school and moderated externally, and the rest in papers sat in one session. The specialism that matters is subject and level together, not the programme as a whole.
programmes.countryNote: The check for a Diploma tutor is narrow: which subjects have you taught at Higher Level, in which years, and what do students most often lose marks on in that subject's papers. A tutor who answers in generalities about the IB rather than specifics about the subject has told you what you needed to know.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four published criteria per subject, each marked from zero to eight and converted to a one to seven grade by the school. There is no external paper in most years, so everything rests on how well a student writes to a published descriptor.
programmes.countryNote: The check for an MYP tutor is whether they ask to see the task sheet and the criterion wording before discussing content. One who starts from a textbook chapter has not understood what is being marked, which in the MYP is the whole job.

programmes.name: The Extended Essay, TOK and internal assessments
programmes.description: Independent assessed work that must be the student's own: research question, data, drafts and every sentence. Up to three diploma points come from the Extended Essay and TOK combined, and each subject's internal assessment contributes to its grade.
programmes.countryNote: This is the single sharpest vetting question available to an Ajman parent. Ask what the tutor will and will not do with an Extended Essay. A clear line, stated without hesitation, is a reliable signal. An offer to help produce the text is a reason to end the conversation.

ajman/best-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: For each subject below, there is a question a genuine specialist answers in a sentence and a generalist cannot. Use them. They are not trick questions, and a strong tutor will enjoy being asked.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Ask where method marks are most often thrown away. A specialist will talk about working done in rough and never transferred to the answer space, and about proof questions at Higher Level. A generalist will talk about practising more past papers.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Ask what makes a modelling answer incomplete. The useful answer is a result computed correctly and left without an interpretation sentence in the context of the scenario, which is where the marks sit across the papers.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Ask what separates bands in the internally assessed investigation. Uncertainty treatment and a genuine evaluation of method is the answer; a tutor who says the write-up needs to be neater has not marked one.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Ask how a four-mark explanation question should be answered. The answer should mention a chain of reasoning in steps rather than a single sentence, and units on gradient answers, which is the recurring avoidable loss.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Ask how outline, explain and evaluate differ in expected depth. A specialist answers immediately and references the mark allocation printed beside the question; the answer tells you whether they teach to the paper.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Ask what a correctly drawn diagram is worth without an explanation that refers to it. The honest answer is less than a simpler answer that does refer to it, and evaluation is what separates the top band.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Ask why a fluent essay can sit in the middle bands. The answer is that it summarises rather than analysing how meaning is constructed, and the fix is a paragraph habit rather than more reading.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Ask what a correct general answer about a business tool scores on a stimulus question. Very little, because application to the named organisation is the examined skill, and a specialist says so without prompting.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Ask how studies should be used in an answer. Recited as evidence for an argument rather than narrated, with evaluation distinguished from description, and with the internally assessed study handled methodologically rather than descriptively.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Ask what makes a TOK essay lose marks despite being well written. Not answering the prescribed title is the answer. A tutor who talks about interesting ideas rather than the title has not supervised one through marking.

ajman/best-ib-tutor.regionsTitle: What the search looks like from each part of Ajman
ajman/best-ib-tutor.regionsIntro: The vetting questions are the same wherever you live. What differs across the emirate is how thin the local option set is, and therefore how much a family gives up by insisting that the tutor be nearby.

regions.name: Al Nuaimiya
regions.note: The best-served part of the emirate for local classified-advert tutors, mostly covering mainstream subjects at school level. Diploma Higher Level cover is a different matter, and the local pool thins sharply once a specific subject and level are named.

regions.name: Al Rashidiya
regions.note: Central Ajman, where word-of-mouth recommendations circulate quickly between families at the same schools. Useful as a starting list, but a recommendation from a parent whose child took a different subject at a different level is weaker evidence than it feels.

regions.name: Al Jurf
regions.note: Close to the Sharjah boundary, so families here often receive quotes from Sharjah-based agencies with a travel element added. Ask explicitly whether the quoted rate includes travel and what happens when the road is blocked.

regions.name: Al Mowaihat
regions.note: Villa communities where in-home arrangements are commonly offered with a two-hour minimum. That minimum is a travel cost in disguise, and it is worth comparing against an hour of specialist teaching with no journey attached.

regions.name: Al Yasmeen and Al Zahya
regions.note: Families who have often moved out from Dubai and are comparing against what they previously paid. Prior price is a weak guide here, because the Dubai rate included a market with far more local specialists in it.

regions.name: Ajman Corniche and Al Rumailah
regions.note: Short local journeys and late-returning parents. The practical vetting question in this cluster is whether a provider will genuinely hold a 9pm slot during coursework weeks rather than agreeing to it and then reshuffling.

regions.name: Emirates City and Al Alia
regions.note: The longest daily travel in the emirate for students at schools across the border. Any arrangement that adds a further journey should be questioned on reliability before price, because cancellations here are the common failure mode.

sections.heading: What a superlative can and cannot mean here
paragraphs: Taken literally, the search has no answer. There is no body that assesses IB tutors in the UAE, no published comparison based on measured outcomes, and no mechanism by which anyone could know who teaches a given subject most effectively. The providers answering the question are answering an advertising brief, and a page asserting the top position is demonstrating a marketing budget rather than a teaching record.

Taken as the question behind the question, it has a good answer. What a parent means is: how do I avoid wasting a term and a few thousand dirhams on someone who turns out to be a competent graduate with no examining experience. That is answerable, because the difference between a specialist and a generalist shows up quickly in how they talk about marks.

The substitution worth making is from reputation to evidence. Reputation in a small market is a handful of recommendations from families whose children took different subjects at different levels, which is weaker information than it feels. Evidence is what a tutor says when asked where marks are lost in a named subject, and what a piece of marked work looks like when it comes back. Both are available before committing to anything.

This also reframes price. The most expensive provider in a market with no quality signal is not reliably the strongest; it is the one that has positioned itself at the top of the range, which may reflect examining experience or may reflect a marketing decision. Published market rates in this country run from roughly AED 45 to AED 650 an hour, and the span tells you about positioning rather than about teaching.
bullets: No authority assesses or ranks IB tutors in the UAE

sections.heading: The eight checks that actually discriminate
paragraphs: These are the questions worth asking, in the order that saves the most time. They work because each has an answer a parent can judge without knowing the subject, and because weak providers answer them in a recognisably different way from strong ones. None of them is adversarial, and a good tutor will answer all eight without discomfort.

Start with specificity. Which subjects, at which level, in which years. A tutor who has taught Chemistry at Higher Level for six years says so in those terms; one who teaches sciences generally will reach for the programme name instead of the subject and level. Then ask the marks question for that subject, which is the single most informative question on the list, because an answer about specific question types cannot be improvised.

Then the boundary question: what will you not do with an Extended Essay or an internal assessment. A clear, immediate line is a strong signal, and hesitation or an offer to help produce the text is a reason to stop. Then the record question: what will I receive after each session. Then the availability question: what happens if you cannot cover something we need. Then the permit question. Then references, asked specifically rather than generally. And finally the exit question, which most parents never ask and which shapes the whole arrangement.

Run as a set, these take twenty minutes and a trial session. That is a small amount of work against the cost of discovering in March that a Higher Level subject has been taught at Standard Level depth since September, which is the single most common expensive failure in this market and one that nobody discovers early by accident.

sections.heading: Warning signs visible before you speak to anyone
paragraphs: Several of the most useful signals are on the page already, which means a parent can shorten the shortlist before making contact. Each item below was observed in the live UAE tutoring market during research for these pages, and each tells you something about how the provider handles facts generally rather than only about the specific claim.

The most common is a star rating with nothing countable behind it. One provider in this market publishes a self-asserted aggregate rating, and in at least one case two different rating figures appear on the same page with different review counts. Self-serving review markup is against Google's structured-data policy and, as a commercial representation to UAE consumers, it is a problem beyond search. A rating without a dated, attributable review set is decoration.

The second is an outcome promise. A specific final grade, a promised improvement, a refund tied to a result: all of these describe something the provider does not control, because the examination is marked by the board and the work is the student's. The third is a regulator claim. Describing a tutoring service as approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or Cambridge misrepresents what those bodies do. A Dubai educational services permit for a training institute is a real and specific thing issued to institutes with premises; it is not a general endorsement and it does not exist for a tutor at all.

The remaining ones are quick. A statistic with no sample size, date or method. A foreign telephone number as the conversion path on a UAE page, which two ranking providers currently use. A UAE office address that does not appear to exist. A published price that contradicts the figure in the page's own structured data. An offer to supply completed coursework, which one provider in this market advertises openly at a published price. Any one of these justifies removing a provider from the list.

sections.heading: Provider models, compared on what you are actually buying
paragraphs: Competitor pages in this market tend to compare themselves against an unnamed alternative that is always worse. A more useful comparison is between models, because the model determines what can go wrong and what recourse a family has. Five models cover almost everything available to an Ajman household, and each has a genuine use.

A specialist agency or platform offers a pool and some process, which matters most when a family needs an unusual subject and level. The risks are tutor rotation and the gap between the person described and the person teaching. An international marketplace offers breadth and price transparency, with the weakest verification and often prices quoted in a currency UAE families do not transact in. An independent local tutor can be the strongest relationship available and carries the least institutional backup, so the individual checks matter more.

A tuition centre with premises offers group teaching at a lower price per hour on a fixed timetable, and in Dubai such an operation requires an educational services permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. School-run support is usually included in fees and is timed to the school day rather than to an Ajman commute, and in Abu Dhabi, professional-ethics rules for school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid tutoring of students at their own school.

The useful reading is the span rather than any single cell: the same subject at the same level is sold between roughly AED 45 and AED 650 an hour in this market, which is a statement about business models rather than about teaching.

sections.heading: Credentials: what examiner status means and what it does not
paragraphs: Examining experience is genuinely useful. Someone who has marked a paper has seen a thousand student answers against a mark scheme, which is exactly the knowledge that makes feedback specific rather than general. So it is reasonable for a parent to want it and reasonable for a tutor who has it to say so.

Two cautions follow. The first is verification: current examiner status is a contractual relationship with a board, it changes year to year, and it is not usually something a parent can check independently. A provider describing its tutors collectively as examiners, without naming anyone or any year, is making a claim that cannot be tested. We do not describe tutors as examiners unless the individual's status can be evidenced, and we would rather lose the comparison than make an unverifiable claim.

The second caution is about what examining confers. It does not give access to unreleased papers, to grade boundaries before they are set, or to marking in progress. A provider hinting at inside knowledge is either misunderstanding the role or implying something improper, and either way it is a reason for concern rather than confidence. Boundaries are set after papers are marked, following a review of candidate performance, which is why nobody can know them in advance.

What to ask instead is narrower and more useful. How many years have you taught this subject at this level. What do students lose marks on in this specific paper. Have you marked work against this mark scheme. The third question gets at the same underlying experience as the examiner claim, without requiring either party to rely on a credential nobody can check.
bullets: Marking experience is useful; current examiner status is rarely verifiable by a parent

sections.heading: Using the permit question as a vetting tool
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated rather than informal, and the regulation gives a parent a straightforward question to ask. The private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. The official service is listed as the issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, with a two working day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

The published eligible categories are broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts is published, so a specific figure quoted by anyone should be treated with scepticism rather than repeated.

The vetting value is less in the answer than in the reaction. A tutor who knows what the permit is, says whether they hold one and explains which category they applied under is telling you they take the formal side of the work seriously. One who dismisses the question as irrelevant is telling you something about how they will handle a record of sessions or a disputed invoice. The permit is free, so cost is not a defence.

Two related checks fit here. If the tutor is a teacher, ask whether your child attends their school, since Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for school staff have been reported as prohibiting paid tutoring of students at their own school and the permit carries a code of conduct. And if the provider operates as a centre with premises in Dubai, ask which permit it holds, because a KHDA educational services permit for a training institute is a specific authorisation with its own process and renewal requirements.

sections.heading: Reviews, ratings and statistics, read properly
paragraphs: Social proof is the weakest evidence in this market and the most heavily used. The reason is structural: there is no independent review platform for UAE tutoring with verified transactions behind it, so almost every figure a parent sees is self-published by the party it flatters. Reading it properly mostly means discounting it and replacing it with something better.

Three specific failures recur. Ratings that differ between the visible page and the structured data behind it, which search engines can discount and which signals carelessness at best. Review counts that do not reconcile with the claimed student numbers. And figures presented without a sample size, a date or a method, which cannot be evaluated by anyone including the provider.

The replacement is specific references. Not a testimonial page, but a parent whose child took the same subject at the same level with the same tutor, willing to answer three questions: did the same person teach throughout, what did you receive in writing, and would you book again. That is a small ask and a strong signal, and a provider who cannot produce one relevant reference for a subject they claim to specialise in has told you about the depth of that specialism.

We publish no rating on these pages, and that is deliberate rather than modest. We have no countable, dated, attributable review set to put behind a number, and publishing one anyway is precisely the practice described above. If and when there is a real one, it will appear with its sample size and its date attached.

sections.heading: Trialling properly, and the limits of what any tutor can do
paragraphs: A trial lesson is usually treated as a sample and is better used as a test. The useful trial has the student's most recent marked paper or current draft in front of the tutor, not a generic worksheet, because what you are evaluating is diagnosis rather than charm. A tutor who can look at a marked script and name three specific recurring losses in forty minutes has demonstrated the thing you are buying.

Four things are worth watching. Whether the tutor asks for the evidence before offering a plan. Whether the student talks, or is talked at for an hour. Whether anything is written down and sent afterwards. And whether the tutor says anything inconvenient, because a provider who never disagrees with a parent in a first conversation is managing a sale rather than a student.

Then there are the honest limits. No tutor can promise a grade, because the examination is marked by the board and the work is the student's. No tutor can recover marks already locked into a submitted internal assessment. No tutor can produce the work that must be the student's own, and any offer to do so puts the qualification at risk rather than helping it. No tutor can fix in six weeks what two years produced, though paper discipline in six weeks is worth real marks near a threshold.

And there is availability, which almost nobody in this market discloses. For a narrow Higher Level combination, a minority language or coursework supervision in a short window, there may be no suitable specialist free when a family needs one. The honest options are a different slot, a wait, or a recommendation to look elsewhere. We will say which applies rather than putting a generalist into a specialist seat, which is the failure a family discovers too late to fix.

process.title: Shortlist by what is already visible
process.description: Remove any provider showing a rating with no dated reviews, a promise about a final grade, a claimed regulator approval, a statistic with no sample size, or a non-UAE contact number on a UAE page. That usually halves the list before you speak to anybody.

process.title: Ask the eight questions
process.description: Subjects and levels taught, where marks are lost, what they will not do with assessed work, what you receive in writing, what happens when they cannot cover something, the permit, a relevant reference, and how to end the arrangement. Twenty minutes, and the answers sort themselves.

process.title: Trial on the real material
process.description: One free session, with no card details taken, using your child's most recent marked paper or current draft rather than a generic exercise. You are testing whether the tutor can diagnose from evidence, which is the whole of what you are buying.

process.title: Commit to a small block, in writing
process.description: A defined number of sessions with an agreed end point and a stated way out. Nothing about a good arrangement requires a long minimum commitment, and a provider confident in the work does not need one.

process.title: Review against the evidence, not the relationship
process.description: At the end of the block, compare the agreed end point with the starting position. Continue, change focus, change tutor or stop. A provider who has made the exit easy from the start makes this a decision rather than a confrontation.

whyPoints.title: We publish no rating
whyPoints.description: There is no countable, dated, attributable review set behind a number we could honestly print, so we print none. If that changes, the figure will appear with its sample size and date, which is the only form in which a rating means anything.

whyPoints.title: We claim no accreditation
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no licence, accreditation or partnership from the IB, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or Cambridge. Those bodies regulate schools and qualifications. A provider implying otherwise is making a claim worth testing.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits stated, not hidden
whyPoints.description: For a narrow Higher Level combination or a minority language there may be nobody suitable free in the window you want. We will say so and suggest where else to look rather than placing a generalist and letting the term reveal it.

whyPoints.title: A line on assessed work we will not move
whyPoints.description: The student chooses the question, does the work and writes every sentence. We teach skills on other examples, read what exists and ask questions. We decline requests to supply text for an internal assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay.

whyPoints.title: Specialists reachable from a small emirate
whyPoints.description: Because teaching is online, the pool for a specific subject and level is national rather than limited to who will travel into Ajman on a weekday evening. In a thin local market that is the difference between a specialist and a substitute.

whyPoints.title: An exit stated before you commit
whyPoints.description: A defined block, an agreed end point and a way out without penalty. Making it easy to leave is the clearest signal a provider can give about its confidence in the work, which is why it is worth asking every provider for it.

faqs.question: Is there an official ranking of IB tutors anywhere in the UAE?
faqs.answer: No. No authority assesses or ranks individual tutors, no register of tutor quality exists, and no published comparison is based on measured student outcomes. Regulators oversee schools and qualifications rather than private tutors, and the permit regime covers the right to tutor rather than the standard of teaching. So any page answering a superlative search directly is advertising. The practical substitute is a short set of checkable questions plus a trial session using your child's own marked work, which produces better information than any ranking could.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor in the first five minutes?
faqs.answer: Two things. Which subjects have you taught, at which level, and in which years. Then: where do students most often lose marks in that subject. The first answer should be specific rather than a list of curricula; the second cannot be improvised by anyone who has not marked student work, because a real answer names question types and mark allocations rather than recommending more past papers. If both answers are strong, the rest of the vetting is worth doing. If either is vague, you have saved yourself an hour.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor has genuinely taught at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Ask for the subject, the level and the years, then ask a level-specific question and listen to the answer. For Analysis and Approaches, ask what separates Higher Level from Standard Level in the papers. For a science, ask what the internally assessed investigation needs that a Standard Level student finds hardest. Then ask for one reference from a parent whose child took that subject at that level. A general testimonial is not evidence about your subject, and a provider claiming a specialism should be able to produce one relevant name.

faqs.question: Does calling a tutor an examiner mean anything I can verify?
faqs.answer: Rarely. Current examiner status is a contractual relationship with a board, it changes year to year, and a parent usually cannot check it independently. A collective claim that a provider's tutors are examiners, with nobody named and no year given, cannot be tested at all. Examining also confers no access to unreleased papers, marking in progress or grade boundaries, which are set after papers are marked. Ask instead how many years they have taught the subject at that level and whether they have marked work against that mark scheme.

faqs.question: A provider shows a high star rating with many reviews. Should I trust it?
faqs.answer: Treat it as decoration unless the reviews are dated, named and countable. There is no independent review platform for UAE tutoring with verified transactions behind it, so most figures are self-published by the party they flatter. In this market, rating figures have appeared that contradict another figure on the same page, and review counts that do not reconcile with claimed student numbers. A rating that differs between the visible page and the structured data behind it can also be discounted by search engines. Ask for one relevant reference instead.

faqs.question: An advert promises a specific final score. What does that tell me?
faqs.answer: That the provider is promising something it does not control. The examination is marked by the board, internal work is moderated externally, and the work itself is the student's. A promise about a final grade, about a fixed improvement, or a refund tied to a result is a commitment nobody in this position can honour, and the fact that it was made tells you how the provider handles claims in general. Our pages say what tuition can realistically move and over what period, which is a less exciting statement and a true one.

faqs.question: Is an agency better than an independent tutor for IB subjects?
faqs.answer: Neither is better in general; they fail differently. An agency gives you a pool, which matters for an unusual subject and level, plus some process, and it risks tutor rotation and a gap between the profile and the person who turns up. An independent tutor can be the strongest relationship available and carries no institutional backup, so the permit question, the record-keeping question and the reference question matter more. Decide by the failure you would least tolerate, and get the replacement or notice arrangement in writing either way.

faqs.question: What does it mean if a UAE tutoring page lists a foreign phone number?
faqs.answer: Usually that the support, and sometimes the teaching, is not where the page implies. Two providers ranking for these searches route UAE parents to numbers outside the country, and one shows a Dubai address on a page aimed at another emirate. Neither is automatically disqualifying, but both are things to ask about directly: where are the tutors based, where is the support team, and what hours do they work in Gulf Standard Time. A provider that is straightforward about it has nothing to hide; one that is evasive has answered the question.

faqs.question: How many trial sessions should we take before committing?
faqs.answer: One properly run trial is usually enough to judge diagnosis, and two sessions is enough to judge whether the student engages. Use the real material: the most recent marked paper or the current draft, not a generic worksheet. Watch four things. Does the tutor ask for the evidence before proposing a plan. Does the student talk. Does anything arrive in writing afterwards. And does the tutor say anything inconvenient, because a first conversation with no disagreement in it is a sales conversation.

faqs.question: Should I ask whether a tutor holds a private tutoring permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the reaction matters as much as the answer. The private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible categories including school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule of amounts. Since the permit costs nothing, dismissing the question tells you about attitude rather than about cost.

faqs.question: Can I ask for a reference from another parent?
faqs.answer: Yes, and ask for a specific one: a parent whose child took the same subject at the same level with the same tutor. Three questions are enough. Did the same person teach throughout. What did you receive in writing after each session. Would you book again. A provider claiming depth in a subject should be able to produce one relevant name, and a testimonial page with no subjects or levels attached is not a substitute. If no relevant reference exists, that is itself information about the claimed specialism.

faqs.question: Is the most expensive tutor usually the strongest?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, in a market with no independent quality signal. Published rates in this country run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the budget end to AED 650 at the top, with qualified online tuition around AED 150 to 300 and specialist work from AED 200 to 450 and above. That span reflects business models and positioning as much as capability. Price does correlate with scarcity: a genuine specialist in a narrow Higher Level subject costs more because few people can do it. Pay for the scarcity, having tested it, rather than for the position on a rate card.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram claim to be accredited by the IB or by KHDA?
faqs.answer: No, and it is worth being explicit. IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence, registration or partnership from the IB, from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE as an organisation, Cambridge or Pearson. Those bodies regulate schools, qualifications and, in the case of a Dubai training institute with premises, a specific educational services permit. None of that is a general endorsement of a tutoring provider, and no tutoring provider can hold one. Any page implying otherwise is making a claim a parent should ask it to evidence.

faqs.question: Would the strongest IB tutor for our child be someone based in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Possibly for a mainstream subject, and much less likely for a specific Higher Level combination. Ajman is a small emirate, few of its schools run the full Diploma, and the local pool of people who have taught a named subject at Higher Level is thin. Insisting on proximity in that situation means choosing availability over expertise without necessarily realising it. Our teaching is delivered one-to-one over live video, so the match is made nationally on subject and level. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we run only in India.

faqs.question: What should make us end an arrangement rather than persevere?
faqs.answer: Four things. Nothing arrives in writing, so the hours cannot be audited. The same person is not teaching each week without that having been agreed. A second marked attempt at the same question type shows no movement although the between-session work was done. Or the tutor offers, at any point, to produce part of an internal assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay. The last one is immediate and non-negotiable, because the risk falls on your child's qualification rather than on the provider's reputation.

ajman/best-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Replace the ranking with a test you can run yourself
ajman/best-ib-tutor.closingBody: There is no best IB tutor in Ajman in any measurable sense, and a page claiming the title has told you about its advertising rather than its teaching. What there is, is a short test: eight questions that a specialist answers specifically and a generalist cannot, a handful of warning signs visible before you make contact, and one trial session judged on diagnosis rather than on manner. Run it on us and on everyone else you are considering. Send your child's most recent marked paper, take the free trial with no card details taken, and judge the written note that follows against anything else you receive.

ajman/best-igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: The profiles below are IGCSE subject specialists who teach to a named syllabus code rather than to a general idea of maths or science. Each works one-to-one over live video, and each will mark a baseline past paper before the first full lesson is planned.

intro.heading: The word "best" is doing a lot of work in that search
paragraphs: An IGCSE tutor is only good relative to a specific syllabus, a specific paper and a specific gap. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 cover similar ground, but they are tiered differently, structured differently and marked to different schemes. A tutor who is excellent on one and guessing at the other is not the right match, however impressive the degree. The first question worth asking any tutor is which code they teach to, and the second is what they do in week one.

Ajman adds a practical constraint. Private schools here sit under the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level regulator, the private-school set is small, and a large share of households work in Dubai or Sharjah. That combination produces two effects a tutoring plan has to respect. Specialist subject teachers for the harder Extended papers are thin on the ground locally, and a weekday session realistically starts after 6.30pm once a parent has cleared Emirates Road.

The honest answer to scarcity is not to pretend otherwise. IB Gram matches Ajman families to subject specialists who teach over live video, one-to-one. That removes the radius problem entirely: a child in Al Mowaihat taking Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 Extended gets a physics specialist rather than the nearest generalist who can drive over. Home visits are a service IB Gram offers only in India, and this page makes that explicit rather than burying it.

What follows is the detail a parent needs to run the decision themselves. Which tier your child is entered for and what it caps their grade at. Which papers they sit and how long each one is. Where the marks actually leak in each subject, named by topic. What the market charges in AED per hour across the provider models in this part of the UAE. The exam calendar read backwards from the paper to the entry deadline, because the deadline is months earlier than most families expect. And the five-subject rule the Ministry of Education applies when it looks at an IGCSE certificate for equivalency.

There is one more thing worth saying before the detail starts. The pages competing for this search average about 2,300 words and most publish no price, no exam date and no syllabus code at all. That is not a reason to trust this page instead; it is a reason to check it. Every regulatory statement here is attributable to u.ae, KHDA, MoHRE or the exam board that published it, every AED figure is attributed to the provider or rate table it came from, and anything unverified is marked as unverified rather than smoothed over. IB exam-session dates in particular are not published here, because the IB's own site could not be confirmed directly and a date a family plans around has to come from the school's IB coordinator.

None of it needs a tutor to be useful. If you read the tier table and the mark-loss section and conclude your child needs six focused weeks on one paper rather than a year of weekly sessions, that is a better outcome than a subscription. The page is written so you can tell the difference.
