Core or Extended entry, which most quotes are issued without knowing

sections.heading: The practical component: a fifth of the grade and the hardest hour to buy locally
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of the 0610 grade comes from either Paper 5, a practical test sat in the school's laboratory, or Paper 6, a written paper about experimental work. Which one a student sits is a school decision made at entry. Many Ajman families do not know which applies to their child, and a surprising number of students find out in the examination hall.

That matters commercially, because the two routes have completely different costs. Paper 6 is a written paper. It rewards knowing how to tabulate results, plot a graph properly, identify the independent and dependent variables, name a control, state a source of error and propose an improvement that is actually testable. Every one of those is teachable over a shared screen with past-paper questions, and it is among the best value blocks a family can buy, because schools routinely under-revise it.

Paper 5 is harder to help with honestly. The student handles apparatus in their own school laboratory, and no tutor can replicate that. What a tutor can do is drill the thinking that surrounds the practical work: how to record repeat readings, when to discard an anomalous result and say so, how to describe a method so another person could follow it, and how to answer the evaluation questions that carry marks at the end. Any provider claiming to deliver laboratory practice remotely is selling something that does not exist.

The practical papers also reach backwards into the theory course. The food tests belong to human nutrition. The osmosis investigation belongs to movement into and out of cells. The photosynthesis rate experiment belongs to plant nutrition. A block of practical work therefore repairs theory topics at the same time, which is the reason it tends to be the most efficient spend in the whole 0610 plan.

sections.heading: Spending nothing first: what moves a 0610 mark without a tutor
paragraphs: Several of the most reliable improvements in a Biology grade cost nothing, and a page that prices tutoring without saying so is not being straight with you. Start with the school. Ask the science teacher for the mark breakdown of the last mock by question rather than the total. A total tells you there is a problem; the breakdown tells you whether it is recall, application, practical or timing, and those four problems have four different solutions, only two of which need paying for.

Next, ask which tier and which practical route your child is entered for, in writing. It is free, it takes one email, and it prevents the single most expensive error described on this page. While you are asking, request the school's scheme of work for the rest of the year, so that any tutoring you do buy can follow the class rather than run parallel to it.

Then there is the student's own past-paper habit. Working through questions with the mark scheme open beside them teaches nothing, because recognising a correct answer is not the same as producing one. Working through them closed, then marking honestly against the scheme afterwards and writing out the corrected version, is the single highest-return unpaid activity available in this course. Cambridge publishes specimen and past materials through schools and its own channels; your child's teacher is the right route to them, and nobody should be supplying copies of board material outside that.

If, after all that, the gaps are specific and the student is still short, that is the point at which paid hours start earning their rate. A tutor working on a diagnosed list of three topics and a known paper is worth considerably more per hour than one hired to be generally helpful, and will usually be needed for fewer hours.

sections.heading: Entries, series and the dates that cost money when missed
paragraphs: Cambridge runs IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every examination centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge is explicit that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after consulting the wrong one. For a family in Ajman whose child sits papers at a Sharjah or Dubai centre, checking the zone against the school's own timetable is a five-minute job worth doing.

The gap between entry and examination is larger than most parents expect, and it is the reason a tier conversation in March is usually too late. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series illustrate the pattern: the examination period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries were due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades on 27 February 2027, results were released on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. UAE schools sit the June and November series rather than that one, but the shape of the timeline is the same: entries close months ahead of the first paper.

Pearson's International GCSE calendar runs on its own schedule, with series in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why any plan should be built against the live official timetable rather than against a date copied from a page like this one.

Counted backwards from a June paper, the useful markers are simple. The autumn term is when a weekly slot is cheap and available. The winter mock is the diagnostic that tells you what to buy. February and March are when the practical component should be addressed, because it is the part the school revises last. April is for timed full papers. May is for sleep, and for nothing that a tutor can sell you.

sections.heading: What the fee does not buy, and the line a tutor works inside
paragraphs: No fee buys a grade. Any provider offering one in this market should be read carefully, because a promise of a specific outcome in a public examination is a claim nobody can honour and a claim UAE consumer rules take seriously. What a fee buys is teaching time, marking and a record of what changed, and a parent is entitled to see all three.

A fee also does not buy coursework. Cambridge IGCSE Biology has no written coursework component, but the honesty principle still applies to practical write-ups and any school-assessed work: a tutor teaches method, explains where a scheme awards marks, and gives feedback on work the student has produced themselves. A tutor who offers to supply finished answers for submission is creating a malpractice risk that sits with the student, not with them.

Nor does a fee buy board material. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and the right route to them is the school or the board's own site. Reference them, link to them, work from what the school provides; do not accept a provider distributing copies as a selling point.

On the legal side, private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work rather than casual work. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts is published, so none is quoted here. It is a fair question to ask anyone you are about to pay.

process.title: Send the mock script, not the grade
process.description: The useful first message contains the last Biology paper with the marks shown by question, the tier your child is entered for if you know it, and the practical route. A grade on its own tells us almost nothing. A script tells us whether the problem is recall, phrasing, application or the clock, and those need different tutors and different numbers of hours.

process.title: A free 50-minute trial lesson
process.description: One lesson with no card details taken beforehand and no commitment afterwards. It runs as a diagnostic: a few questions across different topics and command words, a written answer produced and marked live, and a direct opinion at the end about what is wrong and roughly how long it takes to fix. If the answer is that you do not need paid hours, that is what you will be told.

process.title: A written plan with a number attached
process.description: After the trial you get the topic list in priority order, the papers each session targets, the number of sessions proposed and what that costs in AED. The plan says which parts you should do without us, because several of them are free. Nothing is charged until you agree the plan, and the plan is a working document rather than a package.

process.title: Weekly sessions with written output
process.description: Each session leaves something behind: a marked answer, a corrected version written by the student, and a short note on what to practise before the next one. That record is what makes progress arguable rather than felt, and it is what you should ask any provider for regardless of whether you work with us.

process.title: A review at week six, honestly
process.description: Six sessions in, we compare the diagnostic against a fresh timed paper and say whether the change is real. If the marks have moved, the plan continues and may shorten. If they have not, we change the tutor or tell you the approach is wrong. Continuing to invoice while nothing moves is the commonest failure in this market and the easiest one to avoid.

whyPoints.title: Prices on the page, with sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider that published it and dated to October 2026. Three of the most visible competitor pages in this market publish no price at all, and one of them asks the price question in its own FAQ and then declines to answer it. A family should be able to judge a quote before speaking to anybody.

whyPoints.title: The tier question asked first
whyPoints.description: Core and Extended are different courses with different papers and different mark schemes. We ask which one your child is entered for before quoting, because a quote issued without it is guesswork and a tutor working from the wrong past papers is worse than no tutor at all.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Saying so lets a family compare like with like instead of discovering the format after payment, and it removes the travel line that sits silently inside every in-home rate.

whyPoints.title: A pool that is not bounded by a driving radius
whyPoints.description: The constraint on Biology help in Ajman is not money; it is how few people within a short drive have taught Extended 0610 through to a series. Video delivery replaces a radius with availability, which is the one structural advantage of the format and the reason it is the format we use.

whyPoints.title: Marked written work, every session
whyPoints.description: Half the 0610 grade sits in a structured theory paper where phrasing decides marks. That skill is built by writing answers and having them marked against the scheme, not by listening to explanations. Every session produces a marked answer and a corrected rewrite, and you can read both.

whyPoints.title: The honest no
whyPoints.description: If a trial lesson shows that the gap is timing or effort rather than understanding, we say so and do not sell you twenty hours. If no specialist is free for the subject and slot you need, we say that too rather than filling the slot with somebody who teaches a different science.

faqs.question: What does a Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610 tutor cost per hour for a family in Ajman?
faqs.answer: The published market in the UAE runs from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour for generalist online tuition, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, and AED 200 to 450 and above for an IGCSE or IB specialist. In-home visits sit between AED 180 and 500 because travel is priced inside the rate. Those figures come from EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, TutorChase and the Bestimate 2026 rate survey, read in October 2026. IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson, once the tier and the time remaining before the series are known, and there is no travel line in it.

faqs.question: Is Biology 0610 cheaper to tutor than Chemistry 0620 or Physics 0625?
faqs.answer: Slightly, in most of this market, and for a supply reason rather than a difficulty one. More teachers are comfortable teaching Biology to IGCSE level than are comfortable with Physics, so the pool is deeper and the scarcity premium is smaller. That gap narrows sharply at the Extended tier and disappears entirely in February and March, when every competent science tutor in the northern emirates is booked. If a quote for Biology comes in above the specialist band, ask what is in the hour that justifies it, and expect the answer to involve marking.

faqs.question: How many paid hours does a Year 11 Biology student in Ajman usually need?
faqs.answer: It depends almost entirely on where the marks are being lost. A student at 55 per cent on Paper 4 with scattered partial credit across every question is typically looking at fifteen to twenty-five hours spread over a term, because the work is marked written practice and that cannot be compressed. A student at the same mark who simply ran out of time needs perhaps six, plus a clock. A student missing whole topics needs a plan with the school rather than a tutor. The diagnostic in a first lesson exists to tell these apart before anyone commits.

faqs.question: Does preparing for Paper 6 cost less than preparing for Paper 5?
faqs.answer: Preparation for Paper 6 is usually better value, because Paper 6 is a written paper about experiments and therefore responds directly to written practice over a shared screen. Variables, tables, graph plotting, sources of error and improvements are all teachable remotely and are reliably under-revised in school. Paper 5 is a practical test sat in the school laboratory, so a tutor can teach method, recording and evaluation but cannot replicate the apparatus. Both carry 20 per cent of the grade. The first thing to establish is which route your child's school entered them for, because the two need different work.

faqs.question: My son is entered for Core Biology. Is it worth paying to move him up to Extended?
faqs.answer: A tier change is a school decision taken against the Cambridge entry deadline, not something tutoring can arrange, so the first conversation is with the science coordinator rather than with us. Where a change is still possible, the question is whether the student can absorb the supplement material in the time left and still hold the core content securely. If the answer is yes, the certificate ceiling moves from grade C to A*, which matters for any route into A Level or Diploma Biology. If the answer is no, paying for Extended teaching buys a worse Core result.

faqs.question: Are there cheaper ways to raise a 0610 grade in Ajman than one-to-one tutoring?
faqs.answer: Several, and they should be tried first. Ask the school for the mock mark breakdown by question rather than the total, so you know whether the loss is recall, application, practical or timing. Confirm the entry tier and practical route in writing. Get the scheme of work for the rest of the year. Then have the student work past-paper questions with the mark scheme closed, mark honestly afterwards and rewrite the weak answers. None of that costs anything, and it is also what makes any paid hours you do buy go further.

faqs.question: Why do Biology tutoring quotes in the northern emirates rise between January and April?
faqs.answer: Because supply is fixed and demand is not. The number of people in and around Ajman who can teach Extended Biology to examination level does not change during the year, but the number of families wanting them rises sharply once winter mock results come home. By March most competent science tutors in the area are committed through the June series, and the remaining availability is priced accordingly. Booking a weekly slot in October costs less and secures a better tutor than booking the same help in March, which is the strongest practical argument for starting early.

faqs.question: Do you charge for the first Biology session?
faqs.answer: No. The first 50-minute lesson is free, with no card details taken beforehand and no obligation afterwards. It is run as a diagnostic rather than a sample lesson: a spread of questions across topics and command words, one written answer produced and marked live, and a direct opinion about what is actually wrong. You then receive a written plan with a number attached before anything is charged. If the lesson suggests the problem does not need paid hours, that is what the plan will say.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover 0610 Biology and 0620 Chemistry for the same student?
faqs.answer: Often, and it usually reduces the per-hour figure because one person is filling two slots. The test is whether they have taught both to examination level rather than whether they feel confident in both. Ask which papers they have taught most recently in each, and ask to see how they mark a structured answer in the weaker of the two. Where the honest answer is that they are strong in one and passable in the other, two specialists for fewer total hours is usually the better purchase than one generalist for more.

faqs.question: How much of the 0610 grade is already decided before the written papers?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent of it, through the practical component, is decided by work done in or about the laboratory rather than in the theory papers. The tier is also fixed in advance, and with it the ceiling on the grade. Everything else is still open. That matters for budgeting: a family discovering in April that the practical paper has not been revised has a fifth of the grade in play and very little time, which is why a block aimed at Paper 5 or Paper 6 in February is one of the most efficient purchases in the whole course.

faqs.question: Which of the twenty-one 0610 topics should we pay for first?
faqs.answer: Whichever the mock script says, and the script usually says one of four. Inheritance and genetics, because it carries method marks and rewards being taught properly. Enzymes and biological molecules, because the vocabulary recurs across digestion, respiration and photosynthesis. Transport and gas exchange, because the explanation chains are long and partial answers score poorly. And the practical skills behind Paper 5 or 6. Ecology and human influence usually comes last in the teaching order and is largely recall, which makes it the worst use of a specialist hour and the best use of a weekend.

faqs.question: Does a family in Ajman pay more because few Biology specialists live nearby?
faqs.answer: For in-home tuition, yes, and noticeably. A small emirate with a small private-school set has few people who have taught Extended 0610 through to a series, and anyone travelling to a villa in Al Mowaihat or a tower in Emirates City is pricing the drive into the hour whether the invoice itemises it or not. Online delivery removes that constraint, because the pool is no longer bounded by a driving radius. That is the main reason the format exists here rather than a claim that screens teach better than rooms.

faqs.question: Is a monthly Biology package better value than paying per session?
faqs.answer: Only after you divide. Packages advertised in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, which works out near AED 100 an hour, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions, which lands closer to AED 200 to 225. A package is good value when the sessions will genuinely be used and bad value in a month with half-term, travel or examinations in it. Ask what happens to unused sessions before agreeing, and ask whether marking is included or billed separately.

faqs.question: What should a 0610 quote tell me before I accept it?
faqs.answer: Six things. Which tier and which practical route it assumes. How many sessions, over how many weeks. Whether marked written work is included or only explanation. Who the tutor is and which papers they have taught most recently. What happens if the match is wrong after two sessions. And what the total comes to in AED rather than per hour. A quote missing any of those is not yet a quote, and a provider who will not put them in writing has told you something useful.

faqs.question: Does a Biology tutor charging an Ajman family need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need a private tuition work permit from MoHRE, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. It is a reasonable question to ask anybody before you pay them.

ajman/cambridge-igcse-biology-0610-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the script, not the search
ajman/cambridge-igcse-biology-0610-tutor.closingBody: If you take one thing from this page, make it the mock paper rather than the rate table. Send the last Biology script with marks shown by question, tell us the tier and the practical route if you know them, and take the free 50-minute diagnostic. You will get a written plan in AED, a priority list of topics, and an honest note on which parts of it you should do yourselves without paying anyone. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled late enough to survive an Ajman commute. If no specialist is free for your subject and slot, we will say so rather than fill it.

ajman/cambridge-igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Cambridge IGCSE subjects to Ajman students over live video. Each starts by confirming the syllabus code and tier from the school's entry details, because a Core candidate and an Extended candidate in the same classroom are preparing for different papers with different grade ceilings.

intro.heading: Start with the code, the tier and the series
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE is a family of separate syllabuses rather than a single qualification, and almost every avoidable problem in preparing for it comes from treating the whole thing as one undifferentiated course. A student revising from a guide bought for the wrong syllabus, practising the wrong tier, or working to a timetable from the wrong administrative zone has been let down by information rather than by teaching. Those three facts are free to establish, they take one email to the school to confirm, and between them they decide almost everything that follows in a preparation plan.

The syllabus code is the first. Mathematics is 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, English First Language 0500, Economics 0455, Business Studies 0450, Computer Science 0478, Additional Mathematics 0606, Accounting 0452. A code pins down the content, the paper structure and the mark scheme conventions for a given exam year. Two schools in the same district can enter the same subject under different codes, and a code can be revised between years, which is why the version matters as much as the number.

The tier is the second. Many Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended papers with different content and different grade ceilings. A Core candidate sitting excellent papers cannot reach the top grades; an Extended candidate who should have been entered for Core can lose marks across a whole series. That decision is made by the school, usually in Year 10, and it is reversible only within the centre's entry deadlines. Parents in Ajman are rarely told it is a decision at all.

The series is the third. Cambridge examines in a June series and a November series for IGCSE and O Level, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and operates a March series in some regions. Entries close months before papers are sat. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone version was used.

Those four paragraphs cover more administrative ground than most tuition pages address in their entirety, and they are deliberately first. An Ajman family whose child attends school here or across the border in Sharjah can confirm all of it with one email to the exams officer. After that, the useful work is subject-specific: which papers carry the marks, where the method marks sit, how the practical papers are examined, and what a marked script should look like when it comes back. Teaching is delivered one-to-one over live video, since IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India.

ajman/cambridge-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Cambridge runs a stage-by-stage structure, and Ajman families usually meet three parts of it. Knowing which stage a child is in determines whether the assessment is diagnostic, internal or externally examined for a certificate.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The stage before IGCSE, where schools may enter students for Checkpoint tests in English, mathematics and science. Checkpoint is diagnostic rather than certificating: it reports attainment against the Cambridge curriculum framework and is often used by schools to decide tiering for IGCSE two years later. Cambridge runs Checkpoint tests in March, May and October.
programmes.countryNote: In Ajman and the neighbouring emirates, Checkpoint results are frequently the evidence a school uses when deciding whether a student is placed on the Core or Extended pathway. That makes Year 9 a more consequential year than families realise, and a diagnostic weakness addressed then is considerably cheaper than a tier correction in Year 11.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Separate syllabuses by subject, each with its own code, content, paper structure and assessment conventions. Many subjects are tiered into Core and Extended with different grade ranges available. Grading is reported either on the 9 to 1 scale or on A* to G depending on the syllabus, and grade thresholds are set after each series rather than fixed in advance.
programmes.countryNote: Most Ajman private schools entering international candidates use Cambridge, and a single school can enter different subjects under different boards. The code and tier therefore have to be confirmed subject by subject rather than assumed from the school's general curriculum description.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The stage after IGCSE for students on the Cambridge pathway rather than the Diploma, assessed by externally marked papers with some subjects carrying practical components. AS can be taken as a standalone qualification or as the first half of the A Level, which matters for the UAE equivalency route where Advanced Subsidiary results are explicitly recognised.
programmes.countryNote: For a student in Ajman planning on a UAE university, the Advanced Level route carries a published equivalency requirement: one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside the IGCSE requirement. That makes the AS decision an admissions decision rather than only an academic one.

ajman/cambridge-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are listed with their Cambridge codes and with the component that usually decides the grade. Confirm the paper structure against the syllabus for your child's exam year, because Cambridge revises syllabuses and a guide bought for an earlier version can describe papers that no longer exist.

subjects.name: Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Assessed by written papers at each tier, with one calculator and one non-calculator component in the current structure. Method marks are available on almost every structured question, which makes working written in rough and never transferred to the answer space the single largest avoidable loss at both tiers.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Taken alongside or after 0580 by stronger candidates, covering calculus, trigonometry and series at a level closer to AS than to IGCSE. Students who arrive without secure algebraic manipulation find the pace unforgiving, and the usual remedy is algebra drill rather than topic coverage.

subjects.name: Physics 0625
subjects.description: Multiple choice and theory papers at each tier, plus either a practical test or the alternative to practical paper. Electricity and circuits is the topic Ajman students most often arrive weakest in, and the alternative to practical rewards apparatus knowledge and error analysis rather than recall.

subjects.name: Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Multiple choice and theory papers at each tier with a practical component. Mole calculations and the qualitative analysis ion tests decide the grade; students who memorise the tests as a list rather than as observations tied to a conclusion lose the application marks on the Extended theory paper.

subjects.name: Biology 0610
subjects.description: Content volume is the visible problem and command terms are the real one. Describe, explain and suggest carry different expectations, and marks are lost where a student writes the same depth of answer throughout a paper regardless of the mark allocation shown beside each question.

subjects.name: English First Language 0500
subjects.description: A reading paper and a directed writing and composition paper, with a separately reported speaking endorsement in some centres. The reading responses are marked on selection of detail and inference; fluent general answers without close reference to the text sit in the middle bands.

subjects.name: Economics 0455
subjects.description: A multiple choice paper and a structured questions paper. Diagram accuracy is assessable in itself, and an explanation that never refers back to the diagram the student drew scores below a simpler answer that does. Evaluation is what separates the top band in the extended responses.

subjects.name: Business Studies 0450
subjects.description: A short answer and structured paper plus a case study paper. The case study rewards application to the specific business in the material; a technically correct general answer about a business tool with no reference to the case loses most of the available marks.

subjects.name: Computer Science 0478
subjects.description: One paper on computer systems and one on algorithms, programming and logic. Pseudocode and trace tables are where marks are won and lost, and students who have only written code in an editor struggle with hand-traced algorithm questions under time pressure.

subjects.name: Accounting 0452
subjects.description: Layout and format carry marks alongside the arithmetic, so a correct figure in the wrong statement scores less than a presented account with a minor error. Adjustments at the year end are the recurring difficulty, and practice has to be on full questions rather than isolated entries.

ajman/cambridge-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: What changes between Ajman districts for an IGCSE candidate is which school entered them, which board that school uses, and how long the daily journey leaves for evening work. None of it changes the syllabus, which is why the code and tier are worth confirming wherever you live.

regions.name: Al Nuaimiya
regions.note: The largest concentration of IGCSE candidates in the emirate, served by big day schools within reach. Families here can usually get a code and tier confirmation in person from the exams officer, which is faster than any email.

regions.name: Al Rashidiya
regions.note: Central Ajman with towers and villas near the Corniche. Year 11 students in this cluster typically take one weekday evening slot, with timed paper practice done at the weekend when a full two-hour sitting is possible.

regions.name: Al Jurf
regions.note: Quick access to Sharjah schools and a slow evening return. Students entered for the November series here benefit from starting paper practice in the summer rather than waiting for the autumn term to settle.

regions.name: Al Mowaihat
regions.note: Villa sub-districts with school runs into Sharjah. Siblings at different stages are common, and Year 9 Checkpoint work for one child often sits alongside Year 11 Extended preparation for another.

regions.name: Al Yasmeen and Al Zahya
regions.note: Newer Emirates Road communities with Dubai-facing commutes. These households are the most likely in the emirate to have a child entered under Pearson Edexcel rather than Cambridge, which changes the mark scheme conventions entirely.

regions.name: Al Helio and Al Rawda
regions.note: Low-rise villa areas with a quiet room usually available, which matters for timed paper practice more than it does for ordinary teaching. A full uninterrupted two-hour sitting is the hardest thing to arrange in a busy household.

regions.name: Emirates City and Al Alia
regions.note: High-rise blocks with the longest daily travel in Ajman for students attending school across the border. Evening sessions here start late, and a fixed online slot avoids adding any further journey to an already long day.

schoolClusters.city: Ajman day schools entering international candidates
schoolClusters.note: Private schools in Ajman are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority. These are the schools where most Cambridge IGCSE entries in the emirate originate, and where the exams officer is the right first point of contact for codes and tiers.

schoolClusters.city: International schools on the Emirates Road side

sections.heading: Core and Extended: the decision most parents are never told about
paragraphs: Many Cambridge IGCSE subjects are tiered. Core papers cover a reduced content set and make the lower grade range available; Extended papers cover additional content and make the upper grades available. A student entered for Core cannot reach the top grades however well they perform, and a student entered for Extended who is not ready for it can lose marks consistently across every paper in the subject.

The entry decision belongs to the school and is typically made in Year 10, often on the basis of internal assessment or Checkpoint evidence from Year 9. It can be changed, but only inside the centre's entry window, which closes well before the papers. Once that window has passed, the tier is fixed for the series regardless of how the student's performance develops.

What that means for a family is that the tier question has a deadline. The right time to ask whether the entry still matches the student's performance is in the first half of Year 11, with marked work in hand, not in the spring. The question to put to the exams officer is specific: which tier is my child currently entered for in each subject, what is the centre's deadline for changing it, and what evidence would support a change.

There is a related trap worth naming. Revision material bought without checking the tier teaches content the student will never be examined on, or omits content they will. Extended-only topics are a recurring source of wasted preparation for Core candidates and of unpleasant surprises for Extended candidates working from a Core guide. The syllabus for the exam year states which content belongs to which tier, and it is published by Cambridge rather than by a bookshop.

sections.heading: Codes, components and where the marks sit
paragraphs: A Cambridge syllabus code is a precise instruction about what will be examined and how. Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 each specify their own component structure, and the sciences in particular follow a recognisable pattern: a multiple choice paper and a theory paper at each tier, plus either a practical test or an alternative to practical paper depending on what the centre offers.

Component numbers matter because past-paper practice is organised by them. A student practising the wrong component is practising the wrong question style, even within the right subject and tier. The useful habit is to write the subject, code, tier and component numbers on one sheet at the start of Year 11 and to check every practice paper against it. That takes ten minutes and prevents a term of misdirected work.

Within the papers, the mark allocation printed beside each question is the instruction nobody reads. A two-mark question wants two points, a six-mark question wants a developed chain of reasoning, and the student who writes a paragraph for the first and a sentence for the second has mismanaged a paper regardless of their subject knowledge. Teaching command-term depth against the printed allocation is one of the fastest grade changes available in Year 11.

Because Cambridge revises syllabuses, every statement about paper structure carries a version. Confirm the component pattern against the syllabus document for your child's exam year rather than against a guide or a tutoring page, including this one. Cambridge publishes those documents on its own site, and reading the assessment overview section takes a few minutes and settles the question definitively.

sections.heading: The six administrative zones, and the timetable version trap
paragraphs: This is the most consequential piece of Cambridge administration almost nobody outside an exams office knows. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and the exam timetable differs between zones. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam because the wrong zone version was used.

For a family in Ajman the practical risk is specific. A revision plan built from a timetable found online, or from a friend's child at a school in another country, can place a paper on the wrong day. The student who revises in the wrong order loses preparation; the student who arrives on the wrong day loses the paper. The only safe source is the timetable the centre itself issues, and the only safe question to the exams officer is which zone the centre sits in.

The same caution applies to anything downloaded from a search result. Cambridge publishes key dates and timetables for each series on its own site, and provisional timetables are released ahead of a series and can be revised. A date copied from a third party in September may no longer be accurate in January, which is why this page points at the official source rather than restating a full timetable.

Ajman adds one local wrinkle for the many students entered by schools across the border. The centre is the school, not the home, so the zone that governs the timetable is the school's, not the emirate the family lives in. Families with two children at schools in different emirates have occasionally found themselves working from two different timetable versions in the same household, which is exactly the situation the official issue from each centre resolves.
bullets: Every Cambridge centre sits in one of six administrative zones
Timetables differ by zone and the correct version is essential

sections.heading: Series and entry deadlines, as Cambridge publishes them
paragraphs: Cambridge examines IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series, runs a March series in some regions, and offers Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Entries are made by the centre, not by the family, and they close months before the papers. That lead time is where most families lose options they did not know they had.

The published key dates for the March 2027 series show the shape clearly. The exam period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027. Final entries were due on 27 November 2026, which is more than two months before the first paper. Forecast grades are due on 27 February 2027. Results are released to centres on Cambridge Direct on 13 May, with certificates following in late June.

Read backwards, that calendar has consequences for a tutoring plan. Any tier change has to happen before the entry deadline. Any decision about dropping or adding a subject has the same deadline. Forecast grades, which schools submit, are produced from internal evidence, so a student who wants that figure to reflect their current ability needs the evidence in the school's hands before the submission date rather than after it.

For families comparing boards, Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May and June and in November. Its November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is a further reason to work from the live official document rather than a restated date.

sections.heading: The practical papers, and how practical skill is examined
paragraphs: Parents considering online tuition for a science subject reasonably ask how practical work is handled. The answer is that Cambridge examines practical skills on paper. Depending on what the centre offers, a student sits either a practical test or the alternative to practical paper, and in both cases the examined material is apparatus knowledge, variable control, measurement technique, sources of error and the interpretation of results.

That is teachable remotely, and in some respects it is taught better remotely than in a crowded laboratory. The alternative to practical paper rewards a student who can read a described setup, identify the independent and dependent variables, spot what has not been controlled, and explain why a particular reading is unreliable. Those are reasoning skills practised on past questions and diagrams rather than physical skills practised at a bench.

The practical work the school does still matters, and nothing here replaces it. A student who has handled a measuring cylinder, a thermometer and a circuit board writes better answers about them. What a tutor adds is the examined layer: the conventions of recording results to an appropriate precision, the language the mark scheme accepts for an error discussion, and the structure of a conclusion that evaluates rather than restates.

One practical point for an Ajman family. Find out from the school which component your child sits, because the practical test and the alternative to practical paper are different papers with different preparation. Past-paper work aimed at the wrong one is a common and entirely avoidable waste, and the answer is in the centre's entry details rather than in any general advice about science revision.
bullets: Practical skill is examined on paper, by test or by the alternative to practical

sections.heading: Grade scales and thresholds: what a grade actually represents
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE results are reported either on the 9 to 1 numeric scale or on A* to G, depending on the syllabus and the version in use. Both appear in UAE schools, sometimes in the same student's results, which causes confusion when a family tries to compare a sibling's grades or an older set of results against a newer one.

What sits behind either scale is a grade threshold: the mark at which a grade begins for that component and series. Thresholds are set after the papers have been sat and marked, following a review of candidate performance, which is why they move between series. A paper that was harder than its predecessor can produce the same grade from a lower mark. That is the mechanism, and it is the reason a raw percentage from a school mock cannot be mapped onto a Cambridge grade with any confidence.

Two consequences follow for how marked work should be read. First, a mock percentage is useful as a comparison against the same paper marked the same way, not as a grade prediction. Second, an improvement of a few marks near a threshold can be worth a whole grade, which is why targeted work on a single recurring question type is often more productive late in Year 11 than broad revision.

Cambridge publishes threshold information for past series on its own site, and schools have access to it. This page deliberately does not reproduce threshold tables, syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes: they are Cambridge's material, and reproducing them would be a copyright matter rather than a service. The right approach is to reference them, cite where they live and point a family at the official source.
bullets: Results appear on 9 to 1 or A* to G depending on the syllabus version
Grade thresholds are set after each series and move between series
A mock percentage is a comparison, not a grade prediction
Past papers, mark schemes and threshold tables belong to Cambridge and are referenced, not reproduced

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel for the same subject
paragraphs: Both boards are present in UAE schools and Ajman families frequently have children entered under each, sometimes in different subjects at the same school. The question of which is harder has no useful answer, because the difficulty is in the match between the student and the assessment style rather than in the board. The question that does have an answer is how they differ in practice.

The differences that matter are structural. Codes and component patterns are board-specific, so past-paper practice must come from the right board. Mark schemes accept different wording and reward different working even where a topic appears in both specifications. Tiering is handled differently between boards and subjects. Grading scales may differ. And session structures are not identical: Cambridge examines in June and November with a March series in some regions, Pearson in May and June and in November.

The practical implication is narrow and important. A family that buys a revision guide, joins a study group, or hires a tutor for the wrong board has bought something that will partially work and partially mislead. Partial misleading is worse than ignorance in an exam, because the student has rehearsed answers that will not earn full credit. Confirming the board subject by subject takes one email.

Where a student is entered under different boards in different subjects, the plan has to respect that rather than smooth it over. Practice material, timing conventions and even the vocabulary used to describe questions should follow the board for that subject. This is one of the clearest arguments for a specialist per subject rather than a single generalist covering the whole timetable.

sections.heading: Private candidates and the northern emirates
paragraphs: Some Ajman students need to sit a Cambridge subject their school does not offer, or to retake outside a school entry, or to take an examination while between schools. Cambridge examinations are sat at a Cambridge exam centre, which means a private candidate has to find a centre that accepts private entries and enter through it. The centre handles the entry, the timetable and the invigilation.

That has three practical consequences. The centre's entry deadline governs, not the student's readiness, so the search for a centre has to begin months before the series. The centre's administrative zone determines the timetable version. And the centre decides which components it can offer, which matters most for the sciences, where a practical test requires facilities that an alternative to practical paper does not.

Costs sit with the centre and vary, so no figure is published here; ask the centre directly and in writing. Families should also ask what the centre requires in terms of identification and prior documentation, since a private candidate has no school file behind them and the paperwork is the part that most often runs late.

A tutor's role for a private candidate is the same as for a school candidate, with one addition: making sure the preparation matches the components the centre has actually entered. It is the one situation where confirming code, tier and component is not administrative tidiness but the whole basis of the plan, because there is no classroom teacher quietly keeping the student on the right paper.

faqs.question: My child's school just says British curriculum. How do we find the actual syllabus code?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's exams officer directly, subject by subject, and ask for it in writing. A single school can enter different subjects under different boards and codes, so the curriculum description on a school website is not a reliable answer. The code pins down the content, the component pattern and the mark scheme conventions for the exam year, which is what revision material and past-paper practice have to match. Mathematics is 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, English First Language 0500, Economics 0455 and Computer Science 0478 in the current Cambridge set.

faqs.question: What is the real difference between Core and Extended papers?
faqs.answer: Content and grade ceiling. Core papers cover a reduced content set and make only the lower part of the grade scale available. Extended papers cover that content plus additional material and make the upper grades available, including the top band. A capable student entered for Core is capped however well they perform, and a student entered for Extended before they are ready loses marks across every component. The school makes the entry decision, usually in Year 10, and it can only be changed inside the centre's entry deadline.

faqs.question: Can a student move from Core to Extended partway through Year 11?
faqs.answer: Only within the centre's entry window, which closes months before the papers. For the Cambridge March 2027 series, for example, final entries were due on 27 November 2026 against an exam period starting 3 February 2027. So the practical answer is that the conversation needs to happen in the first half of Year 11, with marked work in hand to support it. Ask the exams officer which tier your child is entered for in each subject, what the centre's deadline for a change is, and what evidence would support one.

faqs.question: Why would the exam timetable differ between one Cambridge centre and another?
faqs.answer: Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and exam timetables differ between zones. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. Since the centre is the school rather than your home, the zone follows the school. For Ajman families whose children attend school in Sharjah or Dubai, that means the timetable must come from the school's own issue rather than from a search result.

faqs.question: Are the June and November Cambridge series the same papers?
faqs.answer: They are separate series with their own papers, timetables, entry deadlines and grade thresholds. Cambridge examines IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series, operates a March series in some regions, and runs Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Thresholds are set after each series based on candidate performance, so the mark needed for a given grade is not identical between sessions. Practice should use past papers from the same series pattern your child will actually sit.

faqs.question: How is IGCSE Physics practical work assessed if my child studies online?
faqs.answer: On paper. Depending on what the centre offers, a student sits either a practical test or the alternative to practical paper, and in both cases what is examined is apparatus knowledge, variable control, measurement precision, sources of error and interpretation of results. Those are reasoning skills that are practised on past questions and described setups, which works well in a one-to-one online session. School laboratory work still supports the answers. Find out which component the centre has entered your child for, because the two papers need different preparation.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge IGCSE graded 9 to 1 or A* to G?
faqs.answer: Both scales are in use depending on the syllabus and version, and UAE schools sometimes report a mixture in the same set of results. What matters more than the scale is the grade threshold behind it: the mark at which each grade begins for that component and series. Thresholds are set after the papers are marked, following a review of candidate performance, so they move between series. That is why a raw percentage from a school mock cannot be converted into a Cambridge grade with any confidence.

faqs.question: What is a grade threshold and does it change between series?
faqs.answer: It is the mark at which a particular grade begins for a given component in a given series, and yes, it changes. Thresholds are set after the papers have been sat and marked, which allows the standard to be held steady when a paper turns out harder or easier than its predecessor. Two consequences follow. A mock percentage is only useful compared against the same paper marked the same way. And a few marks gained near a threshold can be worth a whole grade, which is why targeted work on one recurring question type often beats broad revision late in Year 11.

faqs.question: Which is harder for the same subject, Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel?
faqs.answer: Neither, usefully. The difficulty lies in the match between the student and the assessment style rather than in the board. What does differ is structural: codes and component patterns, series and entry deadlines, tiering arrangements, and the wording a mark scheme accepts. A student who rehearses answers from the wrong board has practised something that will only partially earn credit, which is worse than not practising at all. Confirm the board subject by subject with the exams officer, since one school can use both.

faqs.question: Can my child sit Cambridge exams as a private candidate in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Cambridge examinations are sat at a Cambridge exam centre, so a private candidate has to find a centre that accepts private entries and enter through it. The centre handles the entry, issues the timetable for its administrative zone and provides invigilation. Three things follow: the centre's entry deadline governs rather than the student's readiness, so start looking months ahead; the available components depend on the centre's facilities, which matters for science practicals; and fees and documentation requirements vary, so ask the centre directly and in writing.

faqs.question: Does UAE equivalency count five IGCSE subjects or six?
faqs.answer: The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One provider ranking for these searches publishes a six-subject figure for UAE candidates, which does not match that reported rule. Equivalency is a Ministry of Education process, so confirm the current requirement on the ministry's own channel before planning subject choices.

faqs.question: What does a Cambridge IGCSE tutor cost for a family in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Published market figures put budget online tuition from roughly AED 45 an hour, with platforms publishing from AED 33 to 52 and from AED 45 to 65, and qualified subject tutors online between about AED 150 and AED 300; one provider published IGCSE tuition from AED 150. Specialist exam-year work runs AED 200 to 450 and above. In-home visits sit around AED 180 to 500 because travel is inside the rate. Those are other providers' published figures. Our own quote follows the free trial lesson and depends on the subject, the tier and how many weeks remain before the series.

faqs.question: Would a Cambridge tutor teach at our house in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. IGCSE teaching for Ajman students is delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen for working through past questions and marked scripts returned in writing. For a specific syllabus code the practical gain is access to someone who teaches that code regularly, rather than choosing from the small number of people willing to drive into the emirate on a weekday evening.

faqs.question: What should a marked Cambridge paper look like when it comes back?
faqs.answer: Question by question, with the marks available, the marks awarded and a short reason drawn from the mark scheme's own language. Method marks should be recorded separately from the final answer, because the two tell different stories: a right answer with no working loses marks that were available, and a wrong answer with sound method keeps marks the student did not know about. A single percentage hides both. The resulting sheet should be readable by a parent who does not know the subject, which is the test it has to pass.

faqs.question: How late can we start and still change a grade in one series?
faqs.answer: It depends on what is still reachable rather than on the number of weeks. With a term remaining there is room for content work and question-type discipline together. With six to eight weeks, the realistic territory is timing, question selection, command-term depth and transferring working into the answer space, which near a grade threshold can be worth a grade. With two weeks, honest advice is timed papers and sleep rather than new material. An honest provider will tell you which case you are in before quoting for a block.

Those answers cost nothing and they determine whether every subsequent hour of practice is aimed at the right paper. Send the replies with the most recent marked paper, take the free trial lesson, and the block that follows will be built on the components your child will actually sit.

intro.heading: Emirates City runs on the Emirates Road, and so does its homework
paragraphs: Emirates City is a cluster of residential towers on the Ajman side of Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, built for people who work somewhere else. Rents are lower than in Sharjah and considerably lower than in Dubai, the towers are tall, and the trade a household makes when it moves here is money for road time. That trade is the single most important fact about tutoring in this district, and no competitor page mentions it.

Work through what it means on a weekday. A child at a school in central Ajman is on a bus before 7am. A child at a campus on the Emirates Road belt leaves at about 6.45am. A child crossing into Sharjah for Muwaileh or Al Nahda leaves earlier still and gets home after 4.45pm. Meanwhile the parent who would supervise homework is commuting to Dubai and is not through the door before 7.30pm, sometimes later. The homework window and the supervision window do not overlap.

Families solve that in one of three ways, and two of them do not work. They leave the child to study alone and hope, which works for a self-directed sixteen-year-old and for nobody else. They book a visiting tutor for 5.30pm and watch the arrangement collapse over four weeks of Emirates Road traffic. Or they book a fixed appointment at an hour that actually exists in their week, which in this district is often 8pm, and accept that it happens on a screen.

The second feature of the district is the housing itself. A tower apartment is a different study environment from a villa: rooms are shared, the living room has a television in it, siblings are closer together, and the quiet hour has to be negotiated rather than assumed. That is a solvable problem and it is worth naming, because a tutoring arrangement that ignores it produces a lesson in which a nine-year-old is talking over the student.

What this page does, then, is arithmetic rather than atmosphere. It maps departure and return times against the earliest slot that holds. It prices what travel adds to a tutor's AED rate and who pays for it. It states what subject coverage actually exists and what the fallback is when it does not. And it counts the examination year backwards from the board deadlines that Cambridge and Pearson publish themselves, because those deadlines sit months before the papers and a commuting family is the most likely to miss one.

On delivery, stated once and plainly: tuition for Emirates City families is one-to-one online over live video on a booked slot. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses, and home visiting is a service we offer in India only. In a tower on the Emirates Road, the absence of a drive is the product rather than a limitation of it.

ajman/emirates-city.programmesIntro: Three programmes cover the district, and each one asks something different of a commuting household. The primary years need short frequent contact, the International GCSE years need deadline management, and the Diploma needs an evening block protected rather than filled.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Cambridge and Pearson
programmes.description: The qualification most Emirates City students take, across both boards depending on the school. What makes it unforgiving for a commuting family is the deadline structure: entries close months before the papers, tiers are fixed at entry, and forecast grades are submitted on a published date. Cambridge allocates centres to six administrative zones with different timetables and states that the wrong zone version is the candidate's own risk.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman private schools sit under the federal Ministry of Education, so there is no emirate portal where an Emirates City parent can look up how a school handles entries. The practical substitute is the exams officer. Ask in September for the zone-specific timetable, the entry deadline and the tier, and put all three in the family calendar, because a parent home at 7.30pm will not catch a deadline announced in a bag note.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led units rather than subject chapters, with descriptive reporting instead of percentages. For a primary child the useful support is short and frequent rather than long and weekly: two half-hour sessions on number facts and written method do more than one hour, because attention at that age is the binding constraint and so is the parent's availability to settle the child beforehand.
programmes.countryNote: In a tower apartment with younger siblings, a half-hour online session at 5pm is far easier to hold than a visiting tutor's arrival at the same time. The lesson can happen at the dining table while a parent cooks within earshot, which is the arrangement most Emirates City households actually run, and it is one of the few cases where proximity genuinely does not help.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, with internal assessments the student designs and writes and a single session of written papers. The programme assumes substantial independent work, which suits a student who is already home alone between 4.45pm and 7.30pm and destroys one who is not. The difference is structure rather than ability, and structure is the thing a fixed weekly appointment supplies.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma provision near Emirates City means a daily journey, usually towards the Emirates Road belt or into Sharjah. A student leaving at 6.30am and home at 4.45pm has an evening block that must hold homework, coursework and any tuition. Protecting that block matters more than filling it, which is why the plans on this page are finite and reviewed rather than open-ended.

ajman/emirates-city.subjectsIntro: Requests from Emirates City lean commercial and quantitative, which reflects the households: accountancy, computer science, economics and the sciences come up far more often than literature. Codes are given where Ajman and Sharjah schools commonly enter them, and your own entry letter is the authority.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Accounting (0452)
subjects.description: A subject that rewards format discipline. Marks go to correctly laid-out ledgers, trial balances and final accounts, and a candidate with sound understanding and sloppy presentation scores below one with the reverse. Practice is quick to mark and quick to improve, which makes it one of the best uses of a short weekly slot.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Theory paper and practical problem-solving, with pseudocode conventions that candidates lose marks on because they write in a programming language instead. Trace tables, binary conversion and the logic questions are high-return areas that respond to drilling rather than to explanation, so sessions are built around sets of questions.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Diagram marks are the easiest in the subject and the most often lost: unlabelled axes, a shift drawn the wrong way, no new equilibrium marked. The data-response questions need answers about the extract rather than about economics in general, which is a discipline rather than a knowledge problem and takes about six sessions to fix.

subjects.name: Pearson International GCSE Physics (4PH1)
subjects.description: Pearson assesses practical understanding inside the written papers rather than through a separate alternative-to-practical option, so candidates need to reason about apparatus they have not handled recently. Equation recall under time pressure and the extended six-mark answers are where Higher tier candidates lose the marks that separate grades.

subjects.name: Pearson International GCSE Chemistry (4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole calculations, electrolysis and the organic section carry a disproportionate share of the available marks. Question ordering and mark tariffs differ from Cambridge's, which matters because a student practising the wrong board's papers builds the wrong pacing instincts even when the chemistry is identical.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE First Language English (0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the reading responses reward control of register and precise use of the passage. Candidates lift phrases wholesale and lose marks for not reshaping them, or write a competent piece in the wrong form. Short, frequent writing with specific feedback moves grades faster than reading more texts does.

subjects.name: IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Standard Level still includes a non-calculator paper, which is where students who relied on technology at IGCSE discover the gap. Calculus and functions carry most of the marks, and the exploration needs genuine personal engagement rather than a textbook topic restated with the student's name on it.

subjects.name: IB Economics
subjects.description: Two papers at Standard Level plus internal assessment commentaries built on recent news articles, which is a sourcing task before it is a writing one. Candidates lose marks by explaining theory at length and never applying it to the article in front of them, and by drawing diagrams that are decorative rather than analytical.

subjects.name: IB Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and waves dominate Standard Level, and the examination keeps asking for explanation in the language of named principles. Uncertainty handling in the individual investigation is the other systematic loss, and it is rarely taught at the level the criteria expect because class time goes to content.

ajman/emirates-city.regionsTitle: Emirates City and the roads out of it

regions.note: A major destination for Emirates City school buses. Departure before 6.30am and a return after 4.45pm, which rules out any afternoon arrangement and sets the earliest realistic slot at about 6pm.

sections.heading: Who lives in Emirates City, and what time they actually get home
paragraphs: The households in these towers made a specific trade. Rent in Emirates City is lower than in Sharjah and much lower than in Dubai, and the price is road time: an adult commute of an hour or more each way, and a school run that starts before 7am. People make that trade deliberately and it works. What it does not survive is a tutoring arrangement designed for a family with a driver and a villa.

The numbers are worth setting out, because once they are on paper the decision makes itself. A child bussed into central Ajman is home by about 3.45pm. A child at an Emirates Road belt campus is home by 4.15pm. A child crossing to Muwaileh or Al Nahda is home between 4.45pm and 5pm. A parent commuting into Dubai is home at 7.30pm or later. There is a two-and-a-half to three-hour window in which a child is home and no adult is, and then an evening in which both are home and tired.

Most tutoring providers price for the first window because it looks empty. It is the worst time to use. A fifteen-year-old alone in an apartment at 5pm with a tutor on a screen and nobody else home will do the hour, more or less, and the household has no idea what happened in it. A session at 8pm with a parent in the next room and a written note afterwards is a different product even if the teaching is identical, and it is the one that produces a plan a family can act on.

The exception is a self-directed student, and they exist. A DP2 candidate who wants a marked component and a correction session does not need supervision and should take the earlier slot while they are fresh. The decision is about the student rather than about the hour, and it is worth making explicitly rather than by default.
bullets: Children are home between 3.45pm and 5pm depending on the school direction

sections.heading: Departure, return and the earliest slot that holds
paragraphs: This table is the most practical thing on the page and it took twenty minutes with a map and a few parents to build. It maps the school directions Emirates City families actually use against the earliest tuition slot that survives contact with reality. Survives is the operative word: a slot that works on paper and fails twice a month is worse than a later one that never moves, because the sessions that help are the ones that happen.

Two rules fall out of it. First, add thirty minutes to the return time before scheduling anything, for food and for the twenty minutes of nothing that a teenager needs after a long bus. Second, if the slot depends on a parent being home, use the parent's arrival time rather than the child's. Those two adjustments account for most failed arrangements in this district.

The last row is the one families recognise. Where the supervising parent commutes into Dubai, the realistic choice is either an 8pm session with an adult present or an earlier one that runs unsupervised. Both are legitimate; they are just different products, and the written record matters much more in the second case. We would rather say that than sell a 5.30pm slot into a household where nobody is there to see it.

Worth noting what is absent from the table: the tutor's journey. In an online arrangement there is none, which is why the earliest feasible slot depends only on the family. The next section prices what happens when the tutor has to drive the Emirates Road instead.

sections.heading: Studying in a tower apartment: the problems nobody writes about
paragraphs: Tutoring advice is written as though every student has a desk in a quiet room. In a two or three-bedroom apartment with two or three children, the study environment is a negotiation and it has to be set up once rather than improvised nightly. This is unglamorous and it determines whether an hour of teaching lands or evaporates.

The specific problems are consistent across these towers. The living room has a television and the youngest child in it. Bedrooms are shared, so a sibling doing nothing is a sibling in the room. The dining table is the best surface and also where dinner happens. Headphones solve more than any other single intervention, because they remove the household's noise and, just as importantly, stop the lesson leaking into the household. A cheap pair is the highest-return purchase a family on this page can make.

Devices are the second constraint. A shared laptop with three users and a phone as the backup is normal, and it is workable if the session is booked around it rather than against it. What does not work is a lesson on a phone propped against a water bottle: the student cannot write and watch at the same time, and screen-shared work is the main reason online delivery is useful at all. A tablet with a stylus, or a laptop with paper beside it, is enough.

The last piece is the agreement itself: one hour, one room, door closed if there is a door, and everyone else told in advance. Families who make that explicit once stop having the conversation every week. Those who do not end up with a tutor competing for attention against a cartoon, which is a waste of an AED 200 hour whoever is teaching.
bullets: Headphones are the single highest-return purchase for a tower household

sections.heading: What travel adds to a tutor's rate, and who pays for it
paragraphs: Market rates for tutoring in this part of the UAE are published by a handful of providers and they split cleanly by format. A qualified subject tutor working online sits in the AED 150 to 300 band, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist exam-year work runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase quoting AED 270. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate's Dubai rate table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors going higher. Budget online work starts far lower: EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. All read in October 2026.

The in-home premium is not a margin, it is a journey. A tutor driving to Emirates City from central Ajman is spending fifteen to twenty minutes each way. From Sharjah at 5pm it is thirty to forty-five. From Dubai in the evening peak it is an hour or more. Nobody works for free, so that time is inside the rate, and the household also pays it in a second currency: setup, the doorstep conversation at both ends, and the days the tutor simply does not arrive on time.

The table splits the formats out with the travel made visible. Read the right-hand column, which is the one that costs a commuting family most. An online session consumes an hour of the evening block and nothing else. Everything involving a vehicle consumes more than an hour, and the group-class option consumes two journeys out of a block that is three hours long in total.

IB Gram does not publish a rate card here. There is a free trial lesson with the tutor who would teach the course and a consultation that prices the actual plan, because the number depends on level, on how scarce the specialist is, and on how many weeks remain before the series.

sections.heading: From a tower on the Emirates Road: what each arrangement assumes
paragraphs: This page targets a home-tutor search, so the question deserves answering rather than deflecting. A visiting tutor at an Emirates City apartment is a real option, sold by real providers, and for a young child or a household with no quiet space it can be the better product. The honest objection is not quality, it is the road: the arrangement assumes a predictable drive at the exact hour the Emirates Road is least predictable.

IB Gram delivers to Emirates City as one-to-one online tuition over live video. We do not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists in India only. The argument for it in this district is narrow and strong. The specialist pool stops being people willing to drive to a tower on the Ajman side of the Emirates Road, which is a small group, and becomes people who teach that board at that level, which is a much larger one.

The table lists what each arrangement quietly assumes, because assumptions are where these decisions go wrong. Online tuition assumes a device, a connection and one room that can be quiet for an hour, and if a household cannot supply those then it is the wrong choice, headphones or not. A visiting arrangement assumes a predictable drive. A centre class assumes two spare journeys. Sibling help assumes goodwill, which is usually present, and subject knowledge, which at exam level often is not.

One honest recommendation before any of it. Where the school runs subject-support sessions and has a specialist in that subject, those are already inside the fees and take no travel from anybody. For a commuting household that is the cheapest possible fix, and a provider who never mentions it is selling hours rather than solving a problem.

sections.heading: Coverage and the fallback, stated before you book
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit, which is strange, because every matching service has one. Subject scarcity is real and it is uneven: IGCSE mathematics has the widest pool of anything, and a smaller Diploma subject at Higher Level in a specific term may have nobody free at all. A family that is told this up front can plan. A family that discovers it in week three has lost three weeks.

The pattern is geographic as well as subject-based. The northern emirates have fewer UAE-based specialists than Dubai across almost every subject, which is a straightforward consequence of where the schools and the teachers are. For Emirates City that means the honest answer to some requests is a specialist working from outside the UAE on Gulf Standard Time, and that answer is given at matching rather than buried.

What we will not do is put a generalist into a Higher Level slot and hope the student does not notice. They do notice, usually in the third session, and by then a term has gone. If nobody who teaches that syllabus at that level is available in the window you need, the answer is no, with an estimate of when it changes.

The table is the current shape of that coverage, written to be checked rather than admired. Ask about your own subject and level specifically, because the shape moves between terms and the autumn is tighter than the spring.
