sections.heading: Spending nothing first: what to try before paying anyone
paragraphs: A page written around cost should be honest about the hours that cost nothing, because some Higher Level problems are solved by them and a provider that pretends otherwise is selling rather than advising. Four things are worth doing before a single dirham changes hands, and together they take a weekend.

Ask the school for the subject's dated deadline sheet and the mark breakdown from the last internal assessment, component by component. A Higher Level student losing marks on Paper 1 and holding up on Paper 2 has a non-calculator algebra problem, which is a different purchase from a student who is weak across both. Without that split, any tutoring plan is a guess, and you will pay for the guessing.

Then read the last marked script with your child, not for the total but for where the working stopped. Higher Level mark schemes pay for method, and the commonest pattern in a Higher Level script is a student who knew the technique and never wrote the line that earned the mark. If that is what the script shows, the fix is habit rather than content, and it is cheaper and faster than it feels.

Third, ask the subject teacher directly what they would do with an extra ninety minutes a week. Teachers answer this question well and are not usually asked it. Fourth, use the free trial lesson as a diagnostic rather than as a sample: send the marked script in advance, ask for a written diagnosis afterwards and decide on the basis of that document. One free trial lesson per student, no card details required, and if the diagnosis says tutoring is not the answer, that is a useful free outcome rather than a failed sale.

process.title: Send the evidence, not the worry
process.description: Start with three documents: the most recent marked Higher Level script, the component mark breakdown, and the school's dated deadline sheet for the exploration. Those three tell a specialist more in ten minutes than a conversation does in an hour, and they are what makes the first quote a plan rather than a range.

process.title: Free trial lesson, used as a diagnosis
process.description: One free trial lesson per student, with no card details required. The tutor works a problem with your child, probes where the method breaks and writes a short diagnosis afterwards naming the component at fault. You decide after reading that document, not during the call.

process.title: Agree the plan and the number
process.description: A written plan with the number of sessions, the session length, what marking is included and what the month costs. Higher Level work is usually ninety minutes rather than sixty, and a block aimed at Paper 3 or the exploration is stated separately so you can see what each part of the plan is buying.

process.title: Weekly teaching with marked evidence
process.description: Sessions run on live video on Gulf Standard Time, with written working photographed and marked between them. After each session you get a short note in plain English: what was taught, what was practised, what is still wrong. That note is the thing to read if you are deciding whether to continue.

process.title: Review at four weeks against the script
process.description: Four weeks in, the question is whether the marked scripts have moved, not whether everyone feels better. If the component at fault has not shifted, we change tutor, change approach or say plainly that tutoring is not the lever. A review date fixed at the start is what makes that conversation easy to have.

whyPoints.title: The money question answered first
whyPoints.description: Published AED bands by provider model, with each figure attributed to the rate card it came from and dated. Three of the providers ranking for this search publish no price at all and two quote in dollars, so a dirham figure with a source attached is the least a UAE family should expect before a first session.

whyPoints.title: Higher Level specialists, not general maths tutors
whyPoints.description: Proof by induction, vector planes, Maclaurin series and Paper 3 are Higher Level content with no Standard Level counterpart. The pool of people who teach them well is narrow everywhere and almost non-existent inside Ajman, which is the whole reason the delivery model is online rather than local.

whyPoints.title: Evidence a parent can check
whyPoints.description: Timed scripts marked against the published mark scheme, with method marks separated from accuracy marks, and a written note after every session. You are not asked to judge progress by atmosphere; you are given the document the judgement is based on.

whyPoints.title: Clear academic honesty limits
whyPoints.description: A tutor here questions a topic, teaches a technique, reads the student's own draft and gives criterion-by-criterion feedback. No part of an exploration is supplied. Providers in this market sell completed internal assessments; that route ends in a malpractice investigation and this one does not touch it.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built for the northern emirates
whyPoints.description: Slots from 17:00 for families whose school bus arrives early, and late evening or weekend morning slots for households commuting back from Dubai and Sharjah. A Higher Level ninety-minute block is easier to protect on a Saturday morning than at 20:30 on a Tuesday, and we will say so.

whyPoints.title: Honest about availability
whyPoints.description: Higher Level Analysis specialists are a small pool and the diary tightens sharply before the May session. If nobody suitable is free in your slot we say so and offer the alternatives, rather than filling the hour with a generalist and charging a specialist rate for it.

faqs.question: What does an IB DP math AA HL tutor in Ajman charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Published UAE rates for a qualified online subject tutor run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, and AED 200 to AED 450 for a Diploma specialist, with budget platforms advertising from AED 33 and one premium provider publishing AED 650. Those figures were read from providers' own published material in October 2026 and are market rates rather than an IB Gram price list. Higher Level Analysis sits at the upper half of the specialist band because the course runs to 240 taught hours and carries content, including Paper 3, that no Standard Level course covers. Ask for the hourly figure, the session length and whether marking is included before the first session.

faqs.question: Why is a Higher Level Analysis hour priced above a Standard Level one?
faqs.answer: Three reasons, all structural. The Higher Level course is 240 taught hours against 150 at Standard Level, so there is simply more to teach. It contains material with no Standard Level counterpart at all, including proof by induction, complex numbers in Euler form, Maclaurin series and vector equations of planes. And it carries a third paper worth a fifth of the grade which has to be prepared separately from the topic syllabus. The pool of tutors who can teach all of that confidently is narrower than the pool who can teach Standard Level, and a narrower pool prices higher in every market.

faqs.question: Does a tutor based outside Ajman cost our family more?
faqs.answer: For online lessons, no. Where a tutor sits makes no difference to an hour delivered over live video, and it is why the specialist pool available to an Ajman family online is the same one available to a family in Dubai. For an in-home visit it makes a large difference, because a tutor driving from Dubai or Sharjah into Ajman in evening traffic spends forty to seventy minutes each way and that time is paid for inside the hourly rate. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, so the travel question does not arise on our side.

faqs.question: How many Higher Level maths sessions does a term usually come to?
faqs.answer: It depends which problem you are buying against. A summer bridge from IGCSE into DP1 is typically six to eight sessions. A component block aimed at Paper 1 sketching or Paper 3 technique is usually six to ten, which is short enough to state at the outset and judge on marked scripts. Exploration supervision is a handful of scheduled sessions timed to the school's internal deadlines. A DP2 student who is behind on content as well as technique is a different scale of plan, and anyone quoting that without seeing a marked script first is guessing.

faqs.question: Is Paper 3 preparation billed separately from weekly lessons?
faqs.answer: It usually should be, because it is different work. Paper 3 cannot be revised topic by topic: each question invents its own mathematics in the stem and walks the candidate through it in scaffolded parts, so what is being trained is reading an unfamiliar argument under time pressure. That needs whole past questions sat under the real one-hour constraint and then marked line by line, which does not fit inside an ordinary sixty-minute teaching slot. Pricing it as a defined block makes the cost visible and makes it obvious when the block is finished.

faqs.question: What does exploration supervision add to the bill?
faqs.answer: A small number of scheduled sessions rather than a continuing weekly charge, and the cheapest version is bought early. Two or three sessions at the topic-selection stage, spent testing whether the mathematics reaches Higher Level and whether the data exists, prevent the expensive case: a student fifteen pages into a topic with no Higher Level mathematics in it. Feedback is given criterion by criterion against the five criteria and the twenty marks. The student's own work stays their own throughout, which is both an IB requirement and the reason this is supervision rather than production.

faqs.question: Are AA HL tutoring fees in Ajman quoted with VAT included?
faqs.answer: Ask, and ask in writing, because practice varies across this market and we will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition as settled fact without a Federal Tax Authority citation to hand. What matters practically is whether the figure you were quoted is the figure you will pay. A quote should state the amount in dirhams, the session length in minutes, whether marking between sessions is inside that figure, and whether any tax is added on top. A provider that cannot answer those four questions in one message is not ready to take your money.

faqs.question: If we can only spend AED 180 an hour, is Higher Level support still worth starting?
faqs.answer: Yes, but spend it narrowly. At that level the realistic purchase is a diagnosis and a single component rather than a standing weekly arrangement across the whole course. Get the marked script read, identify whether the loss is non-calculator algebra, calculator technique or Paper 3 reading, then buy a short block against that one thing and judge it on the next marked script. Fortnightly ninety-minute sessions with written marking in between often beat weekly hours at the same monthly spend, because the marking is where most of the diagnosis actually happens.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram arrange a Higher Level maths tutor to teach at an address in Ajman?
faqs.answer: No. Every UAE lesson is delivered one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service offered only in India. On the merits, that is also the better arrangement for this particular course: a family in Al Rawda or Al Zorah choosing locally is choosing from whoever is within driving distance, while the same family online is choosing from Analysis and Approaches specialists outright. The honest cost of online delivery is supervision, which we handle with the camera on the page, working photographed for marking and a written note to the parent after each session.

faqs.question: Is a pair of students cheaper per head for Higher Level maths?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes; per outcome, often not. Two Higher Level candidates can share a session productively only if their gaps genuinely overlap, which at Higher Level is less common than at Standard Level because the ways students fail this course diverge sharply. One cannot start a proof; the other knows the content and bleeds accuracy marks. A shared hour then teaches each of them half the time. Where a pair does work well is Paper 3 practice and mark scheme reading, which benefit from two people arguing about the same script.

faqs.question: Do Higher Level maths rates in the northern emirates climb before the May session?
faqs.answer: Rates drift upward across this market as the session approaches, but availability tightens faster than price does. By February the binding constraint for a Higher Level family is usually not the dirham figure but whether any Analysis and Approaches specialist is free at 19:30 on a weekday. The practical implication is that the cheap time to buy Higher Level support and the effective time to buy it are the same time, which is early in DP1 or over the summer before DP2, not after the mock results arrive.

faqs.question: Should we pay for a block of ten lessons up front?
faqs.answer: Only after a free trial and a written diagnosis, and only if the block has a stated purpose. A block aimed at a named component with marked scripts as the evidence is a reasonable thing to commit to, because you can tell at session five whether it is working. A block bought as a general discount on an open-ended arrangement is harder to judge and harder to exit. Ask what happens to unused sessions, whether the slot is held through the school holidays, and what the review point is before paying for any package.

faqs.question: Do we pay for the time a tutor spends marking a Higher Level script?
faqs.answer: Somewhere in the price, yes, and a provider that claims otherwise is either not marking properly or has hidden it in the hourly figure. Marking a full Paper 1 against the published mark scheme, separating method marks from accuracy marks and writing a usable note on it, takes most of an hour. The question to ask is not whether it is paid for but whether it is happening: ask to see a marked script from the first month, with annotations against the mark scheme rather than a tick and a total.

faqs.question: What happens to our plan if no Higher Level Analysis specialist is free in our slot?
faqs.answer: We say so. Higher Level Analysis is the narrowest maths specialism in the Diploma and the diary tightens sharply from January, so there are weeks when the honest answer to a 19:30 weekday request is that nobody suitable is available. The realistic alternatives are a weekend morning slot, a fortnightly ninety-minute session with written marking in between, or a later start date with the work resequenced. Filling the hour with a general maths tutor and charging a specialist rate for it is the one option we will not offer.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest honest first step if our child is on a grade 3 at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Four free things, in this order. Ask the school for the component-by-component mark breakdown, so you know whether Paper 1 or Paper 2 is the problem. Read the last marked script with your child, looking for where the working stopped rather than at the total. Ask the subject teacher what they would do with an extra ninety minutes a week. Then use the free trial lesson as a diagnostic, sending the script in advance and asking for the diagnosis in writing. If that document says a level change is the better answer, that is a useful free outcome.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Higher Level maths and a second Diploma subject for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, because a single tutor covering Higher Level Analysis and Physics HL removes a scheduling problem and a second invoice. The limit is honest competence: the overlap between people who teach Higher Level Analysis well and those who teach a second Higher Level subject well is not large, and a tutor who says yes to every subject on the list is a warning rather than a convenience. Where the double is not available, two specialists on alternating evenings is the better purchase.

ajman/ib-dp-math-aa-hl-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the marked script and a free trial lesson
ajman/ib-dp-math-aa-hl-tutor.closingBody: If your child is taking Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level in Ajman and the grade is not where it should be, the first useful step costs nothing. Send the most recent marked script, the component mark breakdown and the school's dated deadline sheet for the exploration. The trial lesson that follows is free, one per student, with no card details required, and it ends in a written diagnosis naming the component at fault and the number of sessions a plan would take. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and if the diagnosis says tutoring is not the lever, we will tell you that instead.

ajman/ib-dp-math-aa-sl-tutor.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors we would match to a Standard Level Analysis student in Ajman: people who teach this specific course, who know that Paper 1 and Paper 2 reward different habits, and who are willing to tell a family when the honest answer is a level change rather than another ten hours.

intro.heading: Standard Level Analysis, and the question underneath the search
paragraphs: The search for a Standard Level Analysis tutor is almost never only about mathematics. Underneath it sits a question about level: is my child in the right course, and if not, is it too late to move? That question has a real answer, it has a deadline attached, and it belongs to the school rather than to a tutor. Any page that skips straight to booking hours has skipped the most consequential decision a Diploma maths family makes.

Standard Level Analysis and Approaches is 150 taught hours across five topic areas, examined by two papers of 80 marks each, carrying 40% of the grade apiece, plus a mathematical exploration worth the remaining 20%. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator. Paper 2 allows a graphical calculator. That single difference accounts for more lost marks than any topic on the syllabus, because a student who learned the course with a device in hand meets Paper 1 as an unfamiliar exam rather than a familiar one.

The pattern we see in Ajman specifically comes from the route students take into the course. Most arrive from Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE at a school in the emirate or across the Sharjah border, where a good grade was earned by producing correct answers quickly. Standard Level pays for the argument, the units, the degree of accuracy and the sketch with its asymptotes labelled. A capable IGCSE student can lose six or seven marks a paper to those conventions while understanding every piece of mathematics in front of them, and that is a fixable problem rather than a capability one.

There is also a structural constraint worth naming. Ajman's private schools sit under federal Ministry of Education supervision, and only a small number run the full Diploma. A Standard Level maths class here can be a handful of students taught alongside the Higher Level group, which means a child who needs the Standard Level pace explained twice may not get it twice. That is the most common honest reason a family in this emirate buys one-to-one time, and it has nothing to do with the student being weak.

What follows is written for the decision first and the hours second. There is a topic-by-topic map of where the 150 hours go, a ranked list of where Standard Level candidates actually leak marks, a table on moving between levels and what each month of delay costs, the exploration criteria with their mark allocations, and the Ministry of Education equivalency position for a school leaver. Lessons themselves are delivered online, one to one; IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE, and that is stated here rather than discovered later. The aim throughout is that a parent finishes the page knowing which of three things they are buying: a different course, a different examination habit, or a specific piece of mathematics that was never properly taught.

ajman/ib-dp-math-aa-sl-tutor.programmesIntro: Standard Level Analysis sits inside a longer sequence, and where a student joined it changes what the first month of tuition should do. These are the three entry routes we see most often from Ajman households.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
programmes.description: The Standard Level Analysis course covers number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus across 150 taught hours. It shares a common core with the Higher Level route but stops short of proof by induction, complex numbers in polar form, Maclaurin series and the vector strand. Assessment is Paper 1 without a calculator, Paper 2 with one, and the exploration, with the two papers weighted equally at 40% each.
programmes.countryNote: In Ajman the course is often taught in a small combined class, with Standard Level students in the room while Higher Level content is being delivered. One-to-one time here is frequently about pace and attention rather than ability, and the first job is usually to establish which of the two papers is actually losing marks before any content is retaught.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Mathematics, standard strand
programmes.description: The standard strand of MYP mathematics is the designed route into Standard Level Analysis. Reporting is against four criteria out of eight rather than a percentage, so the signal a parent needs is criterion-level: strength in knowing and understanding with weakness in communicating predicts exactly the mark loss Standard Level punishes, because Paper 1 pays for written method rather than for the final number.
programmes.countryNote: Few Ajman campuses run the full IB continuum, so most Standard Level candidates in the emirate have not come through MYP at all. Where a student has, the useful document is the final MYP criterion profile, and it is worth asking the school for it before DP1 begins rather than after the first report.

programmes.name: IGCSE Extended into Standard Level Analysis
programmes.description: This is the commonest route into the course and the one that produces the most predictable first-term problems. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 both reward a correct answer reached efficiently. Standard Level Analysis rewards radian measure as a working unit, exact values, labelled sketches and a stated degree of accuracy. None of those are hard; all of them are new, and together they account for most of the drop a strong IGCSE student sees in their first DP1 report.
programmes.countryNote: An Ajman student who sat IGCSE without the Additional Mathematics paper has usually never met differentiation or radians. A short bridging block in the summer before DP1 is the cheapest and least pressured point to close that gap, and it is the one window in the sequence with no school deadline competing for the same hours.

ajman/ib-dp-math-aa-sl-tutor.subjectsIntro: The five Standard Level topic areas, what each actually assesses and the specific way marks go missing in it. This is the map a plan should be built from, because the repair for a functions problem looks nothing like the repair for a statistics one.

subjects.name: Number and algebra
subjects.description: Sequences and series, laws of exponents and logarithms, the binomial theorem for positive integer indices, and simple proof. Standard Level marks disappear here to log manipulation done in the wrong order and to geometric series questions where the common ratio is identified correctly and then substituted into the sum of the wrong number of terms.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.description: Function notation, domain and range, composite and inverse functions, quadratics in all three forms, rational functions of the simplest type, exponential and logarithmic models, and transformations of graphs. Paper 1 asks for sketches with intercepts and asymptotes labelled; an unlabelled sketch of the right shape earns very little, and this is the most common single source of avoidable loss.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.description: Three-dimensional solids, the sine and cosine rules, arc length and sector area in radians, the unit circle, Pythagorean identities, double angle formulae and trigonometric equations. Radian measure is the crux: students convert to degrees to think, solve, and then forget to convert back, which costs the accuracy mark on an otherwise complete answer.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Sampling, measures of central tendency and dispersion, box plots, linear correlation and regression, probability of combined events, conditional probability, discrete random variables and expected value, the binomial distribution and the normal distribution. Most Standard Level loss here is procedural rather than conceptual, which makes it the fastest topic to improve under tuition.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.description: Limits informally, differentiation of polynomials and standard functions, the chain, product and quotient rules, tangents and normals, stationary points and their nature, kinematics, and integration including definite integrals and areas. The expensive habit is differentiating correctly and then answering a question the command term did not ask, particularly where the stem says justify rather than find.

subjects.name: Paper 1 technique without a calculator
subjects.description: Exact values, surds, simplification by hand, sketching, and algebraic rearrangement under time pressure. This is not a topic but it behaves like one, because a student who learned the course with a graphical calculator in hand has to be taught the paper as a separate skill. Standard Level students who are stronger on Paper 2 than Paper 1 almost always have this gap rather than a content gap.

subjects.name: Paper 2 technology technique
subjects.description: Using a graphical calculator to solve numerically, find intersections, evaluate definite integrals, run regressions and handle normal distribution calculations. The skill is knowing when reaching for the device is faster than algebra and when it loses the method marks. Drilling it is quick work and often the single highest-yield fortnight in a Standard Level plan.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: Independent mathematical writing marked against presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. At Standard Level the use of mathematics criterion is judged against Standard Level content, so the ceiling is reachable with the syllabus the student has actually been taught, which makes topic choice less perilous than at Higher Level but no less important.

subjects.name: Command terms and mark scheme literacy
subjects.description: Find, calculate, show that, justify, hence, hence or otherwise, sketch and state each promise the examiner something different. The word hence means the previous part must be used, and ignoring it forfeits method marks even when the answer is right. Reading mark schemes with a student for two sessions reliably moves scores without teaching any new mathematics.

That is the structural reason a capable Standard Level student can go unnoticed for a term, and it is worth asking the school directly how the two levels are timetabled.

ajman/ib-dp-math-aa-sl-tutor.modesIntro: Three shapes a Standard Level plan takes. The right one depends on whether the problem is content, technique or the level itself.

modes.description: The default for a Standard Level student with a specific content gap and time to close it. Sixty minutes is enough at this level because the topics are self-contained in a way Higher Level topics are not: a session can teach logarithm laws, practise them and diagnose what remains without running out of hour. Delivered over live video with the student's written working visible on camera.

sections.heading: Is Standard Level the right place to be, and who decides?
paragraphs: The level decision is the most valuable thing on this page, so it goes first. A Diploma student takes three subjects at Higher Level and three at Standard, and mathematics is frequently the subject where that split is wrong. A student placed at Higher Level because they were strong at IGCSE, who is now at a grade 3 and spending four evenings a week on one subject, is losing marks in the other five as well. Moving to Standard Level is not a retreat from the Diploma; it is a reallocation of 90 taught hours.

The decision belongs to the school, not to a tutor and not to a parent in isolation. Schools hold internal deadlines for level changes, usually clustered at the end of the first term of DP1 and again before the final registration window, and those dates differ between an Ajman campus and a Sharjah one. The first thing to ask for is the date in writing. A family that knows the deadline can make a considered decision; a family that discovers it a week late has had the decision made for them.

There is a mirror case worth naming, because it is less often discussed. A student comfortably scoring a 7 at Standard Level in DP1, intending to read a quantitative subject at university, may be in a course that closes a door. Some degree routes name Higher Level mathematics as a requirement or a strong preference, and the only reliable source for that is the university's own published entry page for the specific programme and year of entry.

Where a tutor is genuinely useful in this decision is evidence. A level conversation goes much better when the family brings the component mark breakdown, two marked scripts and a written diagnosis than when it brings a worry. That is what the free first lesson is for here: not a sample lesson, but a document naming whether the problem is content, technique or level.

sections.heading: Two papers, 80 marks each, two completely different habits
paragraphs: Standard Level Analysis is examined by two papers of 80 marks, each worth 40% of the grade. They share a syllabus and almost nothing else. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator and rewards algebraic control, exact values and clean written method. Paper 2 allows a graphical calculator and rewards judgement about when to use it. Treating them as one exam with a device switched on or off is the most expensive assumption a Standard Level student can make.

On Paper 1, marks are lost in predictable places. Students who have practised on a calculator for two years lose fluency with surds and exact trigonometric values. Sketches arrive without intercepts, asymptotes or stationary points labelled. Logarithms get manipulated in an order that works numerically and not symbolically. None of this is difficult mathematics, and all of it responds quickly to being named and drilled, which is why a student stronger on Paper 2 than Paper 1 is usually a fast improvement rather than a long project.

On Paper 2, the loss pattern inverts. The calculator solves the equation, and the student writes down the answer with no method, forfeiting the marks the mark scheme awarded for the working. Or the opposite: a candidate grinds through algebra by hand on a question designed to be solved numerically in thirty seconds and runs out of time before the last two questions. Paper 2 technique is a decision-making skill, and it is trainable in a fortnight.

The practical diagnostic is therefore simple and worth doing before paying anyone. Ask the school for the Paper 1 and Paper 2 marks separately from the last internal assessment. A gap of more than ten marks between them tells you which habit is missing, and a plan built on that split costs a fraction of a plan built on a total.
bullets: Paper 1: 80 marks, 40%, no calculator, exact values and labelled sketches
Paper 2: 80 marks, 40%, graphical calculator, question selection and timing
Exploration: 20 marks, 20%, internally marked and moderated by the IB

sections.heading: Where Standard Level candidates leak marks, in order of cost
paragraphs: Over a Diploma cohort the losses are not evenly spread, and ranking them changes what the first month of tuition should do. The costliest single pattern is the unlabelled sketch. Standard Level asks for graphs repeatedly, the mark scheme awards specific marks for intercepts, asymptotes and turning points, and a correct shape with none of those marked collects almost nothing. Fixing it is a habit, not a topic, and it is worth perhaps four or five marks a paper.

Second is the command term. Find, show that, justify, hence and hence or otherwise each carry a different instruction. Hence means the previous part must be used, and a student who solves the question independently from scratch loses the method marks even with a correct answer. Two sessions reading real mark schemes alongside real scripts reliably recovers marks here without teaching any new mathematics at all.

Third is accuracy and rounding. The Diploma expects three significant figures unless told otherwise, and intermediate rounding propagates. A long multi-step statistics or trigonometry answer can be conceptually perfect and still drop the accuracy mark. Fourth is radian measure, where students convert to degrees to think and never convert back. Fifth, and only fifth, is genuine content weakness, usually in logarithms or in the interpretation half of statistics.

The order matters because it is the reverse of how most families diagnose the problem. A parent seeing a 4 assumes the mathematics has not been understood and buys content teaching. A marked script often shows a student who understands the mathematics and has not been taught the examination. Those cost very different amounts and take very different numbers of weeks.

sections.heading: Where the 150 hours go, and which ones a tutor should touch
paragraphs: The Standard Level course distributes 150 taught hours across five topic areas, and knowing roughly how that distribution works tells you which gaps are urgent. A student behind on functions is behind on material that the calculus strand will later assume. A student behind on the statistics interpretation is behind on something largely self-contained, which can wait until after the mock without compounding.

The table below sets out each topic area with what it covers, how much of the course it occupies and the specific way marks go missing in it. It is deliberately not a syllabus restatement; the final column is the part a plan is built from, because it names the failure rather than the content.

Two readings of the table are worth making explicitly. First, the topics with the largest share of teaching hours are not the topics where the most marks are lost, which is why hour-counting is a poor way to prioritise tuition. Second, three of the five loss patterns are procedural rather than conceptual, and procedural losses are the ones that move fastest under one-to-one attention.

For an Ajman student the sequencing has one local wrinkle. Where the Standard Level group is taught alongside the Higher Level group, the pace through the shared core is often set by the Higher Level timetable, so Standard Level students can arrive at calculus having had less consolidation on functions than the course intends. That is worth checking against the school's scheme of work before deciding what to reteach.

sections.heading: The exploration at Standard Level: the same twenty marks, a reachable ceiling
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration is twenty marks and a fifth of the final grade, marked internally against five criteria and moderated by the IB. The criteria are presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, and the last of those carries the largest single allocation. At Standard Level that criterion is judged against Standard Level content, which is the most important and least understood fact about the component.

It means a Standard Level student does not need to reach for impressive mathematics. A regression analysis, a well-handled optimisation problem or a careful application of the binomial distribution, used correctly and commented on with understanding, can reach the top of the criterion. Students who try to import Higher Level content they have not been taught usually lose marks in mathematical communication, where notation they do not control is used inconsistently.

The two failure modes we see most often are structural. The first is a topic with no mathematics in it: an interesting question about football, traffic or coffee prices that never becomes a calculation. The second is a calculation with no question in it: pages of correct work with nothing being investigated and nothing concluded. Both are cheaper to prevent than to repair, and both are visible in a single session before any drafting starts.

The honesty limits are fixed and they are the IB's, not ours. The exploration must be the student's own work and the authenticity declaration they sign is a real undertaking. A tutor may question the topic, teach a required technique, read a draft the student has produced and give feedback against each criterion. A tutor may not supply sentences, restructure the argument for them or hand over any part of the finished piece. Any provider offering a completed exploration is offering a malpractice investigation.

sections.heading: Does Standard Level maths close doors? Universities and equivalency
paragraphs: This is the question that makes families reluctant to drop a level, and it deserves a precise answer rather than reassurance. Some university programmes, typically in engineering, physics, actuarial work and parts of economics and computer science, name Higher Level mathematics as a requirement or a strong preference. Many others do not. The only reliable source is the university's own entry page for the specific programme and year of entry, and anyone telling you otherwise from memory is guessing with your child's application.

Separately from university entry sits the UAE Ministry of Education equivalency process, which is what converts a school leaving qualification into a recognised certificate for use in this country. For the British track the published requirements are specific: five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

For the International Baccalaureate the honest position is that no points threshold is published on this page, because we have not read one on the ministry's own site. Secondary sources circulate figures and at least one competing page publishes a subject count for the British track that does not match the ministry's own clarification. Equivalency requirements should be checked on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation channel directly, and the process is something a family does with the authority rather than something a tutoring provider performs on their behalf.

The practical takeaway for an Ajman family weighing a level change is that the equivalency route does not turn on whether maths was taken at Higher or Standard Level, while a specific degree programme might. That reorders the decision: check the two or three universities actually under consideration before deciding, not after.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the Diploma
paragraphs: A Diploma timetable in the UAE is not only the Diploma. Federal rules require private schools to deliver Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside whichever international curriculum they are licensed for, and to follow the Ministry's general regulations in doing so. For a family in Ajman, where private schools sit under federal Ministry of Education supervision, that is the framework the school is working inside.

The practical consequence for a maths plan is timetable pressure. Those mandatory lessons occupy real periods in the week, which means the hours available for Standard Level consolidation at school are fewer than a parent comparing with an overseas school might assume. A student who needs extra practice on functions is competing for time with requirements that are not optional, and that is one of the honest reasons private tuition exists in this market rather than a failure of the school.

There is a second consequence that matters more than families expect. For students for whom Arabic is an additional language, the mandatory subjects carry their own revision load, and they tend to arrive in the same weeks as Diploma internal deadlines. A revision plan that treats the Diploma subjects as the whole workload will overcommit the student in exactly the fortnight when the exploration deadline lands.

The scheduling answer is to build the maths plan from the school's own published calendar, including the mandatory subject assessments, rather than from the Diploma calendar alone. It is also why we would rather hold a fixed weekly slot across a term than move the session week to week: a protected hour survives a busy fortnight, and an improvised one does not.

sections.heading: Twelve weeks counted backwards from the mock
paragraphs: Most Standard Level plans that work are short, dated and counted backwards from a fixed point. The mock examination is a better anchor than the May session, because it is close enough to be real, the school sets it, and the marked script that comes out of it is the single most useful document in the whole process.

In weeks twelve to nine the work is diagnosis and non-calculator habit. The component split is obtained from the school, two marked scripts are read, and the first sessions are spent on whichever paper is weaker, typically Paper 1. Sketching conventions, exact values and command terms are drilled deliberately, because they are the fastest marks on the table and they persist once learned.

In weeks eight to five the content gaps identified in the diagnosis are taught, in the order the course assumes them rather than the order they appear on the syllabus: functions before calculus, radians before trigonometric equations. One timed section is sat every fortnight and marked against the published mark scheme, with method marks separated from accuracy marks so the student can see which kind of mark is being lost.

In weeks four to one the plan narrows to whole timed papers and the review of them. Nothing new is taught in the last fortnight, because new content learned under pressure displaces secure content. After the mock the marked script is read line by line, the plan is rewritten against what it shows, and the exploration deadline is checked against the school's own dated sheet. Published IB session and results dates are deliberately not quoted here: they should be confirmed with the school's IB coordinator or on the IB's own site.

Weeks 8-5: content gaps taught in dependency order, timed section every fortnight
Weeks 4-1: whole papers under time, no new content in the final fortnight

faqs.question: Is an IB DP math AA SL tutor in Ajman worth it if the grade is only one off target?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, because a one-grade gap at Standard Level is most often a technique problem rather than a content one, and technique moves fast. Ask the school for the Paper 1 and Paper 2 marks separately. If one is ten or more marks behind the other, the fix is a habit: labelled sketches, exact values, command terms, three significant figures. A short block of six to eight sessions aimed at the weaker paper, with timed sections marked against the mark scheme, is a reasonable purchase. A plan built on the overall grade alone is not.

faqs.question: How is Standard Level Analysis actually assessed?
faqs.answer: Two written papers and one piece of coursework. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator and carries 80 marks and 40% of the grade. Paper 2 allows a graphical calculator and carries the same 80 marks and 40%. The mathematical exploration carries the remaining 20%, marked out of twenty against five criteria by the school and moderated by the IB. The course itself runs to 150 taught hours across five topic areas. Confirm your child's exact session and internal deadlines with their school rather than from any third-party page.

faqs.question: My daughter understands the maths but loses six marks a paper. What is happening?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly the examination rather than the mathematics. The four recurring culprits are sketches drawn without intercepts, asymptotes or stationary points labelled, command terms ignored where hence or justify required a particular route, intermediate rounding before the final three significant figures, and radian answers converted out and never converted back. None of these are conceptual, all of them are visible on a marked script, and together they routinely account for five to eight marks a paper. Two sessions reading mark schemes against her own script usually recovers most of it.

faqs.question: Should my son drop from Higher Level to Standard Level Analysis, and when?
faqs.answer: That is the school's decision, and the most important thing is to get its internal deadline in writing now, because those dates cluster at the end of the first DP1 term and again before final registration. The case for moving is strongest when one subject is consuming the study time of three and the other five grades are suffering. Before deciding, check whether the specific degree programmes under consideration name Higher Level mathematics on their own published entry pages. Bring the component mark breakdown and two marked scripts to the conversation, not a worry.

faqs.question: Which Standard Level topic is the most expensive to be behind on?
faqs.answer: Functions, because calculus later assumes it. A student shaky on domain, range, inverses and transformations will meet differentiation of composite functions and struggle for reasons that look like a calculus problem and are not. Statistics, by contrast, is largely self-contained and can wait without compounding. That dependency order is why a plan should teach functions before calculus and radian measure before trigonometric equations, rather than working through gaps in the order they appear on the school's scheme of work.

faqs.question: How much Paper 1 practice does a Standard Level student need without a calculator?
faqs.answer: More than most get, and it should be deliberate rather than incidental. Students who learned the course with a graphical calculator in hand lose fluency with surds, exact trigonometric values and algebraic simplification, and that fluency only returns through regular untimed practice followed by timed practice. A realistic pattern is one non-calculator session a fortnight through DP1 and weekly from the start of DP2, with a full timed Paper 1 section marked each cycle so the recovery is measured rather than assumed.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help choose an exploration topic without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the highest-value hour in the whole component. A tutor may question whether the mathematics is reachable at Standard Level, whether the data exists, and whether the question can actually be answered, all before any drafting begins. They may teach a technique the student needs and give feedback on a draft the student has produced, criterion by criterion. What they may not do is supply sentences, restructure the argument on the student's behalf or hand over any part of the finished piece. The authenticity declaration your child signs is a real undertaking.

faqs.question: Does Standard Level maths stop my child studying engineering?
faqs.answer: It can, depending on the university and programme, which is why this needs checking rather than assuming. Engineering, physics, actuarial science and some economics and computer science routes name Higher Level mathematics as a requirement or a strong preference; many other degrees do not. The only source worth relying on is each university's own published entry page for the specific programme and year of entry. Check the two or three institutions actually under consideration before the level decision is made, not afterwards, and ask the school's university counsellor to confirm what they are seeing.

faqs.question: For a Standard Level student in Ajman, how many IGCSE passes does the British equivalency track need?
faqs.answer: Five. The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. At least one page ranking for these searches states six, which is wrong. Equivalency is a process families complete with the ministry or the emirate's attestation channel, not something a tutoring provider performs for them.

faqs.question: Does my child in Ajman still take Arabic and Islamic Education alongside the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Yes. Federal rules require private schools to deliver Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed international curriculum, and Ajman's private schools sit under federal Ministry of Education supervision. For maths planning the point is timetable arithmetic: those are real periods and real assessments, and they tend to land in the same weeks as Diploma internal deadlines. A revision plan that counts only the six Diploma subjects will overcommit your child in precisely the fortnight the exploration is due.

faqs.question: Are Standard Level sessions better weekly or fortnightly for an Ajman household?
faqs.answer: Weekly where the student needs content taught, because gaps compound and a fortnight is long enough to forget a technique. Fortnightly ninety-minute sessions with written marking in between work better where the problem is examination habit, because the marking does much of the diagnostic work and the student needs time to accumulate practice worth reviewing. For families commuting back from Dubai or Sharjah, one protected weekend morning often beats two improvised weekday evenings that keep moving.

faqs.question: What should the first marked script tell us after a month of tuition?
faqs.answer: Three things, specifically. Which paper improved, because an improvement on Paper 2 with Paper 1 flat means the non-calculator work has not been done. Whether method marks are now being collected on questions where the final answer is still wrong, which is the earliest reliable sign of progress. And whether the losses have moved from procedural to conceptual, because that tells you what the next month should teach. A tick and a total tells you none of this, so ask for annotation against the mark scheme.

faqs.question: Is the exploration easier at Standard Level than at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: The ceiling is more reachable, which is not the same as easier. The use of mathematics criterion is assessed against Standard Level content, so a well-handled regression, optimisation or binomial application can reach the top of it, where a Higher Level candidate is judged against Higher Level mathematics. The common Standard Level error is importing content the student has not been taught, which then loses marks on mathematical communication through notation they do not control. Choosing a modest topic and treating it thoroughly scores better than reaching.

faqs.question: We are moving into Ajman mid-year. Can tuition bridge a change of school?
faqs.answer: It can, and the useful first step is paperwork rather than teaching. Ask the previous school for the scheme of work covered to date and the last component mark breakdown, and the new school for its own scheme of work and dated internal deadlines. The gap between those two documents is the actual teaching job, and it is usually narrower than families fear but rarely where they expect. Diploma schemes of work order the same syllabus differently, so a mid-year transfer is typically a resequencing problem rather than a content one.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram run Standard Level maths lessons at homes in Ajman?
faqs.answer: No. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, and home visits are offered only in India. For this course that is also the stronger arrangement, because the number of Standard Level Analysis specialists living within driving distance of Al Hamidiya or Al Tallah is small, and the alternative locally is usually a general maths tutor. The trade-off we accept is supervision, which is handled by keeping the camera on the written page, photographing working for marking, and sending the parent a written note after every session.

faqs.question: What if the free first lesson shows tutoring is not what we need?
faqs.answer: Then that is what the written diagnosis will say, and it is a useful free outcome rather than a failed sale. Some Standard Level problems are solved by the school: a level change, a timetable fix, or a conversation with the subject teacher about a specific topic. Others are solved by habit work the student can do unsupervised once someone has named it. We would rather send a diagnosis that says ask the school for the component split and drill labelled sketches for three weeks than sell a term of hours against a problem that did not need them.

ajman/ib-dp-math-aa-sl-tutor.closingBody: A Standard Level Analysis problem is rarely what the overall grade suggests. Ask the school for the Paper 1 and Paper 2 marks separately, the dated internal deadline for the exploration, and the deadline for a level change. It ends in a written diagnosis naming whether the issue is non-calculator fluency, command terms, accuracy or genuine content, and what a plan would take. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and if the diagnosis points at the school rather than at tuition, it will say so.

intro.heading: Ask for the marked draft before you ask for the price
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge is the one Diploma subject where a parent in Ajman cannot tell from the outside whether anything is improving. There is no textbook chapter to test, no past paper to score out of 80, no weekly vocabulary list. A student says the lesson was interesting, the term ends, and a predicted grade arrives that nobody saw coming. That is why this page is built around evidence rather than method. The useful question to ask any TOK tutor is not what they teach but what they hand back.

What a TOK session should leave behind is an artefact. A written exhibition commentary with marks against each of the three objects. A prescribed title plan with the command words circled and the two areas of knowledge named. An essay draft with band comments in the margin and a global band at the top, matched to the wording of the TOK assessment instrument the IB publishes for examiners. None of that is exotic. It is simply the difference between a conversation and a record.

Ajman adds a practical layer. Private schools here sit under the federal Ministry of Education rather than a Dubai or Abu Dhabi regulator, the IB Diploma cohort in the emirate is small, and a large share of families commute to work in Dubai or Sharjah. The result is late evenings and a thin local pool of teachers who have marked TOK against the real instrument. A specialist reached over video solves the second problem; scheduling on Gulf Standard Time after 7pm solves the first. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, so there is no travel window to lose.

The other reason to insist on marked work is that TOK carries a failing condition. A grade E in Theory of Knowledge, or in the Extended Essay, prevents the award of the Diploma whatever the subject points say. Pairs of letters from the two core components also feed a bonus point matrix worth up to three points on the final total. A family that can see band movement across a term can judge whether a C is drifting towards a D or climbing towards a B. A family relying on impressions cannot, and by the time a predicted grade lands the room for repair has usually gone.

So the sections below do two jobs. They explain, in the IB's own terms, how the exhibition and the essay are scored, what the bands actually describe and where Ajman students lose marks most often. Then they show the week-by-week record a Diploma core support plan in Ajman should generate: who produced what, who scored it, and what changed. If a tutor cannot produce that record, the lessons may still be pleasant. They are not measurable.

ajman/ib-dp-theory-of-knowledge-tutor.programmesIntro: Theory of Knowledge belongs to the Diploma Programme, but the habits it assesses are built earlier. Below is how each IB programme an Ajman family might be inside contributes to the core, and what that means for when support is worth starting.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The two-year Diploma carries three core elements alongside six subjects: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. TOK is assessed by an internally marked exhibition of three objects with a commentary capped at 950 words, and an externally marked essay of up to 1,600 words on one of six prescribed titles released by the IB for each session. The essay counts for two-thirds of the TOK grade.
programmes.countryNote: The Ajman IB Diploma Programme cohort is small enough that a school may run TOK with one teacher across both year groups, often in a timetable slot that gets borrowed for other things. Families here frequently find the exhibition has been completed in a rush. Ajman Academy is the emirate's IB continuum school; several Ajman families also register at IB schools in Sharjah and Dubai and commute, which changes the internal deadline calendar.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP assessment is criterion-referenced, and two of its habits transfer directly into TOK: justifying a claim with evidence, and evaluating the method that produced the evidence. A student who has written MYP criterion D responses has already argued about the limits of knowledge without using the phrase. The Personal Project is the first long independent piece most IB students produce and the first place process documentation is graded.
programmes.countryNote: An MYP student in Ajman moving into DP1 the following August is the ideal moment to start core support, because the exhibition lands early in DP1 while subject content is still light. Work from the Personal Project is useful raw material for a first diagnostic: it shows whether the student can hold a line of argument across pages rather than paragraphs.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: PYP ends with the Exhibition, a collaborative inquiry presented to the school community. The naming is a coincidence, but the demand is related: a student selects a line of inquiry, gathers sources, and explains to an audience why the question matters. PYP also introduces the transdisciplinary skills that TOK later makes explicit, including how a claim is supported and who is entitled to make it.
programmes.countryNote: Only a small number of Ajman schools run PYP, so most Diploma students in the emirate arrive from British or Indian primary routes rather than from the IB continuum. That matters for TOK because those students meet criterion-referenced marking for the first time in DP1, and the vocabulary of the TOK instrument is genuinely new to them rather than a familiar register.

ajman/ib-dp-theory-of-knowledge-tutor.subjectsIntro: A TOK essay is only as good as the examples carrying it, and the strongest examples come from subjects the student already studies. Below are the subjects Ajman Diploma students most often draw on, and what each one contributes to a TOK argument when it is used properly rather than named.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Two assessed tasks, graded A to E. Marks are awarded against a single global instrument for each task, not a checklist, which is why a draft can be factually correct and still sit in the 5-6 band. The instrument rewards sustained, evaluated argument about how knowledge is produced in named areas of knowledge.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: The other half of the bonus point matrix, and the component most often supported by the same mentor. A student who has handled source evaluation for a History or Biology research question already has the material for a TOK paragraph on method and reliability, and the two components reinforce each other when planned together.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The richest source of TOK examples, because historiography is explicit about perspective and evidence. A student who can explain why two accounts of the same event differ, and what each historian had access to, has the backbone of an argument about knowledge in the human sciences and history as areas of knowledge.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Supplies method examples that work: replication, sample size, control variables, and the gap between correlation and cause. An Ajman student whose Biology IA involved an unreliable data set can use it as a first-hand knowledge claim, which is far stronger in TOK than a textbook anecdote about a famous experiment.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Useful for the problem of models. Students meet several incompatible atomic models in sequence and are asked to use each where it works. That is a concrete route into questions about whether a model is true or merely useful, which the natural sciences area of knowledge rewards when argued with a specific case.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The home of measurement uncertainty. A student who has propagated error through a calculation can discuss the limits of precision without hand-waving, and can contrast that with the certainty claimed in mathematics. Strong TOK essays often sit on exactly this comparison between two areas of knowledge.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof is the one place in the Diploma where certainty is available, which makes mathematics the natural contrast class in a TOK essay. Students who have worked through a proof by induction can say what a proof guarantees and what it does not, rather than repeating that maths is objective.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Models with assumptions baked in, applied to messy evidence. Ajman students often have good local material here, from free zone activity to fuel pricing, and a TOK paragraph grounded in a case they can describe outperforms a generic reference to behavioural economics.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Trains the close reading that the prescribed titles demand. Students who have analysed how a text positions a reader are better at noticing that a title says knowledge rather than facts, or replication rather than repetition, and that the wording restricts what counts as an answer.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: The clearest case of knowledge produced under ethical constraint. Students can discuss why certain studies cannot be repeated and what that does to the evidence base, which is a sharper human sciences argument than the usual description of a famous obedience experiment.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Relevant beyond language acquisition for Ajman students, because Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies run alongside the licensed curriculum in UAE private schools under federal rules. Students who study knowledge in two languages have genuine material on translation and the limits of shared concepts.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: The arts area of knowledge is the one most often handled badly, usually because students assert that art expresses feeling and stop. A student with a comparative study behind them can instead discuss how an interpretation is justified, and who in a community of artists and critics decides that it holds.

sections.heading: What a marked TOK draft actually looks like when it comes back
paragraphs: A marked TOK draft returned by a competent reader has four things on it, and a parent in Ajman can check all four without knowing the subject. First, a global band, written as a range out of ten with the instrument's own wording quoted beside it. Second, margin comments that name the fault rather than the feeling, so not awkward but claim asserted, no counterclaim or example named but not used. Third, a short list at the end of changes in priority order. Fourth, a date.

That last item is the one families overlook and the one that makes the record work. Three dated drafts across a term tell you whether the student is moving. A single undated draft tells you nothing, and a set of verbal impressions tells you less. The TOK assessment instrument the IB publishes for its examiners is a global impression tool with five bands, each described in a paragraph rather than a tick list, which is precisely why the band needs to be written down and justified in words a student can act on.

The commonest disappointment is a draft returned with corrected grammar and a comment saying it reads well. Prose quality is not what either TOK task rewards. The instrument asks whether the discussion is sustained, whether the arguments are evaluated, whether claims are supported by specific examples, and whether the response stays with the title or the prompt as written. A draft can be elegant and sit in the 3-4 band because every paragraph describes a position without weighing it.

So the first thing to ask an IB DP Theory of Knowledge tutor in Ajman for is not a plan but a sample of returned work with the student's name removed. If the sample carries a band, reasoning tied to the instrument, and an ordered list of fixes, the tutor marks. If it carries ticks and encouragement, they do not.
bullets: Band written as a range out of ten, with the instrument's language quoted

sections.heading: The exhibition commentary, read as evidence rather than as a task
paragraphs: The TOK exhibition asks a student to choose one of 35 internal assessment prompts, select three specific objects, and explain in a commentary of no more than 950 words how each object connects to that prompt. It is marked in school against the instrument and moderated by the IB, and it contributes one third of the TOK grade. Most Ajman students complete it during DP1, often faster than they should.

Reading an existing TOK exhibition commentary as evidence takes about fifteen minutes and is the cheapest diagnostic available. Three checks do most of the work. Is each object specific, with a real provenance, rather than a category? A particular prayer rug in a particular family, with a date and a story, is an object; prayer rugs in general is a topic. Does each commentary paragraph answer the chosen prompt in its exact wording, or does it drift to a neighbouring question? And is the word budget distributed, roughly 300 words to each object, rather than 600 on the favourite and 150 on the last?

The failures cluster. Students pick objects they can describe instead of objects that argue, which produces three paragraphs of description and a band in the middle. Students change the prompt's wording slightly and answer the question they prefer. Students use a photograph of something generic found online, which strips away the provenance the commentary needs. Each of these is visible on the page, which means it is fixable in one session and verifiable in the next version.

Local objects work well here and are underused. An Ajman student has access to material nobody in a marking pile has seen: a dhow builder's tool from the creek, a federal textbook page in Arabic alongside its English counterpart, a utility bill showing a desalinated water charge. The object does not need to be impressive. It needs to be specific, locatable, and genuinely connected to the prompt the student chose.

sections.heading: The prescribed title plan: the artefact worth producing first
paragraphs: Six prescribed titles are released by the IB for each examination session, and the student answers one of them without altering a word. The essay runs to a maximum of 1,600 words, is marked by an external examiner, and carries two thirds of the TOK grade. Almost every recoverable mark on that essay is decided before any prose exists, in the plan, which is why the plan is the first artefact a session should produce.

A usable plan fits on one page and has five parts. The title copied exactly, with the command terms and the restricting words underlined. A gloss of each key term in the student's own words, because a title that says knowledge rather than information is restricting what counts as an answer. Two named areas of knowledge that genuinely pull in different directions. For each, one real example the student can describe in detail from their own subjects or life. And a counterclaim per area, with its own evidence rather than a sentence of concession.

A plan like that is markable. A tutor can look at it and say, honestly, that the second area of knowledge duplicates the first, or that the example named is one the student cannot actually describe, or that the counterclaim is a restatement. Those judgements take ten minutes and save a fortnight. Compare that with the usual sequence, where a student produces 1,600 words from a one-line idea and then gets told the structure is wrong, with the deadline two weeks away.

Some students find the plan harder than the prose, and that is the point. The plan is where the thinking is assessed. A good prescribed title plan also exposes whether the essay should be attempted at all with that title: if the student cannot name two areas of knowledge they can argue about, choosing a different title from the six is a legitimate and much cheaper decision in week one than in week nine.

sections.heading: Twelve weeks of evidence: the record a core support plan should leave
paragraphs: Week by week is not a marketing frame here. It is how a TOK grade is actually built, because both tasks are long-form and assessed on sustained argument rather than recall. A plan that produces one scored artefact a week is also the only way a parent in Ajman can audit progress without reading TOK themselves. The table below is the shape of a real twelve-week run in DP1, aligned to a school's internal exhibition and essay deadlines rather than to any examination date.

Two features of that record matter more than the rest. The scorer column changes: some artefacts are marked by the tutor, some by the school's TOK teacher, and some by the student against the instrument with the tutor checking the self-assessment. A student who can band their own draft within one band of the tutor has learned the instrument, which is the point of the exercise. The evidence column is written as a comparison, not as a compliment, so week nine says counterclaim now carries its own example, previously a single sentence.

The run also plans for the weeks when nothing is produced. Mock fortnight, school trips and the Ramadan timetable change what a student can do, and a record that pretends otherwise is fiction. Sessions in those weeks switch to reading and oral defence of an existing draft, which still generates evidence without demanding new writing. During Ramadan, families in Ajman commonly move the slot after Iftar, which works for a remote tutor and would be awkward for anyone travelling.

At the end of a run like this, the useful output is one document: the band history, the dated artefacts and the open issues. If the student then moves school, changes mentor or needs a predicted grade conversation, that document is the argument. Nothing in it depends on anyone's opinion of how the lessons felt.

sections.heading: Grade movement: what one letter is worth on the Diploma total
paragraphs: TOK and the Extended Essay are graded A to E and combine in a published matrix to award up to three bonus points on the Diploma total of 45. The matrix is not linear, which is why tracking band movement matters more in some positions than others. Moving TOK from C to B is worth a point if the Extended Essay is already at B or above, and worth nothing at all if the essay sits at D. A family watching the record can see which of the two components is the constraint.

The failing condition is the harder number. A grade E in either TOK or the Extended Essay prevents the award of the Diploma regardless of how strong the six subject grades are. That is not a scare tactic; it is a rule a small number of students meet every session, usually because one core component was left too late while subject revision took every available hour. An evidence record is the early warning, because a draft sitting in the 1-2 band in week eight is a visible fact rather than a worry.

The practical consequence for an Ajman family is about where to spend hours. If the record shows TOK at a secure 5-6 band and the Extended Essay unstarted, the hours belong to the essay. If both sit mid-band, the cheaper letter to move is usually TOK, because its two tasks are shorter and the instrument is the same for both. These are decisions you can only make with two scored records side by side, which is the argument for treating Diploma core support in Ajman as one brief rather than two.

Nobody should promise a letter. The honest claim is narrower and more useful: band positions are visible, the faults that cap a band are nameable, and a student who fixes a named fault usually moves. What happens at moderation and external marking is outside anyone's control, and a tutor who talks about certainties rather than bands is telling you something about themselves.

sections.heading: Academic honesty in TOK, and what the evidence file has to show
paragraphs: TOK is where the boundary between support and malpractice is tested hardest, because the output is argument rather than calculation and the help is invisible once the prose is smooth. The IB's position is clear enough to work with: the work submitted must be the student's own, a supervisor or teacher may discuss and give feedback, and only one draft of the essay may be commented on formally before the final version. A tutor operates inside that same rule, not outside it.

What a tutor may legitimately do is read, question, score and explain. Mark a draft against the instrument. Ask why a counterclaim is a single sentence. Point out that an example is named but never used. Explain what the instrument means by evaluated. Teach the student how to self-band. What nobody may do is supply prose, restructure paragraphs on the student's behalf, choose the three objects, or hand over a model answer for adaptation. IB Gram does not produce assessed work for students, and no amount of deadline pressure changes that.

The evidence record helps here rather than hindering. A file of dated drafts in the student's own voice, with margin comments and a visible band history, is exactly what a school wants to see if a question is ever raised. The pattern that looks bad is the opposite: one weak early draft, then a polished final version with no intermediate stages and a register that does not match the student's other work. Keeping version history is as much a protection as a progress tool.

Generative tools sit in the same frame. A student may use them, as they may use any source, and must then acknowledge them properly; what cannot happen is text generated elsewhere appearing as the student's own argument. For TOK specifically there is a practical reason beyond the rule. Machine prose about knowledge questions is fluent, generic and reliably mid-band, because it describes positions instead of weighing them against named examples the student can actually defend in an oral.

sections.heading: Ajman specifics: the Ministry, the commute and the Arabic requirement
paragraphs: Private schools in Ajman are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, not by an emirate-level authority. The u.ae guidance sets out the regulator map plainly: KHDA covers Dubai, ADEK covers Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority covers Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge covers Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. For a TOK parent this is mostly administrative, but it changes where an inspection report or a complaint actually goes.

The federal baseline also shapes a Diploma student's week here. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must observe the Ministry's general regulations. In practice a DP1 student in Ajman is carrying six Diploma subjects, TOK, the Extended Essay, CAS and the mandatory UAE subjects at the same time. Any honest week-by-week plan has to assume fewer free evenings than a plan written for a student in a lighter system.

The commute is the other local fact worth planning around. A large share of Ajman households work in Dubai or Sharjah, and a parent who leaves Al Mowaihat at seven in the morning is rarely home before seven in the evening. That pushes Diploma core sessions to 7.30pm or later on weekdays, with the bigger blocks at weekends. A remote specialist absorbs that easily. A travelling tutor would spend the commute window in traffic and charge for it, which is one reason the in-home market in the northern emirates is thin at Diploma level.

Tutoring itself is permitted but regulated. An individual giving private lessons in the UAE needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility extending to registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any figure quoted to you should be treated with scepticism.
