sections.heading: What the market charges for Diploma core support, and what to ask before paying
paragraphs: Published rates in the UAE tutoring market spread widely, and Diploma core work sits towards the upper end because the pool of people who have marked TOK against the instrument is small. Budget online providers advertise from around AED 45 to 65 an hour and platform rates from roughly AED 33 to 52, while qualified subject tutors online are commonly quoted between AED 150 and 300. Specialist IB work is quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with one named provider publishing AED 650 for premium sessions and an aggregator reporting in-home visits at AED 180 to 350. Those are the market's numbers, attributed to the sources that published them, not a price list.

Two structures dominate. An hourly rate suits the single diagnostic and the weekly record. A project block, quoted from plan to submission, suits the deadline run and is how most Extended Essay support is sold. The trap in the block is scope: a block that includes unlimited reading of successive drafts conflicts with the one-permitted-draft rule, and a block that includes proofreading is selling something a tutor should not deliver. Ask what the block excludes before asking what it costs.

Three questions separate a marker from a conversationalist. Can you show a redacted sample of returned work with a band on it? Do you hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit, and will you say so in writing? What do you refuse to do with a draft? The third answer is the most revealing. A tutor who cannot name a limit has no limit, and a provider advertising finished Internal Assessments or completed essays is selling the student an expulsion risk rather than a grade.

For context, school fees in the region have their own trajectory: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's economic incentives package. Tutoring is an additional discretionary spend on top of fees, and the evidence record is what tells you whether that spend is doing anything. A family in Ajman buying one scored diagnostic and then deciding is behaving rationally, which is why that option is listed first on this page.

process.title: Send the work that already exists
process.description: Share whatever the student has: a commentary, a title plan, a half-finished draft, or the school's internal deadline sheet. Nothing needs tidying first. A rough draft tells a tutor more than a clean one, because the faults are still visible and the band is honest.

process.title: Take the first lesson at no charge
process.description: A 45-minute session on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled after the Ajman school run and the Dubai or Sharjah commute. The tutor reads the work live, asks the student to defend two claims, and bands what exists. No card details are taken and there is nothing to cancel afterwards.

process.title: Read the marked artefact
process.description: Within a day you receive the scored document: a band out of ten, the instrument's wording quoted against it, margin comments naming each fault, and an ordered list of changes. Decide from that document rather than from a sales conversation whether the match is right.

process.title: Set the record running
process.description: If you continue, each week produces one dated artefact and one score, logged in a single running document. The scorer rotates between tutor, student self-assessment and the school's own marks, so the band history is triangulated rather than one person's view.

process.title: Review at the school's internal deadline
process.description: At the submission point, the band history is closed out with open issues listed. Many families stop there, some continue into the Extended Essay with the same mentor, and either choice is reasonable. Nothing renews automatically and the record belongs to you.

whyPoints.title: Marked work, not impressions
whyPoints.description: Every session produces something readable with a band on it. That is the whole proposition of this page. Parents in Ajman who cannot assess a TOK argument themselves can still assess whether the band history is moving and whether the named faults are being fixed.

whyPoints.title: A specialist pool the emirate does not have locally
whyPoints.description: The IB Diploma cohort in Ajman is small, and the number of people nearby who have marked TOK against the published instrument is smaller. Remote one-to-one removes the geographic constraint, which is the honest reason online delivery suits a Diploma core subject in the northern emirates.

whyPoints.title: A stated limit on what a tutor will do
whyPoints.description: Reading, questioning, scoring and explaining are the job. Supplying prose, choosing objects or polishing a submission to completion are not, and the limit is written here rather than discovered later. This is the opposite of the finished-coursework market operating in this search space.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling that survives an Ajman week
whyPoints.description: Sessions sit after the commute, move after Iftar during Ramadan, and pause through mock fortnights and school trips without penalty. A plan that ignores the mandatory UAE subjects and a DP1 timetable is a plan that quietly stops being followed by October.

whyPoints.title: One brief across the core
whyPoints.description: TOK and the Extended Essay share a bonus point matrix and an instrument-driven marking culture. Keeping both in one record makes it possible to see which component is actually holding the total down, instead of buying hours for whichever one the student complains about.

whyPoints.title: Figures that carry their source
whyPoints.description: Every AED range on this page is attributed to the provider or aggregator that published it, and every regulatory statement is taken from u.ae, KHDA or MoHRE guidance. No IB examination date appears here, because those have to be confirmed against the IB or a school coordinator rather than repeated.

faqs.question: What should an Ajman family receive in writing after a Theory of Knowledge session?
faqs.answer: A scored document. It should carry a band out of ten for the task discussed, the instrument's own wording quoted beside that band, margin comments naming each fault rather than describing the style, an ordered list of changes with the biggest lever first, and a date. The date is what makes a record possible: three dated drafts across a term show movement, while three pleasant conversations show nothing. If a tutor returns only corrected grammar and encouragement, you have bought proofreading rather than TOK support, and the band will not move.

faqs.question: How can I judge whether my child's TOK is improving if I have never studied it?
faqs.answer: You read the band history rather than the argument. The TOK assessment instrument has five bands, each described in a paragraph, and a competent marker will write the band and the reason on every version. Your job is to check three things: that the band is recorded each time, that the named faults from one version are actually addressed in the next, and that the student can say out loud what changed and why. None of that requires you to know what an area of knowledge is.

faqs.question: Why did my daughter's exhibition commentary score in the middle when the writing was good?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the objects describe rather than argue. The exhibition asks for three specific objects connected to one of 35 prompts, explained within 950 words in total. A commentary that tells the reader what each object is, and then asserts a link to the prompt, sits mid-band however well it reads. The repair is mechanical: for each object, state the claim it supports, then state what it fails to show. That turns description into the evaluated discussion the instrument rewards.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting Diploma core support in DP1 rather than waiting for DP2?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the reason is timetabling rather than urgency. The exhibition falls in DP1 while subject content is still relatively light, so there is room to produce, score and revise a commentary properly. By DP2 the same hours are competing with Internal Assessments and examination revision across six subjects, plus the mandatory UAE subjects. Starting in DP1 also means the student learns to band their own work early, which reduces how many paid hours the essay needs later in the programme.

faqs.question: How many objects and prompts does the TOK exhibition actually require?
faqs.answer: Three objects and one prompt. The student chooses a single prompt from the 35 internal assessment prompts published by the IB, selects three specific objects with real provenance, and explains each connection in a commentary capped at 950 words for all three together. The exhibition is marked in school against the assessment instrument and then moderated by the IB, and it contributes one third of the final TOK grade, with the externally marked essay carrying the other two thirds.

faqs.question: Can a tutor change the wording of a prescribed title to suit my son's interests?
faqs.answer: No. The six prescribed titles released for each session are used exactly as published, and an essay answering a reworded version of a title loses marks for relevance no matter how good the argument is. What a tutor can legitimately do is gloss the title: underline the command terms and the restricting words, explain in plain language what the wording excludes, and help the student decide whether a different one of the six titles fits their available examples better. That decision is cheap in week one.

faqs.question: What does a usable prescribed title plan look like on one page?
faqs.answer: Five parts. The title copied exactly, with command terms and restricting words underlined. A gloss of each key term in the student's own words. Two areas of knowledge that genuinely contrast rather than duplicate each other. One detailed, describable example for each, ideally from a subject the student studies. And a counterclaim per area carrying its own evidence rather than a single sentence of concession. A plan in that shape is markable in ten minutes, which is why it is the first artefact a session should produce.

faqs.question: My son's draft has no counterclaim worth the name. How is that fixed in one session?
faqs.answer: By giving the counterclaim equal weight rather than a sentence. A draft that concedes briefly and moves on sits below a draft that argues the opposite position with its own named example and then explains why it is less convincing. In a session the tutor identifies the paragraph where the concession sits, the student supplies a real counterexample from their own subjects, and the paragraph is rebuilt by the student afterwards. The change is usually visible as a band movement in the next dated version.

faqs.question: Does a grade E in Theory of Knowledge really stop the whole Diploma?
faqs.answer: Yes. A grade E in either TOK or the Extended Essay is a failing condition for the award of the IB Diploma, independent of how strong the six subject grades are. The two components also combine in a published matrix worth up to three bonus points on the total of 45. That is why a visible band history matters: a draft sitting in the lowest band in week eight is a fact a family can act on, whereas a vague worry in April is usually too late to fix properly.

faqs.question: If TOK and the Extended Essay are both mid-band, which one should we spend hours on?
faqs.answer: Usually TOK, because both of its tasks are short and share one instrument, so a named fault can be fixed and re-scored within a fortnight. The exception is the matrix position: if the Extended Essay is at D, lifting TOK may add nothing to the bonus points, so the hours belong to the essay instead. This is a decision you can only make with two scored records side by side, which is the argument for keeping both core components in a single brief.

faqs.question: What exactly will a tutor refuse to do with a TOK draft?
faqs.answer: Supply prose, rewrite paragraphs on the student's behalf, choose the three exhibition objects, or hand over a model answer to adapt. The submitted work has to be the student's own, and only one essay draft may be formally commented on before the final version. What a tutor does instead is read, question, score against the instrument and explain what the band language means. Any provider offering a finished essay or a completed Internal Assessment is selling the student a malpractice investigation, not a grade.

faqs.question: Can my child use an AI tool on TOK work, and will anyone be able to tell?
faqs.answer: A tool may be used as a source and must then be acknowledged properly, like any other source; text generated elsewhere presented as the student's own argument is malpractice. There is also a practical reason to avoid it in TOK specifically. Machine prose about knowledge questions is fluent, generic and reliably mid-band, because it describes positions instead of weighing them against examples the student can defend in conversation. A dated version history in the student's own voice is the better protection.

faqs.question: Can sessions move after Iftar during Ramadan, and what happens in mock fortnight?
faqs.answer: Yes to both, and the record is designed for it. During Ramadan most Ajman families shift the slot to after Iftar, which a remote tutor can accommodate without travel. In mock fortnight no new writing is attempted; the session becomes an oral defence of an existing draft, where the student argues their claims without the text in front of them. That still generates evidence, and a claim that survives questioning usually survives the examiner. Sessions pause without penalty for school trips.

faqs.question: Does the Ministry of Education or any emirate authority set what TOK my child studies in Ajman?
faqs.answer: No. TOK content and assessment are set by the IB, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah rather than writing the Diploma syllabus. What the federal rules do require is Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside the licensed curriculum, which affects how many hours a DP1 week actually contains. Internal TOK deadlines are set by each school, so an Ajman student attending a Sharjah campus follows that school's calendar.

faqs.question: Does the TOK grade matter for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency or university entry?
faqs.answer: Equivalency rules are published by the Ministry of Education and should be checked on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority directly, and no IB points threshold is reproduced here because that figure has not been read on an official UAE source. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels. Tutoring is never required for a regulatory process.

faqs.question: What happens if no TOK specialist is free when we get in touch?
faqs.answer: You are told, rather than matched with whoever is available. The pool of tutors who have marked TOK against the published instrument is genuinely small, and a general essay tutor reading a prescribed title plan is not the same service. If nobody suitable is free, the options are to wait for a named slot, start with the Extended Essay side of the core where cover is wider, or take a single scored diagnostic now so the band is at least recorded while you decide.

ajman/ib-dp-theory-of-knowledge-tutor.closingHeading: Start with one scored draft, then decide
ajman/ib-dp-theory-of-knowledge-tutor.closingBody: The cheapest useful thing an Ajman family can do about Theory of Knowledge is put the work that already exists in front of someone who marks against the instrument and ask for a band in writing. That takes one 45-minute session on Gulf Standard Time, costs nothing, and produces a document you keep whatever you decide next. If the band is secure, you have saved the money. If it is not, you know which fault caps it and in what order to fix things. Send the current commentary, title plan or draft, tell us the school's internal deadline, and we will schedule after the commute.

Costs on this page describe the market an Ajman family is buying in; what IB Gram publishes is the model and the free first lesson, with any quote given per subject and per block rather than as a tariff.

intro.heading: Two numbers decide what IB support costs you, and the rate is the smaller one
paragraphs: Every provider in this market advertises the first number and almost none of them discusses the second. The first is the hourly rate. The second is the number of hours, and it is the one that actually determines the cheque. A tutor at AED 150 an hour who needs thirty-two hours to repair a Higher Level problem costs AED 4,800. A tutor at AED 270 who needs twelve costs AED 3,240 and finishes sooner. Comparing rates without comparing hours is the most expensive habit a family can bring to this decision.

The second number depends on three things: whether the gap is technique or content, whether the student does the work set between sessions, and how early you start. All three are knowable before you commit, and the first can be read from a single marked script. That is why this page spends more time on plan shapes and on a calendar than on a rate card, and why the one figure we will not publish is a price for a predicted outcome.

The figures used throughout are market figures with their sources named. A 2026 Dubai tutoring cost survey puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350 an hour, and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500 once travel sits inside the rate. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist work. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 at the budget end, which is generally group or university-student tutoring rather than specialist one-to-one. All were researched in October 2026.

Ajman changes several of those numbers in ways a generic UAE page will not tell you. The emirate is small and its private schools sit under federal Ministry of Education oversight rather than under an emirate authority. A large share of households have a parent working in Dubai or Sharjah, which pushes the usable evening later and shortens the window in which a visiting tutor can arrive. And the local pool of IB subject specialists is thin, which is the single biggest upward pressure on any in-home quote here: scarcity, not quality, sets that premium.

One thing to settle before the detail. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; sending a teacher to a residence is a service we run only in India. The in-home option is priced honestly on this page because you will be quoted for it elsewhere and you deserve a fair comparison. What IB Gram delivers to an Ajman family is one-to-one tuition over live video, with the first lesson free and no payment taken before it. Read the bands below as a yardstick for whatever quote lands in your inbox, and convert every one of them to dirhams per teaching hour before you compare two providers.

ajman/ib-home-tutor.programmesIntro: An hour does not cost the same at every stage, because the work in the hour is different. These are the stages an Ajman family pays for, and what the money is actually buying at each one.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, Years 7 to 11
programmes.description: The cheapest hours in the whole sequence and the ones most families skip. Work is assessed against four criteria per subject on a 1 to 8 scale, and the criterion that scores low is almost always the one asking for evaluation or reflection rather than for knowledge. Support here targets durable skills — writing to a criterion, arithmetic fluency, structured paragraphs — which is why an hour bought in Year 9 does more than an hour bought in DP2.
programmes.countryNote: In Ajman the Middle Years enquiry usually arrives in Year 10, after a report that looked fine until the student met the Diploma's expectations. At market rates the stage sits at the lower end of the qualified-tutor band published by Unitors, because the content demand on the tutor is lower even where the teaching skill required is not.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, first year
programmes.description: The expensive year to under-spend in. Higher Level content accelerates sharply, internally assessed components open, and the core starts making demands at exactly the point the subjects do. Money spent here buys technique that applies across both years: command terms, written method, the discipline of closing an evaluative answer. Money not spent here tends to be spent twice in DP2 under time pressure.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman's IB cohorts are small, so a Higher Level group may number four or five students taught by a teacher carrying two other courses. That is the structural reason DP1 support is the most common enquiry we take from the emirate, and it is why we quote per subject rather than per student.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, final year
programmes.description: The year when rates in this market move, because demand concentrates. Published monthly estimates for weekly one-hour specialist support in an examination year reach AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above, against AED 600 to 1,200 for mid-tier support, in the 2026 survey quoted above. Internally assessed work closes, predicted grades are set, and the remaining movable marks are mostly technique rather than content.
programmes.countryNote: The practical Ajman consequence is availability rather than price. Specialist slots between 18:30 and 21:00 — the only window that survives a Dubai or Sharjah commute — are the first to fill in the second year. Families who hold a standing slot from September pay the same as everybody else and get the hour they need.

programmes.name: The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
programmes.description: Priced by most providers as a separate block, and the block that is most often bought too late. The core is assessed through an exhibition of objects, a prescribed-title essay and a supervised piece of independent research, and the failure mode is almost always sequencing rather than ability. Short blocks of process coaching, bought early, replace long blocks of crisis work bought in the final term.
programmes.countryNote: Supervision sits with the school, and a tutor's contribution is questioning the student's own work against the criteria. One operator in this market advertises finished internal assessments for a four-figure sum; that is the one line item an Ajman family should refuse at any price, because the consequence falls on the student.

ajman/ib-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Rates vary by subject more than most price pages admit, and the reason is supply rather than difficulty. These are the subjects Ajman families most often ask about, with a note on what moves the number.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most requested Diploma subject in this emirate and therefore the best supplied, which keeps quotes near the middle of the qualified-tutor band. Higher Level adds genuine content rather than harder versions of the same content, so hours needed rise steeply at HL even where the rate does not.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Slightly thinner supply than Analysis and Approaches, and a different cost profile: the exploration and the technology papers need a tutor comfortable with the graphic display calculator as a teaching tool rather than as an accessory, which narrows the field and lifts the quote.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Among the dearest hours in the Diploma, because two separate failure modes need two different drills and because Higher Level specialists are scarce in the northern emirates. A quote near the top of the specialist band is defensible here in a way it is not in a well-supplied subject.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Similar scarcity to Chemistry, with a mark-loss pattern that is cheap to fix once named: method written down rather than held in the head. Families often buy a long block when a short technique block would have done, which is a cost of poor diagnosis rather than of the subject.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Better supplied than the other two sciences, so quotes sit lower. The hours tend to be more numerous, because the content volume is large and the extended-response marks turn on command terms that need repeated marked practice rather than a single explanation.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Reasonably supplied and often mis-bought. The movable marks are concentrated in evaluation and in the internally assessed commentaries, both of which respond to a handful of sessions, so a year-long weekly arrangement is frequently more than the problem requires.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Quotes near the middle of the band. The cost risk here is the internally assessed component, where students choose an organisation they cannot get data from and then need far more hours than planned to rescue a question that was never answerable.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Supply is decent, and the hours are predictable because the skills are specific: unseen analysis, the individual oral's connective argument, essay structure. This is a subject where marking-only arrangements often deliver most of the movement at a fraction of the weekly cost.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Thin local supply, which lifts quotes, and a heavy load of precise terminology and studies. Families underestimate the hours because the content reads accessibly; the marks sit in command-term discipline and in the experimental study's method.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.description: The hardest stream to resource locally and therefore the least predictable quote. Teaching conditions are set centrally, including the language of instruction and the separation of classes for Arab and non-Arab students, so material cannot be substituted freely by a private tutor.

sections.heading: The in-home premium, decomposed into minutes
paragraphs: Published in-home rates in this market run from AED 180 to 350 an hour in the 2026 survey quoted above, and from AED 200 to 500 for independent home tutors, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The gap is not a quality gap. It is a travel gap, a minimum-booking gap and a risk gap, and once you can see the three separately you can judge whether any particular quote is reasonable.

Travel comes first. A tutor who drives from Sharjah to Al Jurf and back has spent forty to sixty minutes unpaid unless it is inside the rate, which it always is. Fuel and any tolls go the same way. Then the minimum booking: because the journey is fixed and the teaching is variable, visiting tutors across the UAE price a two-hour minimum, which is why monthly in-home packages in this market appear as four two-hour sessions at AED 1,599 to 1,799 rather than as eight single hours.

Then risk. A cancelled online session costs a tutor an empty hour. A cancelled visit costs them the hour plus the journey, which is why in-home cancellation terms are tighter and why a family that moves sessions around a school calendar pays more for the privilege. None of this is unfair. It is simply what is inside the number, and a visiting tutor who quotes AED 300 for a district forty minutes away is not overcharging, they are pricing their own time correctly.

sections.heading: The two Diploma years as a cash-flow calendar
paragraphs: Families budget tuition as a monthly subscription and then discover it is seasonal. The demand on a Diploma student is not spread evenly across twenty-four months: it concentrates around internally assessed deadlines, mock weeks and the final run to papers, and a plan that spends the same amount every month either over-buys in quiet terms or under-buys in the loud ones.

The useful exercise is to lay the two years out and decide in advance which months carry hours. In the first term of DP1 the right purchase is usually diagnosis plus technique, which is cheap and durable. Through the middle of DP1 the internally assessed components open and the core begins, which is where short blocks earn their keep. The first term of DP2 is the heaviest, because components close while content continues. The final stretch is technique and timed papers, and the month after the papers costs nothing at all.

The indicative monthly figures in the table come from the published 2026 estimates for weekly one-hour support: AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-tier and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year support. They are the market's numbers, not a quote, and the point of the table is the shape rather than the totals.

One planning note that saves real money. No IB session or results date is published on this page, because those dates have not been confirmed from the IB's own site for this project. The school's coordinator holds the authoritative internal calendar, including component deadlines that sit months before anything external. Ask for it in September of DP1 and build the spending plan on that document rather than on a guess.

sections.heading: Who actually bears which cost in each arrangement
paragraphs: Cost incidence is the part of this market nobody writes down. Every arrangement contains the same underlying costs — travel, preparation, marking, resources, a room, cover when somebody is unavailable — and the arrangements differ in who carries each one. A quote that looks cheap often looks that way because a cost has been moved onto the family or onto the student without being named.

The clearest example is marking. A session spent reading the student's work for the first time is a session in which you paid a specialist rate for silent reading. A tutor who marks before the hour has absorbed that preparation into their rate, which makes their rate look higher and their hours fewer. Over a term the second arrangement is usually cheaper and always more useful, but you cannot see that from the two numbers on the advert.

The second example is cover. If a tutor becomes unavailable mid-block, somebody bears the cost of the gap: either the family waits, or the provider rematches and the new tutor spends a session catching up, or the marked-work record travels and the handover costs nothing much. Which of those happens is worth agreeing before the second lesson rather than in March.

The third is the room. An in-home visit uses your room, your electricity and your household's silence for two hours; an online session uses a corner of a desk. Neither is free, and for an apartment household in Al Nuaimiya the second is considerably less disruptive than the first. The table sets the comparison out in full.

sections.heading: Reading a quote: per hour, per session, per month, per subject
paragraphs: Four units are in common use in this market and they are not interchangeable, which is how two quotes that look similar turn out to differ by half. Ask which unit you are being quoted in and convert everything to one before you compare anything.

Per hour is the cleanest and the rarest at the premium end. Per session matters because a session is not always sixty minutes: ninety-minute and two-hour sessions are standard for in-home work, so AED 400 a session may be AED 200 an hour or AED 267 an hour depending on length. Per month is the hardest to read, because a monthly figure hides both the session length and the number of sessions. The AED 799 monthly online package seen in this market covers eight sessions, which is roughly AED 100 a session; the AED 1,599 to 1,799 in-home monthly figures cover four two-hour visits, which is AED 200 to 225 an hour. Same market, very different arithmetic.

Per subject is the unit that catches families out at the end. A quote given for a student is not a quote for three subjects, and the assumption that a weekly hour can rotate between Chemistry, Mathematics and English is how a plan ends up delivering a third of a session in each. If you need two subjects, price two arrangements and decide whether you want both, rather than buying one and dividing it.

Two further questions worth asking in writing. Does the figure include the tutor's marking time, and is that marking done before the session or inside it? And what is the position on tax: we will not state the VAT treatment of tuition fees as a matter of fact, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation nobody in this market provides, but any provider quoting you a figure should be able to say plainly whether their own number includes it.

sections.heading: Six things that move the number in Ajman specifically
paragraphs: Generic UAE price pages give you a national band and leave you to guess where your own emirate sits inside it. Six local factors do most of the work here, and five of them push upwards.

Specialist scarcity is the largest. IB provision in Ajman is concentrated rather than widespread, so the local pool of people who can mark a Higher Level Chemistry investigation is small, and a small pool prices like a small pool. The commute is the second: with many households having a parent working in Dubai or Sharjah, the usable evening starts late and the slots between 18:30 and 21:00 are the only ones that reliably work, which concentrates demand into a narrow window. Travel distance is the third, and it varies sharply by district — Al Rashidiya is cheap to reach, Al Jurf is not.

The fourth is the two-hour minimum convention on visits, which doubles the smallest amount you can buy. The fifth is the academic calendar: Ramadan compresses the school day and shifts sessions later, and the months around internally assessed deadlines concentrate demand across every family at once. The sixth factor pushes the other way, and it is the only one that does: because lessons can run over video, an Ajman family is buying from a national pool rather than a local one, which is why online specialist rates in this market sit below in-home rates rather than above them.

One factor that should not move the number, and sometimes does: a provider's claim to regulator approval. No tutoring platform in this market holds an endorsement from the International Baccalaureate, the Ministry of Education or any emirate authority, and a premium charged on the strength of an implied seal of approval is a premium on nothing. IB Gram holds no such accreditation and claims none.

sections.heading: The cheapest intervention in the two years, and when to buy it
paragraphs: The highest-value money in a Diploma, measured by grade movement per dirham, is almost always spent in the summer between the two years, and almost nobody spends it there. The reason is arithmetic rather than pedagogy. A content gap in a Higher Level subject is measured in dozens of teaching hours, and a weekly hour during term is consumed by whatever is urgent that week, so the gap never closes while new content keeps arriving on top of it.

A fortnight of daily hours in a quiet period behaves completely differently. There is no new content arriving, no homework competing, and the tutor can work through a syllabus in sequence rather than triaging. Families who do this typically spend less in total than families who buy a weekly hour for eighteen months, and they start DP2 without the deficit that would otherwise have shaped the whole year.

The second cheapest intervention is earlier still: the year before the Diploma begins. A student entering DP1 secure in algebraic manipulation, able to write a paragraph with a controlling idea and used to working against a criterion rather than for a teacher's approval has access to the whole programme. One who is not may be paying for remedial work in two subjects for two years. Middle Years support is quieter, less urgent and considerably better value than anything purchasable in DP2.

The most expensive intervention is the one bought six weeks before papers for a gap that is two years wide. It is also the one most often sold, because that is when parents are most frightened. A short block repairs technique and cannot install a syllabus, and we will say so at the diagnostic. The honest conversation at that point is about triage — which subjects to protect, and whether a later session is the sensible route for the weakest.

sections.heading: What the money does not buy, at any rate
paragraphs: Three things are not purchasable, and a provider who prices them is selling something they cannot deliver. The first is a grade. No tutor can promise a Diploma score or a specific improvement, and any package priced against a predicted total is a claim about an outcome controlled by the student and the examiner. The gate on every page of this site blocks that claim, and it should.

The second is motivation. A tutor can see the work, mark it and tell you honestly when it has not been done. They cannot make a seventeen-year-old open a book at eight o'clock, and where that is the actual problem the sessions become a weekly receipt for the same information. If the diagnostic reaches that conclusion, we will say it rather than invoice around it for a term — which is cheaper for you and more sustainable for us.

The third is authorship, and this is the one with consequences. One operator researched in this market advertises completed internal assessments at a four-figure price. Buying that transfers the risk entirely onto your child: awarding bodies treat authorship breaches as malpractice, the penalty can reach an entire entry rather than one component, and the student confirms the work is their own as part of submitting it. A tutor may teach the skill, read the criteria, question a draft the student has written and mark a timed task. That is the whole of the permitted range, and it is enough.

What the money does buy is specific and checkable: diagnosis of where the marks are going, training in the technique that recovers them, marked work every week, and a written record you can read without the subject guide. Judge any arrangement on whether those four things arrive, not on how reassuring the conversation was.

sections.heading: Why this is delivered over live video, and what that removes from the bill
paragraphs: Every lesson for an Ajman family runs one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. The student needs a device with a camera, a reliable connection, paper and the same desk each week. Work is photographed and sent ahead so the tutor has marked it before the hour begins, which means the billed time is teaching rather than reading.

Three cost lines disappear in that arrangement and it is worth being specific about which. Travel, both the tutor's and the hidden cost of your evening. The two-hour minimum booking, because there is no journey to justify, so a single hour is a purchasable unit. And the scarcity premium, because the pool is no longer whoever can reach your district by 19:00. That third one is the largest in a small emirate, and it is the reason online specialist rates in this market sit below in-home rates rather than above them.

Two things get worse, and they belong in the same paragraph as the savings. A screen cannot supervise a reluctant student into starting, and it cannot handle laboratory apparatus. Where supervision is the real requirement, the honest recommendation is the in-home market option priced earlier on this page, and we would rather say that at the diagnostic than afterwards. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, and pretending otherwise would waste your evening.

For the typical Ajman enquiry — one Higher Level subject, a grade below target, components approaching — the format is not a compromise. It is the reason a household in Al Mowaihat can hold a standing 19:30 slot with a specialist in the subject rather than a weekly appointment with the nearest available generalist.

sections.heading: What a quote from us looks like, and the honest no
paragraphs: You send the subject, the level, the year group, a photograph of a recent marked piece and the two evening windows that genuinely work. We come back with a named tutor, their subject and level coverage, a proposed slot in Gulf Standard Time and a figure for a defined block rather than a tariff. The first lesson is free and is a diagnostic; no payment is taken before it, and there is no obligation to continue afterwards.

The quote names three things explicitly, because those are the three that go wrong elsewhere. How long a session is. Whether marking is included and when it happens. And what the block is for, with an end date, so that it does not quietly become a subscription. If you want two subjects, you get two figures, because a rotating hour is not two arrangements.

The availability answer is given straight, which is rare in this market. Mathematics, the three sciences, English A and B, Economics, Business Management and Psychology are generally coverable within a few days at both levels. Some ab initio languages, the arts at Higher Level and Arabic as a first language take longer or cannot be covered, and when that is the case we say so rather than holding an enquiry open. Telling you where the gap is lets you look in the right place.

And there is a point at which the honest answer is to spend nothing. If the diagnostic says the gap is supervision, or that the student is carrying three Higher Levels they cannot carry, or that six weeks will not close a two-year deficit, you will hear that at the free lesson. The week-six review exists for the same reason: six marked pieces on the table, one question about whether the targeted criterion moved, and a willingness to recommend stopping if it did not.

If the honest conclusion is to spend nothing, that is what you will be told, and there is nothing to cancel.

process.description: A figure for a defined number of hours with a named target and an end date, stating session length, whether marking is included and when it happens. Two subjects get two figures. Nothing renews automatically, because an undefined block becomes a subscription and nobody notices the moment it happened.

process.title: Weekly marked work, prepared before the hour

The session is spent on the marks rather than on reading, and a written note follows naming the criterion targeted and whether it moved. That note is what the week-six review reads.

process.title: Review at week six and decide
process.description: Parent, student and tutor look at six marked pieces and answer one question: has the targeted criterion moved? If it has, pick the next target or stop. If it has not, either the diagnosis or the match changes. A provider unwilling to hold that conversation has told you something useful.

faqs.question: What does an hour with an IB home tutor in Ajman cost once travel is inside the number?
faqs.answer: Market figures researched in October 2026 put in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350 an hour in a 2026 Dubai cost survey, with independent home tutors charging AED 200 to 500 once travel sits inside the rate. A qualified subject tutor working online sits lower, around AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB tuition from AED 200 and TutorChase quoting AED 270 for specialist work. The gap between those bands is travel, a two-hour minimum booking convention and cancellation risk rather than teaching quality. These are market rates, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Why is the hourly rate the least useful number in a tutoring quote?
faqs.answer: Because the cheque is rate multiplied by hours, and providers publish only the first half. A tutor at AED 150 who needs thirty-two hours costs AED 4,800; one at AED 270 who needs twelve costs AED 3,240 and finishes sooner. The number of hours depends on whether the gap is technique or content, whether the work set between sessions gets done, and how early you start. All three are knowable in advance, and the first can be read from one marked script, which is why a diagnosis is worth more than a rate card.

faqs.question: Which months of the two Diploma years cost an Ajman family the most?
faqs.answer: The first term of the second year, by a clear margin. Internally assessed components close while new content is still arriving, mocks follow, and predicted grades are set, so demand for specialist hours concentrates across every family at once. Published monthly estimates for weekly one-hour specialist support in an examination year reach AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above, against AED 600 to 1,200 mid-tier. The quiet months are the first term of the first year and the weeks after the papers, when the right spend is nothing at all.

faqs.question: An Ajman provider quoted us a monthly figure — how do I work out what the hour costs?
faqs.answer: Only once you have converted it. A monthly figure hides both session length and session count, which is where comparisons go wrong. An AED 799 monthly online package seen in this market covers eight sessions, roughly AED 100 each. In-home monthly figures of AED 1,599 to 1,799 cover four two-hour visits, which works out at AED 200 to 225 per teaching hour. Same market, very different arithmetic. Ask how many sessions, how long each one is, whether marking is included, and whether unused sessions carry forward before you compare anything.

faqs.question: Should a tutoring quote in Ajman include VAT, and how do I ask about it?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider directly whether their own quoted figure is inclusive, and ask for it in writing. This page deliberately does not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as a matter of fact, because doing so properly requires a Federal Tax Authority citation that nobody in this market supplies, and an unsourced tax statement on a price page is worse than silence. What is reasonable to expect is that any provider can tell you plainly whether the number they quoted is what leaves your account, and can produce a tax registration number if they hold one.

faqs.question: When in the two Diploma years does money work hardest?
faqs.answer: In the summer between the two years, and almost nobody spends it there. A content gap in a Higher Level subject takes dozens of teaching hours, and a weekly hour during term gets consumed by whatever is urgent that week, so the gap never closes while new material keeps landing on top of it. A fortnight of daily hours in a quiet period works through a syllabus in sequence instead of triaging. Families who do this usually spend less in total than those buying a weekly hour for eighteen months, and start the final year without the deficit.

faqs.question: Do IB tutors charge more than IGCSE tutors, and is that justified?
faqs.answer: They generally do, and the published figures show it: Unitors lists IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Part of that is content depth, since Higher Level subjects reach further than an IGCSE syllabus. Part is scarcity, especially in a small emirate where the pool of people who can mark a Higher Level science investigation against its criteria is thin. And part is the core, because Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay need process coaching that an IGCSE tutor has never had to give. The premium is real rather than invented.

faqs.question: Who pays for the tutor's marking time between sessions?
faqs.answer: Somebody always does, and the question is whether it is named. A tutor who reads the student's work for the first time during the session has been paid a specialist rate for silent reading, which makes their rate look competitive and their hours high. A tutor who marks before the hour has absorbed that preparation into the rate, so the rate looks dearer and the hours are fewer. Over a term the second is usually cheaper and always more useful. Ask whether marking is included and whether it happens before the session or inside it.

faqs.question: What happens to the fee if we cancel a session during exam leave?
faqs.answer: Agree this before the second lesson, because the answer differs sharply by format. A cancelled online session costs a tutor one empty hour, so notice terms are usually looser. A cancelled visit costs them the hour plus the journey, which is why in-home cancellation terms are tighter and why a family that moves sessions around a school calendar pays for the flexibility. Settle three things in writing: the notice period, whether a missed session can be moved rather than forfeited, and what happens to a block during an extended school break.

faqs.question: Is a group class in Ajman worth the saving over one-to-one?
faqs.answer: It buys a different product rather than a cheaper version of the same one. At the AED 33 to 65 per-head band published by Tutopiya and EdFlik in October 2026, a group block delivers broad syllabus coverage and a cohort to pace against, which suits a student behind on content across a whole subject. What it cannot do is diagnose one student's specific loss pattern. If you do not yet know why the grade is stuck, buy the diagnosis first; coverage without diagnosis usually repeats material the student already had.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to our villa in Ajman, and what would that cost instead?
faqs.answer: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. Everything for an Ajman family runs one-to-one over live video at times set in Gulf Standard Time. The in-home market genuinely exists and is priced on this page so you can weigh it fairly: AED 180 to 350 an hour in the 2026 survey, AED 200 to 500 for independents once travel is inside the rate, usually with a two-hour minimum. The one thing it buys that a screen cannot is an adult in the room, which matters when supervision is the real need.

faqs.question: How many hours should we budget for one Higher Level subject across both years?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether the gap is technique or content, and the diagnosis is cheap compared with guessing. Technique repairs — command terms, written method, closing an evaluative answer — are typically weeks of marked practice rather than months, so a short block plus maintenance can be enough. A missing third of a Higher Level syllabus is dozens of teaching hours and is best bought concentrated rather than weekly. Ask for the component-level marks behind the current prediction; they convert a vague worry about the subject into a countable list of movable marks.

faqs.question: Does a higher hourly rate mean a stronger IB tutor?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, and the market gives you reasons to be careful in both directions. At the top end, BartyED publishes AED 650 for premium named tutoring, and a rate at that level is a claim about scarcity rather than a proof of effectiveness. At the bottom, AED 33 to 52 generally buys group teaching or a university student rather than specialist one-to-one. What correlates with movement is far more mundane: who marks the work, against what, how quickly it comes back, and whether the plan for the next three weeks is specific enough to be proved wrong.

faqs.question: What should an Ajman family refuse to pay for at any price?
faqs.answer: Finished coursework. One operator researched in this market advertises completed internal assessments at a four-figure sum, and buying that moves the entire risk onto your child: awarding bodies treat authorship breaches as malpractice, penalties can reach a whole entry rather than one component, and the student confirms the work is their own at submission. Also refuse to pay a premium for a claimed regulator endorsement. No platform in this market holds approval from the International Baccalaureate, the Ministry of Education or an emirate authority, and IB Gram claims none.

faqs.question: Can we try one lesson before committing to any monthly spend?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is how it is designed to work. The first lesson is a free diagnostic, no payment is taken beforehand, and there is no obligation to continue afterwards. What you receive from it is a written diagnosis: which loss patterns are present in the student's own marked work, which are weeks of work and which are a term, and what the first three weeks would target. If the honest answer is that the school's own support, a different subject or nothing at all is the better purchase, you will be told at that point rather than later.

intro.heading: Two curricula, one budget: where the money actually goes
paragraphs: The household this page is written for has two education bills running in parallel and no clean way to compare them. An IGCSE child needs subject support with a two-year horizon and a published exam series at the end. A Diploma child needs subject support plus coursework supervision plus a route decision in mathematics, across a programme that is longer, heavier and priced differently. Treating them as one line item called tutoring is how a family ends up spending evenly and solving nothing.

Start with the published rates, because the gap between the programmes is real and it is not arbitrary. Unitors publishes IGCSE support from AED 150 an hour and IB support from AED 200. Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts an IB, IGCSE or A-Level specialist at AED 200 to 450 and upwards, with an in-home one-to-one visit at AED 180 to 500 including travel. TutorChase publishes AED 270 and BartyED AED 650. At the lower end, EdFlik lists from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, which are different products rather than bargains for the same thing.

The Diploma premium has three components and only one of them is prestige. The first is syllabus breadth: a DP subject tutor has to hold both the content and the assessment architecture, including how the Internal Assessment is marked against lettered criteria. The second is scarcity, which in Ajman and the northern emirates is severe for Diploma subjects, because the schools offering the Diploma are fewer and the teachers attached to them fewer still. The third is coursework supervision, which is slow, individual work that cannot be delivered to a group at any price.

There is a cost most households miss entirely until it arrives: the transition. A student finishing IGCSE and starting the Diploma is not continuing; they are changing the assessment model, the expected independence and the volume of written work at the same time. The gap between a strong IGCSE grade and a comfortable first DP term is usually weeks of specific work rather than months, and it is far cheaper handled in July and August than repaired in November, which is when most families first see it.

One point to settle before any budgeting. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in Ajman, and home visits are a service offered only in India. For a two-curriculum household that removes the hardest scheduling problem in the whole arrangement, because two children needing different specialists on the same evening cannot both be served by somebody driving. Everything that follows is arithmetic you can check, built from rates other providers have published and attributed to them by name.

Funding is best concentrated on one to three subjects at a time rather than spread across nine, with the selection rotating as error logs close. Mathematics usually comes first because it underpins the sciences, and the second subject should be chosen from mock evidence.
programmes.countryNote: Across Ajman the IGCSE tutor pool is deepest in Mathematics and English and thinnest in Additional Mathematics 0606 and Computer Science 0478. That matters for budgeting: the scarce components carry a premium, so a plan that needs one of them should be costed differently from one that needs 0580.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme, final years
programmes.description: Assessed against criteria rather than against papers, which produces students who reason well and have never sat a timed terminal examination. The Personal Project adds a supervised independent task. Support here is mostly about building examination stamina and the habit of writing to a criterion before the Diploma demands both at once.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman families whose child is in MYP at a school in Dubai or Sharjah often arrive assuming the move into DP is a continuation. It is a change of assessment model. The useful spend is a short block in the final MYP year on timed writing and on reading a criterion descriptor, which is cheap and prevents an expensive first DP term.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment marked against lettered criteria with published mark allocations. The programme is two years long and the spending curve is not flat: the second year costs far more than the first.
programmes.countryNote: The Diploma tutor pool in the northern emirates is genuinely thin, because the schools running DP are concentrated in Dubai and Abu Dhabi and the teachers with marking experience are attached to them. For an Ajman household this is the clearest case where delivery over video is not a preference but the only route to a Higher Level specialist.

programmes.name: IGCSE or MYP into the Diploma
programmes.description: The cheapest high-value block on this list and the one most often skipped. Three to six weeks of specific work over the summer on the subjects where the entry point sits above the IGCSE exit point, plus the independence habits the Diploma assumes: reading a syllabus, planning a written response without a scaffold, and meeting an internal deadline nobody chases.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman students moving into sixth form frequently change school and emirate at once, adding a longer commute and a new deadline culture to an already steep term. Doing the bridging work in July and August, while the family is still on an Ajman summer schedule, removes one variable from a transition that already has several.

ajman/ib-igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones Ajman households fund across both curricula. For each, the note is about where the cost actually sits rather than about the content, because the content is not what makes one subject more expensive to support than another.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches (IB DP)
subjects.description: The most expensive subject to support in the Diploma and the most commonly needed. HL carries Paper 3 and a proof-heavy content load, and the Internal Assessment exploration needs supervision that is slow and individual. Scarcity in the northern emirates is real, so this is where a budget gets tested first.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation (IB DP)
subjects.description: Cheaper to support at SL than AA SL in most cases, because the technology-led content suits a shorter session cycle. The route decision matters more than the rate though: some university programmes expect AA, and switching after the first term costs far more than getting the choice right.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The deepest pool and the most competitive rate across Ajman. A household funding both curricula should expect this to be the cheapest hour they buy, and should not use it as the benchmark for what a Diploma hour will cost.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: A scarcity premium at IGCSE level, and the single best preparation for Maths AA HL. Funding 0606 properly in Year 11 frequently reduces the Diploma mathematics bill in Year 12, which is the clearest example of sequencing paying for itself.

subjects.name: Physics (IB DP and Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: At Diploma level the Internal Assessment investigation is where supervision hours concentrate, and those hours price higher than teaching hours. At IGCSE the written practical component is the undertaught block. Two different problems, two different rates, one subject name.

subjects.name: Chemistry (IB DP and Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Diploma HL chemistry is among the most requested and least available subjects in the northern emirates. Expect the upper end of the published specialist band, and expect the Internal Assessment block to be costed separately from weekly teaching.

subjects.name: Biology (IB DP and Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: Moderate rates at both levels. The Diploma Internal Assessment is the cost driver, since a well-scoped investigation takes several supervision sessions before any data exists. Scoping early is the cheapest intervention available in the subject.

subjects.name: Economics (IB DP and Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: At Diploma level the Internal Assessment commentaries are a discrete, datable block of work rather than an ongoing cost, which makes them easy to budget. The evaluation marks on Paper 1 and Paper 2 are where weekly teaching earns its keep.

subjects.name: Business Management (IB DP) and Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Reasonable supply at both levels. The Diploma HL research project is a supervision cost; the IGCSE case-study application is a teaching cost. Families regularly assume the two are interchangeable and budget one rate for both.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature (IB DP)
subjects.description: The Individual Oral and the Higher Level essay are the expensive components, because both need repeated feedback on the student's own drafts rather than content delivery. Fortnightly cycles work better than weekly ones here, which lowers the monthly figure.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Wide apparent supply, narrow real supply. The marking skill is band-referenced annotation of directed writing, and most of the local field cannot demonstrate it. Ask for a marked script with band references before accepting any rate.

subjects.name: Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Internal Assessment supervision
subjects.description: Priced as blocks rather than as weekly hours, because the work is episodic: scoping, then a draft, then feedback, then a redraft. Every session here is feedback on work the student has written. Nothing is supplied for submission, and the student signs an authentication statement to that effect.

ajman/ib-igcse-home-tutor.regionsIntro: For a household funding two curricula, what varies between Ajman communities is how many separate specialists the evening has to accommodate and what time the second child can realistically start.

regions.name: Al Nuaimiya
regions.note: Short school runs mean the first session can start by 6.30pm and a second child can follow at eight. The most workable part of the emirate for a two-child, two-curriculum evening.

regions.name: Al Rashidiya
regions.note: Two children in different schools on different curricula is the norm here rather than the exception. Sessions are staggered across different evenings instead of stacked, which spreads the monthly cost more evenly.

regions.name: Al Jurf
regions.note: Longer internal journeys compress the usable evening. Households here often fund one child intensively for a term and the other the term after, which is usually the right decision anyway.

regions.name: Al Mowaihat
regions.note: Villa households with Dubai and Sharjah commutes. The Diploma child's session normally takes the later slot, because Diploma work tolerates a late start better than Year 10 content does.

regions.name: Al Zahya and Al Tallah
regions.note: The communities most likely to be running an IGCSE child and a Diploma child at once, with access to Dubai and Sharjah schools. Also where the two-curriculum budget question comes up most often.

regions.name: Al Helio and Al Rawda
regions.note: Quiet by eight and close to the local school cluster, so two sessions on one evening is practical. That makes a concentrated month cheaper to arrange here than elsewhere.

regions.name: Ajman Corniche and Al Rumailah
regions.note: Apartment living where two children cannot both have a quiet room at once. The usual answer is one weekday evening each and weekend mornings for timed work.

regions.name: Emirates City and Al Alia
regions.note: The latest arrival times in Ajman, so a two-session evening rarely fits. Diploma supervision blocks are often moved to weekends here, which suits episodic coursework work well.

regions.name: Al Yasmeen and Al Zorah
regions.note: Space for two study areas and quiet evenings, which is the ideal setup for parallel sessions. The constraint is specialist availability rather than anything domestic.

regions.name: Masfout and Manama
regions.note: The inland exclaves, where no Diploma Higher Level specialist is reachable by car on any weekly basis. For these households the delivery format is not a preference at all.

sections.heading: Why a Diploma hour costs more than an IGCSE hour in this market
paragraphs: The gap is visible in the published figures. Unitors lists IGCSE support from AED 150 an hour and IB support from AED 200, which is a clean comparison because it is the same provider quoting both. Bestimate's rate table groups IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists together at AED 200 to 450 and upwards, with in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500 including travel. TutorChase publishes AED 270. At the top of the market BartyED lists AED 650. None of those are our prices; each is attributed to the provider that published it, researched in October 2026.

Three things drive the Diploma premium. Breadth is the first: a DP subject tutor needs the content, the paper structure, the Higher Level extensions and the Internal Assessment criteria, which are marked against lettered descriptors with published mark allocations. Teaching the content without being able to mark against those criteria leaves the coursework component untouched, and the coursework component is a substantial share of the subject grade.

Scarcity is the second and in Ajman it dominates. The schools running the Diploma in the UAE are concentrated in Dubai and Abu Dhabi, so the teachers with marking experience are attached to those schools and those cities. A twenty-minute evening radius from an Ajman address contains very few of them and frequently none for a Higher Level science. That scarcity is priced, and it is priced more steeply the further north you are.

The third is the nature of supervision. Coursework supervision is slow, individual and cannot be delivered to a group. A scoping conversation about a research question takes as long as it takes, and the value of it is entirely in the specificity. That work sits at the top of any sensible rate card, and it should be bought as a dated block rather than as an open weekly commitment.

sections.heading: One household, two curricula: a worked Ajman budget
paragraphs: Abstract bands are not a budget. So here is the arithmetic for a realistic Ajman household: one child in Year 11 on IGCSE carrying nine subjects, one child in Year 13 on the Diploma with three Higher Level subjects, both sitting terminal examinations in the same academic year. That is the hardest version of the problem and it is common in the Emirates Road communities.

The first discipline is to stop funding evenly. Two children do not have equal need in the same term, and splitting the money down the middle guarantees that neither gets enough to move anything. The Year 13 Diploma child has the shorter runway and the higher stakes, so the autumn money concentrates there, including a dated supervision block for whichever Internal Assessment is furthest behind. The Year 11 child gets one subject weekly, usually Mathematics, with a second added from mock evidence in the new year.

Apply the published monthly bands to that shape and the household figure becomes visible. A Higher Level Diploma subject at one to two sessions a week sits in the AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above band in an exam year. An IGCSE subject at one session a week sits at AED 600 to 1,200 in the mid band. Add a supervision block priced separately, and an exam-year household total in the region of AED 2,000 to 3,500 a month across both children is a realistic planning figure rather than a worst case.

The table works three household scenarios through to a monthly figure. The numbers are built from the published bands attributed earlier and from Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions, which run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. They are planning figures, not quotations.

sections.heading: The IGCSE to Diploma gap, subject by subject
paragraphs: One competitor page in the researched set has a single subheading on the IGCSE to IB gap. Nobody has a structured subject-by-subject version, which is odd, because it is the most predictable expense in the whole two-curriculum budget and the easiest to plan for.

The gap is not uniform. In mathematics it is large and specific: a student arriving at Maths AA HL from IGCSE 0580 Extended without 0606 is missing calculus fluency and proof technique, and will spend the first term catching up on both while new content arrives. In the sciences the gap is less about content and more about the investigation: a DP Internal Assessment demands a scoped research question, controlled variables and an uncertainty treatment that IGCSE never asked for. In English it is about independent critical argument rather than directed response.

The practical point is that these gaps have durations, and the durations are short if the work is done before term starts and long if it is done during term. Three to six focused sessions in July and August, at the IGCSE rather than the Diploma rate, routinely prevent a first-term deficit that then needs a year of Diploma-rate hours to clear. For an Ajman family also absorbing a new school and a longer commute, doing it in the summer is the only point at which the week has room in it.
The table maps the common routes. The weeks column is an honest typical range for a student who did reasonably well at IGCSE, not a promise, and a student who scraped the grade will need more.
