ajman/igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Four funding shapes cover nearly every Ajman enquiry. Which one you are buying changes the total far more than the hourly rate does, and most families only discover that halfway through.

programmes.name: Year 9 pre-IGCSE groundwork
programmes.description: The cheapest hour a family will ever buy, because it is bought before anything has gone wrong. Year 9 work is about algebraic fluency, scientific notation, data handling and writing in paragraphs, and it is usually fixed in a single term of fortnightly sessions rather than a weekly commitment. Funded here, the same outcome costs a fraction of the Year 11 version.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman schools make tier decisions for Mathematics and the sciences early in Year 10, and those decisions are made on Year 9 attainment. A family that spends modestly in Year 9 is often buying access to the Extended or Higher tier, which no amount of Year 11 spending can retroactively open up once entries have closed.

programmes.name: The two-year Cambridge IGCSE run
programmes.description: Weekly or fortnightly support across one to three subjects for the full two years. This is the largest single education purchase most families make outside school fees, and it is the one most often bought without a budget. The sensible structure is a small number of subjects funded properly rather than every subject funded thinly, because an hour spread across four papers teaches nobody anything.
programmes.countryNote: Across the two years, Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Multiply by twenty-two months of term time and the two-year figure is a number worth looking at before the first session, not after the twentieth.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes run 4MA1 for Mathematics A, 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 for the sciences, 4EA1 for English Language A. Tiering is Foundation and Higher. Practical understanding is examined inside the written papers rather than in a separate component, which slightly narrows what tutoring needs to cover and occasionally narrows the fee with it.
programmes.countryNote: Edexcel's November series is the quietly useful one for an Ajman budget. A single weak subject can be re-sat in November without repeating a year, which converts what would have been a full extra year of fees into a dated block of sessions. The entry window closes months earlier, so the saving is only available to families who plan in the autumn.

programmes.name: Single-subject re-entry and resits
programmes.description: The narrowest and most cost-efficient purchase on this list: one paper, one error log, a fixed number of sessions, a stated finish date. Because the content was covered once already, the work is almost entirely technique and timing, and technique moves faster than content. Open-ended arrangements make no sense here and should be refused.
programmes.countryNote: A resit candidate in Ajman normally sits as a private candidate through an approved centre, and centres set their own administrative charges on top of the board's entry fee. Ask the centre for the full figure in writing before planning the tutoring budget, because that cost lands in the same month as the sessions.

ajman/igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Rates are not uniform across subjects. The driver is scarcity of people who can mark the paper, not difficulty of the content, and the two are often unrelated. Here is where the premium sits in the Ajman market and why.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The deepest supply pool in the emirate, so the most competitive rate. Expect to find qualified maths tutors across the whole published band rather than only at the top, and expect a wide quality spread at the lower end. The price signal here is weak; ask for marked evidence instead.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: A genuine scarcity premium. Few tutors in the northern emirates teach 0606 regularly, and those who do often sit at the specialist end of the band. If a quote for 0606 comes in at a budget rate, the likely explanation is that the tutor has not taught the syllabus rather than that you found a bargain.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Mid to upper band. The written practical component on the Cambridge route narrows the pool further, because teaching it needs familiarity with how experimental skills are examined on paper. Tutors who can do that part credibly price accordingly, and it is usually worth it.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Similar to physics, with the organic pathways and electrolysis content concentrating demand in the months before the series. Rates on chemistry visibly firm up in the spring term, which is one of the few places where seasonality genuinely shows in a quote.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Broad supply, moderate rate. The risk is paying a general science tutor a biology rate: the extended-response marking in biology is a specific skill, and a tutor who cannot show marked examples of it is being paid for the subject label rather than the capability.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Rates vary more than any other subject, because almost anyone can present as an English tutor and very few can mark directed writing against the published bands. The useful filter is a marked sample with band references on it, and that filter removes most of the lower end of the market.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Widely available at mid-band rates across Ajman and Sharjah. The pitfall is being sold 0500 technique at a 0510 price, or the reverse. The two are assessed on different criteria and confirming which code your child is entered for is the single cheapest thing you can do before agreeing a rate.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Competitive rates, thin specialist depth. Many tutors can teach the content and fewer can train case-study application, which is where the grade is decided. Ask for a marked extended answer showing where the application and evaluation marks were awarded before you accept a rate at the upper end.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Upper-mid band, with scarcity driven by diagram marking. A tutor who corrects axes, titles and shift arrows on a student's own diagram is doing the job; one who presents finished diagrams is not, and that distinction is worth more than a hundred dirhams an hour of nominal seniority.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: The clearest scarcity premium after 0606. Paper 2 algorithm design and pseudocode tracing needs a tutor who has marked it, and that pool is small in the northern emirates. Online delivery widens the pool enormously, which is where the price advantage of video becomes concrete rather than theoretical.

subjects.name: Accounting (Cambridge 0452)
subjects.description: Mid band, with a short seasonal spike. Format discipline carries most of the marks, so sessions are heavy on timed practice and light on explanation, which means fewer total hours are usually needed than families budget for. That is a saving worth taking.

subjects.name: Geography (Cambridge 0460)
subjects.description: Lower-mid band and broadly available. Case-study specificity is what moves marks, and building it is more about structured recall work between sessions than about hours in the session, so a fortnightly arrangement often delivers the same result as a weekly one at half the cost.

sections.heading: What the Ajman and northern-emirates market charges for IGCSE tuition
paragraphs: An IGCSE hour in the UAE is sold at between roughly AED 45 and AED 650, and the first job of this section is to show you which band you are being quoted from. The bands are real and the boundaries between them are about who the tutor is rather than what they teach. A university student revising alongside your child is a different product from a teacher who has marked the paper, and both are legitimate purchases at the right price for the right problem.

Every figure in the table is attributed to the provider that published it, with the date of the research. That is not a formality. Three of the six strongest-ranking pages in this search publish no price whatsoever, and one of them asks the price question in its own FAQ and then declines to answer it. A sourced number is checkable; an unsourced one is marketing. If a provider will not tell you which band they sit in before a call, you already know something useful.

Read the band against the problem rather than against your budget. A Year 9 fluency gap in algebra is genuinely well served at the lower end, because what is needed is supervised practice and someone to notice when a method is wrong. A Year 11 student losing evaluation marks on Economics 0455 extended questions is not, because the person at that rate has probably never marked one. Paying specialist money for a fluency problem is as wasteful as paying budget money for a marking problem, and families do both.

One structural point about the in-home band. The AED 180 to 500 range for a one-to-one visit includes travel, and travel is not a service. It is a cost that has to be covered before any teaching happens, and in Ajman, where most subject specialists live in Sharjah or Dubai, it is a large one.

sections.heading: Eight things that move the number on an IGCSE quote
paragraphs: Once you know the bands, the useful question is what pushes a specific quote up or down inside them. There are eight common variables and they are not equally important. Subject scarcity and delivery format do most of the work; session length and payment terms do almost none, despite being the two things families negotiate hardest.

Scarcity is the big one and it is counter-intuitive. Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 and Computer Science 0478 cost more in the northern emirates than Physics 0625 does, not because they are harder but because fewer people in reachable distance have marked them. That is precisely the premium that disappears when delivery stops depending on reachable distance, which is the single strongest financial argument for video in a market like Ajman.

Timing is the second. Chemistry and Mathematics rates visibly firm up in the spring term as the June series approaches, and a family that starts in October is buying at a different price from a family that starts in March. The honest version of this is not that providers raise prices opportunistically; it is that the available specialists fill their evenings, and what is left is priced as scarcity. Starting early is a discount nobody advertises.

sections.heading: The travel line nobody itemises, and what it costs an Ajman household
paragraphs: In-home quotes in the UAE are almost always presented as a single hourly figure with travel folded in, which conceals the most interesting number in the whole arrangement. Work it out and the picture changes. A specialist based in Sharjah coming to Al Mowaihat for a one-hour session is committing somewhere around ninety minutes to two hours of total time in the evening peak. The teaching is one hour of that. The rest is a cost the family pays for without receiving anything.

That is why the in-home band sits at AED 180 to 500 while the same tutor delivering online sits at AED 150 to 300. The gap is not a premium for presence; it is a reimbursement for a drive. And the gap is wider in Ajman than in central Dubai, because the specialist pool is further away. A household in Masfout or Manama cannot buy the service at all on a weekly basis, at any price, because there is no rate at which a twice-weekly inland round trip is rational for a tutor.

There is a second, less visible cost: the session gets worse. A tutor arriving at 7.15pm after fifty minutes on Emirates Road is not at their best, and a student who has been told to wait at home rather than get on with homework has lost the same fifty minutes. Whatever the merits of face-to-face teaching in principle, the version being sold in this corridor is frequently a tired adult and a restless teenager at the end of a long drive.

None of this makes in-home tutoring a bad product. For a Year 7 child who needs supervision as much as instruction, for a student who genuinely cannot work on a screen, or where a local tutor happens to live three streets away and teaches the right paper, it can be exactly right. It is just rarely the right answer for an Ajman Year 11 student who needs a specialist on a specific component, and the honest reason is geography rather than ideology.

sections.heading: Monthly packages, and the arithmetic providers do not show you
paragraphs: Monthly packages are the normal way this market sells, and they are worth reading as arithmetic rather than as offers. The published shapes in the UAE include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Divide those out and the effective hourly rates are very different from the headline, which is the point of packaging.

Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions give a cleaner comparison: roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. A family funding two subjects at the specialist end during Year 11 is therefore looking at a four-figure monthly commitment, and that is a number to see in October rather than to discover in March.

The structural risk in a package is not the price. It is the incentive. A prepaid three-month block gives a provider a reason to keep delivering sessions after the problem has been fixed, and gives the family a reason to keep attending in order not to waste the money. Both reasons are bad. A monthly arrangement with a written review at week six creates the opposite pressure, which is why that is how this works here, and why there is no joining fee or prepaid term to recover.

sections.heading: Two years, nine subjects: a worked IGCSE budget for one Ajman child
paragraphs: Families budget per hour and spend per year, which is how a modest-sounding rate becomes a surprising annual figure. Work the whole thing through once, in advance, and most of the stress comes out of it. Take a typical Ajman student carrying nine IGCSE subjects across Years 10 and 11, roughly twenty-two months of term time once holidays are removed.

Nobody funds nine subjects and nobody should try. The realistic shape is one to three subjects supported at any one time, with the selection changing as error logs close. A workable plan looks like this: Year 10 carries one subject weekly, usually Mathematics, because it underpins the sciences. Year 11 autumn adds a second, chosen from the mock results. The spring term before the series runs two subjects with a dated intensive on the weakest paper. Total funded subject-months across the two years come to somewhere between twenty-five and forty, not one hundred and ninety-eight.

Apply the published monthly bands to that and the arithmetic is tractable. Thirty funded subject-months at the mid band of AED 600 to 1,200 is a two-year total in the region of AED 18,000 to 36,000, and the same plan at the budget band is materially less while buying materially less. An in-home version of the same plan costs more because of the travel component, and in Ajman specifically it also costs availability, since the specialist for the weakest paper may simply not be drivable.

The number worth writing down is the one per recovered mark rather than per hour, and it cannot be calculated in advance. What can be done is to spend the first six weeks establishing whether this is a technique problem or a content problem, because the two have completely different durations and therefore completely different totals. That is exactly what the free first lesson and the week-six review exist to establish, before the big number is committed.

sections.heading: Why this is delivered over video, and what that does to the bill
paragraphs: IB Gram delivers UAE tuition one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE; those are offered only in India. That is stated here rather than buried, because the phrase you searched for was a home tutor and you are entitled to know exactly what is on offer before you read another word about price.

The financial effect is straightforward. Removing the drive removes the component that pushes the in-home band to AED 180-500 and keeps the online band at AED 150-300. More importantly for Ajman, it removes distance as a constraint on who can teach your child. The 0606 specialist, the 0478 algorithm marker, the person who has actually marked Cambridge written practical papers: none of them need to be within forty minutes of Al Rawda. That is not a cost saving dressed up as a benefit. It is the reason the saving exists.

The trade-offs are real and worth naming. A screen is worse for a young child who needs an adult physically present to stay on task. It needs a stable connection and a quiet room, which is harder in a shared Corniche apartment than in a Zorah villa. It requires a tablet or laptop and, for maths and sciences, ideally a writing surface the tutor can see. Where those conditions cannot be met, in-home tuition from a local provider is the better purchase and we will say so rather than sell around it.

What video does not compromise is the evidence. Marking happens on a shared screen in front of the student, scripts are saved rather than left in a notebook, and the raw-mark log is a document a parent can open at any time. An in-home session in a kitchen produces none of that unless the tutor chooses to build it, and most do not.

sections.heading: Tutoring in the context of the rest of the education bill
paragraphs: A tutoring figure means little in isolation. It sits alongside school fees, transport, exam entry and the various administrative charges that arrive in the same months, and the only sensible way to judge it is against that whole bill. For families in the northern emirates with a child enrolled in Dubai, there is useful public context: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total.

Scale is worth knowing too. Dubai's private school sector in 2024-25 held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen different curricula, with the UK curriculum accounting for 37% of enrolment, Indian 26%, American 14% and the International Baccalaureate 7%. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. That is the market Ajman families are competing in for sixth-form places, and it is why IGCSE grades carry weight beyond the certificate itself.

Exam costs belong in the budget and cannot be stated here, because they are set by the board and by the centre rather than by us, and a private candidate's administrative charge varies between centres. Ask the school exams officer, or the approved centre if your child is sitting privately, for the full figure in writing. It lands in the same month as the heaviest tutoring and families are regularly caught by that overlap.

The last item is the one nobody budgets: repeating a year. An extra year of private school fees dwarfs any plausible tutoring spend, which is the honest commercial case for funding a weak subject properly in Year 10 rather than hoping. It is also the case for the November re-entry route, which converts a lost year into a dated block of sessions.

sections.heading: Ten questions to ask before you accept an IGCSE quote
paragraphs: A quote is a document you are allowed to interrogate, and in this market the answers are more informative than the number. Ten questions cover almost everything, and three of them tend to end conversations quickly.

Ask which band the rate sits in and why. Ask which syllabus code and component the tutor has marked, and for a redacted sample of that marking. Ask whether travel is included and how long the journey to your area takes, because an honest answer tells you whether the rate is sustainable or will quietly rise. Ask what happens if you cancel after one session. Ask whether the figure includes VAT; providers should be able to state the position on their own pricing in writing, and nobody should be inventing a general tax ruling for you. Ask who is actually delivering the session, because agencies sometimes quote at a specialist rate and allocate at a general one.

Then the three uncomfortable ones. Ask for the circumstances in which they would recommend stopping. Ask what evidence you will receive and when. And ask whether they are promising an outcome, because any answer that commits to a specific grade or an improvement figure is a reason to end the conversation: no tutor can commit to a mark on a results slip, and offering to is either a misunderstanding of the examination or a deliberate one.

One Ajman-specific check. The UAE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and administered by MoHRE, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee. A quote that itemises a licensing or permit cost is charging you for something that is free. That is a small amount of money and a large amount of information about who you are dealing with.
bullets: Which band is this rate, and which component has the tutor actually marked?
Is travel included, and how long is the journey to my area in the evening?
What evidence will I receive after each session, and when?
Under what circumstances would you tell me to stop paying?

process.title: Say what you are solving
process.description: Send the subject list with syllabus codes from the school's entry statement, the tier your child sits in, and what the last report or mock said. A rate quoted without that information is a guess, and guessed rates are the ones that move after a month.

process.title: Take the free hour
process.description: One full session at no cost, spent on a past-paper question set. It produces a marked script and a written view of whether this is a three-week technique problem or a term-long content problem. Those two have very different totals, and you should know which you are funding.

process.title: Price the plan, not the hour
process.description: Work out how many subject-months you are actually buying across the rest of Year 10 and Year 11, then apply a monthly band to it. Most families discover the plan is smaller and the total larger than they assumed, which is a better thing to discover in October than in March.

process.title: Start monthly, review at six weeks
process.description: Billed monthly with no joining fee and no prepaid term. At week six you receive a written review with a recommendation that may be to change subject focus or to stop. Reschedules inside the month are not charged, because Ajman evening traffic is not something you control.

process.title: Add a second subject only on evidence
process.description: A second subject is added when the first one's error tally is visibly closing, not when the term starts. Funding two subjects thinly from the outset is the most common way an IGCSE budget gets spent without a grade moving.

whyPoints.title: Figures with a source attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED number on this page names the provider that published it and the month it was researched. Three of the strongest pages in this search publish no price at all, and one asks the price question in its own FAQ and then declines to answer it.

whyPoints.title: No travel in the quote
whyPoints.description: Sessions run over live video, so nothing in the price is paying for a car on Emirates Road. In Ajman, where most subject specialists are based in Sharjah or Dubai, that is the largest single component removed from an in-home rate.

whyPoints.title: Specialists regardless of distance
whyPoints.description: A household in Masfout or Al Mowaihat reaches the same 0606 or 0478 specialist as one in Al Nuaimiya. Distance stops being a filter on who can teach your child, which is where the real value of video delivery sits.

whyPoints.title: Monthly, with a reason to stop
whyPoints.description: No joining fee, no prepaid block and a written review at week six that can recommend stopping. Prepaid packages create an incentive to keep teaching after the problem is solved; monthly billing creates the opposite one.

whyPoints.title: Market rates, not our price list
whyPoints.description: The bands here describe what the UAE market charges, attributed to their sources. For what a specific plan would cost, the free first lesson and the follow-up conversation give you a figure based on your child's actual papers rather than a tariff.

whyPoints.title: Nothing promised about grades
whyPoints.description: No session, block or intensive carries a promised grade, score or improvement figure. What is committed to is the evidence, the review dates and an honest recommendation, including the recommendation that a tutor is the wrong purchase.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE home tutor in Ajman charge per hour in 2026?
faqs.answer: Across the UAE market, an in-home one-to-one visit with travel included is published at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table at AED 180 to 350 and home-tutor listings at AED 200 to 500. In Ajman the figure tends to sit in the upper part of that band for anything specialist, because most subject specialists are based in Sharjah or Dubai and the quote has to cover the drive. The same teaching delivered over live video is published at AED 150 to 300. Those are market figures, attributed to their sources, not a price list.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home rate in Ajman higher than the same tutor online?
faqs.answer: Because you are paying for a journey as well as a lesson. A specialist travelling from Sharjah to Al Mowaihat for a one-hour evening session commits roughly ninety minutes to two hours in total, of which only one hour is teaching. That unpaid time has to be recovered somewhere, and it is recovered in the hourly rate. The published gap between the AED 180 to 500 in-home band and the AED 150 to 300 online band is largely that recovery. In Ajman the gap widens, because the specialist pool sits further away than it does in central Dubai.

faqs.question: Is a monthly IGCSE package cheaper than paying session by session?
faqs.answer: Slightly, and the saving is usually smaller than the risk. Published UAE packages include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, which work out at roughly AED 100 and AED 200 to 225 an hour respectively. The discount against a per-session rate is real but modest. The problem is the incentive: a prepaid block gives a provider a reason to keep delivering sessions after the problem is fixed, and gives you a reason to keep attending so the money is not wasted. Monthly billing with a review avoids both.

faqs.question: Should I be paying for a tutor's travel time to Al Mowaihat?
faqs.answer: If someone is driving to Al Mowaihat in the evening peak, then yes, somebody has to pay for it, and pretending otherwise just means the rate rises later. The honest question is whether you want to buy it at all. For a Year 7 child who needs an adult present, it can be worth every dirham. For a Year 11 student who needs a specialist on Cambridge 0606 or a written practical paper, you are paying a large travel premium for a smaller pool of available tutors. Over live video the travel line disappears and the pool stops depending on distance.

faqs.question: How much should two years of IGCSE support cost for one child?
faqs.answer: Work it in subject-months rather than hours. A realistic plan across Years 10 and 11 funds one to three subjects at a time, totalling roughly 25 to 40 funded subject-months rather than every subject for twenty-two months. At Bestimate's mid monthly band of AED 600 to 1,200 for weekly one-hour sessions, thirty subject-months lands somewhere around AED 18,000 to 36,000 across the two years. The budget band is materially less and buys materially less. The exam-year specialist band of AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above per month moves the total upwards sharply.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE tutor charge more for Physics than for Business Studies?
faqs.answer: Usually a little, but the bigger gaps are elsewhere. The driver is scarcity of people who have marked the component, not difficulty of the subject. In the northern emirates, Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 and Computer Science 0478 carry the clearest premiums, because very few reachable tutors teach them regularly. Physics 0625 sits mid to upper band partly because of the written practical component. Business Studies 0450 looks competitive on price but has thin specialist depth, so the risk there is paying a fair rate to someone who cannot train case-study application.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates in Ajman climb as the June series gets closer?
faqs.answer: Effectively yes, and not because providers raise prices opportunistically. Specialist evening slots fill through the spring term, so a family starting in March is choosing from what is left rather than from the whole pool, and what is left prices as scarcity. Chemistry and Mathematics show this most visibly. The practical consequence is that starting in October is a discount nobody advertises: the same tutor at the same nominal rate, chosen from a wider set, with more weeks to work with. Late starts cost more and deliver less for structural reasons rather than commercial ones.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper university-student tutor a false economy at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Not always. For a Year 9 or early Year 10 fluency problem, where the need is supervised practice and someone to notice a wrong method early, the budget band of AED 45 to 150 is a sensible purchase and the alternative is overpaying. It becomes a false economy at the point where the problem is mark-scheme technique on a specific component. Somebody who has not marked Economics 0455 extended responses cannot teach the evaluation marks, however well they understand economics. Match the band to the problem rather than to the budget, and expect to change band as the problem changes.

faqs.question: Are IGCSE tutoring fees in the UAE subject to VAT?
faqs.answer: That depends on the provider's own tax position, and this page will not state a general ruling for you. What any provider should be able to do is tell you in writing whether their quoted figure includes VAT, and show a tax registration number if they hold one. If a quote is silent on the point, ask before you agree it, because the difference is material on a four-figure monthly commitment. For the treatment of education services in general, the Federal Tax Authority's own guidance is the only source worth relying on, not a tutoring company's summary of it.

faqs.question: Should a tutor's quote include a charge for the MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: No, and if it does, that is useful information. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page for private tutor licensing lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. A quote itemising a permit cost is charging you for something that costs nothing.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects can one Ajman family realistically fund?
faqs.answer: One to three at any given time, and fewer than families expect. The failure pattern is funding four subjects thinly, where each gets a fortnightly half-hour of attention, nothing closes, and a year's budget is spent without a grade moving. The alternative is to fund one subject properly until its error tally is visibly closing, then rotate the money to the next. Mathematics is usually first, because it underpins the sciences. The second subject should be chosen from mock results rather than from a feeling about which teacher your child dislikes.

faqs.question: What is a fair price for a 90-minute IGCSE session in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Take the hourly band the tutor sits in and expect a small discount per hour for the longer slot, because setup and settling time is amortised across more teaching. A qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300 an hour should therefore price ninety minutes somewhat below one and a half times the hourly figure. The ninety-minute slot is worth buying where a full structured paper is being worked through, since a 60-minute session cannot contain an attempt and its marking. For technique drills, two shorter sessions usually beat one long one.

faqs.question: Do two siblings sharing one IGCSE session halve the cost?
faqs.answer: The cost per child falls, and so does the attention per child, in roughly the same proportion. It works where both children are on the same board, the same subject and a similar level, which in practice means twins or a tight year gap. It works badly where one is sitting Cambridge 0580 and the other Edexcel 4MA1, because the papers and mark schemes differ and the session becomes two half-sessions. Two separate marked records still have to come out of it. Tell us both sets of codes and we will say honestly whether one session fits.

faqs.question: Who pays the IGCSE exam entry fee for a private candidate in the UAE?
faqs.answer: The family does, through the approved centre that enters the candidate, and the total has two parts: the board's entry fee for each syllabus and the centre's own administrative charge. Centres set the second part themselves, so the figure varies and no honest page can quote it for you. Ask the centre for the full amount in writing before you build a tutoring budget, because entry money and the heaviest tutoring month usually arrive together. Entry deadlines also sit months ahead of the papers, so this is an autumn conversation rather than a spring one.

faqs.question: What does the first month of IGCSE tutoring in Ajman actually cost?
faqs.answer: The first lesson costs nothing. After that, a single subject at one session a week sits inside the published monthly bands: roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, on Bestimate's estimates. There is no joining fee and no prepaid term, so the first month is also the smallest commitment available. What you should have at the end of it is four marked scripts, an error tally and enough information to decide whether month two is worth buying.

ajman/igcse-home-tutor.closingHeading: Get a figure based on your child's actual papers
ajman/igcse-home-tutor.closingBody: The bands on this page describe the UAE market with sources attached. What a specific plan costs depends on which subjects, which codes and how many months, and that is a short conversation rather than a tariff. Start with the free first lesson: one full session on a past-paper question set, a marked script at the end of it, and a written view of whether you are funding a three-week technique fix or a term of content. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, billed monthly, with no joining fee and nothing prepaid.

ajman/igcse-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach over live video and name the boards and components they mark. For any science subject, ask specifically whether they have marked the written practical paper, because that is a separate skill from teaching the science and it is the one most often assumed.

intro.heading: Why a saved record is the real argument for teaching IGCSE over video
paragraphs: The debate about online tutoring is usually conducted at the wrong level. People argue about presence and rapport, which are genuine but unmeasurable, and ignore the thing that is measurable: what exists after the hour ends. A video session with a shared screen and a digital annotation tool produces a document. A session at a kitchen table in Al Rawda produces a used notebook and a verbal summary at the door. Six months later, one of those is still readable and one of them is not.

For an IGCSE student that difference compounds. The whole discipline of examination technique is pattern recognition across repeated attempts: the same unit dropped, the same compare question answered as two unrelated paragraphs, the same calculation finished without its final accuracy mark. Nobody can see a pattern across fourteen sessions from memory. You can see it immediately in a log that tallies error types, and the student can see it too, which is the part that actually changes behaviour in a fifteen-year-old.

There is a second structural advantage in Ajman specifically, and it is about who is available rather than how the lesson runs. A student in Al Zorah or Masfout who needs Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 or Computer Science 0478 is unlikely to find that specialist within a drivable evening radius. Over video, distance stops being the filter. The constraint becomes whether the tutor has marked the component, which is the right constraint, and the one that a family can actually check.

The honest counterweight needs stating early. A screen is worse for a younger child who needs an adult in the room to stay on task at all. It needs a quiet space and a connection that holds through the evening, which is harder in a shared Corniche apartment than in a villa. It needs a way for the tutor to see handwritten working, because maths and physics cannot be taught by talking. Where those conditions cannot be met, in-home tuition from a local provider is the better purchase, and we would rather say that than sell around it. Those four conditions are worth checking before the first session rather than after the third, because every one of them is cheap to fix in advance and expensive to discover in week three, when a month has gone and nothing has been produced.

What IB Gram offers in the UAE is one-to-one tuition over live video on Gulf Standard Time. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE; those exist only in India. Nothing here involves a promised grade either. What is committed to is the record, the review dates and an honest recommendation at week six, including a recommendation to stop if the evidence says the problem is not one a tutor can fix.

ajman/igcse-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Four IGCSE routes come up repeatedly from Ajman households, and each one changes what a video session needs to be capable of. The science routes differ most, because they examine practical skill in two different places.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE sciences with a written practical paper
programmes.description: Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 each examine experimental skills through a written component rather than a laboratory assessment on the alternative route. The skill being tested is reading an experimental description, handling and plotting data, identifying sources of error and writing precise observations. All of that is taught from past papers and data sets.
programmes.countryNote: This is the single best case for video delivery in the whole IGCSE suite, because there is no apparatus involved on either side. An Ajman student with a laptop and a graph-paper notebook is working with exactly the same material as a student in a laboratory would be for that paper, and the tutor can annotate the data table live.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences
programmes.description: Physics 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1 and Biology 4BI1 examine practical understanding inside the main written papers rather than in a separate component. Questions describe an experiment and ask the candidate to interpret, evaluate or improve it, so the technique is embedded rather than isolated. Structured calculations run longer with more carried-forward steps.
programmes.countryNote: For a family comparing providers in Ajman, the useful question is whether the tutor knows which of these two models their child sits. Preparing Cambridge written-practical technique for an Edexcel candidate produces practice that feels productive and prepares for a paper that will not be set.

programmes.name: Mathematics and Additional Mathematics
programmes.description: Cambridge 0580 and 0606, Edexcel 4MA1 and 4MB1. These need a visible writing surface more than any other subject, because the marks live in the method rather than the answer. A tablet with a stylus, a document camera or simply a phone on a stand pointed at paper all work; a webcam pointed at a face does not.
programmes.countryNote: Additional Mathematics 0606 is where video delivery earns its keep in the northern emirates. The pool of tutors who teach it regularly is small and concentrated towards Dubai, so a student in Al Helio or Emirates City reaching one at all generally means reaching them over a screen.

programmes.name: English, humanities and the written subjects
programmes.description: English First Language 0500, English as a Second Language 0510 and 0511, Business Studies 0450, Economics 0455, Geography 0460. Here the artefact is a piece of writing with band-referenced annotation on it, and shared documents handle that better than paper does, because two people can be in the same draft at once.
programmes.countryNote: Written subjects benefit from the saved record more than any others, because improvement in writing is slow, cumulative and almost invisible week to week. Four annotated drafts side by side in April are the only honest way to show an Ajman family what changed since January.

ajman/igcse-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: For each subject below, the question that matters for a video session is what the tutor and student need to be able to see. Where that need is met, format stops mattering; where it is not, no amount of goodwill fixes it.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Needs the student's working visible in real time, not the final answer read aloud. A stylus tablet or a phone propped over paper solves it. With that in place, a tutor can stop a wrong method at the second line rather than after the student has committed to five minutes of it.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: The same visibility requirement, with higher stakes because proofs are graded on the derivation. Sessions are mostly the tutor watching the student write and intervening, which is why the writing surface is the whole technical requirement for this subject.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Circuit diagrams and free-body diagrams need annotation both ways. The written practical component on the Cambridge route is taught entirely from past papers and data tables, so the absence of a laboratory is not a limitation for that paper at all.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Mechanism arrows and electrolysis diagrams are drawn collaboratively on a shared canvas. Observation language for the alternative-to-practical paper is drilled from past-paper descriptions, which is exactly how the paper itself presents the experiment to the candidate.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The extended-response marking is the work, and it is text, so shared documents handle it cleanly. Data-handling questions are better over video than on paper, because the tutor can highlight the exact gridline the student should have read the figure from.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Two people editing the same draft is a genuine improvement over passing a sheet of paper back and forth. Band descriptors are pasted beside the paragraph being discussed, so the student sees which band the sentence they just wrote belongs to.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Reading tasks are screen-shared with the question and text side by side, which mirrors how the student will work in the hall. Task-fulfilment marking is noted directly on the draft, where the student can see which instruction was not addressed.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Case-study application is trained by highlighting the stimulus and the answer at the same time, which is awkward on paper and trivial on a screen. The repeated fault, a generic answer that ignores the case, becomes obvious when both documents are visible together.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagrams are drawn by the student on a shared canvas and corrected in place: axes labelled, curves titled, shifts given an arrow and a reason. Correcting the student's own diagram is the teaching; presenting a finished one is not.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: The best-suited subject on the list. Pseudocode is typed into a shared document and traced line by line in a trace table that both people fill in. Specialists who mark Paper 2 are thinly spread in the northern emirates, so video is usually the only route to one.

subjects.name: Geography (Cambridge 0460)
subjects.description: Map and graph skills work well on a shared screen, where the tutor can point at the exact contour or bar being misread. Case-study recall is built through structured tasks between sessions, which is where most of the gain actually comes from.

subjects.name: Accounting (Cambridge 0452)
subjects.description: Ledger format discipline is trained in a shared spreadsheet, with the student entering and the tutor correcting headings, dates and sides in real time. Timed practice is run with a visible clock, because speed is the real constraint on this paper.

ajman/igcse-online-tutor.regionsIntro: What changes between Ajman communities for an online session is connection stability, household noise and what time the house is quiet. Those three things decide the slot, and they vary more across the emirate than people expect.

regions.name: Al Nuaimiya
regions.note: Dense apartment blocks where evening bandwidth is shared and the living room is rarely empty. The practical fix is a 6.30pm slot before the household peaks, with the student on a wired connection if one is available.

regions.name: Al Rashidiya
regions.note: Mixed housing near the city core. Families with two children in sessions on the same evening are advised to stagger rather than overlap, because two video streams and a television is where a connection usually gives up.

regions.name: Al Jurf
regions.note: Varied connection quality depending on the block. Sessions here are built to survive a drop: the shared document holds the work, so a reconnection costs thirty seconds rather than the thread of the lesson.

regions.name: Al Mowaihat
regions.note: Villa households across Mowaihat 1, 2 and 3, usually with a study room and a stable line. The constraint is arrival time rather than bandwidth, since most parents here are coming back from Dubai or Sharjah.

regions.name: Al Zahya and Al Tallah
regions.note: Newer developments with newer infrastructure and generally the most reliable evening connections in the emirate. These households often run an IGCSE and an IB child on different evenings rather than the same one.

regions.name: Al Helio and Al Rawda
regions.note: Established residential streets, quiet by eight in the evening. Good for the longer ninety-minute slot that a full structured paper and its marking actually needs.

regions.name: Ajman Corniche and Al Rumailah
regions.note: Seafront apartments where noise rather than bandwidth is the problem. Timed paper attempts are moved to weekend mornings as standard, because a timed paper needs silence more than it needs a tutor.

regions.name: Emirates City and Al Alia
regions.note: Towers with variable in-building connectivity and the latest arrival times in Ajman. Sessions commonly start at 8pm or later, and a phone hotspot is kept as the fallback rather than as an emergency.

regions.name: Al Yasmeen and Al Zorah
regions.note: Low-density villas with quiet evenings and room for a dedicated desk. Also the clearest example of why video matters here: the specialist for a scarce component is never going to be a short drive away.

regions.name: Masfout and Manama
regions.note: The inland exclaves. Connection quality is the only question that matters, because there is no in-home alternative at any price and the whole arrangement depends on the line holding for an hour.

The annotated file is saved and sent the same evening.

sections.heading: What an online IGCSE session produces that a kitchen-table one does not
paragraphs: Start with the artefacts rather than the atmosphere. A video session with a shared screen, a shared document and a digital annotation layer generates a set of files as a by-product of how it works. The annotated script exists because the marking happened on screen. The error tally exists because the annotations are categorised. The raw-mark log exists because the marks were entered as they were awarded. None of that requires extra admin from the tutor, which is why it actually happens.

A session at a table produces the same teaching and almost none of the record. The marking lives in a notebook that goes back in a bag. The diagnosis lives in a two-minute conversation at the door, usually with whichever parent is home. The pattern across fourteen sessions lives nowhere at all. That is not a criticism of in-home tutors as teachers; it is an observation about what the format leaves behind, and it is the thing that matters most in March when somebody has to decide which topics get the last four weeks.

For a parent in Ajman who is driving back from Dubai during most sessions, the saved record is also the only way to be present. You cannot hover in a doorway at 7.30pm if you are on Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road. You can read four annotated scripts at eleven o'clock, and you can see in thirty seconds whether the same error type is still being made. That is a better form of oversight than standing in a kitchen pretending to understand a chemistry mark scheme.

The table lists the artefacts, how the video format generates each one, and how to check it. If a provider cannot produce any given row on request, the session is not producing it, whatever the format.

sections.heading: Science practicals when the lesson is on a screen: how experimental skill is actually examined
paragraphs: This is the objection every online provider gets and almost none of them answer with specifics. The specifics are reassuring. At IGCSE, experimental skill is examined on paper, not at a bench, on the routes most UAE schools use. On the Cambridge science syllabuses there is a written component that presents the experiment in text and asks the candidate to tabulate, plot, interpret and evaluate. On the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences, practical understanding is examined inside the main written papers through questions that describe a method and ask the candidate to improve or critique it.

Read that again, because it determines what tutoring can and cannot do. Nothing in either model requires the candidate to perform an experiment in front of an examiner. What is being tested is the ability to read a method precisely, record data to a consistent number of decimal places, plot a line of best fit with a sensible scale, identify the dominant source of error rather than list every possible one, and write an observation in the language the mark scheme credits. All of those are text and data skills, and all of them are better taught with the data table on a shared screen than on a photocopy.

The school laboratory still matters enormously, and this page is not arguing otherwise. Handling apparatus is how a student builds the physical intuition that makes the written questions make sense, and that belongs in the school's own lessons where the equipment and the supervision are. What a tutor adds is the examination layer on top: which of the student's observations would have earned the mark and which would not. That layer is almost never taught explicitly, which is why it is where the recoverable marks sit.
The table sets out the two assessment models side by side with the specific question of what a screen can and cannot deliver for each. The honest column is the last one.

sections.heading: The setup that makes or breaks a session in an Ajman apartment
paragraphs: Most of what goes wrong with online tutoring is logistics rather than pedagogy, and almost all of it is fixable in one conversation before the first session. The non-negotiable item is a way for the tutor to see the student's handwritten working in mathematics and physics. A webcam pointed at a face is useless for this. A stylus tablet is ideal, a document camera is excellent, and an old phone propped on a stack of books pointing down at an A4 pad works perfectly well and costs nothing.

The second item is a room where the door closes. This is harder in Al Nuaimiya or on the Corniche than in Al Zorah, and it is worth solving rather than tolerating. A student doing algebra in a living room with a television on is losing half of every session, and no tutor can compete with a television. Where no quiet room exists, the better answer is to move the session to a weekend morning rather than to persist with an evening slot that was never going to work.

The third is connection planning rather than connection quality. Evening bandwidth in dense Ajman blocks is shared and it dips. The design response is to make the session survivable rather than to demand perfection: the work lives in a shared document that both sides can see, so a dropped call means thirty seconds of reconnection rather than a lost thread. A phone hotspot should be set up in advance as the routine fallback, not discovered as an emergency in week three.

The fourth is less obvious. Agree who is in the room. A parent sitting in on the first session is useful. A parent sitting in on every session usually produces a student who performs for the parent rather than works, and the error tally stops being honest. The arrangement that works is parental access without parental presence: you can join any session unannounced, and the normal pattern is that you read the record instead.

sections.heading: Verifying the person on the screen
paragraphs: Distance delivery removes geography as a constraint and puts the burden on verification instead, which is a fair trade as long as the verification is real. There are four things a family in Ajman can check, and all four are reasonable to ask for before a paid session.

First, the permit position. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and administered by MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's service page for private tutor licensing lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. A provider should be able to tell you plainly how the permit position applies to the person teaching your child.

Second, the component. Ask which syllabus code and which paper the tutor has marked, and ask for a redacted sample of that marking. This filter removes more unsuitable tutors than any qualification check, because teaching a subject and marking a specific component are different competencies and only the second one predicts whether your child's technique improves. Third, the limits on assessed work: a tutor explains criteria and marks the student's own draft, and nothing is supplied for submission. Fourth, examiner claims. If somebody is presented as an examiner, ask for evidence of current status, and treat any suggestion that examiner status brings access to boundaries or paper content as a reason to walk away.

One more thing worth knowing. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That rule is press-reported rather than read from the current policy document, so verify it directly if it is material to you, but the principle is sound everywhere: your child's own classroom teacher, privately, is not the arrangement to seek.

sections.heading: The things a screen does worse, said plainly
paragraphs: A page that lists only advantages is advertising. There are four real weaknesses in video delivery and a family deciding between formats deserves them stated as clearly as the benefits.

The first is age. A nine or ten-year-old frequently needs an adult physically present to stay on task, and a screen cannot supply that. The second is specific learning differences and attentional difficulty: some students work substantially better with a person beside them, and that is not a motivation problem to be solved with a better platform. The third is physical practical work, which belongs in the school laboratory and cannot be replicated at a desk. The fourth is the household itself: a student with no quiet space and an unstable evening connection will have a worse experience over video than at a table with a tutor, regardless of who the tutor is.

Where any of those apply, the better purchase is in-home tuition from a local Ajman or Sharjah provider, and we would rather tell you that at the enquiry stage than take a month's fees first. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, so there is no version of our service that solves those four problems, and pretending otherwise would waste your time and your money.

What video does well is narrow and valuable: it reaches specialists regardless of distance, it generates a record as a by-product, it absorbs a late arrival from Dubai without renegotiating anything, and it is well matched to the way IGCSE actually examines experimental skill. For a Year 10 or Year 11 student with a quiet room, a writing surface and a specific component problem, that combination is hard to beat in the northern emirates. For a Year 5 child who will not sit still, it is the wrong product.

sections.heading: Where an online-taught candidate actually sits the examination
paragraphs: Tutoring format and examination arrangements are separate questions, and families reasonably confuse them. Being taught over video changes nothing about where or how the papers are sat. A student enrolled at a school in Ajman, Sharjah or Dubai sits the papers at the school as an internal candidate, entered by the school's exams officer, on the school's timetable, exactly as they would if they had no tutor at all.

The position differs for a private candidate: someone resitting a single subject, someone being educated at home, or someone adding a subject their school does not offer. A private candidate must be entered through an approved examination centre, and centres set their own administrative charges in addition to the board's entry fee. Those arrangements have to be made well in advance, because entries close months before the papers rather than weeks.

One overseas-specific detail is worth repeating whichever route applies. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a different timetable version for each, stating that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and then a final one, so the live PDF on the board's own site is the only safe source for a date. Any revision plan counted backwards from the wrong set of dates is wrong by the same margin.

A tutor's role in all of this is limited and should be stated as such. We can tell you what questions to ask the exams officer and what the published board guidance says. We cannot enter a candidate, cannot act as a centre, and do not perform or guarantee any part of an entry or equivalency process. Anybody suggesting otherwise is overstating what a tutoring service is.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies alongside an IGCSE programme
paragraphs: This is the gap in the whole UAE tutoring search. No competitor page in the researched set treats the mandatory UAE subjects as anything more than a chip in a subject list, and yet they occupy real timetable hours in every private school in the country and appear on real reports. For an Ajman family planning tuition around a child's week, that matters practically.

The federal position is the starting point: private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. Private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit under the Ministry of Education's supervision, so that federal baseline is the frame your child's school works within. Dubai schools sit under KHDA, and a child commuting from Ajman into a Dubai school will be subject to KHDA's own detailed requirements rather than to anything set in Ajman.

Those KHDA requirements are worth knowing for the cross-border families, because they are specific and they are published. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies. KHDA also requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, and states that using different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is prohibited.

The practical consequence for a tutoring plan is twofold. First, those lessons consume hours, so a realistic weekly plan has fewer slots in it than a parent assumes. Second, the content rule means any support in these subjects has to work from the school's own prescribed material rather than from an invented scheme of work. And note the separate point for equivalency: on the British track, Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required GCSE or IGCSE subjects.

sections.heading: Six weeks of online tutoring: what should exist at the end of it
paragraphs: Six weeks is the right review point because it is long enough to produce comparable data and short enough that a wrong decision has not cost much. By then the shared folder should contain roughly six annotated question sets, two timed attempts marked against the published scheme, an error tally with category counts, and a written review that takes a position.

The test to apply is simple and unsentimental. Compare the error tally in week one with the tally in week six. If the same categories dominate at the same frequency, the sessions have been delivering content rather than correcting technique, and the plan is wrong regardless of how pleasant the sessions have been. If the categories have shifted, the plan is working and the next question is only about rate: how many sessions for the remaining items, and on what basis is that estimate made.

There is a third possible outcome and it should be named out loud. Sometimes six weeks of evidence shows that the barrier is not academic at all. A student arriving at a session exhausted at 7pm after a Sharjah school day and a long drive home is not short of teaching; a student who has not done a single between-session task in six weeks is telling you something about engagement rather than ability. In both cases the right recommendation is to change the schedule or the conversation at home, not to buy more hours.

A provider that cannot describe the circumstances under which you should stop paying is not describing a service. The review at week six exists to make continuing an active decision rather than a default, and for an online arrangement with no travel sunk into it, stopping is genuinely costless on both sides. That is worth something in a market where several providers sell prepaid terms.
bullets: Six annotated question sets and two marked timed attempts in the shared folder

faqs.question: Is an online IGCSE tutor as effective as someone sitting next to my child?
faqs.answer: It depends almost entirely on the student rather than on the format. For a Year 10 or Year 11 student with a quiet room and a way for the tutor to see their handwritten working, video is at least as effective and has one clear advantage: the marking is saved, so a pattern across a term is visible rather than remembered. For a younger child who needs an adult physically present to stay on task, or a household with no quiet space and an unstable evening connection, in-home tuition from a local provider is genuinely the better purchase and we will say so.

faqs.question: How are IGCSE science practicals taught if the lesson is on a screen?
faqs.answer: On the routes most UAE schools use, experimental skill is examined on paper rather than at a bench. Cambridge Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 assess it through a written component that presents the experiment in text; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences examine practical understanding inside the main written papers. So what is being tested is tabulating data, plotting a line of best fit, identifying the dominant source of error and writing observations in mark-scheme language. All of that is taught from past papers, with no apparatus on either side. School laboratory work still matters and belongs at school.

faqs.question: What equipment does my child need for an online IGCSE session in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Less than most families expect. A laptop or tablet with a working microphone, a room where the door closes, and a way for the tutor to see handwritten working. That last item is the only one people get wrong: a webcam pointed at a face is useless for maths. A stylus tablet is ideal, a document camera is excellent, and an old phone propped on a stack of books pointing down at an A4 pad works perfectly well and costs nothing. A phone hotspot set up in advance covers the evening bandwidth dips common in dense Ajman blocks.

faqs.question: Can I watch an online IGCSE lesson or see a recording of it afterwards?
faqs.answer: You can join any session unannounced, and that access is the point rather than a concession. What we suggest instead, after the first session, is reading the record: the annotated script, the error tally and the between-session task sit in a shared folder you can open at eleven at night. Routine parental presence tends to produce a student who performs for the parent rather than works, which makes the error tally less honest. Access without presence is the arrangement that keeps the evidence usable, and it suits parents who are driving back from Dubai at session time.

faqs.question: How do I verify that an online tutor is permitted to teach in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask directly how the MoHRE private tuition work permit applies to the person teaching your child. Private tutoring is regulated through a permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Then verify the thing that predicts teaching quality: which syllabus code and component the tutor has marked, with a redacted sample.

faqs.question: Our internet in Ajman drops in the evening. Does that ruin a session?
faqs.answer: Not if the session is designed for it. Evening bandwidth in dense blocks in Al Nuaimiya or on the Corniche is shared and it dips, so the work is held in a shared document that both sides can see rather than only in the video call. A dropped connection then costs about thirty seconds of reconnection instead of the thread of the lesson. Set up a phone hotspot as the routine fallback before the first session rather than discovering you need one in week three. If drops are constant rather than occasional, move the slot to a weekend morning.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my child's handwritten working over video?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for mathematics and physics it is the whole requirement. With a stylus tablet the student writes directly into a shared canvas the tutor annotates. With a document camera or a phone on a stand over paper, the tutor sees each line as it is written and can stop a wrong method at the second step rather than after five minutes of commitment to it. The script is then saved as a file and sent. That is better than paper in one specific respect: the annotated version still exists in April.

faqs.question: Where does an online-taught IGCSE student actually sit the exams?
faqs.answer: Exactly where they would have anyway. A student enrolled at a school in Ajman, Sharjah or Dubai sits the papers at the school as an internal candidate, entered by the exams officer on the school's timetable. Tutoring format changes nothing about it. A private candidate, meaning a resit, a home-educated student or someone adding a subject the school does not offer, must be entered through an approved examination centre, and centres set their own administrative charge on top of the board's entry fee. Those arrangements are made months ahead, because entries close long before the papers.

faqs.question: Does my child still need Arabic and Islamic Education alongside IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Yes, in some form. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. In Ajman, private schools sit under Ministry of Education supervision; a child commuting into a Dubai school falls under KHDA's own detailed requirements, which mandate Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of the licensed international curriculum. Those lessons consume weekly hours, so a tutoring timetable has fewer free slots than parents assume. Note that Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the five subjects counted for British-track equivalency.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring a poor fit for a child who is easily distracted?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it should be tested rather than assumed. A screen gives a distractible student other tabs, and no tutor can compete with a phone face-up on the desk. The practical mitigations are real: a shorter session, a shared document that shows whether anything is being written, and a rule that the phone is in another room. What does not work is persisting with an evening slot in a room with a television on. If six weeks of evidence shows nothing is being produced between sessions, the honest recommendation is to change the format rather than buy more hours.

faqs.question: How long should an online IGCSE session be for a Year 10 student?
faqs.answer: Sixty minutes for technique drills, ninety where a full structured paper is being worked through, because an attempt and its marking cannot both fit into an hour. Beyond ninety minutes attention degrades for most fifteen-year-olds on a screen, and two shorter sessions in a week usually beat one long one for retention. In Ajman the practical limit is often the clock rather than the attention span: a session that cannot start until 8.30pm because the Dubai commute ran late should be sixty minutes, not ninety.

faqs.question: Can one online tutor cover both Cambridge and Edexcel science papers?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it should be checked explicitly rather than assumed. The science content overlaps heavily, but the assessment models differ in a way that changes teaching. Cambridge examines experimental skill through a written component on the alternative route; Edexcel embeds practical understanding inside the main written papers. A tutor who has marked only one model will prepare your child for a paper that will not be set. Ask which codes they have marked, 0620 and 0625 or 4CH1 and 4PH1, and ask for a redacted marked sample from each one they claim.

faqs.question: What should six weeks of online IGCSE tutoring have produced?
faqs.answer: A shared folder containing roughly six annotated question sets, two full papers sat alone under exam timing and marked against the published scheme, an error tally with category counts, and a written review that takes a position. The test is to compare the tally at week six with week one. If the same categories dominate at the same frequency, the sessions delivered content rather than corrected technique and the plan needs changing. If they have shifted, the only remaining question is the rate of progress and the estimate for what is left.

faqs.question: Does an online tutor need to know which Ajman school my child attends?
faqs.answer: Yes, for three specific reasons rather than as small talk. The school determines the exam board and the components entered, which decides what is practised. It determines the internal deadline calendar for any coursework, which decides the order work is done in. And it determines the school day, which decides what time a session can realistically start: a child at a school in Sharjah or Dubai gets home materially later than one at a school in Al Nuaimiya. None of that requires any contact with the school, and no relationship with any school is implied.

faqs.question: Can online sessions move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they normally should. School hours shorten during Ramadan and the useful part of a student's evening shifts late, so holding a 6.30pm slot through the month tends to produce sessions nobody gets anything from. The usual arrangement is to move to a post-Iftar slot for the month, or to shift to a daytime weekend session instead. Because delivery is over live video with no travel involved, moving a session costs nothing to anyone and needs no notice beyond the courtesy of asking. Revision planning around the month is agreed in advance rather than improvised.

ajman/igcse-online-tutor.closingHeading: Send a mock script and see what the first session finds
ajman/igcse-online-tutor.closingBody: The most useful thing you can send is a photograph of your child's most recent marked paper, along with the syllabus codes from the school's entry statement. The first session is free, runs one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and is spent marking a question set on a shared screen rather than on introductions. You keep the annotated file and the first error tally whatever you decide afterwards. At week six you compare the tally with week one and take a decision, and because there is no travel sunk into the arrangement, stopping costs nothing.
