ajman/igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover the IGCSE subjects Ajman families ask about most: the two maths routes, the three separate sciences, and first-language English. Each card names the boards and the papers that tutor marks. Ask to see a marked sample from a previous student before you book any paid block of lessons.

intro.heading: What an IGCSE tutor in Ajman is actually being hired to fix
paragraphs: Most families in Al Nuaimiya or Al Mowaihat start looking after a Year 10 report where the predicted grade slipped a band and nobody explained why. The usual cause is not that the child stopped working. It is that answers are being written in the wrong register for the mark scheme: a four-mark explain question answered as a two-mark state, a correct calculation handed in without its unit, a six-mark extended response in biology that lists true facts and never links them in the order the examiner credits. That is a diagnosable fault with a name, and faults with names get fixed in weeks rather than years.

So this page is built around what a session leaves behind rather than what it promises. A lesson that produces no artefact cannot be checked by you, by the school, or by the student in April when the revision actually matters. After a session here there is a scanned question with ticks and crosses on it, a line in the log that says what the raw mark was, and one sentence on what to practise before the next one. Three weeks of that is enough for a parent to decide whether to continue, and it is the only honest basis for that decision.

Ajman geography shapes the timetable more than anything else on this page. A large share of parents in Al Rashidiya, Al Jurf and Emirates City work in Dubai or Sharjah, and the drive back along Emirates Road or Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road does not reliably finish before seven in the evening. A 4pm slot that works for an Abu Dhabi villa is unusable here. Sessions for Ajman students are normally set between 6.30pm and 9.30pm on weekdays, with Saturday and Sunday mornings held for paper practice under timed conditions, because a timed paper needs a quiet house.

The board mix matters too. Ajman schools run both Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, and a number of Ajman children sit in Sharjah or Dubai classrooms, which widens the mix again. The papers are not interchangeable. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 tiers its candidates into Core and Extended with different paper pairs; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 tiers as Foundation and Higher. A tutor who does not ask for the syllabus code on the front of your child's exam entry is guessing, and guessing shows up as practice on questions that will never be set.

One thing to settle before you read further. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video; IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in Ajman, and home visits are a service offered only in India. Nothing on this page promises a grade either. A tutor can teach technique, mark work honestly and keep a record, and no tutor can commit to a number on a results slip. If a provider quotes you one, that is the moment to close the tab.
bullets: A marked script, a mark-scheme reference and a raw-mark figure after every paper attempt
Cambridge and Edexcel codes stated in writing, because the papers are not interchangeable
Evening slots built around the Emirates Road commute back into Ajman

ajman/igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Four routes cover almost every Ajman student who arrives here. Which one applies is decided by the school's entry policy and by the tier your child was placed in at the start of Year 10, not by preference.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Core tier
programmes.description: The Core tier covers a reduced subject content and caps the attainable grade at C in most syllabuses. In Mathematics 0580 that means Papers 1 and 3; in the sciences it narrows the supplement content out of the specification. Students placed in Core who are tracking a B or above need a tier review with the school early in Year 10, because a late move is an entry change rather than a teaching change.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman schools place Core candidates for different reasons: some to protect a predicted grade, some because the cohort is large and the set structure is fixed. If your child needs Extended for a sixth-form entry requirement in Sharjah or Dubai, raise it in the autumn term. By the November final-entry window the decision has effectively been made for you.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Extended tier
programmes.description: Extended carries the supplement content and the full grade range to A*. In Mathematics 0580 the papers are 2 and 4, with Paper 4 the longer structured paper where the multi-step questions sit. In the sciences the Extended papers reward chains of reasoning rather than recall, which is exactly where a strong Core student stalls when moved up without retraining.
programmes.countryNote: Extended is the tier most Ajman families eventually want, because the A-Level and IB Diploma entry criteria used by schools in Sharjah and Dubai are written in grades the Core tier cannot reach. The honest timeline is two terms of retraining, not two weeks, and the first evidence of it is a raw-mark rise on structured questions rather than on multiple choice.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Edexcel's International GCSE suite uses 4-prefixed codes: Mathematics A 4MA1, Physics 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1, Biology 4BI1, English Language A 4EA1. Tiering is Foundation and Higher. Assessment is written throughout, with practical skills examined on paper rather than in a laboratory, and the question style leans harder on structured calculation than its Cambridge equivalent.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes International GCSE exams in May/June and November each year, and releases provisional timetables ahead of each series. For an Ajman family that matters in one specific way: a November entry gives a Year 11 student a genuine second attempt without losing a year, and the entry window for it closes long before the revision panic starts.

programmes.name: IGCSE to Diploma or A-Level bridging
programmes.description: The gap between a strong IGCSE grade and a comfortable first term of DP or A-Level is mostly about independence: reading a syllabus, planning a written response without a scaffold, and handling content that is introduced once rather than revisited. Bridging work in July and August is short, specific and far cheaper than repair work in November.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman students moving into sixth form often change school and emirate at the same time, which adds a commute and a new set of deadlines to an already steep term. Starting the bridge in the summer, while the family is still on an Ajman schedule, removes one variable from a transition that already has too many.

ajman/igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Ajman parents ask about by name, with the syllabus code and the place marks are most often lost. A tutor should be able to tell you the second part before you book.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Paper 4 and the Higher papers punish method gaps rather than arithmetic. Marks go on unrounded intermediate values, missing units, and ignoring the instruction to show working on a question worth four or more marks. Practice is scored against the mark scheme, so the student sees exactly which line earned nothing.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken by Ajman students heading for Maths AA HL or A-Level Mathematics. Calculus and trigonometric identities carry most of the difficulty, and the common loss is treating a proof as a calculation. Working is the answer here; a correct final value with no derivation attracts very little credit.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Electricity and waves produce the widest spread of marks in any Ajman cohort. Students lose marks by describing a circuit instead of explaining it, and by writing formulae without defining the symbols. Paper 6 on the Cambridge route tests experimental skills in writing, which is a separate technique from the physics itself.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic reaction pathways are where the grade is decided. The recurring fault is answering a why question with a what answer. On the Cambridge route the alternative-to-practical paper rewards precise observation language, which students never practise unless someone makes them.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The content feels manageable and the marks are hard. Extended response questions want linked reasoning in sequence, and lists of true statements score badly. Data questions need the figure quoted from the graph, not a paraphrase of the trend, and that single habit moves several marks per paper.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the comparative reading tasks reward structure over vocabulary. Marks are lost on audience and register, and on summaries that retell rather than compress. Sessions are built on timed writing with the mark scheme bands read aloud, so the student learns what a band boundary actually sounds like.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: A large share of Ajman candidates sit this rather than 0500, and the two are marked on different criteria. The reading tasks reward exact lifting where the question allows it, and the writing tasks reward task fulfilment ahead of complexity. Over-ambitious sentences that collapse mid-clause cost more than simple ones that land.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Application to the case study is the whole examination. Generic answers about motivation or cash flow score in the lowest band however accurate they are. The technique is to quote the stimulus, apply one concept, and evaluate with a reasoned judgement, in that order, every time.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagrams carry marks that students leave on the table: axes unlabelled, no title, shifts drawn without an arrow or a reason. The evaluation marks on the longer questions need a stated condition, and answers that argue one side only cap well below the top band.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Paper 1 theory on data representation and networks is learnable quickly; Paper 2 algorithm design is not. Pseudocode loses marks for undeclared variables and untraceable loops. Trace tables are practised until they are boring, because they are the single most reliable source of marks on that paper.

subjects.name: Geography (Cambridge 0460)
subjects.description: Case-study specificity decides the grade. Named places, figures and dates earn credit; a general description of coastal erosion does not. Skills questions on maps and graphs are the cheapest marks on the paper and the most commonly dropped through rushing.

subjects.name: Accounting (Cambridge 0452)
subjects.description: Format discipline is most of it. Marks follow correct headings, dates and the right side of the ledger, and a single misposting can cascade through a whole question. Practice is done under time, because speed is the constraint that actually decides this paper.

ajman/igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: Ajman is compact, and the difference between one community and the next is mostly about which school run the family does and how far into the evening the working parent gets home. Both change what time a session can realistically start.

regions.name: Al Nuaimiya
regions.note: Dense, central and close to the older Indian-curriculum and British-curriculum schools. Short school runs mean homework starts early, so a 6.30pm session is usually workable here when it would not be further out.

regions.name: Al Rashidiya
regions.note: Mixed low-rise and apartment blocks near the Ajman city core. Families here often have two children on different curricula in different schools, so sibling sessions are staggered rather than stacked back to back.

regions.name: Al Jurf
regions.note: Industrial and residential in parts, with a long internal drive to the Emirates Road junctions. Parents commuting to Sharjah industrial areas tend to ask for the last slot of the evening rather than the first.

regions.name: Al Mowaihat
regions.note: Villa communities spread across Mowaihat 1, 2 and 3, with Dubai and Sharjah commutes for a large share of households. Weekend morning paper practice works better here than a rushed weekday slot.

regions.name: Al Zahya and Al Tallah
regions.note: Newer developments along the Emirates Road corridor, which puts several Sharjah and Dubai schools within reach. These households are the most likely to be running a Cambridge and an Edexcel child at the same time.

regions.name: Al Helio and Al Rawda
regions.note: Established residential areas with a strong local school cluster. Short journeys make a second weekly session practical, which matters most in the term before a November entry.

regions.name: Ajman Corniche and Al Rumailah
regions.note: Apartment living near the seafront, often with shared study space and noise through the evening. Timed paper practice is scheduled for weekend mornings here as a matter of course.

regions.name: Emirates City and Al Alia
regions.note: Towers and new villa plots off the Emirates Road, with the longest commutes in the emirate. Sessions are commonly set at 8pm or later, and reschedules are handled without a fee because the traffic is not the family's fault.

regions.name: Al Yasmeen and Al Zorah
regions.note: Low-density villa areas with quieter evenings and a longer run to school. Families here tend to book a single longer weekly session rather than two shorter ones, which suits paper practice.

regions.name: Masfout and Manama
regions.note: The Ajman exclaves, inland and far from the coastal schools. Online delivery is not a convenience here but the only practical route to a subject specialist, which is why the evidence trail matters even more.

schoolClusters.note: The established cluster, weighted towards Indian and British curricula. Students from these schools arrive asking about Cambridge codes most often, and about tier placement in Mathematics and the sciences almost as often.

schoolClusters.note: Newer schools serving the villa developments, with a wider board mix and more movement between Ajman and Sharjah. Queries from this belt skew towards sixth-form entry requirements and bridging into the Diploma.

ajman/igcse-tutor.modesIntro: Three formats, chosen by what the evidence says the student needs rather than by what is easiest to sell. All three run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, term time
modes.description: One or two sessions a week through the school year, each ending with a marked piece of work and a logged raw mark. This is the format that produces a usable trend line, because a single data point tells you nothing and six weeks of them tells you most of what you need. Sessions are normally 60 or 90 minutes, with the longer slot used where a full structured paper is being worked through.
bullets: Marked question, mark-scheme reference and raw mark recorded every session
One named practice task between sessions, not a worksheet pile
A written review at week six that says continue, change subject focus, or stop
Sessions set after the Ajman evening commute, 6.30pm to 9.30pm on weekdays

modes.title: Timed paper clinic
modes.description: A weekend block in which the student sits a past paper under exam timing with no help, and the session that follows is spent only on the marking. No teaching happens during the attempt. This separates two things families usually blur together: whether the content is known, and whether it can be produced in the time allowed. Most grade losses in an Ajman mock season turn out to be the second problem.
bullets: Full paper under official timing, usually Saturday or Sunday morning
Marked against the published mark scheme, question by question
Error log categorised as content, technique, timing or reading the question
Repeat attempt on a parallel paper three to four weeks later for comparison

modes.title: Pre-entry sprint
modes.description: A short, dated block in the weeks before a November or June series, aimed at a specific paper rather than a subject. It assumes the content is broadly in place and that the problem is execution under pressure. It is the only format with a fixed end point, which is deliberate: a sprint that drifts into a permanent arrangement has stopped being a sprint and the family should be told so.
bullets: Fixed number of sessions with a stated finish date before the paper
Topic selection driven by the error log, not by the syllabus order
Command-word drills on the question types that paper repeats
Closing report listing what was fixed and what was left unaddressed

sections.heading: The marking record: what a tutoring session should leave behind
paragraphs: A session in Ajman should produce a paper trail you can read in five minutes. That means a specific list: the question attempted with its paper and year, the mark awarded out of the mark available, the mark-scheme point that was missed, and one named task to do before the next session. Nothing about that is unusual in a school department. It is unusual in private tutoring, where the normal output is a verbal reassurance at the end of an hour and an invoice at the end of the month.

The reason to insist on it is not bureaucracy. It is that grades move through accumulated small corrections, and small corrections are invisible unless they are written down. A student who stops dropping unit marks in Physics 0625 has gained perhaps three marks a paper. Nobody notices three marks in a conversation. Everybody notices it in a log that shows the same error type falling from six instances to one across four papers, and that log is also what persuades a sceptical fifteen-year-old that the hour is worth attending.

It also protects you as the person paying. With a record, the week-six decision is a reading exercise. Without one, it is a judgement about whether you like the tutor. Those are different questions and only the first one has an answer. If a provider in the UAE market cannot show you a redacted sample of this record from a previous student before you pay, that tells you what their sessions produce, and the answer is nothing you can audit.
The table below is the full artefact list. A parent should be able to ask for any row and receive it the same evening.
bullets: Ask for a redacted sample record from a previous student before the first paid session
Expect the paper, year and question number, not just a topic name
A raw mark out of the available mark, every time, not a percentage
One named task between sessions, with the paper reference attached

table.caption: EVIDENCE A SESSION SHOULD PRODUCE
rows: Which mark-scheme points were earned and which were missed
Tutor, during the session on a shared screen
Direction of travel across attempts on comparable questions
Tutor, updated after every marked attempt
Whether the problem is content, technique, timing or misreading
Tutor, categorised against a fixed list
That the week between sessions has a purpose

Whether to continue, change focus, or stop

sections.heading: Command words in a Cambridge IGCSE paper, and the marks attached to each
paragraphs: Every Cambridge IGCSE question opens with an instruction, and that instruction is a contract about what will be credited. Students who read the instruction as a general invitation to write about the topic lose marks they already know the content for. This is the cheapest fault to fix in the whole examination and the one least often addressed in a normal school lesson, because a class of twenty-eight cannot be marked line by line every week.

The pattern repeats across subjects. State wants a fact and nothing else, and a student who explains it has spent three minutes earning one mark. Explain wants a reason with a mechanism, and a student who states it has written a true sentence that scores nothing. Describe wants the what; account for and justify want the why with a stated criterion. Compare wants both sides and an explicit linking word, and a paragraph on one side followed by a paragraph on the other does not count as a comparison in several mark schemes.

Drilling this is dull and effective. The method is to take six questions from past papers with different command words, cover the body of each, and have the student say what the examiner will credit before writing a word. Ten minutes a week for a term, and the habit sticks. The table sets out the command words that appear most often in Ajman students' papers across Mathematics, the sciences and the humanities, with the shape of the answer that loses the mark.

One caution on sources. Mark schemes and syllabus documents belong to the board and should be read on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com rather than from a photocopy circulating on a parents group. Boards revise wording between series, and a two-year-old handout is a reliable way to practise the wrong thing.

table.caption: COMMAND WORDS AND THE ANSWER THAT LOSES THE MARK
rows: A single correct fact, no reasoning required
A paragraph of explanation around a fact that was never stated plainly
Observable features or a sequence of what happens
Reasons why it happens, with the description assumed
A reason with a mechanism or causal link
A restatement of the observation in different words
Method shown, then the value with its unit
A correct final number with no working and no unit
Both subjects addressed with an explicit linking word
A paragraph on one, then a paragraph on the other, never joined
A plausible answer applied to the unfamiliar context given
A textbook answer that ignores the stimulus entirely
A judgement supported by a stated criterion
A one-sided argument with no criterion and no conclusion

sections.heading: Raw marks, not percentages: how an IGCSE grade actually moves
paragraphs: Parents are given percentages by schools and grades by boards, and neither tells you where the next improvement comes from. Raw marks do. A structured paper worth 130 marks does not reward effort evenly: some question types return a mark per thirty seconds of work and others return nothing for five minutes of writing. Knowing which is which is most of what a good revision plan is.

Work the arithmetic through with the student and the conversation changes. If the Extended maths paper carries around a third of its marks on multi-step structured questions, and the student is routinely losing the final accuracy mark on those, that is a recoverable block of marks sitting in a habit rather than in missing knowledge. Fixing it takes a fortnight of marked practice. Learning a new topic takes a term. Any revision plan that does not sort the student's losses into those two buckets first is spending the expensive weeks on the cheap problems.

Grade boundaries themselves move between series and are published by the board after marking, so nobody can tell you in advance how many marks a grade will cost. That is a reason to work in raw marks rather than predictions, not a reason to avoid the question. The useful framing for an Ajman family is simple: here is the paper, here is where your marks went last time, here is the cheapest block of marks to recover, and here is how many sessions that block realistically takes.

The log makes this visible without anybody needing to believe a claim. Four marked attempts at comparable questions, with the error types tallied, will show whether the cheap block is actually closing. If it is not, the plan was wrong and should change at week six rather than in March.
bullets: Sort losses into content gaps and technique gaps before planning any revision
Technique gaps usually close in two to three weeks of marked practice
Content gaps take a term, so they are started first and reviewed last
Never plan against a predicted boundary; plan against marks on the page

sections.heading: Six weeks, twelve weeks, a full year: what progress looks like on paper
paragraphs: Families ask how long this takes, and the honest answer depends entirely on which of the two problems the student has. Technique faults respond quickly and visibly. Missing content from Year 9 and the first half of Year 10 does not, and anyone who says otherwise is selling. What can be promised is a reporting rhythm, so that by a known date you have enough information to make a decision rather than a guess.

The first block is diagnostic. Three to six sessions, each producing a marked artefact, is usually enough to say what kind of problem this is and roughly how big it is. At the end of it there is a written review that takes a position: continue on this subject, switch the focus to a different paper, add a second subject, or stop because the issue is organisational rather than academic and a tutor is the wrong purchase.

The second block is where marks move. Twelve weeks of weekly sessions with a timed paper every three to four weeks produces four comparable data points, which is the minimum needed to distinguish a trend from a good day. Over a full academic year the pattern changes shape: content coverage through the autumn, technique through the spring, and a dated sprint on specific papers in the final weeks before the series the student is entered for.

The table below sets out what each block produces and what you can fairly judge at the end of it. The last column is the point of the whole exercise, because a block that does not support a decision is just an expense with a timetable.

Continue, change focus, add a subject, or stop
One or two sessions, timed paper monthly

sections.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel: finding out which paper your child will actually sit
paragraphs: This sounds like administration and it decides whether the practice is useful. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel both operate widely in the northern emirates, and an Ajman student can easily be sitting Cambridge Mathematics 0580 and Edexcel Physics 4PH1 in the same series if the school has mixed its entries by department. Practising Cambridge Paper 6 experimental technique for an Edexcel candidate is wasted time that felt productive.

The document that settles it is the exam entry statement the school issues, which lists the syllabus code and the components. Ask the exams officer for it rather than relying on what the textbook cover says, because schools change boards and old books stay on shelves. The code is the thing to write down: 0580, 0620, 0625, 0610, 0500 on the Cambridge side; 4MA1, 4CH1, 4PH1, 4BI1, 4EA1 on the Edexcel side.

The differences are concrete enough to change a revision plan. Cambridge tiers Core and Extended with separate paper pairs and assesses experimental skills through a written alternative-to-practical component on several science syllabuses. Edexcel tiers Foundation and Higher and examines practical understanding inside the main written papers. Question styles differ too: Edexcel structured calculations tend to be longer with more steps carried forward, so an arithmetic slip early costs more.

Once the code is known, everything else on this page becomes specific. The command-word drills come from that board's papers, the timed clinics use that board's timing, and the error log is kept against that board's mark scheme wording. A tutor who never asks for the code is marking against the wrong rubric, and the student is the one who finds out in June.
bullets: Ask the school exams officer for the entry statement, not the textbook cover
Write down the syllabus code for every subject, including the component numbers
Check whether the science route uses a written practical paper or embeds it
Confirm the tier in writing before the final entry window closes

sections.heading: Entry deadlines, timetable zones and the dates that are genuinely fixed
paragraphs: The single most useful administrative fact for a UAE family is that entries close months before the exams. Cambridge's March 2027 series shows the shape clearly: the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries are due 27 November 2026, forecast grades 27 February 2027, results on Direct 13 May and certificates in late June. The entry deadline sits more than two months before the first paper, which is why a decision to add a subject or change tier has to be made in the autumn.

Cambridge runs its main IGCSE and O Level examining in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 Pearson results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

There is a trap specific to overseas centres that is worth knowing. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone. Cambridge also says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. For an Ajman family that means one thing: get the zone from the school, and read the dates off the timetable for that zone rather than off a page found by searching.

IB Diploma dates are deliberately absent from this page. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no session or results date here is confirmed from the IB, and publishing an unverified date on a page parents plan around would be worse than publishing nothing. For any Diploma date, ask the school's IB coordinator or read ibo.org directly.
bullets: Final entries close months ahead of the papers, so tier changes are an autumn decision
Confirm your centre's Cambridge administrative zone and use that timetable version
Pearson publishes provisional timetables before each series; read the live PDF
Treat any IB date not confirmed by the school coordinator as unverified

sections.heading: Coursework, practical papers and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Some IGCSE subjects carry assessed work produced outside an examination hall, and the rules around it are not negotiable. A tutor may teach the skills, explain the assessment criteria, discuss a plan, and give feedback on the student's own finished draft. A tutor may not supply sentences, restructure a piece so that the authorship changes, or hand over a model answer to be adapted. The student is the author of every word submitted, and the signature on the authentication form says so.

This matters commercially as well as ethically, because the UAE market contains providers that sell finished assessed work outright. One of them advertises completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price. Buying that puts the student at risk of a malpractice finding that can cost the whole qualification, and it puts the family in the position of having paid for the risk. There is no version of this that is a shortcut; it is a different and worse outcome bought at a premium.

The practical components are a related question and a cleaner one. On the Cambridge science route, experimental skills on several syllabuses are assessed through a written paper rather than in a laboratory, which means the technique being tested is reading an experimental description, handling data and writing precise observations. That is teachable over video without any apparatus at all, and it is one of the places where online delivery is simply not at a disadvantage.

What a tutor can legitimately do with assessed work is still substantial: unpick the criteria in the student's own words, mark a draft the student wrote against those criteria, ask the questions that expose a weak argument, and hold the student to a timetable. That is the whole job, and done properly it is more useful than the alternative on offer.
bullets: Criteria explained, drafts marked, feedback given on the student's own writing
No model answers supplied for adaptation, and no text written for submission
Written practical papers are taught from past papers and data, not apparatus
Board documents are read on the official site rather than redistributed

sections.heading: The week-six review: four questions to ask, and when to stop
paragraphs: The decision point is week six, and it belongs to the parent rather than the tutor. By then there should be two timed attempts, a handful of marked question sets and an error tally. That is enough to answer four questions, and if any of them cannot be answered from the record, the record is the problem.

First: which error types have fallen, and by how much? A tally that looks the same at week six as week one means the sessions are delivering content rather than correcting habits. Second: what is left on the list, and is it content or technique? Third: how many sessions does the tutor estimate for the remaining items, and what is that estimate based on? Fourth, and least comfortable: is a tutor the right purchase at all? Some students at this stage need a study timetable, a sleep schedule or a conversation with the school, and an hour of paid teaching a week will not touch any of those.

Stopping is a legitimate outcome and should be said out loud. A tutor who cannot describe the circumstances in which a family should stop paying is not describing a service, and a provider whose only answer to a plateau is more sessions has an incentive problem. The pre-entry sprint format exists partly for this reason: it has a stated finish date, so continuing is an active decision rather than a default.

For Ajman families there is one practical addition. If the barrier turns out to be scheduling rather than teaching, say so and fix the schedule first. A student who arrives at a 6.30pm session having left Sharjah at 5.45pm is not going to absorb anything, and moving the slot to 8pm is free. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, so a change of time costs nothing in travel to anyone.

process.title: Tell us the codes
process.description: Send the subject list with syllabus codes and components from the school's entry statement, the tier your child is placed in, and the series they are entered for. Two minutes of accurate information here removes the most common cause of wasted sessions, which is practising the wrong board's question style.

process.title: Free first lesson
process.description: A full session at no cost, spent on a past-paper question set rather than on introductions. It produces the first marked artefact and the first entry in the error tally, so even if you go no further you leave with a diagnosis you did not have before.

process.title: Agree the reporting
process.description: Before any paid session, agree in writing what you will receive and when: the marked script within a day, the running raw-mark log, the error tally reviewed every fourth session, and a written review at week six. Reporting that is not agreed up front tends not to happen.

process.title: Run the first block
process.description: Three to six weekly sessions with one timed paper, set at a time that survives the Ajman evening commute. Reschedules inside the block are handled without a charge, because traffic on Emirates Road is not something a family controls.

process.title: Decide at week six
process.description: Read the review and take a position: continue, change the subject focus, add a second subject, or stop. The tutor states a recommendation with reasons, and the recommendation is sometimes to stop. That is the review working rather than failing.

whyPoints.title: The record exists before you pay
whyPoints.description: You can ask for a redacted sample of a previous student's marked script and raw-mark log before committing to any paid block. A provider that cannot produce one is telling you what its sessions generate, and the answer is nothing you can inspect afterwards.

whyPoints.title: Codes before content
whyPoints.description: Every subject is confirmed by syllabus code and component before teaching starts, taken from the school's entry statement rather than assumed. Cambridge 0620 and Edexcel 4CH1 are both chemistry and they are not the same examination.

whyPoints.title: Specialists rather than proximity
whyPoints.description: A student in Masfout or Al Zorah gets the tutor who marks that paper, not the one who lives nearest. Online delivery over live video is what makes that possible, and for the Ajman exclaves it is the only realistic route to a subject specialist.

whyPoints.title: An evening timetable that matches Ajman
whyPoints.description: Slots are set between 6.30pm and 9.30pm on weekdays and on weekend mornings for timed papers, because a large share of Ajman parents are driving back from Dubai or Sharjah until well into the evening and a tired student learns nothing.

whyPoints.title: No grade promises, in writing
whyPoints.description: No session, block or sprint carries a promised grade, score or improvement figure. What is committed to is the artefact list, the reporting dates and an honest recommendation at week six, including the recommendation to stop.

whyPoints.title: Clear limits on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Criteria are explained and the student's own drafts are marked. No text is supplied for submission and no model answer is handed over for adaptation, which is the line that separates teaching from the malpractice risk sold elsewhere in this market.

faqs.question: How will I know an IGCSE tutor in Ajman is actually making a difference?
faqs.answer: By reading the record rather than asking the tutor. After each session you should receive the marked question script with the mark-scheme points identified, the raw mark out of the mark available, and one named practice task. Every fourth session, the error tally is reviewed, so you can see whether unit losses in Physics or missing working in Mathematics are falling. At week six there is a written review. If error types look the same at week six as at week one, the sessions are delivering content and not correcting habits, and that is a reason to change the plan.

faqs.question: What should a marked past paper from a tutoring session actually look like?
faqs.answer: It should name the paper, the series and the question number, carry ticks against the mark-scheme points earned and crosses against those missed, and show the mark as a raw figure out of the available mark. Alongside it there should be a short note naming the fault in words a fifteen-year-old can act on, such as unit omitted or compare answered as two separate descriptions. A colour-coded sheet with no reference to the mark scheme is decoration. The point of marking is to tell the student which specific line earned nothing.

faqs.question: My son's school in Al Nuaimiya predicts a 5 in Maths. Can that move?
faqs.answer: It can move, and how far depends on which of two problems he has. If the losses are technique, such as unrounded intermediate values, missing units or no working shown on four-mark questions, those usually close within two or three weeks of marked practice. If whole topics from Year 9 and early Year 10 are missing, that is a term of work and it should be started first. Nobody can promise a number on a results slip. What the first three sessions will tell you is which of the two problems this is and roughly how large it is.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge IGCSE syllabus code should I check before booking anything?
faqs.answer: All of them, taken from the exam entry statement the school issues rather than from a textbook cover. The codes that come up most in Ajman are Mathematics 0580, Additional Mathematics 0606, Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620, Physics 0625, English as a First Language 0500 and English as a Second Language 0510 or 0511. The code fixes the tier, the papers and the mark scheme a tutor marks against. Without it, practice can be aimed at a component your child is not entered for, which feels productive and achieves nothing.

faqs.question: Is my child's private school in Ajman inspected by KHDA or by somebody else?
faqs.answer: Not by KHDA, which is Dubai's authority. The Ministry of Education plays the supervisory role for private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, while Dubai sits under KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain under ADEK, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge. If your child commutes to a school in Sharjah or Dubai, the regulator is the one for the emirate where the school sits, not where you live. That matters when you are looking for a published inspection report.

faqs.question: Do Ajman students sit the November Cambridge series or only the June one?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE and O Level examining in both a June series and a November series, so November is available where the school enters candidates for it. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are likewise available in May or June and in November. Whether your child can use the November window is a school decision about entries, not a board restriction, and it has to be raised early because final entries close months before the papers. For a Year 11 student, a November entry can mean a genuine second attempt without repeating a year.

faqs.question: Why does a tutor keep asking which exam timetable zone our school is in?
faqs.answer: Because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a different timetable version for each. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. A revision plan counts backwards from real paper dates, so using the wrong zone's dates shifts the whole plan. Get the zone from the school's exams officer and read the dates from the timetable for that zone.

faqs.question: Where exactly does a tutor stop on an IGCSE coursework piece?
faqs.answer: At the point where authorship would change. A tutor can explain the assessment criteria, discuss a plan, teach the skills the task needs, mark a draft the student wrote and ask the questions that expose a weak argument. A tutor cannot supply sentences for submission, restructure a piece so that the authorship changes, or hand over a model answer to be adapted. The student authors every word submitted and signs an authentication statement to that effect. Providers in this market that sell finished assessed work are selling a malpractice risk at a premium.

faqs.question: We live in Al Mowaihat and both parents work in Dubai. When can lessons run?
faqs.answer: Later than most providers assume. Sessions for Ajman families are normally set between 6.30pm and 9.30pm on weekdays, because the drive back along Emirates Road or Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road rarely finishes before seven. Weekend mornings are kept for timed paper practice, which needs a quiet house and a full uninterrupted slot. If a 6.30pm start means your child arrives having left Dubai at 5.45pm, move it to 8pm. Lessons run over live video, so changing the time costs nobody any travel.

faqs.question: Does somebody tutoring privately in Ajman need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The UAE regulates private tutoring through a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, administered by MoHRE. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

faqs.question: For UAE equivalency, how many IGCSE passes does the British track need?
faqs.answer: On the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. At least one ranking competitor publishes a six-subject figure, which is wrong. Verify the current rule on the Ministry's own channels before planning around it, and note that tutoring is not a requirement of the process.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting IGCSE tutoring in Year 11 after the mock results come back?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, with the focus narrowed. Mock scripts are the best diagnostic document a family ever gets, because they show performance under timing rather than with help available. In Year 11 the sensible purchase is a dated block aimed at specific papers, built from the mock error log rather than from the syllabus order. Expect technique gains to show first and content gaps to need longer. What you should not buy at this stage is an open-ended arrangement with no finish date, because the calendar has already decided when the work stops.

faqs.question: What actually happens in the free first IGCSE lesson?
faqs.answer: It is spent on a past-paper question set rather than on introductions. The tutor works through questions on the subject you have flagged, marking against the published mark scheme as the session goes, on a shared screen so the student sees the marking happen. It produces the first marked artefact and the first entries in the error tally. At the end you receive the script, the raw mark and a short written view of what kind of problem this is. If you stop there, you still keep the diagnosis.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both of my children if they are on different boards?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it should be checked rather than assumed. A tutor who marks both Cambridge 0580 and Edexcel 4MA1 can reasonably take two maths students, because the subject knowledge transfers even though the papers and mark schemes differ. Across the sciences it is less often sensible, since the written practical components are examined differently on the two routes. Sessions are staggered rather than stacked, because two separate marked records have to come out of them. Tell us both sets of codes at the start and we will say honestly whether one tutor fits.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for the subject and paper we need?
faqs.answer: You are told, with a date. Some combinations are genuinely thin in this market, particularly Additional Mathematics 0606 and the Edexcel written practical components in a specific term. The options are a wait with an estimated date, a different but related specialist with the limitation stated plainly, or a recommendation to look elsewhere. What does not happen is a general tutor being presented as a specialist for the paper. You would discover that in the marking, and by then a term would have gone.

ajman/igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Start with one marked paper and decide from there
ajman/igcse-tutor.closingBody: The first lesson is free and it produces something: a marked past-paper question set, a raw mark, and a written view of whether this is a content problem or a technique problem. Send the subject list with syllabus codes from your school's entry statement, say which series your child is entered for, and tell us what time works once the Dubai or Sharjah commute is done. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. At week six you read a written review and decide whether to continue, change the focus, or stop.

intro.heading: Proximity is a filter, and in Ajman it is an expensive one
paragraphs: A near-me search is a request for a shortlist within driving distance. It is a reasonable request and it has a cost that nobody itemises. Every kilometre you add to the requirement removes people from the shortlist, and every person removed raises the price of whoever is left. In a city the size of Ajman, with a specialist pool concentrated towards Sharjah and Dubai, a twenty-minute weekday-evening radius can reduce the field for a specific IGCSE component from a reasonable number of qualified markers to one or none.

The published numbers show the shape of it. An in-home one-to-one visit in the UAE is advertised at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table at AED 180 to 350 and home-tutor listings at AED 200 to 500. The same calibre of teaching delivered online is published at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. The gap is the drive. In Ajman that gap widens, because the drive is longer than it would be for an equivalent family in Jumeirah.

The second cost is less visible and matters more. Narrowing by distance does not narrow randomly; it narrows against scarcity. The subjects where the local pool is thinnest are precisely the ones where specialist marking matters most: Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 and the written practical science components. A parent in Al Zahya searching for a nearby 0606 tutor is likely to find either nobody or somebody whose only qualification for the job is being nearby, and the second outcome is worse than the first because it is harder to detect.

There is a third thing worth naming, because it is where the near-me search is actually right. Parents do not usually mean the same street. They mean someone who understands the school system their child is in, who is awake on Gulf Standard Time, who can run a session on a weekday evening in Ajman rather than at a European afternoon, and who knows what a school report from an Ajman private school actually means. All four of those are genuinely important and none of them requires a car. Three of the four are about timezone and context rather than geography.

IB Gram answers this search with one-to-one tuition over live video on Gulf Standard Time. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. That means we are not the nearby option and do not claim to be. What we are is the option where distance stops filtering the shortlist, so the person teaching your child is chosen on whether they have marked the component rather than on where they parked.

ajman/igcse-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: Four ways an Ajman family buys IGCSE help locally, with what each one actually costs once distance and group size are priced in. The cheapest per hour is rarely the cheapest per mark.

programmes.name: Local in-home one-to-one
programmes.description: Someone drives to your address and teaches one child. The published band is AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included. It is the most expensive format per contact hour and the one with the smallest available pool in Ajman, because the tutor has to be both qualified on the component and willing to spend a working evening in a car.
programmes.countryNote: In Ajman the realistic supply here is strongest in Mathematics and English and thinnest in the specialist components. If you are offered a nearby 0606 or 0478 tutor at a routine rate, ask for a redacted marked sample from that specific paper before agreeing anything, because the price is not doing the signalling you might expect.

programmes.name: Tuition centre group class
programmes.description: A fixed timetable at premises, usually in small groups, with a lower per-hour figure and a syllabus-paced scheme of work. It suits a student who is behind on content across a whole subject and does not suit one who needs a specific component fixed, because a group cannot be redirected to one child's error log.
programmes.countryNote: A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor. In Dubai, a training institute requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. Ask any centre which permit it holds and from whom.

programmes.name: Shared or neighbour-group sessions
programmes.description: Two or three children from the same community splitting one tutor and one rate. Per child it is the cheapest one-to-one-adjacent option available, and it works where the children are on the same board, the same subject and a similar level. Where they are not, it quietly becomes two half-sessions at a discount.
programmes.countryNote: This is common across the Ajman villa communities and it fails for a predictable reason: one child is on Cambridge 0580 and the other on Edexcel 4MA1, so the papers and mark schemes differ and nobody gets a full session. Check the codes of every child in the group before agreeing to the arrangement.

programmes.name: One-to-one over live video
programmes.description: The format on offer here. Published at AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor, with no travel component in the rate and no distance constraint on who is available. The trade is presence: for a younger child who needs an adult physically in the room, this is the wrong product and a local option is better.
programmes.countryNote: For the Ajman exclaves of Masfout and Manama this is not one option among several. There is no rate at which a weekly inland round trip is rational for a specialist, so video is the only route to a 0606 or 0478 tutor at all. That is a geography fact rather than a sales argument.

subjects.description: The thinnest pool on this list. Few tutors in the northern emirates teach 0606 regularly and those who do cluster towards Dubai. subjects.description: Scarce locally and getting scarcer as entries grow. Paper 2 algorithm design and pseudocode tracing needs someone who has marked it, and the Ajman radius rarely contains that person. This is the clearest case on the whole page where distance filtering produces a false choice.

subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Moderate local supply for the content, thin supply for the written practical component. Plenty of nearby tutors can teach waves and electricity; far fewer can train the experimental-skills paper, and that paper is where a diagnosable block of marks usually sits.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Reasonable local supply that visibly tightens in the spring term as the June series approaches. Starting in October gives you a genuine choice of nearby tutors; starting in March gives you whoever still has a Tuesday free, which is a different purchase at a similar price.

subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Broad local supply. The specific skill worth filtering for is extended-response marking, where linked reasoning earns marks and accurate lists do not. A nearby general science tutor will usually teach the content competently and leave that technique untouched.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Apparently abundant locally and genuinely scarce in the only way that matters. Many people present as English tutors; few can mark directed writing against the published bands. Ask for a marked sample with band references on it and most of the local field resolves itself quickly.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Well supplied across Ajman and Sharjah at mid-band rates. The error to avoid is being taught 0500 technique while entered for 0510, which happens because the subjects sound interchangeable and are assessed on different criteria entirely.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Decent local supply, thin specialist depth. Case-study application decides the grade and most nearby tutors teach the content instead. A marked extended answer showing where the application and evaluation marks were awarded is the filter to apply.

sections.heading: What a twenty-minute radius actually contains in Ajman
paragraphs: Start with the geography, because the geography is the argument. Ajman is compact, but the people who have marked IGCSE papers are not distributed in proportion to where families live. The specialist pool across the northern emirates concentrates towards Sharjah and Dubai, where the schools and the teaching jobs are. So a near-me search run from an Ajman address is, in practice, a search for whoever is willing to drive out from there on a weekday evening.

Drive time rather than distance is what matters, and weekday-evening drive time is a different number from the one a mapping app shows at eleven in the morning. The run between Sharjah and the Ajman communities along Emirates Road and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road does not reliably clear before seven. A tutor committing to a 7pm session in Al Mowaihat is committing to leaving at six and getting home around nine. That is a three-hour evening for one hour of paid teaching, and only a particular kind of rate makes it rational.

The consequence is a shortlist that is short in a specific direction. It contains people for whom the drive is short, which correlates with living nearby, which does not correlate at all with having marked Cambridge 0606 or Edexcel 4CH1. Parents experience this as a thin market and interpret it as a quality problem. It is a geometry problem: the filter being applied selects on the wrong variable, and the thing being optimised is not the thing that moves marks.

sections.heading: The scarcity premium, subject by subject
paragraphs: Once you accept that a radius filters on drive time, the next question is which subjects that filter damages. The answer is counter-intuitive: it damages the scarce components, not the hard ones. Mathematics 0580 has a deep pool, so a tight radius costs you choice rather than capability. Additional Mathematics 0606 has a shallow pool concentrated towards Dubai, so a tight radius can remove every qualified marker from the list and leave you selecting between people who have not taught the syllabus.

This produces a specific and expensive failure mode. A nearby tutor is engaged for a scarce component at an ordinary rate, teaches the content competently for a term, and never addresses the examination technique the paper is actually testing. Nobody notices until the mock, because content teaching feels like progress and a parent has no way to distinguish it from technique teaching without marked evidence. The money was not wasted exactly; it bought the wrong thing at a fair price.

The filter that fixes this is not geography and not price. It is a redacted marked sample from the specific component, which takes one message to request and about thirty seconds to assess. Either the sample shows mark-scheme points identified against a real paper, or it does not. Applied honestly, that question removes more unsuitable tutors than any other check available to a parent, and it works identically on a nearby tutor and a distant one.

sections.heading: Price per teaching minute, and why the short session only works online
paragraphs: Hourly rates hide something useful. What a family actually buys is teaching minutes, and the proportion of a booking that is teaching varies enormously by format. An in-home visit carries arrival, settling, finding the right notebook and a courteous departure, which can take fifteen minutes out of a sixty-minute booking. A video session starts within thirty seconds of the agreed time because nobody is parking.

That changes which session lengths are viable. A forty-five minute in-home visit is uneconomic for everyone: the tutor cannot justify the drive and the family is paying a large travel share across a small amount of teaching. So the local market sells sixty, ninety and one hundred and twenty minute blocks, and a student whose problem is one recurring error gets sold an hour of general revision because that is the smallest unit on offer.

Online, the short format becomes available, and for narrow technique faults it is often the better buy. Three forty-five minute slots across a fortnight, each with one stated objective, will close a recurring unit-omission or a misread command word faster and at lower total cost than one long weekly session that tries to cover everything. Conversely, the ninety-minute slot is the cheapest per teaching minute and is the right purchase once full papers need to be attempted and marked in the same sitting.

sections.heading: The four things parents mean by near me, and which ones need a car
paragraphs: It is worth unpicking the search term, because most of what it asks for is available without proximity and one part of it genuinely is not. Four things sit inside it.

The first is the timezone and the evening. A tutor who is awake, available and sharp at 7.30pm Gulf Standard Time, after an Ajman school day and a commute, rather than at the end of a European working day. This is real, it matters, and it needs no car; it needs a tutor whose working hours are built around this timezone rather than around another one. The second is school context: someone who knows what an Ajman private school report means, which boards local schools enter, and that a child commuting to Sharjah gets home later. Also real, also available at distance.

The third is responsiveness: being able to reach a person quickly, reschedule without a negotiation, and get an honest answer the same day. Again no car required, and in practice an arrangement with no travel sunk into it reschedules more easily than one where somebody has already left the house. The fourth is the genuine exception: physical presence. A younger child who needs an adult in the room, a student with an attentional profile that works materially better in person, a household with no quiet space or stable connection. For those, nearby is not a proxy for anything. It is the requirement.

So the honest answer to a near-me search is a question back: which of those four do you need? If it is the fourth, a local in-home provider in Ajman or Sharjah is the right purchase and we are not it, because IB Gram offers no home visits in the UAE. If it is any of the first three, the radius is costing you access to the people who have marked your child's paper, and it is costing you money as well.

sections.heading: Tuition centres: the other thing a near-me search returns
paragraphs: Alongside individual tutors, a local search surfaces tuition centres with premises and a timetable. They are a legitimate and often sensible purchase, and they are a different product from one-to-one in ways worth being explicit about before comparing prices.

A centre sells a paced scheme of work to a small group. That is well matched to a student who is broadly behind across a whole subject and needs the content covered again in order, with the discipline of a fixed weekly slot and other students in the room. It is poorly matched to a student whose content is largely in place and who is losing marks on one component, because a group of eight cannot be redirected to one child's error log however good the teacher is. Paying group rates for an individual problem is as inefficient as paying specialist rates for a fluency gap.

There is a regulatory difference too, and it is useful to know as a consumer. An operation with premises and staff is treated differently from an individual tutor. In Dubai a training institute requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit, obtained through initial approval followed by a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, with annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. An individual providing private lessons needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit instead, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Those are two different instruments for two different things, and a provider should be able to say which one applies to them.

To be plain about our own position: IB Gram operates no premises, centre, branch or office in the UAE, holds no regulator or examination-board permit of any kind, and makes no claim to any. Tuition is delivered one-to-one over live video. Any provider in this market implying a regulator endorses them should be asked to produce the permit number, because the permit is a specific document issued for a specific activity.

sections.heading: What a genuinely local tutor gives you that distance cannot
paragraphs: This page has argued hard in one direction, so it should concede properly in the other. There are things a nearby tutor provides that no amount of bandwidth replicates, and a family for whom those things matter should buy locally without apology.

Physical presence is the main one and it is not sentimental. A ten-year-old who will not stay at a desk without an adult beside them is not going to be fixed by a better platform. A student who is genuinely dysregulated by screens, or who has a processing profile that works much better with a person in the room, is in the same position. A tutor who can take a pen out of a child's hand, turn the page, and sit in a short silence while something lands is doing something a camera cannot do, and anyone claiming otherwise is selling.

There are smaller advantages that add up. A local tutor can see the bedroom the homework is attempted in, which is diagnostic in a way a video call is not. They can be handed the actual exercise book rather than a photograph of it. They absorb household context without anybody having to explain it. For a family where the problem is as much organisational as academic, that observational access is worth real money.

The reason this page still argues for video in Ajman is narrower than a general claim about formats. It is that the specific subjects where IGCSE marks are most often recoverable, the scarce components, are the subjects where the local field is emptiest. For Mathematics 0580 with a nearby, well-reviewed tutor who has marked Paper 4, book them. For 0478 Paper 2 from an address in Al Zorah, the nearby option is unlikely to exist, and the honest alternative is a specialist on a screen.

sections.heading: When nothing nearby covers the subject: the fallback, disclosed
paragraphs: No competitor page in the researched set discloses a coverage limit, and several conceal non-local delivery behind an overseas phone number. Here is ours, stated before you enquire rather than after.

Some subject and component combinations are genuinely thin even without a distance filter. Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 Paper 2, and the written practical science components at specific times of year are the recurring ones. When no tutor who has marked that component is free, there are exactly three honest responses and we will give you one of them with a date attached.

The first is a wait: a named estimate of when a specialist becomes available, usually at the start of a new teaching block. The second is a related specialist with the limitation stated plainly: a 0580 Extended specialist taking a 0606 student can do real work on calculus technique while being clear about what they have not marked, and you decide whether that trade is worth making. The third is a recommendation to look elsewhere, including at a local Ajman or Sharjah provider or at a tuition centre, which is sometimes simply the right answer.

What does not happen is a general tutor being presented as a specialist. You would find out in the marking, and by then a term would have gone and the window before the series would have closed. The whole value of being told a limit is that it arrives while you still have time to act on it, which is why availability is confirmed before any payment rather than after the first invoice.

sections.heading: Starting this week: what actually has to happen
paragraphs: A near-me search is usually urgent. Something has gone wrong in a report or a mock and the parent wants someone on it now. So here is the realistic timeline rather than a marketing one.

Confirming what is needed takes one message: the subject, the syllabus code and component from the school's entry statement, the tier, and a photograph of the most recent marked script. With that, matching to a tutor who has marked the component is usually a matter of a day or two for mainstream subjects. For the thin combinations above, it can be longer, and you will be told a date rather than kept waiting hopefully.

The first session is free and is spent marking a question set rather than on introductions, so the diagnosis exists at the end of the first hour rather than the third. After that it is billed monthly with no joining fee and nothing prepaid, which matters when the decision is being made quickly: a fast start should not create a long commitment. Sessions sit between 6.30pm and 9.30pm on weekdays, with weekend mornings for timed papers.

What cannot be compressed is the work itself. A technique fault takes two to three weeks of marked practice to close, and a content gap takes a term, and no start date changes those durations. The honest version of urgency is to start the diagnosis immediately so that the fortnight before the mock is spent on the right thing, rather than to promise a speed the examination does not permit.
